lecture.İkinci kalıbımız eksiği söylüyor: eksik: Our second pattern names what is missing: the verb of lacking is built with the dative, so the thing missing becomes the subject.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız savunmayı söylüyor: ayr: Our second pattern states the defence: a separable verb and a fixed preposition. After the preposition comes the accusative.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız kararı söylüyor: dönüşlü b: Our first pattern states the decision: a reflexive verb and an infinitive phrase. The reflexive pronoun comes straight after the verb.
Our first pattern defines the profession by its work. We use an indefinite personal pronoun and then a relative clause.
lecture.Koşul bağlacından sonra fiil sona gider;: After the conditional conjunction the verb goes last; when the subclause is first the main clause starts with the verb. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi: panel. Burad: Hello! The module's last lesson: the panel. The difficulty here is not speaking but speaking briefly and exactly to the point. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Ofiste bir gün. Ofis dili kişis: Hello! A day at the office. Office language is impersonal: what is talked about is not who did it but what was done. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yeni modül: mizah ve incelik. V: Hello! A new module: humour and subtlety. And the first lesson is one of PERCEPTION — hearing the opposite of what is said. Ready?
lecture.Modülü bitirdin. Konuşmada mentorunla bi: You have finished the module. In the speaking you will talk a decision over with your mentor: what your options are, what they would do in your place.
lecture.Türkçede niyet tek ekle çıkar; Almancada: English splits the sentence in two as well, but the object comes after the infinitive; in German it comes before it. The words first.
lecture.Yani 'Pek iyi şarkı söyleyemem'. Almanla: That is, 'I cannot sing very well'. Germans do not say 'I cannot do it at all' here; this softer form is used far more.
lecture.Yani 'Sabunu nerede bulurum?' Almancada: That is, 'Where do I find the soap?' In German the order in this question is fixed: the question word first, the verb straight after it.
lecture.Artık hangi gün ve saat müsait olduğunu: You can say which day and time suit you now. You are going to arrange a class time at a gym.
lecture.Artık ne iş yaptığını anlatabilirsin. Şi: You can say what you do for a living now. You are at a party at a neighbour's house and someone asks about your job.
lecture.Belirsiz özne ve kip fiilinin yumuşak bi: An indefinite subject and the soft form of the modal. It builds a piece of advice that points at nobody and holds for everyone.
lecture.Bugün günübirlik bir gezi planlıyoruz. P: Today we are planning a day trip. When the plan depends on the weather you have to build a conditional clause. Ready?
lecture.Bugün pazardayız! Meyvenin fiyatını sorm: Today we are at the market! We will learn to ask the price of fruit, to fix the quantity and to understand the total. Ready?
lecture.Doğru atıf üç şey ister: kim, ne dedi, n: A proper citation wants three things: who, what they said, and where. The reported mood takes on the second of these. The words first.
lecture.Doğru. Kadın komşu için kelimenin sonuna: Correct. For a woman neighbour an ending is added to the end of the word, and because the word is feminine the possessive takes its feminine form too.
lecture.Doğru. Zorunluluk fiili ikinci sırada, g: Correct. The verb of obligation is in second place, and the past form and the passive auxiliary stand side by side at the end of the sentence.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir sergide gördükle: You are ready. In the speaking you will describe what you saw at an exhibition: which work, what it reminded you of, what it made you feel.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada duyduğun bir tıbbi g: You are ready. In the speaking you will report a medical advance you heard about: what was found, how it was tested, what it means.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada girişim planını anla: You are ready. In the speaking you will set out your business plan: what you will start, on what condition it works, what would make you give up.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada kitap kulübünde bir: You are ready. In the speaking you will present a book at the book club: what you liked, which part was hard, who you would recommend it to.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada sınav kaygısını bir: You are ready. In the speaking you will talk about exam nerves with a teacher: what you dread, and what you would do if it happened.
lecture.İki kelimelik bir istek. Karşılaştırma b: A request of two words. The comparative here gives not a measure but a direction: shorter than it is now.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız aynı işi kısa yapıyor:: Our second pattern does the same job briefly: a preposition and an indefinite pronoun. It enters a reservation without building a subclause.
lecture.ise 'görünüşe göre muhtemelen öyle'. Tür: means 'apparently, and probably so'. English renders both of them as 'apparently' — and that is exactly why they get mixed up.
lecture.Kelime kelime 'ben otuz yıl yaşlıyım' de: Word for word 'I am thirty years old' — which is just how English says it, and German says the age in exactly the same way.
lecture.Koşul cümlesinde fiil en sonda, ana cüml: In the conditional clause the verb is at the very end, in the main clause the verb comes right after the comma and the subject behind it: both rules are in place.
lecture.Mastar öbeğinde küçük bir edat ve mastar: In the infinitive phrase a little preposition and the infinitive stand at the end of the sentence; the object comes before the infinitive. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün para. Bu deyimlerin ikisi: Hello! Today, money. Two of these idioms come from old currencies and yet they are still in daily use. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Müzakerenin son turundasın. Bur: Hello! You are in the last round of the negotiation. Here the language has one job: to have the last word without closing the door. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba. Son ders. Beş yüz dersin sonund: Hello. The last lesson. You are at the end of five hundred lessons and today there is no new rule — only a reckoning. Ready?
lecture.Modülü bitirdin. Konuşmada bir arkadaşın: You have finished the module. In the speaking you will recommend a dish to a friend: which dish, which ingredients, what goes with it.
lecture.Üç kelimelik bir cümle ama telefonda en: A sentence of three words, and yet the most useful sentence there is on the phone. Its subject is impersonal; it describes the situation itself.
lecture.Üç soru kelimesi artık cebinde. Şimdi bi: The three question words are in your pocket now. It is the first day of a German course and you will get to know the person next to you.
lecture.Yani 'Aktarma yapmam gerekiyor mu?' Türk: That is, 'Do I have to change?' English puts a verb at the front for this question too, and German simply fronts the verb itself, with no extra 'do'.
lecture.Yardım etmek, vermek, güvenmek gibi fiil: Verbs like to help, to give and to trust want the dative; the relative pronoun goes into that case too. The words first.
lecture.'bu yüzden'. 'Es gab Stau, deshalb habe: 'that is why'. 'Es gab Stau, deshalb habe ich mich verspätet.' deshalb in first place, habe second, ich third.
lecture.'Vardı' demenin yolu. Ardından gelen isi: The way to say 'there was'. The noun that follows goes into the accusative; its subject always stays the same and never changes with the person.
lecture.Belirsiz özne tekil, izin fiili ona uymu: The indefinite subject is singular, the verb of permission agrees with it and the main verb is last: the correct build of a rule that holds for everyone.
lecture.Bugün bir daveti reddediyoruz. Almancada: Today we are turning down an invitation. Refusing is not rude in German, but you are expected to say why. Ready?
lecture.Bugün hava durumunu konuşuyoruz. Bu, sev: Today we are talking about the weather. This brings the level's only new tense: the future. Ready?
lecture.Doğru. Fiil yalın hâlde, özne söylenmemi: Correct. The verb is in its bare form and the subject is not said; this is the familiar imperative exactly. Germans say it to each other every evening.
lecture.Doğru. Zarf cümlenin ilk öğesi olduğu iç: Correct. The adverb is the sentence's first element, so the finite verb comes right after it and the subject stands after that.
lecture.Dolaylı soru bir yan cümledir; yani fiil: An indirect question is a subclause, which means the verb goes last. This is where English speakers slip most. The words first.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir arkadaşınla dizi: You are ready. In the speaking you will debate a series finale with a friend: what you liked, what you liked it in spite of, what you had expected.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir arkadaşınla güve: You are ready. In the speaking you will talk about trust with a friend: who you trust, whose advice you listen to.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir beslenme danışma: You are ready. In the speaking you will discuss your habits with a nutritionist: what you are trying, what you find hard.
lecture.Hazırsın. Şimdi bir tanıdığınla iş yerin: You are ready. Now you will talk about the people at work with someone you know; describe each one with a relative clause.
lecture.İki cümle de aynı kalıpla kuruldu: asıl: Both sentences are built on the same pattern: the main verb waits at the very end. If you want to tell your plan, one sentence is enough as well:
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız bir şeyin normal olduğu: Our second pattern says that a thing is normal. It is one of the sentences you need most in a new country.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız tavsiye veriyor: bir sı: Our second pattern gives advice: an adjective plus an infinitive phrase. An impersonal structure, so it blames nobody.
lecture.İzin fiiliyle açılan kibar bir soru. Ken: A polite question opened with the verb of permission. The person being introduced is in the dative and stands right after the verb.
lecture.Kimin adına alındığını söyleyen edat bel: The preposition that says on whose behalf it is taken brings the accusative, and the separable prefix stands at the end of the sentence.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün arabayla yoldayız. Yol di: Hello! Today we are out on the road by car. The language of the road is built on conditions: if it rains, if the petrol runs out. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün aynı olayı üç ayrı dille: Hello! Today we will tell one and the same event in three different languages: as news, as a formal letter and as a chat with a friend. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün birini yatıştıracağız. Al: Hello! Today we will calm somebody down. German has a ready-made sentence of two words for this. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün çok işine yarayacak bir n: Hello! Today a trick you will find very useful: put in the objection before the deadline and send the grounds afterwards. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün okuduğun kitabı anlatacak: Hello! Today you will present the book you have read. The shortest way to present a book is the relative clause. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün renkler. Ve bu grup en ya: Hello! Today, colours. And this group is one of the most deceptive: in none of them is the colour meant literally. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve en resmî s: Hello! The module's last lesson and its most formal scene: the hearing. Here the source of every sentence is stated. Ready?
lecture.Sıfat burada bir zarf gibi kullanılıyor: The adjective is used here like an adverb and takes no ending at all; in German there is no difference in form between adjective and adverb.
lecture.Üçüncü kalıbımız aynı konunun iki yanını: Our third pattern shows the two sides of one subject: on the one hand this, on the other hand that. It keeps the debate balanced.
lecture.Ara açıklama, açıkladığı kelimeyle aynı: An inserted explanation takes the same case as the word it explains; here the subject is in the nominative, so the explanation is nominative too:
lecture.Artık kuralları anlayabilir ve anlatabil: You can understand the rules and explain them now. The building manager is going to stop you at the door and go through them.
lecture.Ayrılabilen fiilin ön eki cümlenin sonun: The separable verb's prefix is at the end of the sentence; the preposition that names who you work with brings the dative.
lecture.Bir meslek söylenirken artikel kullanılm: No article is used when a profession is named. English is the odd one out here: it says 'a pilot' and German does not.
lecture.Bu bağlaçtan sonra çekimli fiil cümlenin: After this conjunction the finite verb goes to the end of the sentence; since the subject is the same, an infinitive phrase could have been used as well:
lecture.Bugün ilgi alanını anlatmayı öğreniyoruz: Today we are learning to talk about your interests. This verb wants both a reflexive pronoun and a preposition of its own. Ready?
lecture.Burada iki fiil var ve dikkat: asıl fiil: There are two verbs here and mind this: the main verb goes right to the end of the sentence — English does not do that, it keeps the verb before the object.
lecture.Çekimli fiil ikinci sırada, asıl fiil en: The finite verb in second place, the main verb at the very end and in the infinitive. However long the sentence gets, that last word always stays last.
lecture.Dilek kipiyle verilen tavsiye emir gibi: Advice given in the subjunctive does not sound like an order; it sounds like a suggestion. In a moment of panic that difference matters. The words first.
lecture.Doğru. Posta kodu dişil bir kelime olduğ: Correct. Postcode is a feminine word, so the possessive comes in its long form, and the question is built with 'how'.
lecture.Dönüşlü zamir kip fiilinden hemen sonra,: The reflexive pronoun right after the modal, the main verb last and unsplit. This is the first sentence to say at the office.
lecture.Edat başta, soru kelimesi onun getirdiği: The preposition first, the question word in the case it brings and the verb in second place: this is the sentence reception really asks.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir mali müşavirle b: You are ready. In the speaking you will discuss your return with a tax adviser: what you can claim, when the refund comes.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir meslektaşına çey: You are ready. In the speaking you will present the quarterly results to a colleague: what the trend is, what stands out, and why.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada birine kısa bir röpo: You are ready. In the speaking you will conduct a short interview: ask, press further and sum up what they said in your own words.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada öfkeli bir müşteriyl: You are ready. In the speaking you will talk to an angry customer: name the feeling first, then come back to the matter and offer a solution.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız emin olmadığını söylüyo: Our second pattern says you are not sure. This pattern stops you giving wrong information, and in an official place that matters.
lecture.İkisi de dilek kipinde ve ikisi de soru: Both are in the subjunctive and both are in question form: they leave the other side room to say no. The words first.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız artan değişimi anlatıyor:: Our first pattern describes a growing change: an adverb and the comparative of the adjective. It is the pattern of weather talk.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız kararı anlatıyor. Yardımcı: Our first pattern tells of the decision. The auxiliary is in its past form and the participle last; who took the decision is not said.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız nötr bir adı tanımlıyor. N: Our first pattern describes a neuter noun. With a neuter noun the relative pronoun stays the same even as an object; only the verb goes last.
lecture.Karar ve gerekçe mastar öbeğiyle kurulur: The decision and its grounds are built with an infinitive phrase: a little preposition and the infinitive, both at the end of the sentence. The words first.
lecture.Köpek eril bir kelime ve burada nesne, b: Dog is a masculine word and the object here, which is why that familiar ending came. The rule really does work the same everywhere.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kiracı hakları. Hukukta b: Hello! Today, tenants' rights. In law a claim that is not put in the right verb phrase does not count as a claim. Ready?
Hello! Today we will write a farewell speech. This kind must be short, carry an image and leave nobody out. Ready?
Last one: 'I switched my phone on to ring you.' — 'Ich habe mein Handy eingeschaltet, um dich …' (a separable verb!)
lecture.Tanımlanan şey yan cümlenin öznesi olduğ: When the thing described is the subject of the subclause the relative pronoun stays in the nominative and the verb goes last. The words first.
lecture.Almanca bunun için tek bir sıfat kullanı: German uses a single adjective for this: deadline-keeping. Write that word and your right is not lost. The words first.
lecture.Artık anlamadığını söyleyebilir ve itira: You can say you did not understand and you can object now. An official is rattling something off at you.
lecture.Artık mesaj yazabilir ve doğru kapatabil: You can write a message and close it properly now. You are going to text a friend: they are expecting you this evening.
lecture.Artık paylaşımlı ev görüşmesine girebili: You can go to a house-share viewing now. You have gone to look at a place and the flatmates are meeting you.
lecture.Bugün bir taşınmayı anlatıyoruz. Almanya: Today we are telling of a move. People move very often in Germany and this story is useful in every conversation. Ready?
lecture.Bugün otel resepsiyonundayız. Rezervasyo: Today we are at a hotel reception. Announcing the booking and asking the right questions is half of the stay. Ready?
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir memurla oturma i: You are ready. In the speaking you will discuss extending your residence permit with an official: ask what is needed and explain your own case.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir tedarikçiyle fiy: You are ready. In the speaking you will bargain over price with a supplier: put your offer, ask for a gesture and settle on a figure.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir toplantıyı yönet: You are ready. In the speaking you will chair a meeting: open the agenda, steer the discussion, minute the decision and close.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir uyku danışmanıyl: You are ready. In the speaking you will describe your nights to a sleep adviser: what you do before bed, what happens in the night.
lecture.Hitaptaki sıfat dişil bir isme göre ek a: The adjective in the greeting has taken its ending from a feminine noun and the thanks are the standard continuation of a formal letter: the opening is right.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız endişeyi söylüyor: dönü: Our second pattern voices the worry: a reflexive phrase and the same conjunction. The reflexive pronoun comes straight after the verb.
Our first pattern says you are not sure. In questions with no question word this conjunction is used and the verb goes last.
lecture.Kimin şerefine kadeh kaldırıldığını söyl: The preposition that says whose health is being drunk brings the accusative, and the separable prefix stands at the end.
lecture.Merhaba! Bilgisayar çalışmıyor ve destek: Hello! The computer is not working and you are going to ring the support line. The first question is always the same: why it is not working. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün en hassas konu: neyin söy: Hello! Today the most delicate subject: what may be said. And here the job of language is neutral — to draw a distinction. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün müzik. Ama konu müzik değ: Hello! Today, music. But the subject is not music, it is power: who sets the tone, who does as they are told. Ready?
lecture.Türkçede 'ne kadar' deriz; Almancada sor: English puts an adjective beside the question word too — 'How high are the fees?' — and German asks the amount in exactly that way.
lecture.Artık iş gününü baştan sona anlatabilirs: You can describe a working day from beginning to end now. At the office you will explain the working hours to a new colleague.
lecture.Artık kibarca hayır diyebilirsin. Şimdi: You can say no politely now. A friend is asking you out this evening but you have neither the time nor the money.
lecture.Bir de beklenti kalıbı öğreneceğiz: olma: We will learn a pattern of expectation too: the thing you wanted to happen but did not. It is built with the subjunctive. The words first.
lecture.Bu yapı ilk modülde başladı, burada en y: This structure began in the first module and reaches its densest form here. The genitive endings will want care too. The words first.
lecture.Doğru. Almancada ağrı adı vücut bölümüyl: Correct. In German the word for pain joins the body part into a single word; you can do the same for the stomach and the back.
lecture.Edat en başta, hemen ardından soru kelim: The preposition right at the front and the question word straight after it. Because the preposition brings the dative, the question word goes into that case too.
lecture.Eril isim burada belirtme hâlinde. En sı: The masculine noun is in the accusative here. This is the commonest mistake: because the pattern means 'there is', people think the noun stays bare.
Good morning! Today we are at the breakfast table. We will learn to say what you eat and what you drink. Are you ready to start?
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir danışmana itiraz: You are ready. In the speaking you will put your objection to an adviser: what you are objecting to, what your grounds are, what you are asking for.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada kendi başından geçen: You are ready. In the speaking you will tell a small thing that happened to you from beginning to end; the other person will want the details.
lecture.her zaman çoğuldur, tıpkı Türkçedeki 'pa: is always plural, just like English 'chips'. When you ask the price of something plural the verb goes plural too, and
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız kibarca bilgi istiyor:: Our second pattern asks for information politely: the subjunctive and a question word as conjunction. The standard opening of a talk with an expert.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız rica: yapabilmek fiilin: Our second pattern is the request: the subjunctive of to be able in a question. This form is standard when you ask a waiter for something.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız neyin işe yaradığını söylü: Our first pattern says what helps: an impersonal verb and an infinitive phrase. It gives advice without blaming anyone.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir ilan okuyacağız. İlan: Hello! Today we will read an advert. Adverts are written short and what matters is often what is not written. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün hava. Ama hiçbiri gerçekt: Hello! Today, the weather. But none of them is really about the weather — they are all about the mood and the feeling. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün sinirlenmeyi öğreneceğiz: Hello! Today we will learn to get angry — but in measure. The particles work here like a scale. Ready?
lecture.Modülü bitirdin. Konuşmada bir ekip arka: You have finished the module. In the speaking you will give a teammate hard feedback — observation, suggestion, question, in that order.
lecture.Sebep her zaman beden olmak zorunda deği: The reason does not always have to be the size. Give another reason with last lesson's pattern: 'I do not like the colour.'
lecture.Selam! Bugün kardeşlerinden konuşacağız: Hi! Today we will talk about your brothers and sisters and learn German's most used little rule. Ready?
lecture.Almanya'da havuzlarda kurallar nettir ve: The rules at German pools are clear, and if you ask two questions at the entrance the rest comes easily. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Artık evini anlatabilirsin. Şimdi bunu g: You can describe your home now. Now you will use it in a real conversation: a friend is curious about your new place.
lecture.Bu ayrımı bilmeden ev bakarsan fiyatları: If you look for a flat without knowing this distinction you will compare the prices wrongly. Let us learn the words first, then open the distinction up.
lecture.Büfede kimse uzun cümle kurmaz, sıra hız: Nobody builds long sentences at a snack stand, the queue moves fast. That is why the language here is very short. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Cümlenin öznesi kıyafet; iltifat edilen: The subject of the sentence is the garment; the person complimented is in the dative. Exactly the same logic as English 'that suits you'.
lecture.denir. Bu kalıp işlerin nasıl gittiğini: is said. This pattern tells how things are going; being tired is your own state, so it is said with the verb 'to be'.
lecture.Doğru. Edat yönelme hâlinde kaynaşmış ve: Correct. The preposition has fused in the dative and the form of address is written with a capital like a noun — a polite sentence of refusal.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada aile hekiminle sürek: You are ready. In the speaking you will discuss a lasting complaint with your family doctor: how long you have had it, what it might be linked to.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir gönüllü kuruluşt: You are ready. In the speaking you will have an introductory interview at a voluntary organisation: why you want to come, what you can give.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız iki yanı gösteriyor. Her i: Our first pattern shows the two sides. Both halves start with an adverb, so in both the verb moves into second place.
lecture.Merhaba! Ailede büyük bir haber var. Böy: Hello! There is big news in the family. At such moments the sentences always carry the same two things: hope and worry. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Aldığın şey olmadı ve geri götü: Hello! What you bought is not right and you are taking it back. In Germany there is only one condition for this: a reason and a receipt. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Biri sana iğneleyici bir laf at: Hello! Somebody has made a barbed remark at you. Hitting back loses and staying silent loses; there is a third way. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün hayvanları tanımlayacağız: Hello! Today we will describe animals. With verbs that want the dative the relative pronoun changes its form too. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün sohbetin ince ayarı. B2'd: Hello! Today the fine tuning of conversation. At B2 you managed the lift chat; at C1 the point is KEEPING it going. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugünkü ders bir kural değil bi: Hello! Today's lesson is not a rule but a METHOD: how to unpick a forty-word German sentence. Ready?
lecture.Miktar söylemeden alışveriş bitmiyor; üç: Shopping does not finish without saying the quantity; with three words of measure you can get round the whole market. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Son: aynı fikri denn ile — 'Geç kaldım,: Last one: the same idea with denn — 'I was late, because there was traffic.' — 'Ich habe mich verspätet, denn …' (the order does not change!)
lecture.Türkçede 'Adınız ne?' dersin. Almanca bu: In English you say 'What is your name?'. German uses not 'what' but 'how' here; translate from the dictionary and you will get it wrong.
lecture.Artık havadan konuşabilir ve bir sohbeti: You can talk about the weather now and start a conversation easily. You have met your neighbour in the entrance of the building.
lecture.Asıl fiil yok. Yön bildiren edat cümleyi: There is no main verb. The preposition of direction completes the sentence and the verb of going drops away; this is a very natural shortening in German.
lecture.Belgenin dili tuhaf gelebilir: kimse kon: The language of the document can sound odd: nobody is speaking, the document speaks for itself. That is why it is passive. The words first.
lecture.Bu derste tek bir küçük kural var ve hed: There is only one small rule in this lesson and it comes up when you say who the present is for. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bugün hediyelik alıyoruz. Kime ne alacağ: Today we are buying souvenirs. When you say what you are buying for whom, the case you worked on in module 4 comes up again. Ready?
lecture.Bugün kayıp eşyaları konuşuyoruz: bu kim: Today we are talking about lost property: whose is this? The German for that question is built with a special question word. Ready?
lecture.Düz kipte 'yapın' demek emirdir; dilek k: In the plain mood 'do it' is an order; said in the subjunctive it becomes advice. The same sentence, another tone. The words first.
lecture.Hasta olmak bir durum, o yüzden 'olmak': Being ill is a state, so the verb 'to be'. A cold is something you have, so the verb 'to have'.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir arkadaşına duydu: You are ready. In the speaking you will relay a piece of news you heard to a friend — and separate off what is your own opinion.
lecture.Hoş geldin! Bugün yaşını söylemeyi, biri: Welcome! Today we will learn to say your age, to ask someone else's and to tell where you were born. Ready?
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız en üstün derece: bir ed: Our second pattern is the superlative: a preposition and the superlative of the adjective. It singles one thing out within a group.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız geçmişte olan bir işlemi a: Our first pattern tells of an action in the past. The auxiliary is in second place and in its past form, the participle at the very end.
lecture.Karşılaştırma sıfata ek getirir; durumun: A comparison adds an ending to the adjective; to say that things have turned round the other way a separate adverb is used. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bilerek belirsiz konuşaca: Hello! Today we will speak vaguely on purpose. It sounds crafty but half of diplomatic language is exactly this. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Servisteyiz. Usta sana 'bunu de: Hello! We are at the garage. The mechanic does not tell you 'you must change this'; they say 'this needs renewing'. No doer, only the job. Ready?
lecture.Selam! Bugün mesleğini anlatmayı öğrenec: Hi! Today we will learn to talk about your job: to say what you do and to add where you work. Ready?
lecture.Üç hamle: söz al, soruyu sahiplen, itira: Three moves: take the floor, own the question, refute the objection. All three are set patterns and all three make you look calm. The words first.
lecture.Üç şeyi tanımlayacağız: yemeğin kendisi,: We will describe three things: the dish itself, the ingredients and what goes with it. All three with a relative clause. The words first.
lecture.Yani 'ben daha çok … yerim'. İki şey ara: That is, 'I would rather eat …'. It is used when you choose between two things, and this word too stands right after the verb.
You can tell your career history now. You are sitting in front of an interviewer and will go through your CV step by step.
lecture.Bir de tamlama isteyen yeni bir edat var: And there is a new preposition that wants the genitive: the one that says whom a thing goes against. We will test it at the end. The words first.
lecture.Bir resmî yazının iskeleti dörttür: konu: A formal letter has four bones: the subject line, the greeting, the body and the close. Today we will build all four. The words first.
lecture.Bu ders, severek yapmayı anlatan kelimey: This lesson will fix the word for doing something gladly one more time; this time with watching. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bugün bazı fiillerin yanında hep aynı ed: Today we are learning that some verbs always have the same preposition beside them. These prepositions are not chosen, they belong to the verb. Ready?
lecture.Bugün bir odayı döşüyoruz. Hem tadilat k: Today we are furnishing a room. We will learn both the words for doing a place up and how to describe the space between two things. Ready?
lecture.Bugün sebep bildirmeyi öğreniyoruz. Alma: Today we are learning to give a reason. German has three ways of doing it and all three build the word order differently. Ready?
lecture.Cinssiz bir isim, o yüzden sıfat 'es' il: A neuter noun, so the adjective ends in 'es'. When the article does not show the gender of the noun the adjective takes that job on.
lecture.geçmişte tek seferlik olay ya da dönem:: a one-off event or period in the past: 'Als ich ein Kind war, wohnten wir in Izmir.' Childhood is a single period → als.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir kurs danışmanına: You are ready. In the speaking you will set out your goals to a course adviser: what you want in what time, and what your intermediate steps are.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir söylentiyi konuş: You are ready. In the speaking you will discuss a rumour: what you heard, what you know yourself, what you are only guessing.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir yakınınla aranız: You are ready. In the speaking you will talk over a matter between you and someone close: what happened, what you felt, what you want to happen.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada insan kaynaklarıyla: You are ready. In the speaking you will discuss remote working with HR: how many days, on what condition, under which rule.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız düzeltme istiyor: yapab: Our second pattern asks for a correction: a question in the subjunctive of to be able. The polite way of stepping in while the work is going on.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız iş bölümünü söylüyor: d: Our second pattern states the division of work: a reflexive verb. The reflexive pronoun here carries the sense of 'between us'.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız görseli tanımlıyor. İlgi z: Our first pattern describes the image. The relative pronoun takes the gender of the noun described and the verb goes to the end of the clause.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız malzemeyi soruyor. Kaynağı: Our first pattern asks about the material. The preposition that shows the source wants the dative, so the relative pronoun is in the dative too.
lecture.Kendisine tanıtılan kişi yönelme hâlinde: The person being introduced to is in the dative, the person introduced in the accusative and the main verb last: the whole pattern is right.
lecture.Koşul cümlesinde fiil sonda; ana cümle r: In the conditional clause the verb is last; the main clause is built in the formal imperative, so the verb is first and the address pronoun behind it.
lecture.Merhaba! Bir şey sipariş ettin ve bir so: Hello! You ordered something and a problem has come up. Today we will tell what happened with the past of the passive. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Evde bir kutlama var ve hazırlı: Hello! There is a celebration at home and you are getting ready. Today we will learn to put the jobs into time order. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Kalabalık bir ailede kimin kim: Hello! In a big family it is hard to say who is who. The relative clause solves that in one sentence. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Kendi işini kurmayı düşünüyorsu: Hello! You are thinking of setting up your own business. Every decision will have a purpose and you will have to say it. Ready?
lecture.Restoranda ton büfedekinden biraz daha r: The tone in a restaurant is a little more formal than at a snack stand: instead of short orders you build full sentences. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Sıra sende: 'Ne kadar çok okursam kelime: Your turn: 'The more I read the bigger my vocabulary is.' — 'Je mehr ich lese, desto …' (groß → größer)
lecture.Şimdi sen: 'Çanta masanın üstünde duruyo: Now you: what do you say for 'The bag is lying on the table.'? The bag is lying, so use the verb for things that lie.
lecture.Türkçede sayıdan sonra kelime tekil kalı: In English the word goes into the plural after a number, 'two books'. German does the very same and never leaves it singular.
lecture.Umarım hiç kullanmazsın ama artık bu cüm: I hope you never need them, but these sentences are yours now. You have seen an accident in the street and you are ringing the emergency line.
lecture.Almanya'da mesafe kilometreyle değil, da: In Germany distance is given not in kilometres but in minutes: how many minutes you walk, that is all. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Artık pazarda fiyat sorabilir, miktarı a: You can ask the price at the market now, fix the quantity and understand the total. You are in front of the stall and it is your turn.
lecture.Bir de geri alma kalıbı öğreneceğiz. Alm: We will learn a pattern for taking it back too. German does this short and clear: not a long explanation but a single sentence. The words first.
lecture.Bu da kadın komşu için. Almancada meslek: And this one is for a woman neighbour. In German the female form of job and role names is usually made by adding an ending. Please say
lecture.Bu grup Türkçe konuşan için özellikle tu: This group is especially treacherous for an English speaker, because the words are familiar and the meaning is somewhere else entirely. The words first.
lecture.Bugün çocukken ne olmak istediğini anlat: Today we are telling what you wanted to be as a child. For that we will learn the past forms of the modals. Ready?
lecture.Daha eski katman ayrı bir geçmiş biçimiy: The older layer is built with a separate past form: the auxiliary in the past and the main verb as a participle. The words first.
lecture.Doğru. İlk parçada fiil sonda, ikincide: Correct. In the first half the verb is last, in the second the comparative stands right after the conjunction and the verb comes after that.
lecture.Harika! Şimdi bir arkadaşın sana tatilin: Excellent! Now a friend is asking about your holiday. Tell them where you went, what you did there and when you came back.
lecture.Hazırsın! Şimdi görüşme odasındasın: ned: You are ready! Now you are in the interview room: you will say why you applied with 'weil' and how long you have worked with 'seit'.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir koçla hedeflerin: You are ready. In the speaking you will discuss your goals with a coach: say why you are working with um…zu, and the coach will ask 'wozu?'.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir yakınına vekâlet: You are ready. In the speaking you will give a relative power of attorney: what you want them to do, which document is needed, when it takes effect.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada eczacıya danışacaksı: You are ready. In the speaking you will consult the pharmacist: which medicines you take, whether they can be taken together, when you will take them.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız bir şeyin işe yaramadığ: Our second pattern says a thing is not worth it: an impersonal verb and an infinitive phrase. It is the sentence that ends the argument.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız eril bir adı tanımlıyor. Y: Our first pattern describes a masculine noun. To help wants the dative, so the relative pronoun is in the dative too.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız ikinciyi öne çıkarıyor. İk: Our first pattern puts the second one forward. Its second half is a special conjunction and cannot be swapped for the ordinary word of contrast.
lecture.İzin fiilinin olumsuzu 'gerek yok' değil: The negative of the verb of permission does not mean 'no need', it means 'forbidden'. For 'no need' the negative of the verb of obligation is used:
lecture.Karşılaştırmada sıfat ek alır; tercih sö: In a comparison the adjective takes an ending; to say a preference the comparative of the adverb of liking is used. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bir proje sunacaksın. İyi sunum: Hello! You are going to present a project. A good presentation is not one-sided: it gives both the strong and the weak side of the figure. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bilgi soracağız — ama res: Hello! Today we will ask for information — but formally. The politeness of a formal request comes once again from the subjunctive. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir maçı konuşacağız ve s: Hello! Today we will talk about a match and ask the commonest question in the language of sport: was the result deserved? Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün rol değişiyor: ilk kez se: Hello! Today the roles change: for the first time you will be the teacher. You will tell a beginner your own way. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün zor dinleyici. Sunumun ka: Hello! Today, the difficult audience. The quality of a presentation shows in the question round — and there you can be prepared. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Telefonda ton her şeydir çünkü: Hello! On the phone the tone is everything, because there is no face. German's two politest patterns come into play here. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yeni modül: retorik. Ve ilk ara: Hello! A new module: rhetoric. And the first tool is not a new rule — it is using a rule you know on purpose. Ready?
lecture.Örneğin 'çekincesiz tavsiye ederim' güçl: 'I recommend them without reservation' is strong, for instance; saying only 'I recommend them' counts as weak in German. The words first.
lecture.yani 'başlangıç olarak'. Bunu cümlenin s: that is, 'as a starter'. You add it to the end of the sentence — the very place English puts it, so the rule is that simple.
lecture.Yani 'Berlin treni ne zaman kalkıyor?' S: That is, 'When does the train to Berlin leave?' The order is always the same: the question word first, the verb right after it, then who or what.
lecture.'çünkü' demek. Ama dikkat: 'weil' ile ba: It means 'because'. But mind this: in a clause opened by 'weil' the verb goes to the END of the sentence. It does not stay in the middle as it does in English.
lecture.Artık adını harfleyebilir ve bir kelimen: You can spell your name now and ask how a word is written. You are getting a membership card at a library.
lecture.Ayrılabilen fiil ama sonu belirli bir he: A separable verb, but it ends in a certain syllable, so it does not take the participle's syllable; only the prefix stands at the front.
lecture.Bu kural bundan sonra her derste karşına: This rule will come up in every lesson from now on. You are on your coffee break and a colleague is talking about their brothers and sisters.
lecture.Bugün hastalığı işe bildiriyoruz. Almany: Today we are reporting sickness to work. In Germany this is two steps: telling them the same day and sending the certificate. Ready?
lecture.Bugün postanedeyiz. Gönderi biçimleri ar: Today we are at the post office. When you choose between the ways of sending something the superlative is exactly what you need. Ready?
lecture.Doğru. Yan cümlede edilgen geçmiş, ana c: Correct. The subclause is a past passive, the main clause has a verb of movement conjugated with sein and the verb comes right after the comma.
lecture.İki bağlaç kullanacağız: biri iki yanı y: We will use two conjunctions: one puts the two sides next to each other, the other concedes first and then enters a reservation. The words first.
lecture.İkili bağlaçlar bir görüşün iki yanını a: Paired conjunctions hold both sides of a view in one sentence. Their second half is fixed and cannot be changed. The words first.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız davetin ilk sorusu: ger: Our second pattern is the first question of the invitation: a question with the auxiliary meaning to be obliged. You are offering to bring something.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız ikisini birden dışlıyor: Our second pattern rules out both at once. Careful: with this conjunction the sentence is already negative and you do not add another negative.
lecture.İlk hamle 'sanki' yapısıyla kurulur ve b: The first move is built with the 'as if' structure, and it lets you name the problem without putting the other side in the wrong. The words first.
lecture.işi bitiriyor. Türkçede 'severek yerim': does the job. In English you say it with a verb — 'I like eating' — and the liking comes first; in German it is a little word that stands right after the verb.
lecture.Karşılaştırmada iki düzensiz biçim var v: There are two irregular forms in the comparison and both are very common: good and much. These have to be learnt by heart. The words first.
lecture.Kural: abartılı övgü Almancada güven kay: The rule: overblown praise loses you trust in German. A short, concrete sentence is stronger than three adjectives. The words first.
lecture.Mekân ve eser tanımlarken edatlı ilgi cü: When we describe venues and works we will build relative clauses with a preposition. The preposition comes before the pronoun and settles its case. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün anlatacağız. İyi bir hikâ: Hello! Today we will tell a story. A good story wants three things: a beginning, a turn and an ending held back. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir yemeği tarif etmeden: Hello! Today we will describe a dish without giving the recipe: 'the roast my mother makes', 'the pudding I brought yesterday'. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Konsolosluktasın ve hangi belge: Hello! You are at the consulate and you do not know which document is needed. In an official body the question is asked indirectly. Ready?
lecture.Modülü bitirdin. Konuşmada bir konferans: You have finished the module. In the speaking you will meet people at a conference: introduce yourself, say what you work on and make a connection.
lecture.Modülü bitirdin. Konuşmada hastanede bir: You have finished the module. In the speaking you will visit a relative in hospital: ask how they are, offer help, lift their spirits.
lecture.Modülü bitirdin. Konuşmada yaklaşan bir: You have finished the module. In the speaking you will discuss a coming election: what is being promised, what the polls say, what you expect.
lecture.tekrarlanan olay ya da gelecek: 'Immer w: a repeated event or the future: 'Immer wenn ich diese Musik höre, erinnere ich mich an damals.' Every time → wenn.
lecture.Türkçede 'Kaç yaşındasın?' dersin, Alman: English asks 'How old are you?' and German asks it in exactly the same way. The question word first, the verb right after it.
lecture.Yani '… yiyorum'. Türkçede fiil cümlenin: That is, 'I eat …'. English puts the verb straight after the subject, in second place, and German does the same.
lecture.Yani 'İyiyim.' Türkçede cümleye 'ben' il: That is, 'I am fine.' In English you start the sentence with 'I'; in German it starts with 'to me', because the verb is still that verb 'to go'.
lecture.Almanya'da değişim ve iade çok yaygındır: Exchanges and returns are very common in Germany and nobody will push you. There is one condition only: keep the receipt. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Amaç öbeği başta duruyorsa ana cümle fii: If the purpose phrase stands first the main clause starts with the verb — just as with conditional clauses. The same rule as ever. The words first.
lecture.Artık yaşını ve nereli olduğunu anlatabi: You can say your age and where you are from now. You are at a birthday party and you are meeting someone new there.
lecture.Dikkat edeceğin şey sıra: bu parçacık ba: What to watch is the order: if this particle stands next to another adverb it comes FIRST. We will test it at the end. The words first.
lecture.Doğru. Bu bağlaç cümlenin ilk öğesidir,: Correct. This conjunction is the sentence's first element, so the verb comes right after it and the reflexive pronoun stands after the subject.
lecture.Doğru. Genel özne tek kişi sayılır, zoru: Correct. The general subject counts as one person, the verb of obligation is conjugated for it and the main verb is at the end of the sentence; everything is in place.
lecture.Fiil 'yatıyor' anlamında ve edat yönelme: The verb means 'is lying' and the preposition brings the dative, because the question is WHERE. With a feminine noun the article changes in this case.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir arkadaşından tek: You are ready. In the speaking you will ask a friend for technical help: describe the problem, say what you have tried and find out the solution.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir kararını savunac: You are ready. In the speaking you will defend a decision of yours: the other person will say 'but…' and you will answer with obwohl and trotzdem.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir meslektaşınla iş: You are ready. In the speaking you will debate how to get to work with a colleague: give both sides and defend your own choice.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada müşteriye teslim tar: You are ready. In the speaking you will discuss the delivery date with a customer: say conditionally what is possible and name one exception.
lecture.İki bağlaç yeter ve ikisi de resmîdir. B: Two conjunctions are enough and both are formal. The first builds a subclause, the second stands at the head of the main clause. The words first.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız sıranın önemli olduğunu: Our second pattern says the order matters. A passive with no subject: neither the doer nor the done is said, only the action.
lecture.Karşılaştırma sıfata ek getirir; orantı: A comparison adds an ending to the adjective; a proportion is built with a paired conjunction and in the first half the verb goes last. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bir uzmana danışacaksın. Uzmana: Hello! You are going to consult an expert. There is a rule for asking an expert a question: not directly but indirectly. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün akademik dil. Kuralı tek: Hello! Today, academic language. Its rule can be said in one sentence: the writer leaves the sentence and the finding comes forward. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bölge klişeleri. Bu konud: Hello! Today, regional clichés. There is a rule for talking about this: the cliché may be said, but with a wink. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün çalışanın haklarını konuş: Hello! Today we will talk about workers' rights. Legal language always tells decisions taken in the past impersonally. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Üç dakikan var ve karşındaki ki: Hello! You have three minutes and the person opposite will either give money or not. This talk has an architecture. Ready?
lecture.Olmak fiilinin geçmişi. Bu cümlede yardı: The past of the verb to be. There is no auxiliary and no participle in this sentence; a one-word past, just like English 'I was'.
lecture.Sen bu cümlelerde özne değilsin, işlem g: In these sentences you are not the subject, you are the one being processed. That is why you build a passive even when you talk about yourself. The words first.
lecture.Sonu belirli bir heceyle biten yabancı k: Verbs of foreign origin ending in a certain syllable do not take the participle's syllable; the separable prefix stays at the front. It should be:
lecture.Test cümlesi: 'Berlin'e taşındığımda' —: A test sentence: 'when I moved to Berlin' — it happened once → als. 'whenever I go to Berlin' — repeated → wenn. The words first.
lecture.— 'çözülmesi gereken sorun'. Hem edilgen: — 'the problem to be solved'. Both a passive and an obligation, in a single adjective. The densest tool of formal writing. The words first.
lecture.Bir de emir kipi var: 'ilk adımı at'. Em: And there is the imperative: 'take the first step'. In an imperative you have to watch the case of the object. We will test it at the end. The words first.
lecture.Bugün bilgisayar sorununu çözüyoruz. Bir: Today we are solving a computer problem. The German way of giving somebody step-by-step instructions runs through the imperative. Ready?
lecture.Bugün iyi bir haber veriyoruz. Almancada: Today we are giving good news. In German news is not told straight out; first you build up the curiosity, then you tell it. Ready?
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada şefinle eğitim taleb: You are ready. In the speaking you will discuss a training request with your boss: why you want it, what the company gains, how it will be funded.
lecture.İki yapıyı yan yana kullanacağız: zorunl: We will use the two structures side by side: what is obligatory with sein plus zu, what is still possible with lassen plus sich. The words first.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız ağrının yerini tarif ed: Our second pattern describes where the pain is: the verb meaning to pull is used impersonally. Like English 'it aches'.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız emin olmadığını söylüyo: Our second pattern says you are not sure. In questions with no question word this conjunction is used and again the verb goes last.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün aileni tanıtmayı öğrenece: Hello! Today we will learn to introduce your family: you will build sentences like 'This is my mother', 'My son's name is Ali'. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bankadayız. Bankada sorul: Hello! Today we are at the bank. The questions asked at a bank are not direct but indirect — politer and safer. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Dün bir maç vardı. Spor anlatım: Hello! There was a match yesterday. Sports reporting is passive too: who scored is said afterwards, what happened comes first. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Eczanede en önemli soru ilacın: Hello! At the pharmacy the most important question is not the name of the medicine: can they be taken together. For that you need a conditional clause. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Hava ve arazi konuşacağız. Bu k: Hello! We will talk about the weather and the terrain. The language of this subject is comparison: colder, steeper, worse and worse. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! İki dil arasında yaşamak bir ka: Hello! Living between two languages is a state of comparison: which is easier, which are you more at ease in. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! İş arama süreci hep iki katmanl: Hello! Looking for work always has two layers: I applied, then they called me in. Today we will separate those two layers. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Küçük bir kaza oldu. İlk yardım: Hello! There has been a small accident. First-aid instructions are like a recipe: what matters is not who did it but what was done. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yöneticinle konuşacaksın. Alman: Hello! You are going to talk to your manager. In German business language a suggestion must not sound like an order; the subjunctive sees to that. Ready?
lecture.Sıfat bir ismin önünde durduğunda ek alı: An adjective takes an ending when it stands in front of a noun; here the noun is plural and has no article, so the adjective takes the plural ending. It should be:
lecture.Yani 'Berlin'e bir tane, lütfen'. Cümled: That is, 'One to Berlin, please'. There is neither a verb nor a subject in the sentence; nobody at the counter finds it odd, everyone says it this way.
lecture.Zaman ifadesi başta, fiil ikinci sırada,: The time phrase first, the verb in second place, the subject behind it; with a plural noun the negative word is in its plural form too. The sentence is correct.
lecture.Zamir burada 'birbirimizi' demek. Türkçe: The pronoun means 'each other' here. English has that word too — 'we got to know each other' — and in German the sentence stays incomplete without it.
lecture.'Yoktu' demenin yolu: sahip olmak fiilin: The way to say 'there was not': the simple past of to have plus a negative. The negative word changes with the gender of the noun.
lecture.Artık iş çıkışını anlatabilir ve tercihi: You can talk about the end of the working day now and say what you would rather do. A friend is going to ask you out this evening.
lecture.Bazı fiillerin edatı sabittir ve o edat: Some verbs have a fixed preposition and that preposition carries the meaning. When you learn the verb you have to learn its preposition too. The words first.
lecture.Bir de iki terim karışıyor: ihbarsız fes: And two terms get mixed up: dismissal without notice and dismissal with notice. The difference between them is months and money. The words first.
lecture.Bu sıfatın karşılaştırma biçiminde ortad: In the comparative of this adjective one of the middle vowels drops out; the rule itself is the same, only the spelling gets a little shorter.
Today we had a long wait at the office. We will learn both to tell what happened and to open a written complaint. Ready?
lecture.Bunun için tek bir fiil biçimi yeter ve: For this a single verb form is enough, and that form looks like a past but does not tell of the past. It tells a wish. The words first.
lecture.dedik. Kibar biçimde fiil neredeyse hep: we said. In the polite form the verb nearly always stays in the infinitive; the one important exception is the verb 'to be', and you will see it in a moment.
lecture.Denemeden almak Almanya'da pek âdet deği: Buying without trying on is not really the custom in Germany; every shop has fitting rooms and nobody rushes you. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.En kibar isteme biçimi izin fiilinin dil: The politest way of asking is built with the subjunctive of the verb of permission. This form joins a request to asking permission. The words first.
lecture.Güneş açtı ve herkes parkta. Bugün bir y: The sun is out and everyone is in the park. Today we will learn to say what is going on in a place and to make plans together. Ready?
lecture.Hatırlatma: geçmişte bir kez olan şey iç: A reminder: als for something that happened once in the past, wenn for something repeated. Arriving happened once, so als. The words first.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir arkadaşına geçmi: You are ready. In the speaking you will tell a friend about a decision you made in the past: what happened, what you should have done, what you think now.
lecture.İki parçacık aynı işi görüyor — biri kuz: Two particles do the same job — one is commoner in the north, the other in the south. Both are ways of saying 'that is how it is'. The words first.
lecture.İlk bölümü bitirdin. Konuşmada bir ara d: You have finished the first part. In the speaking you will take stock halfway: how the road went, what you are proud of, what comes next.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün Almancanın en sinsi taraf: Hello! Today the slyest side of German: the same sentence, two meanings. What carries the difference is little words and tone. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir nesneyi adını bilmede: Hello! Today we will describe an object without knowing its name: by saying what it is made of and what it is for. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün metni birbirine bağlayan: Hello! Today the little words that bind a text together: references. Without them writing looks like a list. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün mutfaktayız ve birlikte y: Hello! Today we are in the kitchen cooking together. We will learn to say who is doing what. Are you ready to start?
lecture.Merhaba! Kuaförde en zor şey ne istediği: Hello! At the hairdresser's the hardest thing is describing what you want. The polite form of that in German is built with the subjunctive. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi: bir sanat es: Hello! The module's last lesson: what measures the worth of a work of art? This debate runs on sentences of proportion. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi: münazara. Us: Hello! The module's last lesson: the debate. The craft is not crushing the other side but granting them a point and still defending your own. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yemekten sonra artan bir şeyler: Hello! There are leftovers from the meal. Today we will learn to say what you are planning to do with them. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yeni modül: medya. İlk ders man: Hello! A new module: the media. The first lesson is headlines, and headlines have an odd property — most of them have no verb. Ready?
lecture.Soru kelimesi yönelme hâlinin kendi biçi: The question word is the dative's own form. It is what 'who' becomes in this case, and it is always used when you ask whose something is.
lecture.Soru sözcüğü bağlaca döner ve fiil sona: The question word turns into a conjunction and the verb goes last; when there is no question word the conjunction that says you are unsure comes instead. The words first.
lecture.Tanımlanan şey yan cümlenin NESNESİ oldu: When the thing described is the OBJECT of the subclause the masculine relative pronoun changes its form; the feminine and neuter do not. The words first.
lecture.Yani 'Koşuya gidiyorum'. İki fiil yan ya: That is, 'I am going for a run'. Two verbs stand side by side and the second stays bare at the end. The same holds for swimming:
lecture.Yani 'Sinemaya gidelim mi?' Fiil en başt: That is, 'Shall we go to the cinema?' The verb stands right at the front with 'we' behind it; this order makes the sentence both a question and an invitation.
lecture.'Reklamı yapılan ürün' tek bir sıfatla s: 'The advertised product' is said with a single adjective, and it is exactly that density that pays off where the rule is written. The words first.
lecture.Artık arkadaşça öğüt verebilirsin. Şimdi: You can give a friend advice now. You are ringing a friend who has come down with flu and telling them what they should do.
lecture.Artık taksiye binip nereye gideceğini sö: You can get into a taxi now, say where you are going, ask how long it takes and pay. You are in the back seat of the taxi.
lecture.Bir de mastarın isim hâli var: 'dinlerke: And there is the noun form of the infinitive: 'while listening' becomes 'during the listening' in German. This structure comes up a lot in presenting. The words first.
lecture.Bir mecazla kapatacağız, çünkü bu yol ge: We will close with a metaphor, because this road really is like a climb: the summit is in sight but the path does not end. The words first.
lecture.Bu kez yönelme hâlli ilgi cümlelerini ku: This time we will use relative clauses in the dative — verbs like to help and to look after want it. The words first.
lecture.Bugün doğum günü kutluyoruz. Tarih söyle: Today we are celebrating a birthday. The German way of giving a date runs through the ordinals and those numbers take an ending. Ready?
lecture.Bugün ekran süresini konuşuyoruz. Koşul: Today we are talking about screen time. The conditional clause is used here to give the reason for a habit. Ready?
lecture.Bugünkü kalıp, Türkçeye şaşırtıcı biçimd: Today's pattern is one of the ones that turns English upside down. You will see why in a moment. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Daha eski olan katman ayrı bir geçmiş bi: The older layer is built with a separate past form: the auxiliary in the past and the main verb as a participle. The words first.
lecture.Edilgen çatının geçmiş biçimini kullanac: We will use the past form of the passive. The structure is the same, only the auxiliary goes into the past. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Hafta sonu planı, Almanya'da en sık soru: The weekend plan is one of the questions asked most often in Germany. On a Friday everybody asks everybody. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız sırayı veriyor: önce an: Our second pattern gives the order: the adverb meaning first, then the adverb meaning after that. A recipe is not a list, it is a sequence.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız koşul ve sonuç. Yan cümle: Our first pattern is condition and result. The subclause is first, so the main clause starts with the verb; an adverb slipped in between does not change that.
lecture.Kapanış cümleleri kalıptır ve tam olarak: Closing sentences are set phrases and are used exactly as set phrases — what is wanted here is not originality but clarity. The words first.
lecture.Kip fiili ikinci sırada, ayrılabilen fii: The modal in second place, the separable verb last and unsplit. One of the sentences you will hear most at a railway station.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün spor konuşacağız. Niyet v: Hello! Today we will talk about sport. Sentences of intention and advice are built with an infinitive phrase and the infinitive goes right to the end. Ready?
lecture.Olumsuzla birlikte kullanıldığında 'yasa: Used together with a negative it means 'it was forbidden'; this is the pattern you need most when telling about school. First, eight words.
lecture.Randevu almak, buluşma ayarlamak, 'ne za: Making an appointment, arranging a meeting, saying 'when are you free' — all of it hangs on these two little words. Let us learn the days first.
lecture.Sebep bağlacından sonra çekimli fiil cüm: After the causal conjunction the finite verb goes right to the end of the sentence. That one rule makes your complaint understandable. The words first.
lecture.Yan cümlede iki fiil var: asıl fiil önce: There are two verbs in the subclause: the main verb first, the modal at the very end. In the main clause the modal is in second place and the main verb last.
lecture.Yaş söylerken sayı, zaman birimi ve sıfa: When you give an age the number, the unit of time and the adjective come in that order. Even though the unit is plural it always stays the same in this pattern.
lecture.yazan bir metin o cümleyi onaylamıyor —: does not endorse that sentence — it hands it back to its source. A reader who misses this takes the reported claim for the writer's own verdict.
lecture.'Je mehr ich übe, desto besser werde ich: 'Je mehr ich übe, desto besser werde ich.' — in the je half the verb is last (übe), in the desto half the verb comes before the subject (werde ich).
lecture.A1'i bitirdin. Şimdi son bir konuşma: bi: You have finished A1. Now one last conversation: someone will ask how your German is going and you will tell them in your own sentences.
lecture.Artık kime nasıl hitap edeceğini biliyor: You know now whom to address how. It is your first day at work and you will meet your new boss: use the polite form.
lecture.Artık nerelerin gezilebileceğini sorabil: You can ask what there is to see now and give your own recommendation. You are at the tourist information desk and you have one day.
lecture.Bu ders geçen derslerdeki yapının mutfak: This lesson is the kitchen version of the structure from the last lessons: the same rule, new words and a far quicker pace. The words first.
lecture.Bu kalıp bundan sonra sık sık karşına çı: This pattern will come up often from now on. You are talking to a friend who insists on going to work although they are ill.
lecture.Bu yüzden üretim anlatımı baştan sona ed: That is why an account of how something is made is passive from beginning to end and joined by markers of order: first, then, last of all. The words first.
lecture.Bugün Almancanın en çok korkulan konusun: Today we will go into the most feared subject in German, but there is nothing to fear: the adjective taking an ending in front of the noun. Ready?
lecture.Bugün bavul hazırlıyoruz. Ayrılabilen fi: Today we are packing a suitcase. Separable verbs will come up once more in this lesson, this time in a question. Ready?
lecture.Bugün bir düğündeyiz. Kimin kim olduğunu: Today we are at a wedding. Saying who is who and proposing a toast are the two most useful things at a celebration. Ready?
lecture.Fiilin kendi edatı yönelme hâlini getiri: The verb's own preposition brings the dative and fuses with the article; the separable verb stands at the end together with the modal.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada komşunla gürültü mes: You are ready. In the speaking you will discuss the noise with your neighbour: state the fact, suggest without accusing and agree a solution between you.
lecture.İki nesne yan yana: gönderilecek kişi be: Two objects side by side: the person to be sent is in the accusative, and the pronoun saying it is for you is in the dative and comes first.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız eril bir adı tanımlıyor: Our second pattern describes a masculine noun, and this is where the pronoun changes form. For an English speaker the trap is exactly here.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız iki şeyi kapsıyor ve ikinc: Our first pattern covers both and puts the second forward. It does the same job as English 'not only … but also'.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün en insani cümlelerden bir: Hello! Today we will build one of the most human sentences there is: I wish I had. This is the subjunctive looking at the past. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün gününü anlatmayı öğrenece: Hello! Today we will learn to tell your day: when your day starts, when you work, when you sleep. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün tersini yapacağız: ekleme: Hello! Today we will do the opposite: not adding but LEAVING OUT. When it has to, German can drop the subject and the verb alike. Ready?
lecture.Sayıdan sonra kelimenin çoğula girdiğini: You know that a word goes into the plural after a number. The good news: in the plural the trouble with articles is over, they all fall into one form.
lecture.Selam! Bugün ağrı anlatacağız. Doktorun: Hi! Today we will describe pain. The doctor's first question is always the same and if you do not know the answer the examination stops right there. Ready?
lecture.Yardımcı fiil ikinci sırada, ortaç en so: The auxiliary in second place, the participle at the very end. If the sentence starts with a place phrase the subject moves behind the verb. The words first.
lecture.Artık bir yerde neler olduğunu anlatabil: You can say what is going on in a place now and make plans together. You are in the park: your friend has already found a spot.
lecture.Artık yol sorabilir ve gelen tarifi anla: You can ask the way now and understand the directions you get. You are in a street and you need to find the station: ask a passer-by.
lecture.Bedeni sorabiliyor, deneme izni isteyebi: You can ask for the size, ask to try it on and say how it went. You are in front of the fitting room and the assistant is looking at you.
lecture.Bir arızayı bildirmek kirayla ilgili hak: Reporting a fault is part of your rights as a tenant; saying it clearly makes things easier. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bir de iki dönüşlü fiil var: biri alışka: And there are two reflexive verbs: one for taking a habit up, the other for giving it up. Both want a pronoun in the dative. The words first.
lecture.Bu alanda üç fiil çok işe yarıyor ve üçü: Three verbs are very useful in this area and all three have a fixed preposition. Choosing the wrong one makes the sentence unintelligible. The words first.
lecture.Bu belirtide kişi özne olmaz, yönelme hâ: With this symptom the person is not the subject, they stand in the dative; said the other way it comes out as 'I make people dizzy'. It should be:
lecture.Bugün doktordayız. Almancada doktorun sö: Today we are at the doctor's. German has a modal of its own for reporting what the doctor said and we will learn it. Ready?
lecture.Bugün eczanedeyiz. Almanya'da eczacı sad: Today we are at the pharmacy. In Germany the pharmacist does not just sell, they advise as well; being able to ask the right question does the job. Ready?
lecture.Bugün halk eğitim merkezine kayıt oluyor: Today we are enrolling at the adult education centre. These places are cheap in Germany and they have everything — languages, music, sport. Ready?
lecture.Bugün mağazada iki kıyafet arasında kara: Today we are deciding between two garments in a shop. We will learn a pair of conjunctions that puts two options side by side. Ready?
lecture.Bugün nelerin değiştiğini anlatıyoruz. A: Today we are telling what has changed. German has two separate verbs for 'to change' and the two are not the same thing. Ready?
lecture.Dikkat: öbeğin fiili çekilir, ismi asla: Careful: the verb of the phrase is conjugated, the noun never changes. So in the phrase 'in Anspruch nehmen' only nehmen is conjugated. The words first.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada asansörde bir üst yö: You are ready. In the speaking you will meet a senior manager in the lift: keep it short, raise one matter in passing and take your leave politely.
lecture.İki bağlaç kullanacağız: biri önceyi, bi: We will use two conjunctions: one points at what came before, one at the same moment. In both the verb goes to the end of the clause. The words first.
Our second pattern puts the second one forward. Its second half is a special conjunction and cannot be swapped for an ordinary word of contrast.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız en kısa yol: eşyanın adını: Our first pattern is the shortest way: you name the thing, then say it is broken. Exactly the same order as English 'the lamp is broken'.
lecture.Merhaba! Bir liman şehrindeyiz ve gezdiğ: Hello! We are in a port city and we will describe the places we visited. For that we need relative clauses with a preposition. Ready?
Hello! Today you will run the evening. Compering is not talking, it is LINKING: building the passage from each part to the next. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün emeklilik konuşacağız. Bu: Hello! Today we will talk about retirement. At this age most talk is comparison: what it used to be like, what it is now. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün sayıları alıyoruz: yüze k: Hello! Today we take on the numbers: counting up to a hundred, saying your phone number and asking the price. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün seviyenin en pratik dersi: Hello! Today the most practical lesson of the level: moving from 'you' formal to 'you' familiar. Offering it at the wrong moment is hard, and so is refusing. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugünün konusu unvansız liderli: Hello! Today's subject is leadership without a title: giving direction with no authority to do it. Its language is not the order but the suggestion. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Eve girilmiş ve polise bildirec: Hello! There has been a break-in and you are going to report it to the police. In an official report the doer is unknown, so the passive is used. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yolculuk bitti ve anlatma vakti: Hello! The journey is over and it is time to tell it. A good account has two layers of past: what happened and what had happened before. Ready?
lecture.Modülü bitirdin. Konuşmada iki dakikalık: You have finished the module. In the speaking you will take part in a two-minute debate: state your view, give two reasons, close with one sentence.
lecture.Sebebi ince: 'aşılabilir' demek 'sen aşa: The reason is subtle: 'it can be got over' is less accusing than 'you can get over it'. Here the language is choosing an attitude. The words first.
lecture.Süre bildiren edat, yönelme hâlinde bir: A preposition of duration, a time phrase in the dative and a verb in the present: all three are right, because the living there is still going on.
lecture.Teamül şu: teklifi kıdemli ya da yaşça b: The custom is this: the offer is made by the senior or the older one. Refusing is not rude but it wants a courteous sentence. The words first.
lecture.Yani 'Ceketi internetten sipariş ediyoru: That is, 'I am ordering the jacket online'. You learnt the verb to order in the café; in front of a screen the same verb works.
lecture.'-mek için' demek. 'um' virgülden sonra: It means 'in order to'. 'um' comes after the comma, 'zu' right before the infinitive. With a separable verb zu goes into the middle: um … anzurufen.
lecture.Amaç bağlacı özne farklı olduğunda kulla: The purpose conjunction is used when the subject is different and it sends the verb to the end. Saying the purpose takes the rule out of the argument. The words first.
lecture.Artan değişim için sıfatın karşılaştırma: For a growing change the comparative of the adjective is repeated with an adverb; for a proportion a paired conjunction is used. The words first.
lecture.Bu metinde özne neredeyse hiç yoktur: uy: This text has almost no subject at all: it is warned, it is excluded, it is deemed accepted. Unpicking that is C1's job. The words first.
lecture.Bugün bir şeyin nerede olduğunu söylüyor: Today we are saying where a thing is. In German you have to choose two things at once: the right verb and the right case. Ready?
lecture.Bugün bir tartışmayı ve arkasından gelen: Today we are talking about an argument and the apology that follows it. The German pattern for an apology is again built with the dative. Ready?
lecture.Bugün evde bir şey bozulduğunda ne diyec: Today we will learn what to say when something at home breaks. There are two different ways of putting it and both are much used. Ready?
lecture.Bugün haber aktarıyoruz. Duyduğun bir şe: Today we are passing news on. When you say something you have heard a subclause is built and naming the source becomes important. Ready?
lecture.Bugün kendini tanıtmayı öğrendin. Şimdi: Today you have learnt to introduce yourself. Now it is time to use it in a real conversation: you will meet a new neighbour.
lecture.Çok iyi gidiyorsun. Artık hâl hatır soru: You are doing very well. You can ask how someone is and answer now. You have arrived at work and you meet a colleague at the door.
lecture.Değerlendirme dengeli olmalı: neyi başar: An assessment has to be balanced: what you managed and what you did not. Paired conjunctions are there for exactly this. First, our last words.
lecture.Edat ilgi zamirinin önüne gelir ve hâlin: The preposition comes before the relative pronoun and settles its case. English can also leave it at the end of the clause, and German never can. The words first.
lecture.Fiyat sormak tek bir soruyla oluyor ve o: Asking the price takes a single question, and you will use that question in a shop, at the market and in a café alike. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Geçen ders ikiyi karşılaştırdık. Bugün h: Last lesson we compared two. Today we are picking one out of them all, and that has a form of its own. Ready?
lecture.İlk bağlacımız geçmişteki bir dönemi anl: Our first conjunction tells of a period in the past. In the subclause the verb goes last, and if the subclause is first the main clause starts with the verb.
lecture.Kibarlığı taşıyan biçime dilek kipi diyo: The form that carries the politeness is what we call the subjunctive. Two verbs are enough: to be and to have. Those two carry the rest. The words first.
lecture.Kime söyleyeceğin yönelme hâlinde. Yan c: Whom you tell is in the dative. The subclause is in the past and the auxiliary goes right to the end with the participle standing before it.
lecture.Kural anlatan cümlelerde kimin yaptığı s: In sentences that state a rule who does it is not said, because the rule is the same for everyone. That is why the language is passive. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün Almancanın en ince araçla: Hello! Today one of German's finest tools: giving the SOURCE with modal verbs. Three verbs, three different sources. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün amaç cümlesini bir yere d: Hello! Today we will put the purpose clause in one more place: at the front. Said first, the purpose makes the sentence look like advice. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün üslup çevireceğiz. Aynı b: Hello! Today we will translate register. The same information can be written two different ways and which you choose decides your reader. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve seviyenin: Hello! The module's last lesson and perhaps the most C1 subject of the level: the difference in meaning between words that look alike. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yeni bir cihaz aldın ve kutudan: Hello! You have bought a new device and the manual came out of the box. Manuals are written like recipes: who does it is not said. Ready?
lecture.Üçü de aynı işi görür ama tonları farklı: All three do the same job but their tones differ: one states the possibility, one the obligation, and one looks like an adjective. The words first.
lecture.Yer değiştiren fiiller yardımcı olarak b: Verbs of change of place take the first verb as their auxiliary: to go, to come, to set off. All three of today's verbs are from this group.
lecture.'Verileri değerlendirirken' yerine 'değe: Instead of 'while evaluating the data' you say 'in the evaluation of the data'. This is the scientific version of the structure you learnt in the first module. The words first.
lecture.Artık damak tadını anlatabilirsin. Şimdi: You can talk about your taste now. You are on your lunch break: a colleague is asking what you want to eat, so say what you would rather have.
lecture.Artık ihtiyacını söyleyebilir ve aradığı: You can say what you need now and find the shelf you are looking for. You are in a chemist's with a little list in your hand.
lecture.Artık tabağına ne geleceğini kendin beli: You can decide for yourself what goes on your plate now. You are in the works canteen and the cook is telling you what there is today.
lecture.Bir de çoğulda yönelme hâlinin küçük bir: And there is a small dative ending in the plural — like 'bei Lebensmitteln'. We will test that at the end of the lesson. The words first.
lecture.Bir de eksiklik bildiren kişisiz bir kal: And we will learn an impersonal pattern that reports a shortage. It takes a fixed preposition and that preposition wants the dative. The words first.
lecture.Bu bağlacı bu modülde ikinci kez görüyor: You are seeing this conjunction for the second time in this module; the difference is that here the method describes not a recipe but a contribution. The words first.
lecture.Bugün Almancanın belkemiği olan kuralı ö: Today we will learn the rule that is the backbone of German. Once it settles, half of your sentences put themselves right. Ready?
lecture.Bugün bir yolculuk planlıyoruz. Almancad: Today we are planning a journey. In German the preposition for saying where you are going changes with the kind of place. Ready?
lecture.Bugün sakatlık anlatıyoruz. Almancada vü: Today we are describing an injury. In German an unexpected pattern is used for saying you have hurt part of your body. Ready?
lecture.Bunun kipi baştan sona irreal. Bir cümle: The mood of this is unreal from beginning to end. Slip into the plain mood in one sentence and the design turns into a claim and the debate is spoilt. The words first.
