lecture.Dolaylı soruda soru sözcüğü bağlaç olur: In an indirect question the question word becomes a conjunction and the verb goes right to the end. When you cannot make out an announcement this pattern saves you. The words first.
lecture.dürfte: büyük ihtimalle. soll: öyle diyo: dürfte: in all likelihood. soll: so they say. wird: certainly. Choosing the right one of the three makes your forecast defensible. The words first.
lecture.Hatırlatma: zamir kendinden ÖNCEKİ ismin: A reminder: the pronoun is chosen by the gender of the noun BEFORE it. Whatever the noun after it may be, that does not change. The words first.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir meslektaşınla to: You are ready. In the speaking you will go through the minutes of a meeting with a colleague: what was decided, who noted what, what is missing.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir uzman muayenehan: You are ready. In the speaking you will ring a specialist's reception: you have a referral, you want an appointment, you are asking how long the wait is.
lecture.İki kalıp öğreneceğiz: neyi denediğin ve: We will learn two patterns: what you are trying and what you find hard. Both take an infinitive phrase after the comma. The words first.
lecture.İki kalıp yeter: biri öneriyi senin ağzı: Two patterns are enough: one gives the suggestion in your own voice, the other impersonally. Both have an infinitive phrase and zu. The words first.
lecture.İskelet üç parçalı: dinleyiciyi yakalaya: The skeleton has three parts: an opening that catches the listener, a peak towards the end and a last sentence that echoes. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün haber dili. Ajans metnind: Hello! Today, the language of news. In an agency report every sentence has an owner and that owner is named at the start of the sentence. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün spor. Bu grup iş hayatınd: Hello! Today, sport. This group is the set of idioms used most in working life — do not be surprised to hear a football term in a meeting. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün tartışmanın en resmî araç: Hello! Today the most formal tools of debate: the concessive conjunctions. They grant the other side a point and keep your own position. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün veri koruma metinleri. Bu: Hello! Today, data protection texts. What marks these texts is the chain of genitives: a single term can be made of three nouns. Ready?
lecture.Ortaç sıfatları burada bir kez daha karş: Participle adjectives come up once more here, but this time in the language of sport: the winner being celebrated, the team that was beaten. The words first.
lecture.Yani 'Daha çok caz dinlerim'. Türkçede ': That is, 'I prefer listening to jazz'. English switches to a different word for this; in German the same little word simply takes its comparative form.
lecture.'Çalışıyordum, çalıştım' demek. Konuşmad: It means 'I was working, I worked'. In speech you use the two-part form; here one word is enough, and this is the voice of the written language.
lecture.Amacımız iki yönlü: memurun söylediğini: Our aim runs both ways: understanding what the official says and asking your own question properly. The second is usually the more important. The words first.
lecture.Artık bir formun karşısında dilsiz kalma: You will not be struck dumb in front of a form any more. You are registering your address at the town hall: answer the official's questions.
lecture.Artık bir şeyi değiştirebilir, iade edeb: You can exchange something now, return it and give the reason. You are at the returns desk of the shop and it is your turn.
lecture.Artık bisikletle gittiğini söyleyebilir,: You can say you came by bike now, hire a bike and understand the warnings. You are in a hire shop.
lecture.Bir de küçük ama tuzaklı bir dilbilgisi: And there is a small but tricky point of grammar: how a nominalised adjective is declined in the genitive. We will test it at the end. The words first.
lecture.Bir emir cümlesi ile bir yan cümle bir a: An imperative and a subclause together. In the subclause the verb goes right to the end; we will look at this in detail in later modules.
lecture.Bir hatırlatma: çoğul isimlerde ilgi zam: A reminder: with plural nouns the relative pronoun is die, and with a preposition the plural becomes denen. We will use both. The words first.
lecture.Bir örnek: aynı küçük ekmeğin en az üç a: An example: the same little bread roll has at least three names — Brötchen, Semmel, Schrippe. All three are right, each in a different place. The words first.
lecture.Bu kalıplar tanışma sohbetlerinin belkem: These patterns are the backbone of getting-to-know-you talk: you say something about yourself and you get the other person talking. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bugün bir şeyi birine verirken kişinin n: Today we are learning how the person is said when you give something to somebody. In German the one receiving goes into a case of its own. Ready?
lecture.Bugün eski bir fotoğrafa bakıyoruz ve ço: Today we are looking at an old photograph and you are telling about your childhood. For that two verbs have a past form of their own. Ready?
Here the verb is in the infinitive and at the very end. This is how Germans give short instructions: addressing nobody, naming the job directly.
lecture.Çözüm cümlesi yine yöntem bağlacıyla kur: The solution sentence is built with the conjunction of method again — 'you fix it by restarting it'. This lesson is the everyday version of that structure. The words first.
lecture.En sık yapılan hata sonu baştan söylemek: The commonest mistake is giving the ending away at the start. German has ready sentences that stop this — sentences that hold the tension. The words first.
lecture.Geçmişe dönük dilek kipinde bir tuzak va: There is a trap in the past subjunctive: after the auxiliary comes not an infinitive but a participle. We will test it at the end. The words first.
lecture.Hatırlatma: özne aynıysa kısa yol, farkl: A reminder: the short way if the subject is the same, damit if it is different. 'I am here so that THEY hear it' — a different subject, so damit. The words first.
lecture.İkisi de 'yaptım' demek; fark üslupta. K: Both mean 'I did it'; the difference is register. In speech the two-part form is preferred, in writing the one-part form. The words first.
lecture.İlk bağlacımız önceyi gösteriyor. Türkçe: Our first conjunction points at what came before. English builds a separate clause for it too, but in German the verb goes to the end of that clause.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız tabloyu tanıtıyor. Cümle y: Our first pattern introduces the chart. The sentence starts with a place phrase, so the auxiliary comes right after it and the subject after that.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız yazılı ricanın en kibar bi: Our first pattern is the politest form of a written request: the subjunctive of to be, then a conditional clause. In the clause the verb goes last.
lecture.Kökü t ya da d ile biten fiillerde söyle: With verbs whose stem ends in t or d a vowel slips in to make them easier to say, which is why the second one sounds a syllable longer.
lecture.Kritik nokta şu: edattan sonraki zamir,: The critical point is this: the pronoun after the preposition changes with the GENDER of the noun. One thing for a neuter noun, another for a masculine. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Acilde ilk soru hep aynıdır: ne: Hello! In A&E the first question is always the same: what happened. The answer is a narrative and its order is shown by the form of the verb. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir kültür dersi. Almanca: Hello! Today, a lesson in culture. Praise is measured in German and an English speaker who does not know this misreads it constantly. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün masa başında çalışanın kl: Hello! Today the classic problem of the desk worker: the back. What we will learn is the soft form of giving advice. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Evde küçük bir iş var ve aletin: Hello! There is a small job at home and you have not got the tool. Asking a neighbour for something is normal in Germany, but the form matters. Ready?
lecture.Sıra sende: 'Yemek listesini rica ediyor: Your turn: how do you say 'I would like the menu.'? You want a particular thing, so the word keeps its own article.
lecture.Türkçede bunu 'demiş' ekiyle yaparız; Al: English does it with a reporting verb — 'she said that …'; in German the verb itself changes form. In the language of news this is all but obligatory. The words first.
lecture.Üç formül yeter: karşılama, geçiş, duyur: Three formulas are enough: the welcome, the link, the announcement. All three are set phrases and it is good that they are — the listener knows where they are. The words first.
lecture.Yani 'Sağlıklı beslenmek gerekir.' Başta: That is, 'One should eat healthily.' The little subject at the front meant 'everyone'; the rule of obligation works the same way, with the main verb at the very end.
It does not mean 'not bad', it means 'very good'. The reverse holds too — 'there is air above' is a courteous 'not good enough'. The words first.
lecture.'yine de' demek. Ana cümle zarfı: birinc: 'all the same'. An adverb of the main clause: it takes first place, the verb second, the subject third. 'Ich bin müde, trotzdem gehe ich zum Sport.'
lecture.Almanca bu iki hamleyi tek cümleye sığdı: German has paired conjunctions that fit both moves into one sentence, and a letter to the editor is made of almost nothing else. The words first.
lecture.Amaç bağlacı özne farklı olduğunda kulla: The purpose conjunction is used when the subject is different: I am doing it so that THEY are comfortable. After the conjunction the verb goes last. The words first.
lecture.Bir dili öğrenirken en çok unutulan şey: The thing most forgotten while learning a language is how far you have come. This lesson is there to say exactly that. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bir şeyi yemediğini söyleyemezsen tabağı: If you cannot say that you do not eat something there will be surprises on your plate. Three patterns will settle it politely. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bu yapıyı B1'de öğrenmiştin; burada zorl: You learnt this structure at B1; the difficulty here is not the words but what the sentence does: defending yourself without accusing. The words first.
lecture.Bugün balkonu ve bahçeyi anlatmayı öğren: Today we will learn to describe the balcony and the garden. You remember the 'there is' pattern; this time we will put a place in front of it. Ready?
lecture.Bugün geçen haftayı özetliyoruz. Bu, işt: Today we are summing up last week. This is asked constantly at work and in class: what you did, what you got done, what happened. Ready?
lecture.Bugün izin istiyoruz. Almanya'da izin sö: Today we are asking for leave. In Germany leave is talked about out loud but also granted in writing; the language of the two differs a little. Ready?
lecture.Bugün mahalleni anlatıyoruz. Yol tarifi: Today we are describing your area. We will learn the words for giving directions and for saying where a place is. Ready?
lecture.Bugün telefon ve internet aboneliğini ko: Today we are talking about phone and internet contracts. Here the comparative turns into a real decision about money. Ready?
lecture.Hatırlatma: tanımlanan şey yan cümlenin: A reminder: if the thing described is the object of the subclause the masculine pronoun changes. In the feminine, the neuter and the plural nothing changes. The words first.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir teknik destek ha: You are ready. In the speaking you will ring a technical support line: describe the fault, say what you have tried and get a solution or an appointment.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada sana şaşırtıcı bir h: You are ready. In the speaking you will put questions to somebody telling you surprising news: where did you hear it, who is saying it, did you check.
lecture.Hoş geldin! Bugün soru sormayı öğreneceğ: Welcome! Today we will learn to ask questions: where from, where and what. With these three words you can get the other person talking. Ready?
lecture.İkili bağlaçlar iki parçadır ve ikisi bi: Paired conjunctions come in two parts and both are used. Saying one and forgetting the other leaves the sentence half finished. The words first.
lecture.İlk bağlacımız geçmişte bir kez olanı an: Our first conjunction tells of something that happened once in the past. In the subclause the verb goes last, and if the subclause is first the main clause starts with the verb.
lecture.İnternet alışverişinin kelimeleri her si: The words of online shopping are the same on every site; learn them once and every site feels familiar. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.İş görüşmesinin iki temel sorusu var: ne: A job interview has two basic questions: why and how long. You will answer both with this lesson's patterns. The words first.
lecture.Koşul cümlesinde fiil sonda; ana cümlede: In the conditional clause the verb is last; in the main clause the verb comes right after the comma, the subject behind it and the reflexive pronoun behind the subject.
lecture.Merhaba! B1'in son modülüne geldik ve en: Hello! We have reached B1's last module and we start with its finest structure: describing a world that does not exist. 'If I were rich…' Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! İlk modülde bir sunum açmıştın;: Hello! In the first module you opened a presentation; now you will close one. A closing has three parts: summary, conclusion, outlook. Ready?
lecture.Orada konuşma hızlı akar ama kalıplar he: The talk there runs fast but the patterns are always the same; know three of them and you will manage at any stall. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Peki 'Ben İstanbul'dan geliyorum.' demek: And what sentence do you use to say 'I come from İstanbul.'? A small point: no article goes in front of a city name.
lecture.Perondasın ve tren yok. Bugün gecikmeyi: You are on the platform and there is no train. Today we will learn to say there is a delay, to ask when it comes and to say you are waiting. Ready?
lecture.Selam! Bugün adını harflemeyi öğreneceği: Hi! Today we will learn to spell your name. In Germany you are asked to do it everywhere: at the bank, at the doctor's, on the phone. Ready?
lecture.Selam! Bugün dillerden konuşacağız: biri: Hi! Today we will talk about languages: you will learn to ask someone which languages they know and to give your own answer. Ready?
lecture.Tanımlanan şey yan cümlenin öznesi olduğ: When the thing described is the subject of the subclause the relative pronoun stays in the nominative and agrees with the gender of the noun described. The words first.
lecture.Varmak yer değiştiren bir fiil, o yüzden: To arrive is a verb of change of place, so it has taken the first auxiliary; the adjective reporting the damage stands without an ending. The sentence is correct.
lecture.Yine de fark etmek mümkün ve C1'de bekle: Even so it is possible to notice, and that is what is expected at C1: you do not have to laugh, it is enough to see where the play is. The words first.
lecture.Artık müzik zevkini anlatabilir ve terci: You can talk about your taste in music now and say what you prefer. You are coming out of a concert and the person beside you has started talking.
lecture.Bir günün var ve şehri gezeceksin. Bugün: You have one day and you are going to see the city. Today we will learn to ask what there is to see and to give your own recommendation. Ready?
Today we are complaining about a faulty product. You have this right in Germany, but using the right words speeds the process up. Ready?
lecture.Bugün dizi ve program konuşuyoruz. Koşul: Today we are talking about series and programmes. We will see the second form of the conditional clause: what happens when the subclause comes second. Ready?
lecture.Buradaki ikinci kelime artikelin aynısı:: The second word here is the same as the article: der for masculine, die for feminine, das for neuter, die for plural. And mind this: the verb goes right to the end of the clause.
lecture.Cevap şu: var ama KURU. Espri yüksek ses: The answer is this: they have one, but it is DRY. The joke is not flagged out loud, it is hidden inside the sentence and the timing decides everything. The words first.
lecture.Fiilin edatı yönelme hâlini getirmiş ve: The verb's preposition has brought the dative and the main verb is last; in speech the preposition fuses with the article, but writing them apart is not wrong either.
lecture.Gecikme bir sıfat değil, bir isim olarak: Delay is used here not as an adjective but as a noun, and it stands without an article. English says 'our train is delayed' with an adjective instead.
lecture.İki kalıp kullanacağız: olmasaydı ne olu: We will use two patterns: what would have happened without it and what you are proud of. The first is the subjunctive, the second a subclause. The words first.
lecture.İyi bir savunma üç parçadır: görüş, sıra: A good defence has three parts: the view, the reasons in order, the close. Putting them in order lets the listener follow. The words first.
lecture.Kulağa övgü gibi geliyor ama 'eigentlich: It sounds like praise, but 'eigentlich' promises a 'but'. At C1 you are expected both to hear this and to build it. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün beslenmeyi konuşacağız —: Hello! Today we will talk about eating — not by reeling off a list but by telling of your own effort. The pattern for that is the infinitive phrase. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün zor bir konu: kim topluma: Hello! Today a hard subject: who counts as part of society. On subjects like this a one-sided sentence turns into an argument at once. Ready?
lecture.Şuna dikkat et: Türkçede 'Ben bir öğretm: Mind this: in English you say 'I am a teacher'. In German that 'a' is never used when you name a profession; the profession comes straight after.
lecture.Türkçede amaç tek ekle çıkar: -sin diye,: English builds a subclause for purpose too — 'so that …' — but in German the verb goes to the end of it. First, this lesson's words.
lecture.'Anıları uyandırarak etkiliyor' — işte t: 'It moves us by waking memories' — that is exactly this structure. It is the most useful sentence form there is in talk about art. The words first.
lecture.Amaç iki yolla söylenir. Özne aynıysa kı: Purpose is said in two ways. The short way if the subject is the same, the long way if it differs. Today we will practise the short way at work. The words first.
lecture.Artık birini tarif edebilirsin. Şimdi bi: You can describe somebody now. A friend is talking about someone they have just met and you want to know what they are like.
lecture.Artık bu fiilleri doğru kurabilirsin. Şi: You can build these verbs correctly now. You will talk tomorrow's plan over with a friend and you will need these verbs constantly.
lecture.Bir de küçük bir istisna öğreneceğiz: al: And we will learn a small exception: after alles, etwas and nichts the relative pronoun is not das but was. The words first.
lecture.Bir de sıraya bağlı izin kalıbı öğrenece: And we will learn a pattern of permission that depends on order: you may do this only once that has happened. In English we say 'only once …'. The words first.
lecture.Bugün iltifat ediyoruz. Almancada iltifa: Today we are paying compliments. Compliment patterns are short in German, but if the pronoun inside them is in the wrong case the sentence falls apart. Ready?
lecture.Bugün işe ilk gün: kendini tanıtıyorsun: Today is your first day at work: you introduce yourself and others are introduced to you. In Germany this is done with set patterns. Ready?
lecture.Bugün sınav öncesini konuşuyoruz. Heyeca: Today we are talking about the run-up to an exam. Describing your nerves and putting your preparation in order are the sentences built most before an exam. Ready?
lecture.Bugün taşınma gününü konuşacağız. En çok: Today we will talk about moving day. The most useful thing will be asking for help, and one verb is enough for that. Ready?
lecture.Çekince bağlacından sonra fiil sona gide: After the conjunction of reservation the verb goes last. And we will learn a short prepositional phrase that does the same job in one word. The words first.
lecture.Edat ilgi zamirinin ÖNÜNE gelir ve zamir: The preposition comes BEFORE the relative pronoun and settles its case. English can leave it at the end of the clause, and German never can. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! B1'in son dersindesin. Bugün ye: Hello! You are at B1's last lesson. There is no new rule today; today you will take stock of the road you came in your own sentences. Ready?
Hello! Today we will speak without being certain. At B2 you did this with modal verbs; the particle does the same job more lightly. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün eski teknolojiyi konuşaca: Hello! Today we will talk about old technology: cassettes, the radio, the first computers. Talk like this is always comparison. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün miktarları öğreneceğiz: b: Hello! Today we will take on quantities: a kilo, two bottles, three of them. You will be able to say how much you want. Are you ready to start?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün olmamış bir geçmişi tartı: Hello! Today we will debate a past that never happened — 'if only it had been done this way'. German has a structure exactly for this. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Trafik kuralları hiçbir dilde ': Hello! Traffic rules never say 'you do this' in any language; they always speak impersonally. In German the way to do that is the passive. Ready?
lecture.Modülün son dersinde başardığın bir şeyi: In the module's last lesson we are telling of something you achieved. A success story has three parts: the effort, the difficulty and the result. Ready?
lecture.Sıra kelimesi başa geçince özne fiilin a: When the word of order moves to the front the subject falls behind the verb. English has no such swap, so it needs care here.
lecture.Yani 'Bu hangi kanalda?' Televizyonda bi: That is, 'Which channel is it on?' A verb of its own is used for a programme 'being' on television, just as English says 'what's on'.
lecture.Aralarında ince bir fark var: biri sebeb: There is a fine difference between them: one stresses the cause, the other the result, and the third the stance taken in the face of a situation. The words first.
You can tell your day from beginning to end now. Now you will use it in a real conversation: a new colleague is curious about your day.
lecture.Artık sabahını sırayla anlatabilirsin. Ş: You can tell your morning in order now. Now you will use it: your flatmate wants to know why you leave so late in the mornings.
lecture.Bir de öznesiz edilgen öğreneceğiz: kims: And we will learn a subjectless passive: nobody is named and only the doing of the job is reported. This is very common in German. The words first.
lecture.Bir de tartışmayı açık bırakan güzel bir: And there is a fine pattern that leaves the debate open: 'the question to be asked is'. It puts the question on the table without answering it. The words first.
lecture.Bu fiillerde edat anlamın parçası; edat: With these verbs the preposition is part of the meaning; change the preposition and the meaning changes. That is why we learn the verb and its preposition together. The words first.
lecture.Bugün işte telefonu karşılıyoruz. Almany: Today we are answering the phone at work. In Germany this is done with set patterns and knowing them gives you confidence. Ready?
lecture.Bugün toplantıdayız. Görüş bildirmenin A: Today we are in a meeting. The German way of giving an opinion runs through a subclause, and in that clause the verb goes to the end again. Ready?
lecture.Doğru. Boy bir özellik olduğu için 'olma: Correct. Height is a quality, so 'to be'; hair belongs to the body, so 'to have'; both are exactly right.
lecture.Doğrudan söylemek karşı tarafı köşeye sı: Saying it straight out corners the other person. Said in the subjunctive the door stays open and both of you are more at ease. The words first.
lecture.Edilgende yardımcı fiil ikinci sırada, o: In the passive the auxiliary is in second place and the participle last. In sentences that start with a place phrase the subject moves behind the verb. The words first.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız süregelen rahatsızlığı söy: Our first pattern describes a lasting complaint: a verb and a fixed preposition. It is not for a passing pain but for one that has gone on for months.
lecture.İlk kalıbımızda küçük bir sürpriz var. B: There is a small surprise in our first pattern. The verb to begin changes its middle sound in the third person and the piece at the front goes to the end again.
lecture.Karşılaştırma sıfata bir ek getirir. Ort: A comparison adds an ending to the adjective. To compare with the average a preposition is used, and that preposition wants the dative. The words first.
lecture.Koşullu bağlacı ikinci modülde görmüştün: You met the conditional conjunction in the second module; here you will use it to set out a plan. It is a subclause, which means the verb is last. The words first.
lecture.Kural biraz tuhaf: ilk parçada fiil sona: The rule is a little odd: in the first half the verb goes last, in the second it comes right after the adjective. A pattern to be learnt by heart. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Almanya'nın güneyinde ve Ren bö: Hello! In the south of Germany and in the Rhineland the biggest event of the year is the carnival. Today we will tell it in order. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün ifade vereceksin. Buradak: Hello! Today you will give a statement. This language has two rules: say what you saw in the plain mood and what you heard in the reported mood. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kelime oyunları. Ve başta: Hello! Today, wordplay. And an admission at the outset: most of it does not survive translation — because the joke is not in the meaning but in the SOUND. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kötü haberi kurum adına v: Hello! Today we will give bad news on behalf of an organisation. This language has two jobs: accepting responsibility and not making the panic worse. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün mahkeme dilini tanıyacağı: Hello! Today we will get to know the language of the court. Legal language describes not the person but the process, so it is almost always passive. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve edilgenin: Hello! The module's last lesson and the most practical face of the passive: the division of labour. You can list every job without naming anybody. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve konusu DOZ: Hello! The module's last lesson and its subject is DOSE. Ten idioms crammed into one talk is worse than using none at all. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Ortak yaşamın en tartışmalı kon: Hello! The most argued-over subject in living together is cleaning. Today we will both share out the work and say the purpose of every rule. Ready?
lecture.Modülü bitirdin. Konuşmada barınakta bir: You have finished the module. In the speaking you will talk to a worker at the shelter: which animal, what kind of home it needs, what responsibility it brings.
Now let us suggest that they try something. When there are two verbs in the sentence the conjugated one stays at the front and the main verb goes to the very end in the infinitive.
You can tell your weekend plan now. You will talk the weekend over with a friend — say the plans that are not settled yet as well.
lecture.Artık kalkış saatini, peronu ve aktarmay: You can ask the departure time, the platform and the change now; with those three questions you can get anywhere in Germany. You are in front of the information desk.
lecture.Artık mutfakta iş bölüşebilirsin. Şimdi: You can share out the work in the kitchen now. You are at your friend's house, the ingredients are on the worktop and you will cook dinner together.
lecture.Artık ne kadar istediğini söyleyebilirsi: You can say how much you want now. You are in a greengrocer's: the man behind the counter has been waiting for customers since morning.
lecture.Aynı parçacık 'zaten' anlamına da gelir;: The same particle also means 'anyway'; which one it is depends on what the sentence is doing. This double use gets confused at C1. The words first.
lecture.Bir de kalıplaşmış bir ifade öğreneceğiz: And we will learn a set expression: 'to have a right to something'. In German this is built with a noun and a fixed preposition. The words first.
lecture.Biri bir andan önceyi gösteriyor, öteki: One points at what came before a moment, the other at what went on throughout it. Both build a subclause, which means the verb goes last. The words first.
lecture.Bu kuralı kullandıkça yerleşecek. Şimdi: This rule will settle as you use it. You will talk to your teacher at a language course and start your sentences with time phrases.
lecture.Bu üçü sabit kalıplarla söylenir; cümley: These three are said with set phrases; rather than trying to build the sentence yourself it is safer to use the phrase as it stands. The words first.
Today we are comparing the old days with today. This is a subject that works in every conversation and it is built with the simple past of two verbs. Ready?
lecture.Bugün iş görüşmesinin en zor sorusuna ha: Today we will prepare for the hardest question in a job interview: your strengths and weaknesses. The trick is knowing how to enter a reservation. Ready?
lecture.Bugün renkler var. Beş renk öğreneceğiz,: Today there are colours. We will learn five colours, practise saying what colour a thing is and asking for the same item in another colour. Ready?
lecture.Bugün Türkçe konuşan için tamamen yeni b: Today we are learning something completely new for an English speaker: in German an adjective changes its ending when it stands in front of a noun. Ready?
lecture.Davet aldın ama gidemeyeceksin. Bugün bi: You have had an invitation but you cannot go. Today we will learn to turn an invitation down without hurting anyone and to offer another day instead. Ready?
lecture.İlk kalıbımızda 'var' kalıbının başına y: In our first pattern we put the place in front of the 'there is' pattern. When the place comes first the verb comes right after it — you know that rule by now.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir DEĞİŞİMİ anlatmayı öğ: Hello! Today we will learn to describe a CHANGE: something increasing bit by bit. German has a very short pattern for this. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir yemek davetindeyiz. İ: Hello! Today we are at a dinner invitation. We will learn to accept what is offered, to refuse politely and to praise the food. Are you ready to start?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kıyafet deniyoruz. Almanc: Hello! Today we are trying clothes on. In German an adjective takes an ending when it goes in front of a noun, and that ending changes with the article. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün pazardayız ve seçim yapac: Hello! Today we are at the market and we will make a choice. Choosing means comparing: which is fresher, which is cheaper. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün tuhaf bir duyguyu anlatac: Hello! Today we will describe an odd feeling: feeling a stranger when you go back to your own country. The language for that is the 'as if' structure. Ready?

lecture.Merhaba! Siyaset konuşmak Almanya'da nor: Hello! Talking politics is normal in Germany but it has its form: an opinion is said in a subclause, not claimed outright. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yeni modül ve konusu dilbilgisi: Hello! A new module, and its subject is not grammar but TONE. These little words add no meaning to the sentence, they add the speaker's stance. Ready?
lecture.Modülün son dersinde yeni yıl kararların: In the module's last lesson we are talking about new year's resolutions. The modal of firm intention comes up again here. Ready?
lecture.Yazılı nezaket dilek kipiyle kurulur. Se: Written courtesy is built with the subjunctive. Even a hard demand stays polite once it is in the subjunctive, and it loses none of its clarity. The words first.
lecture.Zor olan kalıbın kendisi değil, DEĞİŞMEZ: What is hard is not the pattern itself but its FIXEDNESS. Some phrases take no article and adding one letter makes the sentence amateurish. The words first.
You can say where things are now. Now you will use it: a friend is asking where to put things in your new place.
lecture.Bir de kendiliğinden olan şeyler için dö: And there are reflexive verbs for things that happen by themselves: 'word gets around'. Very close to the English passive. The words first.
lecture.Bu fiilin bir farkı var: kökü vurgusuz b: This verb has a difference: its stem starts with an unstressed prefix, so it takes no participle syllable at all. The separable prefix at the front and the rest plain.
lecture.Bu geçmiş tek parçadır: yardımcı fiil yo: This past is one piece: there is no auxiliary, the verb goes into the past with its own ending. Narrative and formal texts prefer it. The words first.
Today we are telling of a morning that went wrong. It happens to everyone and it is one of the most useful stories to be able to tell. Ready?
lecture.Çok iyi! Şimdi ilanını gördüğün daire iç: Very good! Now you are talking to the landlord about the flat whose advert you saw. Ask questions with polite patterns and try to get a viewing.
lecture.Geçen derste geçmiş zamanı kurduk. Bugün: Last lesson we built the past tense. Today there is a small but important exception: some verbs take a different auxiliary. Ready?
lecture.İki kalıp: biri ikisini de kapsar, öteki: Two patterns: one covers both, the other leaves both out. Whether the verb is singular or plural wants care. The words first.
lecture.Kişi yönelme hâlinde ve saç belirlilik t: The rule is a little strange: the person is in the dative and the hair carries the definite article. These two together are what the possessive in English 'my hair' corresponds to.
lecture.Merhaba! Almanya'da liseden sonra iki yo: Hello! In Germany there are two roads after school: an apprenticeship or university. Today you will say which one you chose and why. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün alışverişin ilk adımını y: Hello! Today we will take the first step in shopping: comparing. Asking the price is not rude in Germany, it is expected. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün alışverişte tercih anlata: Hello! Today we will say what we prefer when shopping — not by the brand name but by the FEATURE. For that we go back to the relative clause. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün gönüllülüğü konuşacağız v: Hello! Today we will talk about volunteering, and grammatically we are on the conjunction of method again: HOW somebody carries something. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün hayvanlar. Almanca hayvan: Hello! Today, animals. German animal idioms work very differently from the English ones — the pig brings luck, for instance. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kuşaklar arası hesap. Bu: Hello! Today, the reckoning between the generations. In this debate both sides are right, and that is exactly why the concessive conjunctions are needed. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün meslekleri tanıtacağız. B: Hello! Today we will introduce professions. Knowing the name of a job is not enough; you have to be able to say what it does in one sentence. Ready?
Hello! Today we will write a formal complaint. And mind this: in German formal correspondence anger is carried not by tone but by grammar. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün sigortayla ihtilaf. Bu ya: Hello! Today, a dispute with an insurer. The language of this correspondence is full of concessive conjunctions: it seems to agree while protecting the claim. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün veda edeceğiz. Veda konuş: Hello! Today we will say goodbye. The tenses of a farewell speech are special: the past perfect is used to tell what came first. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve bütün modü: Hello! The module's last lesson, and it gathers the whole module up: first you will relay a claim, then you will set the truth against it. Ready?
lecture.Modülü bitirdin. Konuşmada vatandaşlık d: You have finished the module. In the speaking you will ask a citizenship adviser what you do not know: what is required, how long it takes, which document is needed.
lecture.Önce olan iş bir basamak geriye çekiliyo: What happened first is pulled back one step and what happened after stays in the ordinary past. That way the order is clear in a single sentence. The words first.
What happened first is pulled back one step — the same job as the English past perfect, 'I had done'. And A&E has a passive language of its own. The words first.
lecture.Tavsiyeyi düz kipte söylersen emir gibi: Advice said in the plain mood sounds like an order. The subjunctive puts a softness in between: not 'I do' but 'I would do'. The words first.
It is used when you introduce yourself on the phone. English says 'This is Ali' rather than 'I am Ali', and German builds it the same way — 'here is Ali'.
lecture.Alan kişi fiilin hemen ardında ve yönelm: The person receiving comes right after the verb and is in the dative; the thing given comes after that. Break the order and the sentence sounds wrong to a German ear.
lecture.Almanya'da davet edilince ne getireceğin: Asking what to bring when you are invited is the usual thing in Germany, and the host generally says so plainly. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Almanya'da neredeyse her şey randevuyla: Almost everything in Germany runs by appointment: the doctor, the authorities, the repairer. These three patterns will do for all of them. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bir günlük ağrı ile aylardır süren bir ş: A pain of one day and a complaint of months are not told with the same word. For the lasting one there is a verb with a fixed preposition. The words first.
lecture.Birincisi tamlama hâli ister ve bu çok a: The first wants the genitive and this gets skipped a lot. The second stands at the head of the main clause and the verb moves right behind it. The words first.
lecture.Bu bağlaç yan cümle kurar, yani fiil son: This conjunction builds a subclause, which means the verb goes last. And that is exactly where the sentence gets its force: the reason stands beside the decision. The words first.
lecture.Bu fiil bir yerden bir yere geçmeyi anla: This verb describes going from one place to another, so it takes the first auxiliary. It is a separable verb and its participle opens up in the middle.
lecture.Bu yapıların Almancada üç biçimi vardı v: These structures had three forms in German and you saw two of them in the last module. Today you will use them at the speed of a phone call. The words first.
lecture.Bugün acil bir diş ağrısıyla telefondayı: Today we are on the phone with an emergency toothache. In an emergency you have to speak briefly and clearly; today we will learn those sentences. Ready?
lecture.Bugün gelecek planlarını anlatıyoruz. Ge: Today we are talking about your plans for the future. You saw the future tense in the weather forecast; here you will use it for your own life. Ready?
lecture.Bugün zor bir konuşmayı öğreneceğiz: kom: Today we will learn a hard conversation: telling your neighbour that something is bothering you. The knack is turning the complaint into a request. Ready?
lecture.Bugünkü iki fiil edatını sabit taşıyor v: Both of today's verbs carry a fixed preposition and both want the dative. The wrong preposition makes the sentence unintelligible. First, the words for the body.
lecture.Çekince bağlacı 'zor ama yine de' der. Y: The conjunction of reservation says 'hard, but even so'. In the clause the verb goes last, and if the clause is first the main clause starts with the verb. The words first.
lecture.Doğrudan fiyat söylemek yerine yön göste: Rather than naming a price outright it points in a direction, a polite bargaining question with an impersonal subject: at a flea market this is exactly how it is said.
lecture.Gerekçe bildiren bağlacı biliyorsun ve o: You know the conjunction that gives grounds and it too sends the verb to the end. Today we will use it in a serious conversation. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir arkadaşına başvu: You are ready. In the speaking you will tell a friend how the application turned out: when it was handed in, what was checked, what answer came.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir tanıdığınla günc: You are ready. In the speaking you will debate a current subject with someone you know: give your view, back it up, say whether you agree with them.
lecture.İlanı tanımlarken ilgi cümlesi kuracağız: We will build a relative clause to describe the advert. When the thing described is the subject of the clause the relative pronoun stays in the nominative. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Almanya'ya yeni gelenin ilk şaş: Hello! The first thing that surprises a newcomer to Germany: the rubbish is not one bin but four or five. Today we will learn the language of those rules. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! B1'in ilk bölümünün son dersind: Hello! We are at the last lesson of B1's first part. There is no new rule today; today you will tell your own road with what you have learnt. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir sergideyiz ve öğrenec: Hello! Today we are at an exhibition and what we will learn is this: what a work did to you. For that we need a few verbs with fixed prepositions. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün herkesin bildiği bir duyg: Hello! Today, a feeling everybody knows: the technology is not working. The good news is that both the complaint and the solution have ready patterns. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün riskli bir kararı anlatac: Hello! Today we will tell of a risky decision, and the skeleton of such accounts is contrast: I left ALTHOUGH it was safe. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün şirket kurallarının dilin: Hello! Today we will work on the language of company rules. In that language sentences are shortened not with subclauses but with noun phrases. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve konusu gel: Hello! The module's last lesson and its subject is the future. But not a forecast, a DESIGN: building a world that does not exist and looking at today from inside it. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi: bir şeyi değ: Hello! The module's last lesson: what is done to change something. Every action will have a purpose and you will say that purpose. Ready?
Hello! A new module: society and the economy. But to be able to talk about these subjects we will first learn to link facts to one another. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yolda bir şey ters gitti ve bir: Hello! Something has gone wrong on the road and somebody needs to know what to do. The politest way of giving advice is the subjunctive. Ready?
lecture.Miktarı belli olmayan yiyeceklerin önüne: We put no article in front of foods of no set quantity, just as English says 'I eat bread' with nothing in front of it. Please say
lecture.Olumsuzluk kelimesi asıl fiilin hemen ön: The negative word stands right in front of the main verb. This is a separable verb, but used together with a modal it does not split.
lecture.Yani '… yemiyorum'. Türkçede olumsuzluk: That is, 'I do not eat …'. In English the negative attaches to the verb; in German it comes as a separate word in front of the food itself.
lecture.Yani 'Affedersiniz, tren garı nerede?' B: That is, 'Excuse me, where is the station?' Leaving the apology off the front is noticed in Germany; always start with it when you speak to someone.
lecture.Almanya'da sofrada yemeği övmek insanı ç: Praising the food at the table makes people very happy in Germany; knowing how to say 'that is enough' is every bit as useful. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bu iki kalıp sohbetin en kolay kapısı: i: These two patterns are the easiest door into a conversation: people want to know what you had for breakfast, and you can ask them. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bugün havalimanındayız. Burada her şey b: Today we are at the airport. Everything here runs in an order of obligations, and the modal that tells that order is the verb of obligation. Ready?
lecture.Etikette fiyat yoksa ne yaparsın? Bugün: What do you do if there is no price on the label? Today we will learn to ask the price, to say you find it dear and to take advantage of a sale. Ready?
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada bir toplantıda mesle: You are ready. In the speaking you will object to a colleague in a meeting: show first that you understood, then state your reservation, then propose a compromise.
lecture.Hazırsın. Konuşmada ekibinle işleri payl: You are ready. In the speaking you will share the work out with your team: discuss what can be done, what has priority and who takes on what.
lecture.İki ortaç bir arada: biri sıfat gibi kul: Two participles together: one is used like an adjective, the other is the past tense itself. Because the verb is one of change of place the auxiliary follows suit.
Our second pattern is the reason: the causal conjunction. After the conjunction the finite verb goes right to the end of the sentence — this is the sentence that justifies your complaint.
lecture.İlk bağlacımız bir şeyi eklerken kullanı: Our first conjunction is used when you add something and its second half is a special conjunction; it cannot be swapped for an ordinary one. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün para biriktirmeyi konuşac: Hello! Today we will talk about saving money. The most basic sentence in this field is a proportion: the higher the return, the higher the risk. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Sunumun en zor kısmı sunum deği: Hello! The hardest part of a presentation is not the presentation but what comes after: the questions. The good news is that there are three ready moves for meeting a question. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yeni modül: para ve kariyer. İl: Hello! A new module: money and career. The first lesson is the tensest conversation of all — pay. And the good news is that language can carry the tension. Ready?
lecture.Selam! Bugün fotoğraflara bakacağız: kim: Hi! Today we will look at photographs: you will learn to ask who somebody is and to build sentences like 'our grandfather', 'her aunt'. Ready?
lecture.Şüpheyi doğrudan söylemek de mümkün ama: Saying the doubt outright is possible too, but turning it into a question works better. Both have a subclause and in both the verb goes last. The words first.
lecture.Üç hamle yeter: öneri getirmek, kararı k: Three moves are enough: bringing a proposal, minuting the decision and drawing it together. All three are set phrases and we will build all three today. The words first.
lecture.Yani '… içiyorum'. Bir bardak ya da bir: That is, 'I drink …'. If you mean a glass or a cup you put an article in front of it; when you say what you drink in general no article is needed.
lecture.Almancada iş çıkışının kendine ait bir k: German has a word of its own for the end of the working day — English has no single word for it. Let us start with that and then go on to the patterns.
lecture.Artık hangi araçla gittiğini söyleyebili: You can say which way you travel now, ask about the stop and the line. You are at the stop and asking the person next to you about the right bus.
lecture.Bağlaçtan sonra çekimli fiil cümlenin en: After the conjunction the finite verb goes right to the end of the sentence. This structure puts the opinion inside a sentence and softens the debate. The words first.
lecture.Bugün komşu adına gelen kargoyu konuşuyo: Today we are talking about a parcel that came for the neighbour. This happens very often in Germany and there are sentences both sides need to know. Ready?
lecture.Bugün mevsimleri ve tarih söylemeyi öğre: Today we will learn the seasons and how to say a date. In dates German does what English does: the day number turns into an ordinal. Ready?
lecture.Bugün muayenehane resepsiyonundayız. Alm: Today we are at a surgery reception. The first step of going to the doctor in Germany is handing over your card and answering a few questions. Ready?
lecture.Bugünkü kalıp, gömülü sorunun daha kibar: Today's pattern is a politer form of the embedded question: it starts with 'I would like to know' and takes the question inside it. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Dönüşlü zamir yönelme hâlinde ve incinen: The reflexive pronoun is in the dative and the part that got hurt carries the definite article. These two together do the job of the possessive in English 'my knee'.
lecture.Harika gidiyorsun! Şimdi gerçek bir kafe: Fantastic! Now you are in a real café: the waiter is coming to take your order. Order with the patterns you have learnt and ask for the bill at the end.
lecture.İki araç var: soruyu yumuşatan parçacık: There are two tools: the particle that softens the question and ready answers that commit you to nothing. The second saves you from being cornered. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir cümleyi duyduğunda so: Hello! Today we will learn the questions to ask when you hear a sentence: where does this come from, who is saying it, is it really so. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir mahalle projesindeyiz: Hello! Today we are on a neighbourhood project: a shared garden. In shared work the rules are not personal, so the language is passive again. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün çoğul yapacağız: iki kita: Hello! Today we will make plurals: two books, many people, a few children. The German plural has a secret and I will tell you that too. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün iki parçacık: biri şaşırt: Hello! Today, two particles: one surprises, the other softens. Both are small and both change the sound of the sentence. Ready?
Hello! Today we are in a professional kitchen. A recipe book does not say 'you do this'; it says 'this is to be cooked so'. That is, the modal passive. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün şehrin görünümünü tartışa: Hello! Today we will debate the look of the city and you will use the possessive relative clause to describe the buildings. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün uzun bir hikâyeyi kısa an: Hello! Today we will learn to tell a long story briefly: a friendship broke and then came back. There are two layers of time. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün yapay zekâyı konuşacağız: Hello! Today we will talk about artificial intelligence and the language of this subject is passive: what can be done is talked about, not who did it. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün zor bir konu: yanlış gele: Hello! Today a hard subject: saying that something is wrong. In German the way to do it is not raising your voice but giving a reason. Ready?
Hello! You are going to make a weekend plan. In German a suggestion is offered in the subjunctive; that way the other person can easily say no. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve en faydalı: Hello! The module's last lesson and its most useful: how you say criticism. German has a threefold order — observation, suggestion, question. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve en insani: Hello! The module's last lesson and the most human of them: visiting the sick. There are three things to say — good wishes, an offer of help and encouragement. Ready?
lecture.Selam! Bugün hâl hatır sormayı öğreneceğ: Hi! Today we will learn to ask how someone is: asking after them, saying how you are and putting the question back to them. Ready?
lecture.Sıra şu: itirazı dile getir, sonra ona k: The order is this: voice the objection, then argue against it. Both are set phrases and both feed on the subjunctive and impersonal structures. The words first.
lecture.Sözleşme dili neredeyse tamamen isimleşm: The language of a contract is almost entirely nominalised and the genitive is everywhere. A missing ending makes the sentence impossible to unpick. The words first.
lecture.Türkçede 'bir çay alayım' ile 'bir çay a: In English too the difference between 'I want a tea' and 'I would like a tea' sits in the verb, and German does exactly the same. The words first.
lecture.Almanca bunu iki kalıpla yapıyor: bir me: German does this with two patterns: an expression of distance and a 'so they say, but'. Without both the cliché turns into a blanket verdict. The words first.
lecture.Artık buluşma ayarlayabilir, uymayan saa: You can arrange a meeting now and politely say no to a time that does not suit. A friend is going to ring you and want to meet this week.
lecture.Bu modülün son dersi. Bugün geçici kiral: This is the module's last lesson. Today we will talk about temporary lets — a very common way in Germany for students and newcomers. Ready?
lecture.Bugün ev sahibinden onarım istemeyi öğre: Today we will learn to ask the landlord for a repair. Saying it in formal language pays off: your request turns into a written record. Ready?
lecture.Bugün kendi hikâyeni anlatıyorsun: nered: Today you are telling your own story: where you came from, what it was like at the start, what it is like now. You will be asked this story many times in Germany. Ready?
lecture.Bunun için iki öbek şart: bir konuyu mas: Two phrases are needed for this: putting a subject on the table and taking on a risk. Both are function-verb phrases and both are fixed. The words first.
lecture.Bunun yolu ilgi cümlesi. Tanımlanan kişi: The way to do it is the relative clause. When the person described is the subject of the clause the relative pronoun stays in the nominative and the verb goes last. First, the professions.
lecture.Cümle tamam. Zorunluluk fiili yön bildir: The sentence is fine. When the verb of obligation is used with an expression of direction the verb of going is not said; at the airport this is exactly what you hear.
lecture.İki hazır kalıp var ve ikisi de kurumsal: There are two ready patterns and both are all but standard in institutional correspondence. And we will watch the object case of the verbs. The words first.
lecture.İki şey lazım: bir iki saniye kazandıran: Two things are needed: an opening sentence that buys you a second or two, and a skeleton that splits the answer into three. Together they shut the panic down. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün ileri müzakere. B2'de fiy: Hello! Today, advanced negotiation. At B2 you bargained over price; at C1 the question is not the price but which subject is opened when. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün lokantadayız. Almancada s: Hello! Today we are in a restaurant. The polite way of ordering in German is built with the subjunctive — not with the tone but with the form of the verb. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün övgü. İkinci modülde ölçü: Hello! Today, praise. In the second module we looked at restraint; here we look from the other side — how do we praise so that it is believed. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün röportaj yapacağız. Röpor: Hello! Today we will do an interview. An interview has two languages: direct when you ask, indirect when you write. We will build both. Ready?
Hello! Yesterday we built a world that does not exist. Today one step further: the thing you want to happen but which is not happening. In English we say 'if only'. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Geçen ders niyeti öğrendik. Bug: Hello! Last lesson we learnt intention. Today we will turn intention into a goal — and a good goal has one condition only: it must be measurable. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Havalimanındayız ve bir şeyler: Hello! We are at the airport and something has gone wrong. Airport announcements are nearly always passive: who did it is not said. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve bir sınavı: Hello! The module's last lesson and a rehearsal for an exam as well: defending your view in two minutes. For that you need ordering and a close. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Nerede kalacağınıza karar verec: Hello! You are going to decide where to stay. Deciding means comparing: which is cheaper, which is quieter. Ready?
lecture.'Bilmek isterdim' demek ve arkasından gö: It means 'I would like to know' and an embedded question follows. The soft form of the verb makes the sentence polite, and in the embedded part the verb is last again.
lecture.Ama bir sınır var: kısalık anlaşılırlığa: But there is a limit: brevity must not damage clarity. Telegraph style pays off in business correspondence, not in an explanation. The words first.
lecture.Artık ne izlediğini anlatabilir, kanalı: You can say what you are watching now, ask about the channel and give the time. You are at home on the same sofa as your flatmate and the remote is in the middle.
lecture.Biri mastar öbeği, öteki araç bildiren b: One is an infinitive phrase, the other a conjunction of means. The second is the exact counterpart of English 'by doing …' and it sends the verb to the end. The words first.
lecture.Bu bağlaçları altıncı modülde kurmuştun;: You built these conjunctions in the sixth module; the difficulty here is where the verb goes after the second half. We will test it at the end. The words first.
lecture.Bu cümleler dolaylı sorulardır, yani fii: These sentences are indirect questions, which means the verb goes last. Asking directly is not rude, but the indirect form shows your level. The words first.
Today we are talking about the noise from upstairs. This is the commonest neighbour problem in Germany and how you say it changes the outcome. Ready?
lecture.Çünkü bu duygu bir olgu değil bir benzet: Because this feeling is not a fact but a likeness: you are NOT a stranger, but you feel like one. The subjunctive carries exactly that. The words first.
lecture.Dikkat edeceğin bir dilbilgisi noktası v: There is a point of grammar to watch: the verb of thanking wants the dative and in the plural the noun takes an ending. We will test it at the end. The words first.
lecture.Fark ettin mi: dördü de aynı iki sesle b: Did you notice: all four start with the same two sounds. That is the mark of the past form; it is added to the front of the verb and in that shape it goes to the end of the sentence.
lecture.Fiil hem kuralsız hem de yer değiştiren: The verb is both irregular and a verb of change of place, so the auxiliary changes too. When the two come together this is where most mistakes are made.
lecture.İyi akşamlar! Bugün bir restorandayız. Ç: Good evening! Today we are in a restaurant. We will learn to order very politely, to choose a starter and to pay the bill. Are you ready to start?
lecture.İyi bir anlatı üç şey ister: sıra (zuers: A good account wants three things: order (zuerst, dann, danach), links (nachdem, während, weil) and a close (am Ende, zum Schluss). The words first.
lecture.Karşılaştırma biçiminin önüne tek bir ke: A single word is put in front of the comparative and the meaning becomes 'more and more'. In English we say 'more and more' or 'increasingly'. The words first.
lecture.Kibarca hayır demek, evet demek kadar ön: Saying no politely matters as much as saying yes. German has a ready pattern for it and one word softens it. Let us learn the words first.
Hello! Today we will describe an image. This is the skill asked for most in a presentation and in an exam: saying what a thing is in one sentence. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir gösteride olacağız ve: Hello! Today we will be at a demonstration and we will ask one single question: why are you here. The pattern for the answer is damit, because the subject changes. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün uzak bir geleceği konuşac: Hello! Today we will talk about a distant future and nothing there is certain. That is exactly why the subjective modals are needed. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün zor bir soru: müzik bizi: Hello! Today a hard question: why does music move us. The answer has to be built as a 'how' and you know the conjunction for that. Ready?
lecture.Modülün son dersinde evdeki arızaları ko: In the module's last lesson we are talking about faults at home. Saying correctly what has broken means the repairer brings the right tool. Ready?
lecture.Neden edilgen? Çünkü kimin tamir ettiği: Why the passive? Because who repaired it does not matter; what matters is that the repair did not work. Rub out the doer and the fact comes forward. The words first.
lecture.Öznel kip fiilleri tam olarak bunu yapıy: The subjective modals do exactly this. A party's own claim and your own forecast are not said with the same sentence pattern. The words first.
lecture.Şimdi kural. Evet-hayır sorusunu gömerke: Now the rule. When you embed a yes-no question there is no question word, so a separate conjunction is put in between and the verb goes to the end of the sentence again.
lecture.Tek dikkat noktası yardımcı fiilin tekil: The only thing to watch is whether the auxiliary is singular or plural. It looks easy but in fast speech that is where people slip most. The words first.
lecture.Yasağı anlatır. Dikkat: izin fiilinin ol: It reports a ban. Careful: the negative of the verb of permission does not mean 'there was no need', it means 'it was forbidden'. It must not be mixed up with the negative of the verb of obligation.
lecture.'Bence etki küçük' yerine 'etkinin küçük: Instead of 'in my view the effect is small' you say 'the effect may be said to be small'. This is the scientific cousin of the institutional language you learnt at B2. The words first.
lecture.Artık spor yaptığını, nerede ve ne sıklı: You can say that you do sport now, where you do it and how often. You are at a gym and the person at the desk is looking after you.
lecture.Bir de Almancanın güzel bir kalıbı var:: And German has a fine pattern: general truths that open with 'whoever starts early'. It gives advice without giving advice. The words first.
lecture.Dolaylı soruda soru sözcüğü bağlaca döne: In an indirect question the question word turns into a conjunction and the verb goes right to the end; if there is no question word the conjunction that says you are unsure comes instead. The words first.
lecture.Gitmek hareket bildirir, o yüzden edat b: To go reports movement, so the preposition must bring the accusative; as written it means 'we are driving about at the seaside'. It should be:
lecture.İki kalıp yeter: neden yaptığın ve sana: Two patterns are enough: why you do it and what it gives you. The first is a purpose phrase, the second a sentence built with the dative. The words first.
lecture.İki parça: koşul cümlesinde geçmişin dil: Two parts: the past subjunctive in the conditional clause, and in the result clause either the past or the present. What gets confused is the tense of the result clause. The words first.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız beklentinin karşılanmad: Our second pattern says the expectation was not met. It does not accuse, it only recalls the expectation — this is the strongest sentence in formal writing.
lecture.İtiraz mektubu üç parçadır: neye itiraz: A letter of appeal has three parts: what you are objecting to, why you are objecting and what you are asking for. For the third you need a subclause. The words first.
lecture.İyi haber: bu deyimlerin çoğu Türkçede d: Good news: most of these idioms exist in English too, because the source is the same. 'Throw in the towel' and 'an own goal' match exactly. The words first.
lecture.İyi öğüdün iki kuralı var: dilek kipiyle: Good advice has two rules: it is given in the subjunctive (a suggestion, not an order) and it comes from your own experience (not from a general truth). The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün alıntı. Ve bir uyarı: alı: Hello! Today, quotation. And a warning: the most dangerous kind of quotation is not the wrong one but the right one torn out of its context. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir şeyin nasıl yapıldığı: Hello! Today we will describe how something is made. In accounts like this who did it is never said — what matters is the order. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün dağda bir yürüyüşü anlata: Hello! Today we will tell of a walk in the mountains. In German the conjunction for an event that happened ONCE in the past differs from the one for a repeated event. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün duyduğun tavsiyeleri akta: Hello! Today we will pass on the advice you have heard. Talk about travel is all hearsay and German marks that with the verb. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün evcil hayvanlardan konuşa: Hello! Today we will talk about pets: you will learn to say which animal you have, its name and how old it is. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün konu sınav ve onun yol ar: Hello! Today the subject is the exam and its travelling companion: nerves. You have to be able to talk about both, because worry that is not spoken of grows. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün küçük ama çok işe yarayan: Hello! Today a small but very useful document: a power of attorney. One line lets somebody act on your behalf. Ready?
Hello! Today we will open a hard subject. There is only one rule in such conversations: say it without accusing. The conjunction of reservation sees to that. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve konusu değ: Hello! The module's last lesson and its subject is change. When you talk about change no word is given for certain, everything is tied to a condition. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Tiyatrodan yeni çıktın ve fikri: Hello! You have just come out of the theatre and you will give your view. The language of an art review is tight: an adjective, a verdict, a reason. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yemek bitti ve kalkma vakti gel: Hello! The meal is over and it is time to get up. For an English speaker this is the really hard part: not the eating but leaving the table politely. Ready?
lecture.Retorikte üçleme her dilde işe yarar ama: The rule of three works in every language, but German also has the pause: the silence between the items is what carries the sentence. The words first.
lecture.Saat, bir dilde en çok kullanılan şeyler: The time is one of the things used most in a language. You need it making an appointment, asking about a train, arranging to meet. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Tutanakta hiç kimse 'dedi ki şöyleydi' d: In the minutes nobody says 'he said it was so'; everyone is relayed in the reported mood. And the order of a subclause is unforgiving here. The words first.
lecture.Türkçede kibarlığı tonla kurarız. Almanc: English builds politeness into the mood as well: 'I had thought …' is heard as a proposal even said flatly, and German works the same way. The words first.
lecture.Yani '… nerede bulurum?' Burada bugünün: That is, 'where do I find …?' Today's rule comes into play here: when what you are looking for is the object of the sentence the article of masculine words changes.
lecture.'-e rağmen' demek. Yan cümle: 'Obwohl ic: It means 'although'. As a subclause: 'Obwohl ich eine Erkältung habe, gehe ich arbeiten.' With the clause first the main clause starts with the verb: gehe ich.
lecture.Artık fiyat sorabilir, pahalı bulduğunu: You can ask the price now, say you find it dear and not miss a sale. You are in a shoe shop and a pair has caught your eye.
lecture.Artık saati sorabilir ve söyleyebilirsin: You can ask and tell the time now. Now you will use it: a stranger will ask you the time and then you will talk about train times.
lecture.Bu yüzden edatlı fiiller ezberlenirken e: That is why verbs with prepositions are learnt together with their preposition. In a relative clause that preposition moves right to the front and settles the case. The words first.
lecture.Dikkat: ilgi zamiri önceki ismin cinsine: Careful: the relative pronoun is chosen by the gender of the noun before it, but the VERB agrees with the number of the noun after it. You have to look in two places. The words first.
lecture.Gözlem 'sen şöylesin' değil 'şu dikkatim: The observation is built as 'this struck me', not 'you are like this'; the suggestion is in the subjunctive; and the question leaves the decision to the other person. The words first.
lecture.Hangi zamiri seçeceğini fiil söyler. Yön: The verb tells you which pronoun to choose. If it is a verb that wants the dative it is dem in the masculine and neuter, der in the feminine and denen in the plural. The words first.
lecture.Hayali söylemek kolay, adımlara bölmek z: Saying the dream is easy, breaking it into steps is hard. We will build both — because without the second the first stays just a sentence. The words first.
lecture.İçlerinden biri övgü, biri uyarı, biri d: One of them is praise, one a warning and one an accusation: 'you could steal horses with him' is one of the strongest expressions of trust in German. The words first.
lecture.İki kalıp yeter ve ikisi de aktarım kipi: Two patterns are enough and both come together with the reported mood. And there is a pair of verbs that gets confused a lot — we will test it at the end. The words first.
lecture.İki şey aynı anda gerekiyor: bir öneri v: Two things are needed at once: a proposal and an honest statement of its limits. Without the second an interim solution is taken for a permanent one. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Almanya'da uzmana genelde doğru: Hello! In Germany you do not usually go straight to a specialist: first your family doctor writes a slip. The language of that process is passive from beginning to end. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün edilgene bir kip ekliyoru: Hello! Today we are adding a modal to the passive. This is the commonest sentence in formal correspondence: 'is to be examined', 'may be submitted', 'cannot be changed'. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün tartışmanın en dürüst cev: Hello! Today we will learn the most honest answer in a debate: 'it depends'. The German pattern for it is built with a preposition. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün yılda bir kez herkesin ba: Hello! Today, the thing that happens to everybody once a year: the tax return. The language of it has two layers — what you did and what was done to you. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi: işinden memn: Hello! The module's last lesson: are you happy in your job? The verbs of this conversation carry a fixed preposition and the wrong one breaks the sentence. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Sağlık konusunu A1'de bir kez g: Hello! We went through health once at A1: where it hurts. Today we go one step further — describing a lasting complaint. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yeni modül: hukuk dili. Ve bura: Hello! A new module: legal language. And something changes here — misunderstanding a clause is not a grammar mistake, it is a loss of money. Ready?
lecture.Ortaç sıfatları burada çok işine yarar —: Participle adjectives are very useful here — 'the praised staging', 'the newly designed set'. One word carries both the information and the verdict. The words first.
lecture.Tarif iki parçadan kurulur: eşyanın adı,: A description is built in two parts: the name of the thing, then the relative clause that sets it apart. The more it sets apart, the better the chance of finding it. The words first.
lecture.Yani 'Ceket kırmızı'. Renk cümlenin sonu: That is, 'the jacket is red'. The colour stands at the end of the sentence and takes no ending at all. English says 'the jacket is red' too; here the two languages work the same way.
lecture.Artık birini davet edebilir, teklifi kab: You can invite somebody now, accept an offer and fix a time. You are ringing a friend: there is a good film on this evening.
lecture.Artık internetten sipariş verebilir, sep: You can order online now, manage the basket and ask about the delivery. But this time the parcel has not come: you are ringing customer service.
lecture.Artık sıra sana geldiğinde ne diyeceğini: You know what to say now when your turn comes. You are in front of the snack stand: give your order, ask the price and say whether you want it to take away.
lecture.Bazı ifadeler kültürel olarak yüklüdür:: Some expressions are culturally loaded: their words can be translated but their meaning does not travel. What you do then is unpack what was meant. The words first.
Today we will learn the rules of the building. Every block in Germany has written rules and understanding them makes your life much easier. Ready?
lecture.Bugün işleri zamana göre örgütlemeyi öğr: Today we will learn to organise jobs by time: before, during and after. There are two new conjunctions and both send the verb to the end. Ready?
lecture.Bugün işten ayrılmayı konuşacağız. Alman: Today we will talk about leaving a job. In Germany this is a completely regulated process and saying it in the right words makes it easier. Ready?
lecture.Burada başkasının söylediği aktarılıyor,: What somebody else said is being relayed here, so the hard form of the modal is right; the soft form would be advice, while this is an instruction being passed on.
lecture.İçerik değişmiyor, ÜSLUP DÜZEYİ değişiyo: The content does not change, the REGISTER does. And what decides the register is not the subject but the ADDRESSEE. This choice is exactly what C1 measures. The words first.
lecture.İki fiilimiz ikiye bölünen türden: cümle: Two of our verbs are of the splitting kind: once the sentence is built the front piece lifts off and goes to the very end. You know the rule; now we will use it on the housework.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız çoğul özneyle çalışıyor: Our second pattern works with a plural subject. With a plural subject the auxiliary goes plural too — English makes the same agreement, so this is one German rule you already have.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız çekince belirtiyor. Zor ol: Our first pattern enters a reservation. You accept that it is hard and yet you say it — with those two together the conversation does not turn into a row.
lecture.Küçük bir kolaylık: 'olmak' fiilinin geç: A small mercy: the past of the verb 'to be' does not split into two parts, it is said in one word. You will use it throughout your sentences of assessment.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir tablo okuyacağız. Rak: Hello! Today we will read a chart. Sentences that report figures are nearly always passive, because who produced the figure does not matter. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün çok kısa ama çok işlevsel: Hello! Today, a very short but very useful genre: the lift chat. Nobody opens a real subject, and yet the relationship is built exactly there. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kendine koyduğun kurallar: Hello! Today we will talk about the rules you set yourself. The 'as if' structure serves here to describe not somebody else but yourself. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün sosyal medyaya bakıyoruz: Hello! Today we are looking at social media, and this lesson follows on from the last one: participle adjectives. This time to tell advertising from opinion. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün uykuyu konuşacağız ve bu,: Hello! Today we will talk about sleep, and that means sequence: what you do before bed, what happens through the night. Two conjunctions are enough. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi: teknoloji bi: Hello! The module's last lesson: does technology set us free or make us dependent? On questions like this a one-sided answer looks weak. Ready?
Hello! A new module: science and technology. But first let us build the language of this field — and its most striking tool is making adjectives out of verbs. Ready?
lecture.Ölçü şu: bir deyim bağlamına oturduğunda: The measure is this: an idiom that sits in its context does not stand out. If it stands out, there is one too many. Today we will try it in an account of a day. The words first.
lecture.Selam! Bugün eczanedeyiz. Asıl işimiz ko: Hi! Today we are at the pharmacy. Our real job is not speaking but understanding: miss the pharmacist's instruction and you will take the medicine wrongly. Ready?
lecture.Sıra sende: 'Adresiniz nedir?' nasıl sor: Your turn: how do you ask 'What is your address?' A small hint: address is a feminine word, so the possessive before it gets a letter longer.
lecture.Tablo duvara doğru hareket ediyor, o yüz: The picture is moving towards the wall, so the preposition brings the accusative. Had the sentence been 'it is hanging on the wall' the dative would have come instead.
lecture.Üç adım: önce özneyi ve çekimli fiili bu: Three steps: first find the subject and the finite verb, then separate off the phrases wedged in between, and last rebuild it in your own sentence. Do not break the order. The words first.
lecture.Yani 'Severek dizi izlerim'. Buradaki kü: That is, 'I like watching series'. The little word here is the same as in the lesson on hobbies; whichever verb you attach it to it gives the sense of doing something gladly.
lecture.'Yapabilir misin' demek. Dikkat çekici b: It means 'can you'. Something is striking here: the main verb you use with this pattern is not conjugated, it stays as it is and goes to the very end of the sentence.
lecture.Artık uzak mı diye sorabilir ve bir yeri: You can ask whether it is far now and describe where a place is. You have a map of the city in your hand and you are at the hotel reception.
lecture.Bu kalıplar iş yerinde her gün kullanılı: These patterns are used every day at work. One of them has a small surprise: a letter in the middle of the verb changes. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bugün alışverişi ekrandan yapıyoruz. Sip: Today we are shopping from a screen. We will learn to order, to put an item in the basket and to talk about how long the delivery takes. Ready?
lecture.Bugün stresi konuşuyoruz. Dönüşlü fiille: Today we are talking about stress. Reflexive verbs come up once more in this lesson, but this time with a modal and a negative. Ready?
lecture.Doğrudan 'hayır, bu yanlış' demek çoğu o: Saying 'no, that is wrong' outright is rude in most settings. Put in the subjunctive the same objection keeps the debate going and does not spoil the relationship. The words first.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız değişimi söylüyor: bir: Our second pattern states the change: a time adverb and the word meaning the other way round. Because the sentence starts with an adverb the verb moves into second place.
lecture.İkincisi ilkinden daha güçlü: en kötü ih: The second is stronger than the first: accepting the worst possibility and carrying on even so. German has a one-word conjunction for it. The words first.
lecture.Kalıbın tamamı ezberlenir: bir edat, yön: The whole pattern is learnt by heart: a preposition, a noun in the dative and a second preposition after it. It does the same job as English 'near the station'.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir araştırmayı özetleyec: Hello! Today we will summarise a piece of research. The business of academic language is shortening, and the method of shortening is always the same: turning the verb into a noun. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir büfenin önünde sırada: Hello! Today we are in the queue at a snack stand. We will learn to order briefly, to ask the price and to ask for the food to take away. Are you ready to start?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bütün araçları bir araya: Hello! Today we bring all the tools together: inverted emphasis, the rule of three, metaphor, the pause, concession. All of it in a single speech. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kendi geliş hikâyeni anla: Hello! Today you will tell the story of your own arrival. The conjunction of this story is settled: the one used for an event that happened once in the past. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün sevdiğin yemekleri konuşa: Hello! Today we will talk about the food you like: we will learn to say what you enjoy eating and what you prefer. Are you ready to start?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün sınır çizeceğiz. Sınır çi: Hello! Today we will draw a boundary. In German drawing a boundary is built with a purpose clause: 'I turn the phone off so that I can clear my head'. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün uzmanların kendi araların: Hello! Today, the language experts speak among themselves: compressed. A relative clause folds in front of the noun into a single phrase. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve en zoru: i: Hello! The module's last lesson and the hardest: standing between two sides. A mediator's language is special — it relays what was said without endorsing it. Ready?
lecture.Yani 'Kız kardeşime bir hediye arıyorum': That is, 'I am looking for a present for my sister'. Now mind the rule: after the word meaning 'for', masculine words change form. On its own
lecture.Yazın en serin yer havuz. Bugün giriş üc: The coolest place in summer is the pool. Today we will learn to ask the entrance fee, to find the changing rooms and to say what you may and may not do in the water. Ready?
lecture.Akşam oldu ve kumanda elinde. Bugün ne i: Evening has come and the remote is in your hand. Today we will learn to say what you are watching, to ask about the channel and to say when the programme starts. Ready?
