lecture.Amaç iki biçimde söylenir: özne farklıys: Purpose is said in two forms: with a subclause if the subject differs, with an infinitive phrase if it is the same. English makes this distinction too, so the split will be familiar. The words first.
lecture.Bir de dikkat edeceğin nokta var: bu yap: And there is a point to watch: this structure uses not the reported mood but the SUBJUNCTIVE. Mix the two and the sentence turns into a claim. The words first.
lecture.Bir de yer bildirirken dikkat edeceğin b: And there is a point to watch when you give a place: the case changes when you say where a thing IS. We will test that at the end. The words first.
lecture.Bu sohbetin dili bilerek bağlayıcı değil: The language of this chat is deliberately non-binding. It says 'we must do this sometime' and gives no date. The subjunctive carries that vagueness politely. The words first.
lecture.Bugün bankadayız ve hesap açıyoruz. Alma: Today we are at the bank opening an account. Every step of life in Germany hangs on a bank account, so this lesson will be very useful. Ready?
lecture.Bugün yeni bir işe başlama sürecini konu: Today we are talking about starting a new job: the application, the interview, the contract. And we will learn to state an intention firmly. Ready?
lecture.Bugünkü iki fiil edatını sabit taşıyor:: Both of today's verbs carry a fixed preposition: which one comes with them is learnt by heart, there is no logic. The wrong preposition makes the sentence unintelligible. The words first.
lecture.Burada bir kural değişiyor: verilen şey: A rule changes here: when the thing given is a pronoun it moves forward and the person falls behind. With two pronouns the accusative one always comes first.
lecture.Daha önce olan iş bir basamak geriye çek: What happened earlier is pulled back one step; we call this the past of the past. The same thing the English past perfect does. The words first.
lecture.Edilgenin geçmişinde yardımcı fiil geçmi: In the past passive the auxiliary is in its past form in second place and the participle at the very end. Used without a subject the auxiliary stays singular. The words first.
lecture.İkili bağlaçları biliyorsun; bugün onlar: You know the paired conjunctions; today we will work them on a social subject. And we will learn to describe a change of preference. The words first.
lecture.Kendi seviyeni değerlendirirken ne fazla: Assessing your own level wants neither too much bravado nor too much hesitation — the subjective modals give exactly that measure. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba ve B2'ye hoş geldin! Bu seviyede: Hello and welcome to B2! At this level you will speak not the language of your own life but that of an institution. The first lesson: opening a presentation. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Almanya'da çok yaygın bir şey v: Hello! There is something very common in Germany: unpaid, voluntary work. Today we will learn to talk about it — and the real question is why. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün Almancanın en yoğun aracı: Hello! Today, German's densest tool: making an adjective out of a verb. It squeezes what a relative clause carries into a single adjective. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün hassas bir konu var. Böyl: Hello! Today there is a delicate subject. On subjects like this the only tool is the conjunction of reservation: accepting the difference and still saying something shared. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kendi öğrenme yöntemini a: Hello! Today we will learn to describe your own way of studying. You will have to say two things at once, so you need the paired conjunctions. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün vücudumuzu Almanca adland: Hello! Today we will name our body in German. At the doctor's, at the pharmacy, at the gym you will get nowhere without these words. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Resmî bir metin okuyacağız. Kur: Hello! We are going to read a formal text. Texts of rules address nobody; they are written in the passive and that makes them cold but clear. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Sigortaya hasar bildirmek bir a: Hello! Reporting damage to an insurer is a matter of narrative: first what happened, then what you did. German shows that order with the form of the verb. Ready?
lecture.Sıralama kelimeleri cümlenin başına geli: The words of sequence come at the front of the sentence and the auxiliary right after them. So the rule of order and the past tense are both working in the same sentence.
lecture.Şehir içinde yürümek her zaman yetmez. B: Walking is not always enough inside a city. Today we will learn to say which way you travel, to ask about the stop and to find the right line. Ready?
lecture.Türkçede 'sen' ve 'siz' var, Almancada d: English has only one 'you'; German has a familiar form and a polite one, and the verb ending changes with it. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Üç öbek işini görür: hak iddia etmek, sü: Three phrases do the job: making a claim, setting a deadline and asserting a right. All three are fixed and all three follow the logic you learnt in the first module. The words first.
lecture.Bir de ince bir ayrım var: zaman belirti: And there is a fine distinction: if a time is given a process is being described and the shortened form is needed. We will test this at the end of the lesson. The words first.
lecture.Bisiklet yolları burada ayrı bir şeritti: Cycle paths here are a lane of their own and standing on one on foot is not taken kindly. Keep that in mind while you learn the words, it will be useful.
lecture.Bugün bir iş görüşmesindesin! Sebep bild: Today you are in a job interview! We will learn 'weil' clauses that give a reason and the 'seit' pattern meaning 'since'. Are you ready to start?
lecture.Bugün paylaşımlı ev görüşmesini öğrenece: Today we will learn the house-share interview. In Germany the flatmates meet the candidate and choose; this interview has a language of its own. Ready?
lecture.Bugün yardım istemeyi öğreniyoruz. Alman: Today we are learning to ask for help. In German the verb of helping wants an unexpected case and everybody who does not know it makes the same mistake. Ready?
lecture.Her kelime olumlu, anlam tam tersi. Alma: Every word is positive and the meaning is the exact opposite. German irony is usually quiet and dry; said with heavy emphasis it stops being a joke and becomes rudeness. The words first.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız ileriye bakıyor: dönüşl: Our second pattern looks ahead: a reflexive verb and another fixed preposition. This preposition is not used for something PAST — there another one is needed.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız isteği ve gerekçeyi birleş: Our first pattern joins the request to the reason: the request in the main clause, the reason in the subclause. The separable verb's prefix stays at the end of the main clause.
lecture.Kural şu: deyim kelimeden değil RESİMDEN: The rule is this: an idiom is made not of words but of a PICTURE, and pictures change from language to language. The right method is to LOOK FOR the equivalent, not to translate. The words first.
lecture.Kural: werden ile kurulan edilgen SÜREÇT: The rule: the passive built with werden is a PROCESS — something is happening. The passive built with sein is a STATE — something has happened and stands so. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bir karar sana haksız geldiyse: Hello! If a decision has struck you as unfair, what to do in Germany is settled: a written appeal. Today we will build the three sentences of that letter. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün ağrıyı tarif edeceğiz. Do: Hello! Today we will describe pain. When the doctor asks 'where', knowing the name of the organ is not enough, you have to know the right preposition too. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kaygıyı konuşacağız. Kayg: Hello! Today we will talk about worry. The language of worry is a question: 'what if it does not happen'. But there is an answer too: 'even if it does'. We will build both. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yeni modül: kültür ve sanat. Bi: Hello! A new module: culture and the arts. When German talks about a book it usually builds a relative clause, and that clause starts with a preposition. Ready?
lecture.Öznel kip fiilleri burada tam da bu işi: The subjective modals do exactly this job here: 'others say so' and 'I reckon so' are said with different verbs. The words first.
lecture.Selam! Bugünkü ders umarım hiç işine yar: Hi! I hope today's lesson is never of any use to you, but when it is needed seconds count. We will learn the sentences to say in an emergency. Ready?
lecture.Şikâyet iki parçadan kurulur: yumuşak bi: A complaint is built in two parts: a soft opening and a sentence of reason. After the causal conjunction the verb goes right to the end. First, the names of the places to eat.
lecture.Şimdi o şaşırtan kısım. Türkçede önce bü: Now the part that surprises. In English you say the bigger part first: twenty-one. German is the other way round, the units first and then the tens, and all of it as one word:
lecture.Tablo duvara doğru hareket ediyor, o yüz: The picture is moving towards the wall, so the preposition must bring the accusative; as written it means 'I am hanging it while it hangs on the wall'. It should be:
lecture.Almanca iki, hatta üç parçacığı üst üste: German can stack two, even three particles, but the order is fixed. 'ja wohl' is possible, the other way round is not. Today we will build the three commonest. The words first.
lecture.Aynı emir, üç ayrı sertlikte söylenebili: The same order can be said at three different strengths. The wrong particle makes you sound either too harsh or too soft; at C1 the dose is measured too. The words first.
lecture.Birincisi ya şaşkınlık ya da 'bunu ikimi: The first carries either surprise or the sense of 'we both know this'. The second takes the order out of a request: not 'look' but 'just have a look'. The words first.
lecture.Bu A1'in son dersi. Bugün yeni bir kural: This is A1's last lesson. There is no new rule today; we will learn to tell what you have learnt. You will use the past tense for your own story. Ready?
lecture.Bugün ev arıyoruz! Almanya'da ev sahibiy: Today we are looking for a flat! The key to talking to a landlord in Germany is politeness: we will learn the 'I would like' and 'could you' patterns. Ready?
lecture.Bugün kendini nasıl hissettiğini anlatıy: Today we are describing how you feel. German has two separate ways of doing it and which one you use depends on the symptom. Ready?
lecture.Bugün kuaförde ne istediğini anlatmayı ö: Today we are learning to say what you want at the hairdresser's. The comparative will be very useful here: shorter, darker, less. Ready?
lecture.Bunun üç girişi var ve üçü de aynı işi g: There are three openings for this and all three do the same job. The sentence that follows is usually in the subjunctive, because the situation is not real. The words first.
Here the person is not the subject but in the dative. The sentence looks as if it has no subject, and indeed the one with the symptom does not stand at its centre.
lecture.Dilek kipiyle sunulan öneri hem kibardır: A suggestion offered in the subjunctive is both polite and retractable — it makes it easier for the other person to say no, and that is a deliberate courtesy. The words first.
lecture.En işlevlisi 'gerçi ama' ikilisi: 'gerçi: The most useful is the 'admittedly, but' pair: 'admittedly it is not ideal, but it is bearable for both sides'. One sentence holds both the understanding and the limit. The words first.
lecture.Günlük dilde bu edatlardan sonra yönelme: In everyday speech you will hear the dative after these prepositions and it is not counted wrong; but in writing and in formal speech the genitive is expected. The words first.
lecture.İyi haber: dört biçimden yalnızca biri d: Good news: only one of the four forms changes. In the masculine object den is said instead of der; in the feminine, the neuter and the plural nothing changes. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kendi işini kurmayı konuş: Hello! Today we will talk about setting up your own business. No sentence on this subject is built as certain — everything hangs on a condition, and so does the language. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kişisel bir ders: iki dil: Hello! Today a personal lesson: living in two languages. And to describe it we need the unreal comparison, because a feeling is not told with a fact. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün zamanın iki bağlacı daha:: Hello! Today two more conjunctions of time: bevor (before) and während (while). We are at the cinema: before the film starts, while the film is on. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Sondan bir önceki ders ve konus: Hello! The next to last lesson and its subject is a big one: the dream of your life. The pattern for telling it is an infinitive phrase built with a verb that has a fixed preposition. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yeni modül: deyimler. Ve baştan: Hello! A new module: idioms. And a warning at the outset — the real danger in this module is not failing to know an idiom but using one you know WRONGLY. Ready?
lecture.Sınav yönergeleri kişisiz yazılır — 'siz: Exam instructions are written impersonally — not 'you are asked' but 'the candidate is asked'. Simply knowing this language earns you marks. The words first.
lecture.Son ders. Bugün A2 boyunca öğrendiğin yo: The last lesson. Today you will tell in your own words the road you came through A2. For that we will learn a few small but important words. Ready?
lecture.Takside konuşma iki cümleden ibarettir:: A conversation in a taxi is two sentences: where to and how long it takes. And there is a three-word phrase said as you get out. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Tek bir şey değişiyor: yardımcı fiil geç: Only one thing changes: the auxiliary is pulled into the past. The participle stays where it is. And there is a small trap, which I will show you at the end. The words first.
lecture.Telefonun bitti ve nerede olduğunu bilmi: Your phone has died and you do not know where you are. Today we will learn to say you are lost and to follow a long set of directions step by step. Ready?
lecture.Yan cümlede Plusquamperfekt (hatte/war +: The subclause in the Plusquamperfekt (hatte/war + Partizip), the main clause in the Präteritum or the Perfekt. With verbs of movement war: 'Nachdem ich angekommen war…'
lecture.Artık bir daveti kırmadan geri çevirebil: You can turn an invitation down without hurting anyone now and offer a new day instead. Your phone is ringing: a friend is inviting you out this evening.
lecture.Artık bir mağazada ne aradığını söyleyeb: You can say what you are looking for in a shop now, make your decision and find the till. Now you are in a real shop: the assistant is coming towards you.
lecture.Bugün Almancanın en şaşırtıcı kuralların: Today we will learn one of the most surprising rules in German: some verbs split in two and one piece goes to the end of the sentence. Ready?
lecture.Bugün iki şeyi karşılaştırmayı öğreniyor: Today we are learning to compare two things. English adds -er to short adjectives just as German does, and German uses that ending for every adjective, however long. Ready?
lecture.Bunu isimleşme ve edilgen birlikte yapıy: Nominalisation and the passive do this together: not 'we took measures' but 'measures were initiated'. Rub out who did it and the event becomes institutional. The words first.
lecture.Kelime kelime 'bana sırt ağrıyor'. Ağrıy: Word for word 'to me the back hurts'. The part that hurts stands with its article and the person who hurts goes into the 'to me' form. Germans use this form most of all.
lecture.Kural basit: kendi yaptığın şeyi etken s: The rule is simple: what you did yourself you say in the active, what the office did in the passive. Not mixing the two is very useful in formal language. The words first.
lecture.Küçük ama kritik bir ayrıntı var: edilge: There is a small but critical detail: in the past passive the auxiliary shortens. This is the presentation-language counterpart of the rule you learnt at B1. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bir şey bozuldu ve tamire mi ve: Hello! Something has broken and you will decide whether to have it repaired or buy a new one. Today we have patterns of intention and advice. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün 'ne kadar çok çalışırsam: Hello! Today we will learn to say 'the more I work the better I get': je … desto. Two comparisons, two clauses, one rule. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün üç kip fiiliyle üç ayrı e: Hello! Today we will build three degrees of certainty with three modals. English grades certainty too, but its modals do not line up one for one with the German ones. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Dün günlük sebep edatlarını kur: Hello! Yesterday we built the everyday prepositions of cause; today their formal siblings. You will see them in announcements, in decisions and in the news. Ready?
lecture.Şimdi kural. Doğrudan soruda fiil başta: Now the rule. In a direct question the verb stands first. When you embed the question inside a sentence the verb goes right to the end and the question word takes on the job of a conjunction.
lecture.Yardım teklifini düz kipte yapmak baskı: An offer of help made in the plain mood can feel like pressure; the subjunctive lightens the offer and the other person can easily say no. The words first.
lecture.Ana cümlede kip fiili ikinci sırada ve a: In the main clause the modal is in second place and the main verb last; in the subclause there is a separate verb and that too is at the very end. Two rules working side by side in one sentence.
lecture.Artık bir sofrada kendini idare edebilir: You can hold your own at a table now. You are at a friend's house: the table is laid and the host cannot wait to fill your plate.
lecture.Bu modülün son dersi. Bugün tanımadığın: This is the module's last lesson. Today we will learn to start a work conversation with somebody you do not know. What helps most is asking your question by asking permission. Ready?
Today we will learn to talk about the housework. Two verbs split in two again — you have seen this before, and now we will practise it on the housework. Ready?
lecture.Bugün nüfus dairesindeyiz. Almanya'da ta: Today we are at the registration office. In Germany you must register your address within two weeks of moving and this lesson is about that job. Ready?
lecture.Bugün sabahını sırayla anlatmayı öğrenec: Today we will learn to tell your morning in order. The words of sequence come at the front of the sentence too, which means we will use yesterday's rule again. Ready?
lecture.Dikkat: bu bir yan cümle bağlacı, yani f: Careful: this is a subclause conjunction, which means the verb goes last. An English speaker slips a lot here, because 'by doing …' has no such order. The words first.
lecture.Dolaylı soruda iki şey olur: soru kelime: In an indirect question two things happen: a question word or a conjunction comes first, and the finite verb goes right to the end. So the plain question order breaks down. The words first.
lecture.İkinci kalıbımız dişil bir adı tanımlıyo: Our second pattern describes a feminine noun. In the dative the feminine relative pronoun takes a different form — this is where an English speaker slips most often.
lecture.Koşul yan cümlesi başta duruyorsa ana cü: If the conditional clause stands first the main clause starts with the verb. We have seen this rule many times; today we fix it in a health setting. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Aşı randevusunda duyacağın cüml: Hello! Most of the sentences you will hear at a vaccination appointment are passive and two of them are almost always the same. Today we will build them. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir gazete yazısına karşı: Hello! Today we will write a reply to a newspaper piece. The rule of this genre is this: first you grant the point, then you object. Otherwise you will not be read. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir yanlış anlamayı düzel: Hello! Today we will put a misunderstanding right. The order for that is settled: first accept how it was heard, then say what you meant. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün ekonomi konuşacağız. Bu k: Hello! Today we will talk about the economy. On this subject it is easy to speak one-sidedly and hard to speak in a balanced way — the paired conjunctions are there for just that. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün mahallenin nasıl değiştiğ: Hello! Today we will describe how the area has changed. Who made the change is often not known, so the language is passive again. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün sağlıklı kalmayı konuşaca: Hello! Today we will talk about staying healthy. Two structures will be useful when you give advice: what helps and how it is done. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugünkü konu birçok insanın hay: Hello! Today's subject is many people's lives: belonging to two places at once. To describe it we have to go back to a single moment in the past. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi: seçim. Bu ko: Hello! The module's last lesson: the election. The most important thing when you talk about this is telling apart what is a promise, what is a poll and what is your own forecast. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Son modüle geldik. İlk ders res: Hello! We have reached the last module. The first lesson is the formal letter and no creativity is wanted here — the phrases are fixed and are used exactly so. Ready?
lecture.Sebebi şu: tutanağı yazan kişi söylenene: The reason is this: the person taking the minutes neither agrees with what was said nor objects to it. They only relay it. The change in the verb builds that distance. The words first.
lecture.Türkçede 'bir porsiyon sosis, lütfen' de: In English you say 'one portion of sausage, please'; this pattern is exactly that. We do not even use a verb: the number of portions at the front, the name of the food in the middle.
lecture.'Kırk euro veriyoruz' bir karardır; 'kır: 'We are giving forty euros' is a decision; 'we could consider forty euros' is an offer. The same figure, but the second keeps the conversation going. The words first.
lecture.Almanya'da bu ürünler eczanede değil, ay: In Germany these products are sold not at the pharmacy but in a shop of their own. Nobody comes up to you inside; if you cannot find something you have to ask. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Amacım bunu sevdirmek değil, ÇÖZDÜRMEK:: My aim is not to make you like it but to make you CRACK it: 'Das nehmen wir mit' is not a promise, it is a postponement. At C1 you have to hear this and to build it. The words first.
lecture.Bir günü anlatmak, öğrendiğin her şeyi b: Telling a day is the best exercise there is for bringing everything you have learnt together: the words of sequence, the times and the past tense. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Dönmek anlamındaki fiil ikiye bölünüyor:: The verb meaning to turn splits in two: one piece stands at the front of the sentence and the other at the very end. The meaning is not complete until you have listened to the end.
lecture.Gara geldin, şimdi bilet lazım. Bugün gi: You have got to the station and now you need a ticket. Today we will practise buying a ticket at the counter, saying whether it is single or return, and finding out the platform. Ready?
lecture.İki tanesi ayrılabilen fiil gibi çekiliy: Two of them are conjugated like separable verbs and one is a fixed phrase. Mixing up their meanings can be genuinely embarrassing here. The words first.
lecture.İkili bağlaç iki parçadan oluşur ve ikis: A paired conjunction is made of two parts and both are said; forgetting one leaves the sentence half finished. And that is exactly where they get mixed up most. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bir eve yemeğe davetlisin. Alma: Hello! You are invited to somebody's home for a meal. This invitation has two questions in Germany: what shall I bring and how was the food. We will learn both today. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün iş hayatının en çok sorul: Hello! Today we will answer the question asked most in working life: why are you doing this? We will refresh the short way of giving a purpose. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün lehçeler. Ama hedef net:: Hello! Today, dialects. But the aim is clear: not speaking but UNDERSTANDING. You do not have to learn a dialect; it is enough not to be lost when you hear one. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Dün öbeklerin mantığını kurduk;: Hello! Yesterday we built the logic of the phrases; today we will learn by heart the five that will help you most. These are all but obligatory in formal correspondence. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! İnternet gitti ve sağlayıcıyı a: Hello! The internet is down and you are going to ring the provider. In technical conversations a direct question sounds harsh; an indirect one is both polite and clearer. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Son modüldeyiz ve burada yeni k: Hello! We are in the last module and there is no new rule here — what you have learnt will work side by side inside real jobs. The first scene: a crisis meeting. Ready?
lecture.Modülün son dersinde yıllık değerlendirm: In the module's last lesson we are at the annual appraisal. Here you have to understand the feedback and also say what you want yourself. Ready?
lecture.Almancada karşılaştırma sıfata bir ek ge: In German a comparison adds an ending to the adjective; with some short adjectives the vowel changes too. The superlative is a pattern of its own. First, the words of the market.
lecture.Ama dikkat: kötü seçilmiş bir metafor ya: But mind this: a badly chosen metaphor does not help, it harms. German has ready and safe images; today we will build them. The words first.
lecture.Anahtar cümle koşullu olandır: 'siz de k: The key sentence is the conditional one: 'if you agree as well'. It leaves the other side room to object and keeps the conversation clear of a formal complaint. The words first.
lecture.Artık kime hediye aradığını söyleyebilir: You can say who you are looking for a present for now, make suggestions and ask for it to be wrapped. You are in a gift shop and the assistant is full of ideas.
lecture.Bugün hayaldeki mesleği konuşuyoruz. Mes: Today we are talking about your dream job. You saw in module 2 that no article is used when you name a profession; here we will add the reason as well. Ready?
lecture.Edilgende yardımcı fiil ikinci sırada, o: In the passive the auxiliary is in second place and the participle last. If the doer has to be named a separate preposition is used and that preposition wants the dative. The words first.
lecture.Gişedeki konuşma çok kısadır: iki kelime: The conversation at the counter is very short: a ticket is bought with two words. You do not have to build a long sentence, but I will show you both. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.İki kalıp yeter. Biri nihai teklifi dile: Two patterns are enough. One softens the final offer with the subjunctive, the other proposes a conditional close — both leave the other side a way out. The words first.
lecture.Kural yine aynı: zamir tanımlanan kelime: The rule is the same as ever: the pronoun looks at the gender and number of the word described. 'jemand' and 'niemand' are masculine, so der; with plural nouns die. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Ailede biri bakıma muhtaç ve bu: Hello! Somebody in the family needs care and you are going to discuss who takes it on. Every decision has a purpose and that purpose has to be said. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün elimizde üç teklif var ve: Hello! Today we have three offers and we will choose one. A sentence of decision is not built without grounds — the conjunction of proportion carries the grounds here. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün markette dolaşıyoruz. Ney: Hello! Today we are walking round the supermarket. We will learn to say what you need and to ask where the thing you are looking for is. Are you ready to start?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün resmî Almancanın sesini ö: Hello! Today we will learn the voice of formal German. On signs, in offices and in letters the same structure appears, and we call it the passive. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugünkü konu kişisel olabilir:: Hello! Today's subject may be a personal one: belonging. And language helps here, because belonging is usually not 'either this or that' but 'both this and that'. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi. Bugün tavsiy: Hello! The module's last lesson. Today we will exchange advice — giving it and asking for it. Both use the same form of the verb: the subjunctive. Ready?
lecture.Modülün son dersinde telefonsuz bir günü: In the module's last lesson we are telling of a day without a phone. Everything you learnt at the start of the module comes together here in an account of an experience. Ready?
lecture.Spor konuşması Almanya'da hiç bitmez: ki: Talk about sport never ends in Germany: who does what, how many times a week. Today we will learn to say that you do sport and to describe how often. Ready?
lecture.Yönelme isteyen fiillerde ilgi zamiri de: With verbs that want the dative the relative pronoun goes into the dative too and takes the same form for a masculine and a neuter noun. In the feminine another form comes. The words first.
lecture.Ama bir ayrım var: bazı değişimler kendi: But there is a distinction: some changes happen by themselves and those are said not with the passive but with the ordinary past. We will learn to tell the two apart. The words first.
lecture.Birini bir yere davet etmek Almancada te: Inviting somebody somewhere is a one-sentence job in German. Today we will learn to invite, to accept an offer and to fix a time. Ready?
lecture.Böyle konularda kesin cümle kurmak riskl: On subjects like this building a firm sentence is risky; German has a structure that can say 'it is probably clear that' and that is what keeps a debate going. The words first.
lecture.Bu zamanı B1'de öğrenmiştin. Buradaki iş: You learnt this tense at B1. The job here is using it to open a talk — 'after working together, leaving feels hard'. The words first.
lecture.Bugün birini davet etmeyi öğreneceğiz. İ: Today we will learn to invite somebody. There are two more verbs that split in two; you know the rule, and now we will practise it in sentences of invitation. Ready?
lecture.Bugün hafta sonu planını anlatmayı öğren: Today we will learn to describe your weekend plan. And there is a word that will be very useful: the one you use when your plan is not settled. Ready?
lecture.Bugün iki küçük kelimeyi ayırt etmeyi öğ: Today we are learning to tell two little words apart. Both give a time, but one describes something still going on and the other a point that is finished. Ready?
lecture.Bugün kısa mesaj yazmayı öğreneceğiz. Al: Today we will learn to write a short message. In German the closing of a message matters almost as much as the message; there are set phrases and all of them are used. Ready?
lecture.Bugün koşul cümlesini öğreniyoruz. Bu ba: Today we are learning the conditional clause. This conjunction can mean both 'if' and 'every time', and it says both with the same structure. Ready?
The subjunctive softens the requests here. But mind this: soft does not mean vague, you still have to say clearly what you want. The words first.
lecture.Dolaylı soruda soru sözcüğü bağlaca dönü: In an indirect question the question word turns into a conjunction and the verb goes right to the end. If there is no question word a conjunction saying you are unsure is used. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün alışkanlıkları konuşacağı: Hello! Today we will talk about habits. The sentences of this subject always answer the question 'how', so the conjunction of method is at the centre again. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün en çok işine yarayacak ye: Hello! Today we are in the place that will help you most: the immigration office. Almost every sentence you hear there is passive and comes out of the same three patterns. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün gökyüzüne bakıyoruz. Bu k: Hello! Today we are looking at the sky. The language of this subject is full of participle adjectives: the planned mission, the manned journey, the newly discovered planet. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün şehirlerin en tartışmalı: Hello! Today the most argued-over subject in the cities: car or bicycle. To be strong in a debate you have to be able to give both sides. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Dün edilgen cümleyi şimdiki zam: Hello! Yesterday we built the passive sentence in the present. Today we will carry it into the past — because formal letters always tell of things already done. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve en yumuşağ: Hello! The module's last lesson and the gentlest: the shelter. Every animal here has a story and telling a story takes a relative clause. Ready?
lecture.Türkçede 'var' demek için tek kelime yet: English needs a subject and a verb for this as well — 'there is' — and German's pair works the same way: the two always go together and the pattern never changes.
lecture.Artık gecikmeyi anlatabilir, ne zaman ge: You can report a delay now, ask when it is coming and say that you are waiting. You are on the platform and the passenger beside you is waiting for the same train.
lecture.Bu yüzden edilgen çatı kullanıyoruz: yar: That is why we use the passive: the auxiliary in second place and the participle at the very end. With separable verbs the participle is built together with the prefix. The words first.
lecture.Bugün bir akşamı sırayla anlatmayı öğren: Today we are learning to tell an evening in order. Telling the events is not enough; you have to say which came first and which came after. Ready?
lecture.Bugün bir şeyi ilk kez yaptığın anı anla: Today we are telling of the moment you did something for the first time: the first concert, the first exam, the first time at the wheel. We will learn to say the feeling along with the event. Ready?
lecture.Bugün dünü baştan sona anlatmayı öğrenec: Today we will learn to tell yesterday from beginning to end. We will use the two auxiliaries together — you know by now which one comes when. Ready?
lecture.Dilbilgisi doğru ama anlam kendi kendisi: The grammar is right but the meaning contradicts itself: the first half says forbidden, the second says obligatory. The negative of the verb of permission means 'it was forbidden'.
lecture.Hoş geldin! Bugün bir aile buluşması pla: Welcome! Today we will plan a family gathering: who is coming, who is bringing what. Everything you learnt in this module comes together today. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün mizahın sınırı. Aynı şaka: Hello! Today, the limit of humour. The same joke makes people laugh in one setting and spoils a relationship in another — and the difference is usually at whose expense it is made. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün öğreneceğin şey dilbilgis: Hello! What you will learn today is less a piece of grammar than a way of behaving: leaving the door open while you object. German has ready patterns for it. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün paranın nereye gittiğini: Hello! Today we will talk about where the money goes. The language of public finance is passive: something is funded, and who funds it is not said. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün rehber sensin. Müze anlat: Hello! Today you are the guide. The language of a museum talk is the past passive: when the work was made, and by whom is usually a secondary matter. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Geçen ders 'gülen adam' vardı:: Hello! Last lesson we had 'the man who is laughing': the person described was the SUBJECT of the clause. Today the reverse: 'the film I love' — the film does not love, it is loved. Ready?
lecture.Yeni zaman: Plusquamperfekt — hatte/war: A new tense: the Plusquamperfekt — hatte/war + Partizip II. 'Nachdem ich gegessen HATTE, ging ich raus.' The English 'after I had …' is what this is. The words first.
lecture.Artık beğendiğini, beğenmediğini ve hang: You can say what you liked, what you did not and which you prefer. You are out shopping with a friend and they want to know what you think.
lecture.Bugün amaç bildirmeyi öğreneceğiz: bir ş: Today we will learn to give a purpose: saying why you do something. English splits the sentence for this too — 'so that …' — and German does the same. Ready?
lecture.Bugün form dilini öğreniyoruz. Formlarda: Today we are learning the language of forms. Instructions on forms are always written in the formal imperative, and knowing that mood is half of filling the form in correctly. Ready?
lecture.Bugün gider hesabına itiraz etmeyi öğren: Today we will learn to challenge the service charge statement. In Germany this statement comes once a year and it is very common for it to be wrong; you have the right to object. Ready?
lecture.Bugün izin ve yasak konuşuyoruz. İzin fi: Today we are talking about permission and prohibition. You met the verb of permission at A1; here we will work on it with its negative and set apart from the other modals. Ready?
lecture.Bugün kirayı konuşmayı öğreneceğiz. Alma: Today we will learn to talk about the rent. There is a distinction in German rental adverts that sounds very odd: warm rent and cold rent. We will look at that too. Ready?
lecture.Geçen ders sebep bildiren bir bağlaç öğr: Last lesson you learnt a conjunction that gives a reason and it sent the verb to the end. Today's conjunction says the same thing but does not touch the word order at all. Ready?
lecture.Hoş geldin! Bugün birini tarif etmeyi öğ: Welcome! Today we will learn to describe somebody: their height, their hair, their glasses. These sentences save your life when you have to find somebody in a crowd. Ready?
lecture.İlk kalıbımız karşılaştırma: sıfat artı: Our first pattern is the comparison: the adjective plus an ending, then the word of comparison. It does the same job as English 'cheaper than', and the order is the same: the adjective first, then what it is compared with.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız yumuşak açılış: özür sözcü: Our first pattern is the soft opening: the word of apology plus the verb to think. Instead of saying 'you brought the wrong one' you say 'I think'; not an accusation but a possibility.
lecture.Kural şu: Almanca cümlede çekimli fiil h: The rule is this: in a German sentence the finite verb is always the second element. English keeps the subject in front of the verb even when something else opens the sentence, so this is the rule that gets missed most. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Kural şu: itiraz doğrudan söylenmez, bir: The rule is this: the objection is not said outright, it is put inside a shell. The subjunctive is that shell — the content of the sentence stays the same and its bindingness drops. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün iklim tartışması. Ama ası: Hello! Today, the climate debate. But the real subject is a trick of language: shifting the responsibility onto the individual and how that is done with nominalised language. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün tutanak yazacağız ve orad: Hello! Today we will write minutes, and there is a strange verb form in them: the verb changes when you relay what was said. We call this the reported mood. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Mülakatın sonundasın ve sana 's: Hello! You are at the end of the interview and you have been asked 'have you any questions'. This moment is an exam moment and the right SENTENCE counts as much as the right questions. Ready?
lecture.Sebebi yer değil, ton: fiil olmayınca cü: The reason is not the space but the tone: with no verb the sentence stands like a fact, not like something somebody did. That is why reading headlines takes care. The words first.
lecture.soll: başkaları öyle diyor. will: kişini: soll: others say so. will: the person's own claim. dürfte: the speaker's guess. English needs three separate expressions for these; German does it with three modals. The words first.
lecture.Yapı basit ama sırası kritik: çekimli ki: The structure is simple but the order is critical: the finite modal in second place, and at the end the participle first and then werden. The order of those two words gets confused a lot. The words first.
lecture.Yapı: 'Je' + Komparativ + yan cümle (fii: The structure: 'Je' + Komparativ + subclause (verb last), comma, 'desto' + Komparativ + verb + subject. The first half is a subclause, the second a main clause. The words first.
lecture.'…'den beri' demek ve her zaman Dativ al: It means 'since' and always takes the Dativ: seit einem Jahr, seit drei Jahren. The difference from English is this: German uses the present for something still going on, where English says 'I have been here for a year'.
lecture.Artık hobini söyleyebilir ve neyi severe: You can say what your hobby is now and what you enjoy doing. You are at a language course and you are on a break: the person next to you wants to get to know you.
lecture.Bu modülü bitirdin: artık aileni tanıtab: You have finished this module: you can introduce your family now, say who does what and say no when you need to. Now you are planning to meet your cousin.
lecture.Bugün ayrılabilen fiillerin geçmişini öğ: Today we are learning the past of separable verbs. These verbs split in two in the present; in the past they do not split, they open up in the middle. Ready?
Today we will learn to meet the neighbours. In Germany it is the usual thing to knock and introduce yourself when you have just moved in; there are ready patterns for it. Ready?
lecture.Bugün maaş konuşmasını öğreneceğiz. Bura: Today we will learn the pay conversation. Politeness here is not a matter of tone but of grammar: the form of the verb changes and the sentence softens. Ready?
lecture.Gömülü soru kalıbını biliyorsun. Bugün o: You know the embedded question pattern. Today we will add something to it: when a yes-no question is embedded a special conjunction goes in between. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.İki gözlem yeter: dakiklik burada bir di: Two observations are enough: punctuality is a language here, and criticism is direct while praise is sparing. Someone who knows both is not hurt, only prepared. The words first.
lecture.İkisi de yan cümle bağlacı: fiil sona. T: Both are subclause conjunctions: the verb goes last. English is the same on the negative: 'before I go' carries no 'not', and a bevor clause does not either. The words first.
lecture.Kural şu: 'Ben öğreniyorum, ben geçeyim: The rule: 'I am studying so that I pass' → same subject → um … zu. 'I am saving so that my children can study' → different subject → damit. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün beklenmeyeni söylemeyi öğ: Hello! Today we will learn to say the unexpected: 'I am ill but I am coming all the same.' There are two ways: obwohl (although) and trotzdem (all the same). Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün birine referans yazacağız: Hello! Today we will write a reference for somebody. The language of this genre is full of participles and every word is weighed — because what is left out carries meaning too. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün evini tanıtmayı öğreneceğ: Hello! Today we will learn to describe your home: how many rooms it has, what sort of place it is. German has a way of its own for saying 'there is', and we will look at it. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün iş gücü piyasasını konuşa: Hello! Today we will talk about the labour market. The sentences of this subject always hide the doer: 'the post cannot be filled' — who cannot fill it is not said. Ready?
lecture.Sahte özne 'es' burada çok işine yarar:: The dummy subject 'es' is very useful here: 'Es muss noch eingekauft werden' — the shopping still has to be done, and who will do it is not yet settled. The words first.
lecture.Almanca burada iki öbek kullanıyor: biri: German uses two phrases here: one for taking something on, the other for being held responsible. The second is passive — because the decision is not yours. The words first.
lecture.Almanya'da sohbet çoğu zaman havayla baş: Conversation in Germany usually starts with the weather; in the lift, at the stop, at the till. Today we will learn to describe the weather and to keep that conversation going. Ready?
lecture.Artık sabah sofrasında ne yediğini ve ne: You can say what you eat and drink at the breakfast table now. You are in the kitchen: your flatmate has made breakfast and is asking what you would like.
lecture.Bir şeyi adım adım anlatabilmek en işe y: Being able to describe something step by step is one of the most useful skills there is: giving directions, describing a dish, telling your day. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bu bir ilgi cümlesi. Tanımlanan şey yan: This is a relative clause. When the thing described is the OBJECT of the clause the relative pronoun of a masculine noun changes form; with a feminine and a neuter noun it does not. The words first.
lecture.Bugün buluşma ayarlamayı öğreneceğiz: bi: Today we will learn to arrange a meeting: asking somebody whether they have time, saying which hour suits and politely saying no if you cannot come. Ready?
lecture.Bugün hafta sonunu anlatmayı öğreneceğiz: Today we will learn to describe your weekend. And there is a short word that will be very useful: the one that says how something was in the past. Ready?
lecture.Bugün iş gününü anlatmayı öğreneceğiz: i: Today we will learn to describe your working day: when work starts, when it finishes, when you take your break. We will see two more separable verbs. Ready?
lecture.Bunu yapan şey aktarım kipi. 'Bilmiyormu: What does this is the reported mood. Say 'he did not know it, apparently' and you are neutral; say 'he did not know it' and you have taken a side. At C1 this difference is measured. The words first.
lecture.Dolaylı soruda düz soru cümlesi bozulur:: In an indirect question the plain question order breaks down: the finite verb goes right to the end. In English something similar happens, and the question turns into a statement. The words first.
lecture.dürfte: büyük ihtimalle. müsste: mantıke: dürfte: in all likelihood. müsste: it stands to reason. könnte: merely possible. The wrong choice makes you sound either too sure or too undecided. The words first.
lecture.Hoş geldin! Bugün genel geçer kurallar k: Welcome! Today we will talk about general rules: what one should do and what one should not. For that we will put together two pieces you already know. Ready?
lecture.Hoş geldin! Bugün sabah sabah işi arayıp: Welcome! Today, first thing in the morning, we will ring work and report that we are ill. Three short sentences are enough, but choose the wrong verb and the sentence sounds odd. Ready?
lecture.Kural basit: mastarın sonuna bir d eklen: The rule is simple: a d is added to the end of the infinitive and then it is declined like an ordinary adjective. The meaning is 'doing'. The hard part is not the ending but its declension. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün başkasının sözünü aktarac: Hello! Today we will relay what somebody else said. German has a separate verb form for this and that form says one single thing: this sentence is not mine. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün eski bir şehir merkezinde: Hello! Today we are in an old town centre. The language of this subject is the past passive throughout: not who restored it but what has been restored. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün mikrofonun arkasına geçiy: Hello! Today you are going behind the microphone. The language of presenting is short and nominalised: not 'the subject we are going to talk about today' but 'the subject of today's episode'. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Uzlaşmanın dili iki parçalıdır:: Hello! The language of compromise has two parts: first you grant the other side their point, then you set your own limit. German does it with paired conjunctions. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Üniversite başvurusu bir bilgi: Hello! A university application is a hunt for information and the language of that hunt is the question. But not a plain question, a softened one: 'I do not know when it closes'. Ready?
lecture.Modülün son dersinde bit pazarındayız. A: In the module's last lesson we are at a flea market. Bargaining is not done everywhere in Germany, but it is done here, and it has a courteous language of its own. Ready?
lecture.'-sin diye, -mesi için' demek. Yan cümle: It means 'so that'. A subclause conjunction: the finite verb goes right to the end. It is preferred when the subject differs — I am saving so that my children can study.
lecture.Artık kaybolduğunu söyleyebilir ve gelen: You can say you are lost now and follow a set of directions right through. You are in a street you do not know and you are going into a shop to ask for help.
lecture.Bugün haftanın günlerini öğreneceğiz ve: Today we will learn the days of the week and see a small rule that will be very useful: one word is used for days and another for times. Ready?
lecture.Gardaki en faydalı yer danışmadır: bir s: The most useful place at a station is the information desk: one question can settle your whole journey. Today we will learn to ask the departure time, the platform and the change. Ready?
lecture.Geçmişte tek seferlik bir dönemi anlatan: The conjunction for a one-off period in the past is not the one for a repeated event. A period counts as one-off too — English does not make this distinction. The words first.
lecture.İlk kalıbımız siparişin kibar hâli: sahi: Our first pattern is the polite form of ordering: the subjunctive of to have plus the adverb meaning gladly. Word for word it means 'I would gladly have'.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün ek işi konuşacağız ve tam: Hello! Today we will talk about a second job, and the prepositions that want the genitive will be very useful here: during the week, despite the load, because of the tiredness. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün iki şeyin birlikte değişt: Hello! Today we will describe two things changing together: as one rises the other rises too. German has a two-part conjunction for this. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugünkü konu hakkında konuşmak,: Hello! Today's subject is harder to talk about than pain: saying that you are struggling. But its language can be learnt and today we will learn it. Ready?
lecture.Şimdi dikkat — burası çok kişinin yanıld: Now mind this — here is where a great many people go wrong. In English you say 'half past seven', that is, you take the hour that has gone as your base. German takes the coming hour instead:
lecture.Telefonda Almanların kendini tanıtma biç: The German way of introducing yourself on the phone differs from the English one: the moment they pick up they say their surname. You will do the same. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Yardım isterken Türkçede soruyu tonla yu: In English we soften a request with the tone, or with a 'could you'. In German the question form is polite enough on its own; you do not need to add anything. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Artık bir restoranda baştan sona idare e: You can manage in a restaurant from beginning to end now. You have sat down and the waiter is coming over: give your order, choose a starter and ask for the bill at the end.
lecture.Bu kez ortaç geçmiş biçimden geliyor. 'G: This time the participle comes from the past form. 'The method that develops' is one thing, 'the method that was developed' another; German says that difference with a single participle. The words first.
lecture.Edilgenin geçmişi bir yardımcı fiilin ge: The past of the passive is built with the past form of an auxiliary; the main verb stays at the end as a participle. The question of who did it is still not asked. The words first.
lecture.İki yönlü imtiyaz kalıbı tam olarak bunu: The two-way concessive pattern carries exactly this: on the one hand how much, on the other hand how much. In both halves the verb comes right after the adjective. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir mağazadayız. Aradığın: Hello! Today we are in a shop. We will learn to say which garment you are looking for, to say you will take the one you like and to ask where the till is. Are you ready to start?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün ilgi cümlesinin en son hâ: Hello! Today the last form of the relative clause: the possessive one. In English we say 'the author whose book is famous'; German does it with two pronouns. Ready?
Hello! Today we will write a formal complaint. In Germany the way to claim a right is not the telephone but a letter, and the language of a letter is politer than speech. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün yemediğin şeyleri ve aler: Hello! Today we will learn to describe what you do not eat and what you are allergic to. This is one of the most useful subjects there is when you eat out. Are you ready to start?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün zor bir konuşmayı yönetme: Hello! Today we will learn to steer a hard conversation. The key is this: saying the PURPOSE of what you say. Then the sentence stops being an accusation. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Dün 'yapmakta olan' sıfatını ku: Hello! Yesterday we built the 'doing' adjective. Today its twin: 'done'. The two look in opposite directions and mixing them turns the meaning round. Ready?
lecture.Bir tanesi özellikle işine yarayacak: pa: One of them will be especially useful: the polite way of saying that money is short. In English we say 'I am a bit strapped'; German has a phrase of its own. The words first.
lecture.Bugün bir davete gidiyoruz ve ne götürec: Today we are going to an invitation and talking about what to take. In Germany you do not go empty-handed, and who the present is for is marked by the grammar. Ready?
lecture.Hoş geldin! Bugün telefonda randevu alac: Welcome! Today we will make an appointment by phone. For that you must not mix up two little words: one goes in front of days, the other in front of times. Ready?
lecture.İki biçim var. Biri ünlem gibi: 'keşke s: There are two forms. One is like an exclamation: 'if only I had said it'. The other is calmer: 'I should have said it'. Both have the subjunctive of the verb to have. The words first.
lecture.Kilit nokta şu: aktarım kipi bir şeyin D: The key point is this: the reported mood does not say that a thing is TRUE; it only reports that somebody said so. We will test this at the end of the lesson. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün Almancanın çok işe yaraya: Hello! Today we will learn a very useful German structure: obligation. Once you have grasped it every similar verb will settle into the same pattern. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir yapımı değerlendirece: Hello! Today we will assess a production. A good review is not one-sided: what you liked and what you did not stand side by side. Its conjunction is contrast. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir yöntem anlatacağız: b: Hello! Today we will describe a method: HOW something is done. German has a conjunction of its own for this and it answers to the English 'by doing'. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün edilgenin kardeşlerini öğ: Hello! Today we will learn the passive's siblings. In German institutional language there are three separate ways of saying 'can be done' and 'must be done' without building a passive. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün iki ülkenin sofra âdetler: Hello! Today we will compare the table manners of two countries. For that we need paired conjunctions: both, neither, on the one hand and on the other. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün iş hayatının en gergin cü: Hello! Today we will build the tensest sentence in working life: making a promise, but a conditional one. German has two patterns for it and both are formal. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün tartışmanın kurallarını k: Hello! Today we will talk about the rules of debate. What is interesting is this: the language of a fair debate is two-part as well, because it holds both sides at once. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün üç ikili bağlaç: ya…ya da: Hello! Today three paired conjunctions: either…or, both…and, neither…nor. English pairs them too; the trap is in the last one: 'weder…noch' is already negative and no nicht is added. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün yapay zekâ etiği. Ve dili: Hello! Today, the ethics of artificial intelligence. And a place where language sits right at the centre: ascribing human qualities to machines usually starts with a slip of language. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi. Dairede en ç: Hello! The module's last lesson. The sentence that helps you most at an office is not a question but the softened form of a question: 'I wonder whether …'. Today we will build it. Ready?
Hello! A new module: social debate. And the first tool is the structure that marks what is not real. You met it at B2; here you will build both of its forms. Ready?
lecture.Almanya'da bir mağazaya girdiğinde satıc: When you walk into a shop in Germany the assistant usually comes over at once and asks what you are looking for. You can answer with a single pattern. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bu bağlacı biliyorsun ama ikinci parçada: You know this conjunction, but the order in the second half will want care again: the comparative right after the conjunction and the verb after that. The words first.
lecture.Bu derste iki fiil ayrımı var: bazı spor: This lesson has a distinction between two verbs: some sports are 'done', others are 'gone to'. And saying how often has an order of its own. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bu iki hamlenin ayrı dilbilgisi var: idd: These two moves have separate grammar: the claim in the reported mood, the fact in the plain mood. The difference shows in the sentence and the listener does not confuse who said what. The words first.
lecture.Bugün sözleşme dilini öğreneceğiz. Bu di: Today we will learn the language of contracts. This language has a feature: who did it is not said, only what happened. In English we call this the passive. Ready?
lecture.Bunun adı edilgen çatı. Türkçede '-ilir,: The name of this is the passive. English builds it just as German does, with an auxiliary and a participle: it is stirred in, it is added. First, the words of the kitchen.
lecture.Dilbilimin cevabı net: norm kullanımı iz: Linguistics gives a clear answer: the norm follows usage, not the other way round. So today's 'mistake' can be tomorrow's rule — and that is not a collapse but a movement. The words first.
lecture.İki tür var: edatla kaynaşanlar (darauf,: There are two kinds: those that fuse with a preposition (darauf, dabei, dadurch) and those that point back along a list (Ersteres, Letzteres). The second will be very useful at C1. The words first.
lecture.İlk parçacık en çok kullanılanı ve üç ay: The first particle is the commonest and does three separate jobs: it softens an invitation, it underlines the known and it answers a negative question in the positive. The words first.
lecture.Kural: eril ve nötr isimler için bir biç: The rule: one form for masculine and neuter nouns, another for feminine and plural. And mind this — the verb agrees not with the pronoun but with the noun AFTER it. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Modülün son dersi ve en lezzetl: Hello! The module's last lesson and the tastiest: you will recommend a dish to somebody. For the recommendation to be good you have to describe the dish, which means the relative clause again. Ready?
lecture.Türkçede ricayı sesinle yumuşatırsın. Al: In English you soften a request with a form of the verb too — 'could you' rather than 'can you'. German works the same way, and without that form the sentence sounds curt. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bazen otobüs beklemeye vakit yoktur. Bug: Sometimes there is no time to wait for a bus. Today we will learn to tell the driver where you are going, to ask how long it takes and to say that short sentence as you pay. Ready?
lecture.Biri koşulu olumlu koyar: şu olursa yapa: One sets the condition positively: we will do it if that happens. The other names the exception: we will do it unless that happens. Mixing the two turns your word inside out. The words first.
lecture.Bu grup mecaz, deyim değil: yani sözcükl: This group is metaphor, not idiom: the words still carry their own meaning but have been moved into another field. In English we say 'the atmosphere is tense' too. The words first.
lecture.Bunun için zıtlık bağlacı lazım: 'yapmam: For this you need the conjunction of contrast: 'although I do'. Because it is a subclause the verb goes last, and if it stands first the main clause starts with the verb. The words first.
lecture.Konuşmada 'ist gerufen worden' dersin, r: In speech you say 'ist gerufen worden', in a report it is written 'wurde gerufen'. Both are right but the genre differs, and being able to read a report is part of B2's business. The words first.
lecture.Kural şu: bu bağlaçtan sonra fiil dilek: The rule is this: after this conjunction the verb goes into the subjunctive, because what is said is NOT real. In English we say 'as if' and the verb can shift too — 'as if he were'; German always marks it on the verb. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bu modülün son dersindeyiz ve e: Hello! We are at this module's last lesson and sitting down in the most dreaded chair: the dentist's. The pattern for pain that you learnt will pay off today in a real scene. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün Almancanın en çok kafa ka: Hello! Today we will settle German's most confusing distinction: who is addressed familiarly and who politely. Two question patterns and one single rule. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir tarif okuyacağız. Tar: Hello! Today we will read a recipe. Recipes are written in an odd language: nobody says 'I do it', everything is told as though it were happening by itself. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün edilgenin üç kısayolunu b: Hello! Today we bring together the three shortcuts of the passive. All three carry a passive sense but all three say different things, and mixing them breaks the sentence. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kuşakları konuşacağız ve: Hello! Today we will talk about the generations, and for that we need conjunctions that name both sides together — because a debate between generations ends the moment one side is blamed. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugünkü ders zor bir cümle için: Hello! Today's lesson is for a hard sentence: telling somebody what you feel. The subjunctive gives courage here, because it makes it easier to say no. Ready?
lecture.Modülün son dersinde koruyucu sağlığı ko: In the module's last lesson we are talking about preventive health: regular check-ups, vaccinations, tests. And we will learn to build advice that holds for everyone. Ready?
lecture.Örnek: 'şefinle konuştuktan sonra' yerin: An example: instead of 'after you have talked to your boss', 'following agreement with your boss'. The same meaning, shorter and more formal. You have to be able to do it both ways. The words first.
lecture.Türkçede bunları ekle yaparsın: başlamad: English uses separate words for these too — 'before it starts', 'while you tidy up' — but in German they change the structure of the sentence. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Artık neyi yapabildiğini, neyi pek yapam: You can say what you can do now and what you are not much good at, and you can ask the other person. You are enrolling on a sports course and the trainer wants to get to know you.
lecture.Bu grup ofiste sık duyulur ve çoğu Türkç: This group is often heard in the office and most of it is close to the English: 'to call the tune' and 'to dance to somebody's tune' are looking at the same place. The words first.
lecture.Bugün küçük bir alışveriş var: sabun, şa: Today there is a little shopping to do: soap, shampoo, toothpaste. We will learn to name them, to say what you need and to ask without getting lost among the shelves. Ready?
lecture.Denedin, aynaya baktın. Sonucu iki kısa: You have tried it on and looked in the mirror. You say the verdict with one of two short sentences. You saw the verb when we did the time, where it meant 'that suits me'; with clothes it does the same job:
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir düşünce deneyi kuraca: Hello! Today we will set up a thought experiment. It is one of the strongest moves in a debate: accepting the other side's claim for a moment and looking at where it leads. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir süreci baştan sona an: Hello! Today we will learn to describe a process from beginning to end: the driving licence. The language of a process is passive, because what matters is not who does it but the order. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün çevrenin nasıl kurulduğun: Hello! Today we will talk about how a network is built. The sentences of this subject have no doer: a contact is made, a job is found through a recommendation — who does it is not said. Ready?
lecture.Renkler alışverişte en çok işine yarayac: Colours are among the most useful words there are when you shop. The good news is this: in the form you will learn in this lesson the colour words do not change at all. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Tarifi aldın ama bir soru kaldı: yürüyec: You have the directions but one question is left: will you walk, or do you need transport? Today we will learn to ask about distance and to describe where a place is. Ready?
lecture.Türkçede plan tek ekle çıkar: '-meyi düş: English builds a plan with an infinitive too — 'I plan to try it'. In German an infinitive phrase comes after the comma and a little word goes in front of the infinitive. The words first.
lecture.Aldığın pantolon evde üstüne olmadı. Bug: The trousers you bought did not fit at home. Today we will learn to exchange them: to say what you want, to give the reason and to answer the question about the receipt. Ready?
lecture.Almancanın en kibar isteme biçimi; Türkç: The politest way of asking in German; like the English 'I would like …'. It is a notch more courteous than the asking pattern you learnt in the café, and in a restaurant you will always hear it.
lecture.Bir doğum günü yaklaşıyor ve hediye lazı: A birthday is coming up and a present is needed. Today we will learn to say who you are looking for a present for, to swap ideas with the assistant and to ask for it to be wrapped. Ready?
lecture.Bu, tanışmanın ikinci cümlesidir; kaçama: This is the second sentence of getting to know somebody; there is no escaping it. Compared with English something goes missing when you name a profession in German, and that is what we will watch. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bugün Almanya'da çok yaygın bir çalışma: Today we will talk about a way of working that is very common in Germany: flexitime. To describe it you need a conditional clause and that clause sends the verb to the end. Ready?
lecture.Bugün geçmiş zamana başlıyoruz ve bu, A1: Today we are starting on the past tense, and this is A1's biggest step. In English the past is built with one word: I bought, I saw. In German the sentence splits in two. Ready?
lecture.Bugün saati öğreneceğiz: saati sormak, s: Today we will learn the time: asking the time, telling the time and asking when something is. There is a point here where German parts from English, and we will look at that too. Ready?
lecture.Hobilerini anlattın; peki neleri yapabil: You have described your hobbies; but what can you do? Today we will learn to say that you can do something, that you are not much good at something, and to ask the other person. Ready?
lecture.İlk kalıbımız niyet bildiriyor: ayrılabi: Our first pattern states an intention: a separable verb plus an infinitive phrase. The separable verb's prefix stays at the end of the main clause and the infinitive phrase comes after the comma.
lecture.Markette iki cümle işini görür: ne aradı: Two sentences will do at the supermarket: saying what you are looking for and asking where it is. Today we will also learn a small but important rule. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir sözleşmeyi feshedeceğ: Hello! Today we will terminate a contract. Without three things a German notice can count as invalid: the date, the notice period and a request for written confirmation. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün dilbilgisinden çok bir tu: Hello! Today we will learn less a piece of grammar than an attitude — but we will say that in German too. The subject is mistakes. A mistake left unspoken grows; spoken it shrinks. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kendi verilerini savunaca: Hello! Today you will defend your own data. The language of this field is the modal passive, because a rule says not what somebody will do but what may not be done. Ready?
lecture.Sıra şu: dinleyiciyi sahneye al, sorunu: The order is this: bring the listener on stage, show the problem, give the solution, explain what makes it different, answer the 'why now'. Today we will build the sentences for it. The words first.
lecture.Yani 'Bunu deneyebilir miyim?' Cümlenin: That is, 'Can I try this on?' Mind the end of the sentence: the main verb stands at the very end. English does not do that, so this order will take getting used to.
lecture.Yüz ders boyunca kurum dilini, edilgeni,: Over a hundred lessons you have built institutional language, the passive, reported speech, participle adjectives and the language of cause and effect. Today we will gather it all into one sentence. The words first.
lecture.En güçlü hamle ayrıştırmak: karşı tarafı: The strongest move is to separate things out: saying where the other side is right and setting apart where they are wrong. In both halves of the pattern the verb comes right after the adjective. The words first.
lecture.İki yol var. Birincisi cümlenin başına b: There are two ways. The first is to put a phrase at the front of the sentence; then the verb comes right after it. The second is to build a subclause; then the verb goes last. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün resmî rapor dili öğrenece: Hello! Today we will learn the language of formal reports. Police and press reports use the past form of the passive — a different form from the one you hear in speech. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yeni bir şehirde en çok işine y: Hello! The most useful skill there is in a new city is asking the way. Today we will learn to ask the way politely and to understand the directions you are given. Are you ready to start?
lecture.Özetin dört parçası vardır: soru, yöntem: An abstract has four parts: the question, the method, the finding, the conclusion. All four are said with set phrases and it is good that they are — the reader knows where to find what. The words first.
lecture.'Sanki her şey kusursuz olmak zorundaymı: 'I behave as if everything had to be perfect' — this sentence names a rule, and a rule that has been named can be argued with. The words first.
lecture.İkili bağlaç iki parçadan oluşur ve ikis: A paired conjunction is made of two parts and both have to be said. Say half and the sentence stays incomplete — like saying 'both' in English and forgetting the 'and'. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün ikinci olumsuzluk kelimes: Hello! Today we will learn the second negative word. You know one of them; that one negated nouns, and this one negates verbs and adjectives. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün nerelerde yaşadığını anla: Hello! Today you will tell where you have lived. On official forms and in a CV the spoken past is not used; the written past is. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün sevdiğin bir yeri anlatma: Hello! Today we will learn to describe a place you love. German has two ways of defining a place and both are right: a pronoun with a preposition, or the single word wo. Ready?
lecture.Niyet Almancada mastar öbeğiyle kurulur:: In German intention is built with an infinitive phrase: a little preposition and the infinitive, both at the end of the sentence. English uses an infinitive here too, but German puts the whole phrase after the comma. The words first.
lecture.Tek seferlik geçmiş için bir bağlaç, tek: One conjunction is used for a one-off past, another for a repeated one. In English both come out as 'when', so the distinction slips past. The words first.
lecture.Türkçede zaten var: 'yapılıyor', 'kapatı: English already has it: 'it is being done', 'it is being closed'. The doer is rubbed out of the sentence. German needs two pieces for it as well and today we will build both. The words first.
lecture.Bu iki kalıp Konjunktiv II ile kurulur —: These two patterns are built with the Konjunktiv II — the subjunctive. They sound softer than saying 'I want' outright, and formal conversation turns entirely on them. The words first.
lecture.Kalıbımız edilgen çatının şimdiki zamanı: Our pattern is the present of the passive. The auxiliary in second place, the main verb as a participle at the very end. There is no need to say who does it — in a recipe the reader will.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün Almanya'da en çok karşına: Hello! Today we will fill in the paper you will meet most often in Germany: the registration form. We will learn to give an address, to say the postcode and to ask for a signature. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir kitap kulübündeyiz. K: Hello! Today we are at a book club. Talking about a book has two parts: describing the book and giving your reasons. For the describing we will go back to the relative clause. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün üçüncü hâl: yönelme. Bazı: Hello! Today the third case: the dative. Some verbs want the dative after them — to trust, to help, to listen. The same happens in a relative clause. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün üçüncü kez bozulan bir ci: Hello! Today there is a device that has broken for the third time. The force of this conversation comes from a list: what has been DONE so far. And that list is built with the past passive. Ready?
lecture.Selam! Bugüne kadar hep kendinden söz et: Hi! Until now you have always talked about yourself. Today we will talk about somebody else: where your friend lives, where they work, when you meet. Ready?
lecture.Yer değiştirmeyen fiiller öteki yardımcı: Verbs with no change of place take the other auxiliary. And there is something else about this participle: it has no 'ge' at the front. Verbs carrying an unstressed prefix never take that syllable.
lecture.'Almancamı geliştireceğim' bir hedef değ: 'I will improve my German' is not a goal but a wish. 'I will pass the exam in six months' is a goal, because it can be measured. Today we will build both in German. The words first.
lecture.Almanya'da trenlerin dakikliği meşhurdur: The punctuality of German trains is famous, but when they are late everybody uses the same two words. What really matters in this lesson is a small choice of verb. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bugün geçmişten bahsediyoruz: son tatili: Today we are talking about the past: your last holiday! In German the past is told with the Perfekt. We will learn to say that you went somewhere and did things there. Ready?
lecture.Bugün iş çıkışını konuşacağız: yorgunken: Today we will talk about the end of the working day: what you do when you are tired, what you would rather do. We will learn a small word and with it you will be able to say what you prefer. Ready?
lecture.Ev konuşması her yerde çıkıyor: iş arkad: Talk about your home comes up everywhere: with a colleague, with a neighbour, while flat-hunting. We will learn three patterns and with all three you can describe your home from top to bottom. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Kaygı konuşulurken hep aynı yapı çıkıyor: The same structure always turns up when worry is talked about: 'if that happens I will do this'. That is, a conditional clause. The rule: if the condition stands first the main clause starts with the verb. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bu modülün son dersi: öğrendiği: Hello! This is the module's last lesson: with the conjunctions you have learnt you will tell a rounded story. The skeleton: zuerst, nachdem, während, plötzlich, deshalb, am Ende. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün bir deneyimi anlatacağız: Hello! Today we will tell of an experience — but not with the spoken past, with the written one. This is the form used in a CV, in an application, in a report. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün kendimizi tanıtmayı öğren: Hello! Today we will learn to introduce ourselves. We will work through three patterns: saying your name, saying where you are from and saying where you live. Are you ready to start?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün para isteyeceğiz — ama hu: Hello! Today we will ask for money — but in legal language. In this language the prepositions of cause want the genitive, and used wrongly the claim looks amateurish. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün seçim yapmayı konuşacağız: Hello! Today we will talk about making a choice: an intensive course or an evening course. Choosing means comparing, so we will refresh the comparative. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Yeni modül ve konusu tek bir ya: Hello! A new module, and its subject is not a single structure but a whole system: the passive. We start with the form that will help you most — reporting finished jobs. Ready?
lecture.Birincisi imkân söyler, ikincisi zorunlu: The first states possibility, the second obligation, and the third stands like an adjective and states a quality. Using two of them in the same sentence is a common mistake. The words first.
lecture.Bu üç cümle merhabadan hemen sonra gelir: These three sentences come straight after hello and a short answer is enough. There is one oddity: Germans use the verb 'to go' when they ask how you are. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Bugün ilk iş gününde işine yarayacak bir: Today we will learn something that will help you on your first day at work: embedding a question inside a sentence instead of asking it outright. This is the commonest way of being polite in German. Ready?
lecture.Dilbilgisi kurulabilir ama Almanca bunu: The grammar can be built but German does not say it this way: when you hurt yourself the reflexive pronoun stands in the dative and the definite article comes instead of a possessive. It should be:
lecture.Kip fiilleri geçmişte Perfekt'e girmez;: Modals do not go into the Perfekt in the past; like to be and to have they use their own short forms. The pasts of to want, to be able and to have to are these:
lecture.Kural şu: sein yardımcı fiili, ortaç, so: The rule: the auxiliary sein, the participle, then the shortened form. The long 'geworden' is not used here, and this is one of the most visible marks of the level. The words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün herkesin konuştuğu konu:: Hello! Today the subject everybody is talking about: everything getting dearer. The language of economics says this not with verbs but with nouns, and those nouns are joined with the genitive. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün ilgi cümlesini insan tari: Hello! Today we will work the relative clause on describing people — but this time not with a particular person, with indefinite words like 'people', 'somebody', 'nobody'. Ready?
lecture.Merhaba! Emir kipinin ikinci yüzünü öğre: Hello! We will learn the second face of the imperative. You know the pharmacist's polite form; today we will take the familiar form you use when you advise a friend. Ready?
lecture.Sıra sende: 'Ara sırasında sohbet ediyor: Your turn: 'We chat during the break.' — instead of 'Während die Pause ist, …' the more natural 'Während der Pause …', but let us build a clause: 'Während wir warten, …'
lecture.Yani 'Hava güneşli'. Baştaki küçük kelim: That is, 'It is sunny'. The little word at the front points at nothing; it is only there so that the sentence is not left without a subject. Leave it out and the sentence stops being German.
lecture.Biriyle tanıştığında en çok konuşulan şe: This is one of the things talked about most when you meet somebody. We will learn three patterns and with all three you will be able to tell your whole day. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.İki edatla başlıyoruz: biri sebep, biri: We start with two prepositions: one of cause, one of contrast. Both want the genitive. In everyday speech you will hear the dative too, but in writing and in an exam this is what is expected. The words first.
lecture.Küçük bir kolaylık: sonu 'oda' kelimesiy: A small mercy: compound words ending in the word for room all take the same article. Notice that and half of them come by themselves. Let us learn the words first.
lecture.Merhaba! Bugün çağrı merkezi. Burada iki: Hello! Today, the call centre. Both sides speak in the passive here: nobody says 'I did it', they say 'it can be done' or 'it needs to be clarified'. Ready?
