de-a1-zeit-haben.goal: The day and time of the meeting have been fixed and the day that did not suit has been ruled out politely.

de-a1-kleidung.scene: You are in a clothes shop and the assistant has come over. Say what you are looking for, choose one of the things they show you, and ask where the till is at the end.
de-a1-kleidung.partner: a slightly chatty assistant who enjoys the job
de-a1-kleidung.openingTr: Good afternoon! Are you looking for anything in particular?
de-a1-kleidung.goal: The item you wanted has been found, one has been chosen and you know where the till is.

de-a1-groesse.scene: You want to try on a jacket you like in a shop. Say your size, ask to try it on, ask where the fitting room is, and say at the end whether it fits.
de-a1-groesse.partner: a hurried sales assistant who still tries to help
de-a1-groesse.openingTr: The jacket has only just come in. What size are you?
de-a1-groesse.goal: Your size has been found, the jacket has been tried on in the fitting room and you have said whether it fits.

de-a1-farben.scene: In a small boutique you like the shirt in the window but you want it in another colour. Ask about the colours, say which one you like, and reply to the colour the assistant suggests.
de-a1-farben.partner: a boutique owner with strong opinions about colour
de-a1-farben.openingTr: This shirt comes in four colours. Which colour are you looking for?
de-a1-farben.goal: You have asked for the colour you wanted and settled whether you are buying it.

de-a1-preis.scene: You want to know the price of a pair of shoes you like in a shoe shop. Ask the price, say you find them expensive, and find out whether anything else is in the sale.
de-a1-preis.partner: a persuasive assistant who knows every offer by heart
de-a1-preis.openingTr: These shoes are on special offer at the moment. Would you like to try them on?
de-a1-preis.goal: The price has been found out and another option in the sale has been discussed.

de-a1-gefallen.scene: You are out shopping with a friend who cannot decide between two jackets. Say which one you like, explain why you find it nicer, and ask for their opinion too.
de-a1-gefallen.openingTr: I just can't decide. What do you think of the black jacket?
de-a1-gefallen.goal: The two jackets have been compared and your friend has decided which one to buy.

de-a1-umtausch.scene: You are at the returns desk of a shop to exchange the trousers you bought yesterday. Say what you want, explain why, answer the question about the receipt, and discuss what you will take instead.
de-a1-umtausch.partner: a till assistant who sticks to the rules but tries to help
de-a1-umtausch.openingTr: Good afternoon! What can I do for you?
de-a1-umtausch.goal: It is clear whether the exchange can be made and what you are taking instead has been settled.

de-a1-geschenk.scene: You are in a gift shop looking for a present for your mother. Say who it is for, reply to the assistant's suggestions, make one of your own, and ask for it to be gift-wrapped at the end.
de-a1-geschenk.partner: a friendly assistant who loves making suggestions
de-a1-geschenk.openingTr: Welcome! Are you looking for a present for someone?
de-a1-geschenk.goal: The present has been chosen and you have asked for it to be gift-wrapped.

de-a1-markt.scene: You are standing in front of a fruit stall at the Saturday market. Ask the price, say how much you want, adjust the quantity, and find out the total at the end.
de-a1-markt.openingTr: All fresh from this morning! What can I get you?
de-a1-markt.goal: What you asked for has been weighed out by the quantity you gave and the amount to pay has been said.

de-a1-apotheke-kauf.scene: You are in a health and beauty shop with a few things on your list. Say what you need, ask where a product you cannot find is, and ask a member of staff for something you cannot see on the shelf.
de-a1-apotheke-kauf.partner: a calm shop worker who never leaves the shelves
de-a1-apotheke-kauf.openingTr: You must be looking for something. Can I help you?
de-a1-apotheke-kauf.goal: The things on your list have been found, or an alternative has been suggested.

de-a1-online.scene: The order you placed online still has not arrived and you have rung customer service. Say what you ordered, ask how long the delivery should take, and find out where the parcel is.
de-a1-online.partner: a calm agent who is used to apologising
de-a1-online.openingTr: Customer service, good afternoon! How can I help you?
de-a1-online.goal: You have found out where your order is and been told when it will arrive.

de-a1-weg.scene: You are out in the street in a strange city and looking for the railway station. Ask a passer-by politely, listen to the directions, and ask again about the part you did not follow.
de-a1-weg.partner: an elderly man in no hurry who enjoys giving directions
de-a1-weg.openingTr: You look lost. Can I help you?
de-a1-weg.goal: The way to the station has been described and the part you missed has been repeated until it was clear.

de-a1-bus-bahn.scene: You are at a bus stop and you want to get to the station. Ask the person beside you which line goes there, find out how many stops it is, and say how you will get there.
de-a1-bus-bahn.partner: a helpful passenger who takes the same line every day
de-a1-bus-bahn.openingTr: Are you waiting for the number three as well?
de-a1-bus-bahn.goal: You have found out which line goes there and after how many stops you get off.

de-a1-ticket.scene: You are at the ticket office of the railway station and you want to go to Berlin today. Ask for the ticket, say whether it is a return, find out the price and ask about the platform.
de-a1-ticket.partner: a fast-talking but polite ticket clerk
de-a1-ticket.openingTr: Next, please! Where would you like to travel to?
de-a1-ticket.goal: The ticket has been bought, the price has been given and you know the platform number.

de-a1-verspaetung.scene: You are waiting on the platform and the train still has not come. Ask the passenger beside you what is going on, talk about how long the delay is, and say what you are going to do.
de-a1-verspaetung.partner: a mildly sarcastic passenger who is used to delays
de-a1-verspaetung.openingTr: Ten minutes late again. Are you waiting for the train to Cologne too?
de-a1-verspaetung.goal: You have found out how long the delay is and settled whether you are going to wait.

de-a1-taxi.scene: You have got into a taxi and you need to go to the airport. Say where you are going, ask how long it will take, make a little conversation on the way, and settle the payment as you get out.
de-a1-taxi.partner: a chatty taxi driver who knows the city inside out
de-a1-taxi.openingTr: Good evening! Where can I take you?
de-a1-taxi.goal: The destination and the journey time have been discussed and the fare has been paid on arrival.

de-a1-stadtplan.scene: You are at the hotel reception with a map of the city in your hand. Say where you want to go, ask whether it is far, find out how many minutes it takes on foot, and get the location described.
de-a1-stadtplan.partner: a receptionist who likes marking the map with a pen
de-a1-stadtplan.openingTr: Good morning! Where would you like to go today?
de-a1-stadtplan.goal: How far away your destination is and how to get there have both been made clear.

de-a1-sehenswuerdig.scene: You are at the city tourist office and you have a free day tomorrow. Ask what there is to see, give your opinion on the suggestions, and explain your own choice with your reasons.
de-a1-sehenswuerdig.partner: an enthusiastic tourist officer who loves the city
de-a1-sehenswuerdig.openingTr: Welcome to our city! How long are you staying here?
de-a1-sehenswuerdig.goal: A plan for tomorrow has been chosen and you have settled where to start.

de-a1-verlaufen.scene: You have realised you are lost and gone into a shop to ask for help. Explain your situation, say where you want to go, listen to the directions and repeat them to be sure.
de-a1-verlaufen.partner: a patient shopkeeper who gives directions calmly
de-a1-verlaufen.openingTr: You look puzzled. Are you looking for a particular street?
de-a1-verlaufen.goal: The right way has been described and you have confirmed you understood it by repeating it back.

de-a1-fahrrad.scene: You are in a bike hire shop and you want to see the city by bike. Ask for a bike, say how many hours it is for, ask the price and find out about the cycle path.
de-a1-fahrrad.partner: a shop owner who loves the bikes like their own children
de-a1-fahrrad.openingTr: Hello! Would you like to hire a bike for today?
de-a1-fahrrad.goal: How many hours the bike is for and what it costs have been settled, and the cycle path has been described.

de-a1-bahnhof-info.scene: You are at the information desk of the station and you want to go to Hamburg today. Ask when the train leaves, find out whether you have to change, ask about the platform and talk about how long the journey takes.
de-a1-bahnhof-info.partner: an information clerk who loves the job and has an answer to everything
de-a1-bahnhof-info.openingTr: Good afternoon! Do you need any information?
de-a1-bahnhof-info.goal: The departure time, the platform and whether you have to change have all been found out.

de-a1-wohnung-zeigen.scene: You have moved into a new place and a friend is asking about it. Say how many rooms it has, describe what sort of place it is, and say what there is.
de-a1-wohnung-zeigen.partner: a friend who cannot wait to see your new place
de-a1-wohnung-zeigen.openingTr: So, how's the new flat? How many rooms has it got?
de-a1-wohnung-zeigen.goal: How many rooms the flat has and what sort of place it is have been described, and your friend has promised to come and see it.

de-a1-zimmer.scene: A friend has come to your home for the first time and you are showing them round. Point out the rooms one by one and give each name with the right article.
de-a1-zimmer.partner: a curious friend who likes everything
de-a1-zimmer.openingTr: Wow, it's lovely here! What sort of room is this?
de-a1-zimmer.goal: All the rooms have been shown and your friend has understood the layout of the flat.

de-a1-moebel.scene: A friend is arranging the furniture in their new flat and asking for your opinion. Say where each piece should go, and choose the right position verbs.
de-a1-moebel.openingTr: Tell me, where shall I put the sofa? In the corner?
de-a1-moebel.goal: It has been settled where every piece of furniture is going.

de-a1-nachbarn.scene: You have just moved in and knocked on your neighbour's door. Introduce yourself, say you have just moved in, and have a short conversation.
de-a1-nachbarn.partner: a warm neighbour who has lived in the building for years
de-a1-nachbarn.openingTr: Good afternoon! You must be the new neighbours, aren't you?
de-a1-nachbarn.goal: You have introduced yourselves to each other and closed your first short chat with a goodbye.

de-a1-hausordnung.scene: You have just moved into the building and the manager is going through the house rules with you. Ask about anything you do not follow and repeat the rules in your own words.
de-a1-hausordnung.partner: a building manager who cares about the rules but is helpful
de-a1-hausordnung.openingTr: Welcome to the building! Do you know the house rules yet?
de-a1-hausordnung.goal: All the rules have been understood and confirmed by you repeating them back.

de-a1-miete-zahlen.scene: You have gone to view a flat and you are talking to the landlord. Ask about the rent, find out whether the service charge is included, and make sure you have the price right.
de-a1-miete-zahlen.partner: a straight-talking landlord who knows the business
de-a1-miete-zahlen.openingTr: Well, how do you like the flat?
de-a1-miete-zahlen.goal: The rent, the service charge and the total have been made clear, and you have said whether you will think it over.

de-a1-putzen.scene: You are dividing up the weekend cleaning with your flatmate. Say which job you are taking on and say what you want them to do.
de-a1-putzen.partner: a flatmate who is not keen on housework
de-a1-putzen.openingTr: So, who's tidying the kitchen today?
de-a1-putzen.goal: The cleaning jobs have been shared out and it is settled who does what and when.

de-a1-umzug.scene: It is moving day and a friend has come to help. Say what you are carrying where, ask them for help, and warn them about the heavy things.
de-a1-umzug.partner: a friend who rushes in to help but is a bit hasty
de-a1-umzug.openingTr: Right, I'm here! What shall I carry first?
de-a1-umzug.goal: It has been settled what goes where and help has been arranged for the heavy things.

de-a1-garten.scene: Your neighbour has seen you on the balcony and started chatting. Say what you have on your balcony, talk about your flowers, and say whether you like sitting out there.
de-a1-garten.partner: a neighbour who is keen on growing flowers
de-a1-garten.openingTr: Your flowers look really lovely! Do you water them every day?
de-a1-garten.goal: Everything on your balcony has been described and you have promised your neighbour a coffee.

de-a1-kaputt.scene: Something at home has broken and you have rung the caretaker. Say what is broken, say how long it has been like that, and ask them to come.
de-a1-kaputt.partner: a caretaker who is rushed off their feet but finds a solution
de-a1-kaputt.openingTr: Caretaker Berger speaking, good afternoon. What can I do for you?
de-a1-kaputt.goal: The fault has been described and it has been settled when the caretaker is coming.

de-a1-hobbys.scene: You are on a break at a language course and have started chatting with the person next to you. Talk about your hobbies, say what you do in your free time, and ask about theirs.
de-a1-hobbys.partner: a curious fellow student who asks a lot of questions
de-a1-hobbys.openingTr: A break at last! What do you actually do in your free time?
de-a1-hobbys.goal: You have both talked about your hobbies and found a shared interest.

de-a1-koennen.scene: You have come to sign up for a sports course and the instructor is asking what you can do. Say what you can do, say what you are not good at, and ask them a question too.
de-a1-koennen.partner: an energetic sports instructor who likes to encourage
de-a1-koennen.openingTr: Glad you're here! Can you swim already?
de-a1-koennen.goal: What you can do has been established and a course time that suits you has been suggested.

de-a1-sport.scene: You have come to look round a gym and the person at the desk is asking questions. Say what sort of sport you do and how often, and ask about the gym's opening hours.
de-a1-sport.partner: a gym adviser who is trying to sell a membership but is sincere
de-a1-sport.openingTr: Welcome! Are you doing any sport regularly at the moment?
de-a1-sport.goal: What sport you do has been discussed and the opening hours and the membership have been made clear.

de-a1-musik.scene: You have started chatting with a stranger on the way out of a concert. Say what you thought of the concert, talk about the music you like, and ask about their taste.
de-a1-musik.partner: an eager music fan who goes to every concert
de-a1-musik.openingTr: That was a great concert, wasn't it? Do you often listen to music like that?
de-a1-musik.goal: You have shared your thoughts on the concert and compared your taste in music.

de-a1-kino.scene: You are ringing a friend to invite them to the cinema this evening. Make your suggestion, talk about which film you will see, and settle the time and the meeting place.
de-a1-kino.partner: an eager friend who is up for any film
de-a1-kino.openingTr: Hey, good to hear from you! What's up?
de-a1-kino.goal: The film, the time and the meeting place have all been fixed.

de-a1-wetter-smalltalk.scene: You have met your neighbour at the entrance to the building. Talk about the weather, say what you are doing today, and ask about their plans too.
de-a1-wetter-smalltalk.partner: a chatty neighbour who walks the dog every morning
de-a1-wetter-smalltalk.openingTr: Good morning! Lovely weather today, isn't it?
de-a1-wetter-smalltalk.goal: A short conversation about the weather has been had and you have both learnt the other's plans for the day.

de-a1-park.scene: You have met a friend in the park on a sunny day. Say what there is in the park, talk about where to sit, and decide together what to do.
de-a1-park.partner: a cheerful friend who likes to plan everything
de-a1-park.openingTr: There you are! Shall we go to the lake or onto the meadow?
de-a1-park.goal: Where you are sitting and what you are doing in the park have been settled.

de-a1-schwimmbad.scene: You are at the ticket desk of a swimming pool. Ask the entrance fee, find out how long you can stay, ask where the changing rooms are, and ask about hiring a towel.
de-a1-schwimmbad.partner: a friendly pool attendant who explains every rule
de-a1-schwimmbad.openingTr: Hello! Would you like a ticket for two hours or for the whole day?
de-a1-schwimmbad.goal: The entrance fee, how long you can stay and the changing rooms have been sorted out, and the towel question has been settled.

de-a1-fernsehen.scene: You are at home in the evening and you and your flatmate cannot agree on what to watch. Say what you want to watch and why, reply to their suggestion, and agree on a time.
de-a1-fernsehen.partner: a flatmate who wants to watch the news every evening
de-a1-fernsehen.openingTr: The news is about to start. Or would you like to watch something else?
de-a1-fernsehen.goal: You have agreed on what to watch and what time it starts.

de-a1-absage.scene: A friend has rung to invite you to something this evening but you cannot go. Say you are sorry, decline politely, explain why, and suggest another day.
de-a1-absage.partner: an affectionate, persistent friend who does not give up easily
de-a1-absage.openingTr: Hello! We're going out to eat this evening. Are you coming along?
de-a1-absage.goal: The invitation has been declined politely, the reason has been given and another day has been suggested.

de-a1-koerper.scene: You are on a first aid course. The instructor is pointing at parts of the body: give their names with the articles and ask for the German of the ones you do not know.
de-a1-koerper.partner: a witty and very patient first aid instructor
de-a1-koerper.openingTr: Welcome to the course! Tell me, what's this called in German?
de-a1-koerper.goal: Every part of the body pointed at has been named with its article and you have learnt the German for the ones you did not know.

de-a1-weh-tun.scene: You are in the doctor's consulting room. Say where it hurts and how long it has been going on, and answer the doctor's questions.
de-a1-weh-tun.partner: a doctor who is in a hurry but listens carefully
de-a1-weh-tun.openingTr: Good afternoon! So what's the trouble?
de-a1-weh-tun.goal: Where the pain is and how long it has lasted have been described, and the doctor has said what happens next.

de-a1-termin-arzt.scene: You are ringing a doctor's surgery to make an appointment. Say why you are coming and discuss which day and time suit you.
de-a1-termin-arzt.partner: a receptionist with a full diary who talks fast on the phone
de-a1-termin-arzt.openingTr: Doctor Weber's surgery, good afternoon! What can I do for you?
de-a1-termin-arzt.goal: The day and time of the appointment have been fixed and you have been told what to bring with you.

de-a1-muessen.scene: A friend of yours is ill but still wants to go to work. Say what they ought to do and talk them into seeing a doctor.
de-a1-muessen.partner: a stubborn friend who complains constantly but comes round in the end
de-a1-muessen.openingTr: I feel awful, but I have to work today. Is that a problem?
de-a1-muessen.goal: Your friend has been talked out of going to work today and into seeing a doctor.

de-a1-apotheke.scene: You have a sore throat and you are at the pharmacy. Describe your symptoms, ask for a medicine, and repeat the pharmacist's instructions to be sure you have them right.
de-a1-apotheke.partner: a meticulous pharmacist who explains everything one step at a time
de-a1-apotheke.openingTr: Good afternoon! Do you have a prescription?
de-a1-apotheke.goal: The medicine has been bought and how to take it has been repeated back and understood correctly.

de-a1-krank-melden.scene: You are ringing your boss in the morning to say you are ill. Say what is wrong, say you cannot come in today, and say when you will be back.
de-a1-krank-melden.partner: an understanding boss who asks question after question
de-a1-krank-melden.openingTr: Good morning! You don't sound well at all. What's happened?
de-a1-krank-melden.goal: Your boss has been told what is wrong and you have agreed when you will be back.

de-a1-imperativ-du.scene: You are ringing a friend who has come down with flu. Give them advice in the informal imperative: what to drink, what to do, what not to worry about.
de-a1-imperativ-du.partner: a slightly whiny friend who is hopeless at looking after themselves
de-a1-imperativ-du.openingTr: I've got such a bad cold! Have you got any tips for me?
de-a1-imperativ-du.goal: Your friend has been given at least three pieces of advice and has said what they will do.

de-a1-notruf.scene: You have seen an accident in the street and rung the emergency number. Say what has happened and where you are, and answer the operator's questions briefly.
de-a1-notruf.partner: a calm-voiced emergency operator who guides you step by step
de-a1-notruf.openingTr: Emergency services, one one two, good afternoon. Where are you?
de-a1-notruf.goal: The place and the state of the accident have been reported and the operator has said a team is on its way.

de-a1-gesund-leben.scene: You are at the doctor's for your annual check-up and they are asking about your habits. Say what you eat and what you do, and answer the doctor's suggestions in your own words.
de-a1-gesund-leben.partner: a rather blunt but well-meaning doctor
de-a1-gesund-leben.openingTr: You say you're often tired. What do you eat every day?
de-a1-gesund-leben.goal: Your habits have been described and you have accepted one change the doctor suggested.

de-a1-beim-zahnarzt.scene: You are in the dentist's chair. Say which tooth has been hurting and for how long, and respond to the dentist's instructions.
de-a1-beim-zahnarzt.partner: a cheerful dentist who talks non-stop
de-a1-beim-zahnarzt.openingTr: Right, open your mouth, please. Where does it hurt?
de-a1-beim-zahnarzt.goal: The tooth that hurts has been found and you have been told what will be done.

de-a1-telefonieren.scene: You have rung an office and the receptionist has answered. Introduce yourself, say who you want to speak to, and say you will ring back if that person is not there.
de-a1-telefonieren.partner: a polite receptionist who speaks formally
de-a1-telefonieren.openingTr: Berger's, good afternoon. What can I do for you?
de-a1-telefonieren.goal: You have reached the person you wanted, or settled when you will ring back.

de-a1-nachricht.scene: You are texting a friend. Say when you will write, say what you will send, and end the conversation with a suitable sign-off.
de-a1-nachricht.partner: a friend who writes short and fast
de-a1-nachricht.openingTr: Hey! Are you going to text me this evening?
de-a1-nachricht.goal: When and what you will send have been settled and the exchange has ended with a goodbye.

de-a1-termin-machen.scene: You have rung a hairdressing salon and you want an appointment. Suggest a day that suits you, discuss the time, and ask to move the appointment if you need to.
de-a1-termin-machen.partner: a hairdresser with a full diary who still looks for a way
de-a1-termin-machen.openingTr: Salon Schnittpunkt, good morning. Would you like an appointment?
de-a1-termin-machen.goal: The day and time of the hairdresser's appointment have been fixed.

de-a1-einladung.scene: You are throwing a party and inviting a friend. Invite them, say when it is, and say what you would like them to bring.
de-a1-einladung.partner: a friend who loves a party and asks questions straight away
de-a1-einladung.openingTr: Oh, a party? When is it, then?
de-a1-einladung.goal: Your friend has said they are coming and it has been settled what they are bringing.

de-a1-perfekt-haben.scene: A friend is asking what you did yesterday. Say what you bought, what you saw and what you listened to; remember to put the past form at the end of every sentence.
de-a1-perfekt-haben.partner: a friend who wants to know every detail
de-a1-perfekt-haben.openingTr: Go on, what did you do yesterday?
de-a1-perfekt-haben.goal: At least three things you did yesterday have been described in the past tense.

de-a1-perfekt-sein.scene: A friend is asking where you went at the weekend. Say where you went, how you got there, and whether you stayed at home for a day.
de-a1-perfekt-sein.partner: a friend who loves travelling and keeps suggesting places
de-a1-perfekt-sein.openingTr: Where did you travel to at the weekend?
de-a1-perfekt-sein.goal: Where and how you travelled, and how you spent one of the days, have been described.

de-a1-gestern.scene: You are talking about yesterday with a friend. Tell your day in order: what you did first, where you went next, what happened in the evening.
de-a1-gestern.partner: a friend who wants to tell you about their day too
de-a1-gestern.openingTr: How was your day yesterday? What did you do first?
de-a1-gestern.goal: Yesterday morning, afternoon and evening have been told in order.

de-a1-wochenende-bericht.scene: It is Monday morning and a colleague is asking about your weekend. Say what you did on each day, say where you went, and give your verdict on how it was.
de-a1-wochenende-bericht.partner: a colleague who needs a chat on a Monday morning
de-a1-wochenende-bericht.openingTr: Good morning! How was your weekend?
de-a1-wochenende-bericht.goal: Both days of the weekend have been described and you have said how it went.

de-a1-jahreszeiten.scene: You are talking about the seasons and your birthdays with someone you have just met. Say which season you like and give the date of your birthday.
de-a1-jahreszeiten.partner: a talkative acquaintance who loves the summer
de-a1-jahreszeiten.openingTr: Which season do you like best?
de-a1-jahreszeiten.goal: The season you like and the date of your birthday have been given, and you have learnt theirs.

de-a1-a1-rueckblick.scene: An acquaintance is asking how your German is going. Say what you have learnt in the past tense, say what you can do now, and say what comes next.
de-a1-a1-rueckblick.partner: an encouraging acquaintance who is proud of you
de-a1-a1-rueckblick.openingTr: So, how's it going with your German?
de-a1-a1-rueckblick.goal: What you have learnt, what you can do now and your next goal have all been described.

de-a2-urlaub.scene: You are having a coffee with a friend who is asking about your last holiday. Say where you went with verbs of movement, and what you did there with the other auxiliary.
de-a2-urlaub.partner: a friend who loves holiday stories
de-a2-urlaub.openingTr: Hello! You were away, of course. Where did you travel to?
de-a2-urlaub.goal: Where you went on holiday, when, and what you did there have been described, and your friend has said something about their own holiday.

de-a2-perfekt-unregel.scene: You are talking about last night with a friend. You lost something, and then something unexpected happened. Use today's irregular participles as you tell it.
de-a2-perfekt-unregel.partner: a friend who listens with interest
de-a2-perfekt-unregel.openingTr: And? What did you do last night?
de-a2-perfekt-unregel.goal: Two things that happened last night have been told with irregular participles, and your friend has said something about their own evening.

de-a2-perfekt-trennbar.scene: You are doing the last check with your flatmate before going away. They ask, and you say what you have sorted out, using the participle of separable verbs.
de-a2-perfekt-trennbar.partner: a flatmate who asks everything twice
de-a2-perfekt-trennbar.openingTr: We're setting off in a minute. Have you got everything ready?
de-a2-perfekt-trennbar.goal: The door, the appliances and the preparations have been gone through one by one, and you have both decided you are ready to leave.

de-a2-gestern-abend.scene: You have run into a friend on the way home from work and they are asking about last night. Tell at least three things in order: what you did first, what happened next, what you did last.
de-a2-gestern-abend.partner: a friend who is always out in the evenings
de-a2-gestern-abend.openingTr: Tell me, what did you do last night?
de-a2-gestern-abend.goal: At least three things from last night have been told in the right order, and your friend has put their own evening in order too.

de-a2-montagmorgen.scene: You are half an hour late for work on a Monday morning. A colleague meets you at the door and asks what happened. Tell the mishaps of your morning in order.
de-a2-montagmorgen.partner: a colleague who meets you at the door
de-a2-montagmorgen.openingTr: There you are at last! What on earth happened?
de-a2-montagmorgen.goal: At least two reasons for being late have been given, and your colleague has mentioned a similar morning of their own.

de-a2-kindheit-foto.scene: You are showing a friend a childhood photo on your phone. They ask what you were like back then; describe how you looked and what you were like, in the past tense.
de-a2-kindheit-foto.partner: a friend who studies the photo and asks questions
de-a2-kindheit-foto.openingTr: Oh, is that you? How old were you back then?
de-a2-kindheit-foto.goal: How the child in the photo looked and what they were like have been described, and your friend has said something about their own childhood.

de-a2-fruher.scene: Your neighbour is much older than you and is talking about the old days. You describe the old days in your own country. Compare what there was, what there was not and what was different.
de-a2-fruher.partner: an elderly neighbour who misses the old days
de-a2-fruher.openingTr: You know, everything here used to be quite different. Was it like that where you are from too?
de-a2-fruher.goal: Then and now have been compared on at least three points, and both of you have said something about which was better.

de-a2-erste-mal.scene: You are sitting with a friend and they ask about something you did for the first time in your life. Tell what happened in order and say how you felt at the time.
de-a2-erste-mal.partner: a friend who loves listening to a story
de-a2-erste-mal.openingTr: Tell me: what do you still remember when you think of your first time?
de-a2-erste-mal.goal: A first experience has been told with both the events and the feeling, and your friend has spoken about their own first time.

de-a2-wochenbericht.scene: It is Monday morning and you are having a coffee with a colleague, summing up last week. Say what you got done, which event took place and what you did not manage.
de-a2-wochenbericht.partner: a colleague whose week was as busy as yours
de-a2-wochenbericht.openingTr: Good morning! How was your week last week?
de-a2-wochenbericht.goal: At least three of the week's jobs have been summed up, one has been marked as unfinished, and your colleague has described their own week.

de-a2-tolle-nachricht.scene: You are ringing a friend and you have good news for them. Build up the suspense first, get them guessing, then tell the news and say how it came about.
de-a2-tolle-nachricht.partner: a close friend who picks up straight away
de-a2-tolle-nachricht.openingTr: Hey! You sound excited. What's going on?
de-a2-tolle-nachricht.goal: The news has been guessed at first and then told outright, and your friend has given their reaction.

de-a2-lebensweg.scene: Someone you have just met at the language course is asking how you came to be here. Say where you came from, what was hard at first and how things are today.
de-a2-lebensweg.partner: someone you have just met on the course who has also just arrived
de-a2-lebensweg.openingTr: And you? How long have you been here?
de-a2-lebensweg.goal: Your arrival, the early difficulty and how things are today have been told in order, and the other person has spoken about their own story.

de-a2-wollte-konnte.scene: You are talking about your childhood dreams with a friend. Say what you wanted to be, why you could not, and what you had to do instead.
de-a2-wollte-konnte.partner: a friend who wants to tell you their childhood dream too
de-a2-wollte-konnte.openingTr: Tell me, what did you want to be when you were a child?
de-a2-wollte-konnte.goal: The childhood dream, the reason it did not happen and how things stand today have been described, and your friend has told you their own dream.

de-a2-schulzeit.scene: You are comparing your school years with a friend. Say what was forbidden and what was compulsory at your school, and what your teachers were like.
de-a2-schulzeit.partner: a friend who remembers their own school quite differently
de-a2-schulzeit.goal: At least one ban and one obligation have been described, the two schools have been compared and you have decided which was stricter.

de-a2-umzug-geschichte.scene: You have moved into your new place and a friend is ringing you. Talk about the flat hunt, moving day and the new place.
de-a2-umzug-geschichte.partner: a friend who is curious about your new place
de-a2-umzug-geschichte.openingTr: And? How did the move go?
de-a2-umzug-geschichte.goal: The flat hunt, moving day and the state of the new place have been described, and your friend has been invited round to see it.

de-a2-kennenlernen.scene: At a dinner someone asks how you and your closest friend met. Say where you met, what your first impression was and how things are between you today.
de-a2-kennenlernen.partner: a curious table companion you have just met
de-a2-kennenlernen.openingTr: You two have known each other a long time, haven't you? How did you meet?
de-a2-kennenlernen.goal: Where you met, the first impression and the friendship today have been described, and the other person has told their own how-we-met story.

de-a2-drei-jahre.scene: A neighbour is asking how long you have been in this city. Say when you arrived and how long you have been living here in separate sentences, then say how long you have been working.
de-a2-drei-jahre.partner: a newly arrived neighbour who wonders how long you have been here
de-a2-drei-jahre.openingTr: Have you been living here long?
de-a2-drei-jahre.goal: Both the point of arrival and the state that is still going on have been said in separate sentences, and the same question has been put back to the neighbour.

de-a2-veraenderung.scene: You have met a friend you have not seen for a long time. Say what has changed in your life in recent years, what you changed on purpose and what changed by itself.
de-a2-veraenderung.partner: an old friend who is seeing you after years
de-a2-veraenderung.openingTr: Goodness, it's been so long! What's changed with you?
de-a2-veraenderung.goal: At least two changes have been described, one marked as deliberate and one as having happened by itself, and your friend has told you their own change.

de-a2-grosseltern.scene: You are talking about childhood memories with a friend. Describe your grandparents' house: what there was, what sort of people they were and what you liked doing there.
de-a2-grosseltern.partner: a friend who describes their own grandmother's house too
de-a2-grosseltern.openingTr: Did you often stay with your grandparents as a child?
de-a2-grosseltern.goal: What was in the house, what the people were like and something you did there have been described, and your friend has told a memory of their own.

de-a2-peinlich.scene: You are sitting laughing with a friend and they ask about the most embarrassing thing that has happened to you. Tell what happened in order and say how you felt at that moment.
de-a2-peinlich.partner: a friend who is ready to tell their own embarrassing memory
de-a2-peinlich.openingTr: Go on, what really embarrassed you?
de-a2-peinlich.goal: The event has been told in order, the feeling at the time has been given, and your friend has shared a memory of their own.

de-a2-erfolg.scene: You are preparing for a job interview and a friend is doing a practice run with you. They ask what you are proud of; describe something you achieved, the work behind it and the difficulty.
de-a2-erfolg.partner: a friend doing a practice interview with you
de-a2-erfolg.openingTr: Right, first question: what are you proud of in your life?
de-a2-erfolg.goal: An achievement, the work behind it and the difficulty faced have been described, and your friend has judged the answer and made a suggestion.

de-a2-arzt.scene: You have had a cough for a week and you have gone to the doctor. Describe your symptoms, say how long it has been going on, and ask what you should do.
de-a2-arzt.partner: a GP who asks questions calmly
de-a2-arzt.openingTr: Good afternoon, do sit down. What's the trouble?
de-a2-arzt.goal: The symptoms and how long they have lasted have been described, the doctor has named a treatment and the patient has repeated it in their own words.

de-a2-symptome.scene: You are not feeling well and a colleague has noticed. Describe your symptoms one by one and say how it started.
de-a2-symptome.partner: a colleague who has noticed and is worried
de-a2-symptome.openingTr: You look pale. Aren't you feeling well?
de-a2-symptome.goal: At least two symptoms have been described with the right pattern, and your colleague has made a suggestion.

de-a2-duerfen.scene: You have come for a check-up after an operation and you want to know what you are allowed to do. Ask one by one about sport, food and work.
de-a2-duerfen.partner: a doctor who speaks plainly and answers briefly
de-a2-duerfen.openingTr: The wound looks good. Do you have any questions?
de-a2-duerfen.goal: Permission has been asked about at least three things, the doctor has allowed or forbidden each one, and the patient has repeated the bans in their own words.

de-a2-hausmittel.scene: A friend has caught a cold and is ringing you. Suggest at least two home remedies, say how to make them and say what each is good for.
de-a2-hausmittel.partner: a friend with a cold who has lost their voice
de-a2-hausmittel.openingTr: I've got a terrible cold. Have you got any tips for me?
de-a2-hausmittel.goal: At least two remedies have been suggested, one described with how it is made, and your friend has said which they will try.

de-a2-apotheke-beratung.scene: You are at the pharmacy and you want something for your cough. Ask whether you need a prescription, how often you take it and how to use it.
de-a2-apotheke-beratung.openingTr: Good afternoon! How can I help you?
de-a2-apotheke-beratung.goal: The product has been bought, the dose and the way to take it have been learnt, and the customer has repeated the instructions in their own words.

de-a2-sport-verletzung.scene: You have injured yourself doing sport and come to the emergency department. Say how it happened, what you have hurt and how it feels now.
de-a2-sport-verletzung.partner: a nurse working fast in the emergency department
de-a2-sport-verletzung.openingTr: What happened? Where does it hurt?
de-a2-sport-verletzung.goal: How the accident happened and what was injured have been described, the nurse has said the next step and the patient has repeated it.

de-a2-krankenkasse.scene: You have come to a new practice for the first time. The receptionist is asking about your insurance and your card; answer, and ask whether the appointment is free.
de-a2-krankenkasse.partner: a fast-talking receptionist at the desk
de-a2-krankenkasse.openingTr: Good afternoon. Have you been to us before? Which health insurer are you with?
de-a2-krankenkasse.goal: The insurance details have been given, any problem with the card has been mentioned and the question of cost has been settled.

de-a2-zahnarzt-termin.scene: Your tooth has been hurting all night and you are ringing the practice in the morning. Describe the pain, say how urgent it is and ask whether you can come in today.
de-a2-zahnarzt-termin.partner: a receptionist on the phone working from the appointment book
de-a2-zahnarzt-termin.openingTr: Berger dental practice, good morning. What can I do for you?
de-a2-zahnarzt-termin.goal: The pain and the urgency have been described, a time has been agreed and the patient has repeated that time.

de-a2-stress.scene: You have been going through a very stressful few weeks and you are talking to a friend. Say what is wearing you out and what helps you.
de-a2-stress.partner: a friend who listens and comes up with suggestions
de-a2-stress.openingTr: You've seemed so on edge lately. Is everything all right with you?
de-a2-stress.goal: The cause of the stress has been described, at least one way of unwinding has been discussed and you have decided to try one of them.

de-a2-vorsorge.scene: You are talking to your doctor at your annual check-up. Say what you do to stay healthy, and listen to and confirm the doctor's advice.
de-a2-vorsorge.partner: a GP who takes preventive care seriously
de-a2-vorsorge.openingTr: Your results look good. So what do you do for your health?
de-a2-vorsorge.goal: What the patient does has been described, the doctor has given at least one piece of advice and the patient has repeated it in their own words.

de-a2-dativ-geben.scene: Your neighbour is at the door and wants to borrow something. Give it to them, say when they should bring it back and add one thing they should be careful about.
de-a2-dativ-geben.partner: a neighbour who has come to the door in a hurry
de-a2-dativ-geben.openingTr: Sorry, could you lend me something for a moment?
de-a2-dativ-geben.goal: An item has been lent, a time to return it has been agreed and the neighbour has said thank you.

de-a2-wem-gehoert.scene: Some things have been left behind in the classroom after a course. You and the teacher are working out one by one whose they are.
de-a2-wem-gehoert.partner: a course teacher pointing at the things one by one
de-a2-wem-gehoert.openingTr: A few things have been left here. Whose is this?
de-a2-wem-gehoert.goal: At least three items have been talked through, one has turned out to be yours and it has been decided what happens to the rest.

de-a2-wechsel-wo.scene: Your flatmate is ringing you and wants you to describe where something they left at home is. Walk round the room and say what is where.
de-a2-wechsel-wo.partner: your flatmate, at work and asking for directions on the phone
de-a2-wechsel-wo.openingTr: Can you have a look? I can't remember where I put my glasses.
de-a2-wechsel-wo.goal: At least three places have been described, the thing being looked for has been found and where it was has been said in one clear sentence.

de-a2-wechsel-wohin.scene: You are arranging your new room with a friend. They keep asking where to put the thing in their hands; you say where it goes each time.
de-a2-wechsel-wohin.partner: a friend walking about with boxes who keeps asking
de-a2-wechsel-wohin.openingTr: I've still got the lamp here. Where shall I put it?
de-a2-wechsel-wohin.goal: Where at least three things go has been said, one has been moved afterwards and the room has been finished.

de-a2-einrichten.scene: You have moved into your new place and you and a friend are furnishing a room. Argue about what goes where; disagree over one piece and come to a decision in the end.
de-a2-einrichten.partner: a friend who wants a different arrangement from yours
de-a2-einrichten.openingTr: So, where does the desk go? By the window?
de-a2-einrichten.goal: Where at least three things go has been discussed, one disagreement has come up and a shared decision has been reached in the end.

de-a2-nachbarschaft.scene: Someone who has just moved into the area is asking you about the neighbourhood. Say what is where, where the nearest stop is and where you do your shopping.
de-a2-nachbarschaft.partner: a neighbour who has just moved into the area
de-a2-nachbarschaft.openingTr: I've just moved in. Where do you do your shopping around here?
de-a2-nachbarschaft.goal: At least three places have been described, the nearest stop has been named and the new neighbour knows where to go.

de-a2-leihen.scene: You are putting something together at home but you have not got the tool. Knock on your neighbour's door, ask for help, borrow a tool and say when you will bring it back.
de-a2-leihen.goal: Help has been asked for, a tool has been borrowed, a promise to return it has been made and thanks have been given.

de-a2-paket.scene: A parcel for your neighbour has been left at your address. Knock on their door, say you took it in, say when it came and hand it over.
de-a2-paket.partner: a surprised neighbour who has been waiting for the parcel
de-a2-paket.openingTr: Oh, hello! Do come in — has something happened?
de-a2-paket.goal: Why you have the parcel has been explained, it has been handed over and the neighbour has said thank you and offered something in return.

de-a2-laerm.scene: Your upstairs neighbour makes a lot of noise at night and you have not slept all week. Knock on their door, start politely, explain the problem and find a solution together.
de-a2-laerm.partner: an upstairs neighbour who has no idea they are making noise
de-a2-laerm.openingTr: Hello, what's the matter? Is something not right?
de-a2-laerm.goal: The problem has been raised politely, the neighbour has explained themselves and the two of you have agreed on something concrete.

de-a2-hausmeister.scene: Two things have broken at home and you are ringing the property management. Describe what is broken, say how long it has been like that and ask them to send someone.
de-a2-hausmeister.partner: a property manager taking notes on the phone
de-a2-hausmeister.openingTr: Weber property management, good afternoon. What's broken at your place?
de-a2-hausmeister.goal: Two faults have been described, a repair has been promised and the day and time have been agreed.

de-a2-neue-stelle.scene: You have found a new job and met up with a friend. Talk about how you applied, how the interview went and what the job is like.
de-a2-neue-stelle.partner: a friend who is looking for work themselves
de-a2-neue-stelle.openingTr: I hear you've got a new job. How's it going, then?
de-a2-neue-stelle.goal: The application, the interview and starting the job have been told in order, and you have given your friend a piece of advice.

de-a2-weil.scene: On the first day of the language course the teacher is asking the class why they are learning German. Give your reason in a subordinate clause and say what you find hard.
de-a2-weil.partner: a course teacher who wants to get to know the class
de-a2-weil.openingTr: Welcome! Do tell me: why are you learning German?
de-a2-weil.goal: At least two reasons have been given in subordinate clauses, one difficult point has been named and the teacher has given a piece of advice.

de-a2-denn.scene: You are stuck in traffic and you will be late for work. Ring your colleague, say how late you will be and explain why.
de-a2-denn.partner: a colleague waiting for you who will put the meeting back
de-a2-denn.openingTr: Hello? Where have you got to? We were going to start at nine.
de-a2-denn.goal: How late you will be and the reason have been given, and you and your colleague have decided what to do.

de-a2-kollegen.scene: It is your first day in your new job. A colleague is showing you round the office and introducing you to people. Introduce yourself and ask who does what.
de-a2-kollegen.partner: a helpful colleague showing you round the office
de-a2-kollegen.openingTr: Welcome to the team! Shall I show you the office first?
de-a2-kollegen.goal: You have introduced yourself, met at least two people and found out who does what.

de-a2-meeting.scene: You are in a team meeting talking about a new project. Give your opinion, make a suggestion and say whether you agree with someone else's.
de-a2-meeting.partner: a team leader chairing the meeting
de-a2-meeting.openingTr: Before we start: what do you all think about the new project?
de-a2-meeting.goal: An opinion has been given in a subordinate clause, a suggestion has been made and the team leader has reached a decision.

de-a2-telefon-arbeit.scene: The phone is ringing in the office and the person being asked for is not there. Take the call, find out who is calling and what about, take the number and say you will pass the message on.
de-a2-telefon-arbeit.partner: a customer trying to reach one of your colleagues
de-a2-telefon-arbeit.openingTr: Good afternoon, could I speak to Ms Keller, please?
de-a2-telefon-arbeit.goal: The caller's name, business and number have been taken and you have said the message will be passed on.

de-a2-pause.scene: You and a colleague are deciding where to go on your lunch break. Say what you would prefer, give your reason and choose what to eat.
de-a2-pause.partner: a colleague who is tired of going to the same place every day
de-a2-pause.openingTr: Shall we go to the canteen again, or somewhere else for once today?
de-a2-pause.goal: Where to go has been decided and you have both said what you are having.

de-a2-urlaub-antrag.scene: You want to take leave in the summer but the team is busy at that time. Give your manager the dates, say how many days you want and suggest what should happen while you are away.
de-a2-urlaub-antrag.partner: a manager looking at the holiday rota
de-a2-urlaub-antrag.openingTr: You wanted to talk about leave? When would you like to be off?
de-a2-urlaub-antrag.goal: The dates and the length of the leave have been given, one obstacle has been discussed and a date has been agreed in the end.

de-a2-krankmeldung-buero.scene: You have fallen ill in the morning and you are ringing the office to let them know. Say what is wrong, say how many days you will be off and discuss how you will send in the note.
de-a2-krankmeldung-buero.partner: someone from HR who has answered the phone
de-a2-krankmeldung-buero.openingTr: Good morning, HR department. What can I do for you?
de-a2-krankmeldung-buero.goal: The illness has been reported, the length has been given and it has been agreed when and how the note will arrive.

de-a2-feedback.scene: You are in your annual appraisal. Your manager is giving you feedback; say where you disagree and why, and put a request of your own politely.
de-a2-feedback.partner: a manager who speaks directly but listens
de-a2-feedback.openingTr: Do sit down. How has this year been for you?
de-a2-feedback.goal: The year has been reviewed, one point has been objected to with reasons, and a request has been made and answered.

de-a2-komparativ.scene: You are in an electronics shop and you cannot decide between two devices. Ask the assistant what the difference is, compare price and quality, and make a decision.
de-a2-komparativ.partner: a sales assistant who knows both products well
de-a2-komparativ.openingTr: Can I help you? Are you looking for anything in particular?
de-a2-komparativ.goal: The two products have been compared on at least two features and one has been chosen with a reason given.

de-a2-superlativ.scene: You are walking round a shopping centre with a friend. Argue about which shop is the cheapest and which is the best, and ask whether there is a sale on.
de-a2-superlativ.partner: a friend who knows every shop and loves comparing prices
de-a2-superlativ.openingTr: Where shall we go first? Where's the best value?
de-a2-superlativ.goal: At least three options have been compared in the superlative and it has been decided where to go.

de-a2-zwei-jacken.scene: You are torn between two garments in a shop and you are asking the assistant for help. Ask to try them on, compare the two and make a decision.
de-a2-zwei-jacken.partner: a sales assistant who praises both but is honest in the end
de-a2-zwei-jacken.openingTr: They both suit you. Which one do you prefer?
de-a2-zwei-jacken.goal: Both have been tried on, compared on at least two features, and one has been chosen with a reason given.

de-a2-adjektiv-ein.scene: You are looking for a garment in a particular colour and pattern. Describe what you are after, give your verdict on what you are shown, and ask for another colour or pattern.
de-a2-adjektiv-ein.partner: a sales assistant bringing different options off the shelves
de-a2-adjektiv-ein.openingTr: Good afternoon! Are you looking for anything in particular?
de-a2-adjektiv-ein.goal: The colour and pattern you wanted have been described, at least two options have been judged and one has been chosen.

de-a2-friseur.scene: You have sat down in the chair at the hairdresser's. Say what you want using comparative forms, ask for one extra service, and give your verdict on the result at the end.
de-a2-friseur.partner: a hairdresser who wants to be sure what you mean
de-a2-friseur.openingTr: Right, what are we doing today? Just a cut?
de-a2-friseur.goal: The request has been made clearly, one extra service has been discussed and a sentence has been said about the result.

de-a2-reklamation.scene: The item you bought turned out to be damaged and you have brought it back to the shop. Explain the problem, say what you want, and say you would like to speak to the manager if that is not possible.
de-a2-reklamation.partner: a till assistant who quotes the rules first but then looks for a solution
de-a2-reklamation.openingTr: Good afternoon. Would you like to return something?
de-a2-reklamation.goal: The problem has been explained, the receipt has come up and a conclusion has been reached about a refund or an exchange.

de-a2-handyvertrag.scene: You are in a phone shop and you cannot decide between two tariffs. Ask about the price, the term and what is included, compare the two and make a decision.
de-a2-handyvertrag.partner: a sales assistant who explains both tariffs
de-a2-handyvertrag.openingTr: Are you looking for a new contract? I'd be glad to show you two offers.
de-a2-handyvertrag.goal: The two tariffs have been compared on price and content and one has been chosen with a reason given.

de-a2-bank-konto.scene: You want to open an account at the bank. Say what you want, ask about the fees and the terms, and find out which documents you need.
de-a2-bank-konto.partner: a bank clerk who explains it step by step
de-a2-bank-konto.openingTr: Good afternoon! You'd like to open an account? Have you got your ID with you?
de-a2-bank-konto.goal: The type of account has been chosen, the fees have been asked about and the documents needed have been found out.

de-a2-post.scene: You want to send a parcel at the post office. Have it weighed, ask about the options, find out the fastest and the cheapest, and choose one.
de-a2-post.partner: a post office clerk listing the options
de-a2-post.openingTr: Good afternoon! Is the parcel going inland or abroad?
de-a2-post.goal: The weight and the price have been found out, at least two ways of sending have been compared and one has been chosen.

de-a2-flohmarkt.scene: You have found something that interests you on a stall at the flea market. Ask what condition it is in, find out the price, haggle politely and reach a conclusion.
de-a2-flohmarkt.partner: a stallholder who loves telling the story behind the item
de-a2-flohmarkt.openingTr: Do have a look round! Is there anything you like?
de-a2-flohmarkt.goal: The condition and the price have been discussed, a polite bit of haggling has taken place and it has been decided whether you are buying.

de-a2-reiseplan.scene: You and a friend are planning the summer holiday. Talk about where you are going, what you are travelling by and where you will stop on the way.
de-a2-reiseplan.partner: a friend with the map open who wants to plan everything
de-a2-reiseplan.openingTr: So, where are we going this year? To the sea or to the mountains?
de-a2-reiseplan.goal: The destination, the means of travel and one stop on the route have been settled.

de-a2-hotel.scene: You have arrived at a hotel and you are checking in. Give your booking, ask something about the room and find out the breakfast time.
de-a2-hotel.partner: a friendly receptionist at the front desk
de-a2-hotel.openingTr: A warm welcome! Have you booked?
de-a2-hotel.goal: The booking has been found, a question about the room has been asked and the breakfast and checkout times have been found out.

de-a2-koffer.scene: You are going away tomorrow and packing the cases. Your travelling companion is asking what has gone in; you remind them what has been forgotten.
de-a2-koffer.partner: a travelling companion who checks everything twice
de-a2-koffer.openingTr: Right, I'm nearly done. Have you packed everything?
de-a2-koffer.goal: At least three items have been gone through one by one, one has turned out to be forgotten and the case has been declared done.

de-a2-flughafen.scene: You are at the check-in desk at the airport. Give your flight, hand over your luggage, ask for a seat and ask what happens next.
de-a2-flughafen.partner: a member of staff working at the check-in desk
de-a2-flughafen.openingTr: Good afternoon, where are you flying to today?
de-a2-flughafen.goal: Check-in has been completed, the seat has been discussed and the next step and the time have been found out.

de-a2-wetterbericht.scene: You are making plans for the weekend but the weather is uncertain. Describe the forecast, make a prediction in the future tense and suggest a plan to match.
de-a2-wetterbericht.partner: a friend who plans around the weather
de-a2-wetterbericht.openingTr: What do you reckon, what will the weather be like at the weekend?
de-a2-wetterbericht.goal: The forecast has been described in the future tense and a weekend plan to match has been agreed.

de-a2-ausflug.scene: You are planning a trip for Sunday but the weather is uncertain. Suggest two separate plans: what you will do if it is fine and what if it is not.
de-a2-ausflug.partner: a friend who wants a plan for every eventuality
de-a2-ausflug.openingTr: We were going to get out on Sunday. What shall we do if it rains?
de-a2-ausflug.goal: Two conditional plans have been made, tickets or costs have been discussed and a meeting time has been settled.

de-a2-camping.scene: You have just arrived at a campsite. Ask the attendant what there is and what there is not: showers, electricity, somewhere to shop. And find out where you can light a fire.
de-a2-camping.partner: an attendant who knows the campsite rules well
de-a2-camping.openingTr: Hello there! Tent or camper van?
de-a2-camping.goal: At least three facilities have been asked about, one rule has been learnt and a pitch has been chosen.

de-a2-stadtfuehrung.scene: You are on a city tour. Ask the guide about the buildings you can see, find out the age and history of one of them, and ask what is nearby.
de-a2-stadtfuehrung.partner: a guide who enjoys telling the history of the city
de-a2-stadtfuehrung.openingTr: Here we are standing in front of the oldest building in the city. Do you have any questions?
de-a2-stadtfuehrung.goal: Questions have been asked about at least two buildings, the history of one has been given and the next stop has been found out.

de-a2-souvenirs.scene: It is the last day of your holiday and you are in a gift shop. Ask what is typical of the area, choose presents for two people and find out the prices.
de-a2-souvenirs.partner: a shop owner who recommends the local specialities
de-a2-souvenirs.openingTr: Are you looking for something to take home? Let me show you something typical.
de-a2-souvenirs.goal: Presents have been chosen for at least two people, a reason has been given for one, and the payment and the change have been discussed.

de-a2-reise-problem.scene: Your flight has been cancelled and you have decided to go on by train. Explain the situation to the clerk at the counter, buy a ticket and find out what time you arrive.
de-a2-reise-problem.partner: a clerk working at the railway ticket counter
de-a2-reise-problem.openingTr: Good afternoon. Where would you like to travel to?
de-a2-reise-problem.goal: The situation has been explained, a ticket has been bought and the arrival time and any change have been found out.

de-a2-geburtstag.scene: It is a colleague's birthday. Wish them well, ask where the celebration will be, and give the date of your own birthday.
de-a2-geburtstag.partner: a colleague who has brought a cake into the office for their birthday
de-a2-geburtstag.openingTr: Come on, have a slice of cake! Is it your birthday soon as well?
de-a2-geburtstag.goal: Birthday wishes have been given, the place and time of the celebration have been discussed and your own date has been said with an ordinal number.

de-a2-party-planen.scene: You and a friend are planning a party at home. Talk about who does what, guess who will come and work out what is missing.
de-a2-party-planen.partner: a friend with the list in hand who wants to share out the jobs
de-a2-party-planen.openingTr: Okay, we've got three days left. What do we need to get?
de-a2-party-planen.goal: At least three jobs have been shared out, who is coming has been discussed and one thing has been identified as missing.

de-a2-gastgeschenk.scene: You and a friend are going to a family dinner this evening and you are discussing what to take. Decide who gets what and plan where to buy it.
de-a2-gastgeschenk.partner: a friend who does not want to turn up empty-handed
de-a2-gastgeschenk.openingTr: We can't turn up empty-handed. What shall we bring?
de-a2-gastgeschenk.goal: At least two gift options have been discussed, one has been chosen and it has been settled where to buy it.

de-a2-hochzeit.scene: You are chatting at a wedding with the person sitting next to you. Ask who is who, give your verdict on the ceremony and propose a toast.
de-a2-hochzeit.partner: a guest from the bride's family who knows everyone
de-a2-hochzeit.openingTr: Are you on the bride's side or the groom's?
de-a2-hochzeit.goal: You have found out who at least two people are, given an opinion on the ceremony and raised a toast.

de-a2-feiertage.scene: A colleague is asking you about the celebrations in your own country. Compare a German celebration with one of your own and describe two differences.
de-a2-feiertage.partner: a colleague who is curious about other cultures
de-a2-feiertage.openingTr: How do you actually celebrate that where you are from?
de-a2-feiertage.goal: Two celebrations have been compared, at least two differences have been named and your colleague has told you about a custom of their own.

de-a2-einladung-absagen.scene: A friend has invited you out for Saturday evening but you cannot go. Turn it down politely, give your reason and suggest another date instead.
de-a2-einladung-absagen.partner: a friend who is a little hurt at being turned down but understands
de-a2-einladung-absagen.openingTr: You are coming on Saturday, aren't you?
de-a2-einladung-absagen.goal: The refusal has been given politely, the reason has been put in a subordinate clause and a new date has been agreed.

de-a2-komplimente.scene: You have run into a friend at a celebration. Pay them a compliment and let them pay you one; talk about how a compliment is answered too.
de-a2-komplimente.partner: a modest friend who deflects a compliment straight away
de-a2-komplimente.openingTr: Oh, you look really good today! Is that new?
de-a2-komplimente.goal: Both of you have paid a compliment, at least one has been answered and the conversation has moved on to something else.

de-a2-streit.scene: You had an argument with a friend yesterday and you have rung today to talk. Say what happened, apologise and suggest making up.
de-a2-streit.partner: a friend who is still a little hurt but open to talking
de-a2-streit.openingTr: Hello. I'll be honest, I'm still a bit cross. What happened yesterday?
de-a2-streit.goal: The incident has been described, an apology has been made, it has been explained that it was not deliberate and the two of you have made up.

de-a2-fernbeziehung.scene: A friend is asking about your family being far away. Say how and how often you are in touch with them, and say what you miss most.
de-a2-fernbeziehung.partner: a curious friend whose own family lives nearby
de-a2-fernbeziehung.openingTr: Your family lives so far away. How often are you in touch?
de-a2-fernbeziehung.goal: How and how often you keep in touch has been described, what you miss most has been said and your friend has made a suggestion.

de-a2-neujahr.scene: You are talking about your new year's resolutions with a friend on New Year's Eve. Give at least two goals and argue about whether one of them is realistic.
de-a2-neujahr.partner: a sceptical friend who breaks their resolutions every year
de-a2-neujahr.openingTr: And? Have you set yourself anything for this year?
de-a2-neujahr.goal: Two goals have been given, the realism of one has been argued over and you have both agreed on one resolution.

de-a2-wenn.scene: A friend is asking what you do in your free time. Describe your habits with conditional clauses: what you do if the weather is fine, what you do if you have time.
de-a2-wenn.partner: a friend who has as little free time as you
de-a2-wenn.openingTr: So what do you do when you get some time off?
de-a2-wenn.goal: At least two habits have been described with conditional clauses and your friend has told you a habit of their own.

de-a2-serien.scene: A friend is looking for something to watch. Recommend a series to them, describe the story briefly and say when you like watching.
de-a2-serien.partner: a friend who watches something every evening but cannot choose
de-a2-serien.openingTr: I just can't find anything to watch. Have you got a recommendation?
de-a2-serien.goal: A series has been recommended, its story has been described and your friend has decided whether to watch it.

de-a2-nachrichten.scene: You have heard a news story and you are telling a friend. Say where you heard it, let them meet it with doubt, and discuss together whether it is true.
de-a2-nachrichten.partner: a friend who doubts every story they hear
de-a2-nachrichten.openingTr: Tell me, have you heard that too? Is it really true?
de-a2-nachrichten.goal: The story has been passed on, its source has been named, the doubt has been voiced and it has been decided how to check it.

de-a2-social-media.scene: You and a friend are talking about how much time you spend on your phones. Say which app you use and when, and say whether you want to cut it down.
de-a2-social-media.partner: a friend who never puts their phone down
de-a2-social-media.openingTr: Look at this, my screen time — six hours. How much is yours?
de-a2-social-media.goal: The way you use it has been described with conditional clauses and an opinion has been given about cutting it down.

de-a2-warten-auf.scene: You still have not had an answer to an application and you are ringing to ask. Say what you are waiting for, say how long you have been waiting and ask when you will hear.
de-a2-warten-auf.partner: a clerk on the phone who has to look it up on the system
de-a2-warten-auf.openingTr: Good afternoon, what can I do for you?
de-a2-warten-auf.goal: What you are waiting for and how long has been said, the clerk has given a date and that date has been confirmed.

de-a2-computerproblem.scene: A friend is having a problem with their computer and has rung you. Find out what the problem is and tell them step by step what to do.
de-a2-computerproblem.partner: a friend in a panic who does not know much about computers
de-a2-computerproblem.openingTr: My computer's gone completely mad! Can you help me?
de-a2-computerproblem.goal: The problem has been understood, instructions in at least three steps have been given and it has been found out whether the problem is solved.

de-a2-fotos-teilen.scene: You are back from holiday and showing a friend the photos on your phone. Describe each photo briefly and say which one you like best.
de-a2-fotos-teilen.partner: a friend who looks at the photos and asks questions
de-a2-fotos-teilen.openingTr: Oh, show me! Where was that, then?
de-a2-fotos-teilen.goal: At least three photos have been described, the favourite has been chosen and the reason has been given.

de-a2-podcast.scene: You are recommending a podcast you listen to. Describe what it is about, say why it is worth it and ask what they are interested in.
de-a2-podcast.partner: a friend looking for something to listen to on the way
de-a2-podcast.openingTr: I need something for the journey to work. Do you listen to podcasts at all?
de-a2-podcast.goal: A podcast has been recommended, its subject and its value have been described and your friend's interests have been found out.

de-a2-online-termin.scene: You are in a formal video call and there is a problem with the sound. Report the problem, suggest a fix and settle how the meeting will carry on.
de-a2-online-termin.openingTr: Good afternoon, can you hear me all right?
de-a2-online-termin.goal: The technical problem has been reported, a fix has been tried and it has been settled how the meeting will carry on.

de-a2-digital-detox.scene: You did not turn your phone on all day and a friend is curious. Say what you did, how you felt at first and what you thought in the end.
de-a2-digital-detox.partner: a friend who wants to try the same but does not dare
de-a2-digital-detox.openingTr: Nobody could reach you yesterday. What were you doing?
de-a2-digital-detox.goal: What you did all day has been described, the feeling at the start and at the end has been given, and your friend has said whether they will try it.

de-a2-buergeramt.scene: You have moved to a new city and come to register your address. Say what you want, ask which documents are needed and find out when you will get the certificate.
de-a2-buergeramt.partner: a clerk behind the counter who asks step by step
de-a2-buergeramt.openingTr: Good afternoon. What can I do for you?
de-a2-buergeramt.goal: The registration has been requested, the documents needed have been found out and it has been settled when the certificate will be ready.

de-a2-formulare.scene: You are filling in a form at an office but you do not understand some of the fields. Ask the clerk, find out what to write and finish the form.
de-a2-formulare.partner: a clerk who explains the form line by line
de-a2-formulare.openingTr: You can fill the form in here. Is there anything you're not sure about?
de-a2-formulare.goal: At least two fields have been asked about and explained, and the form has been finished and handed in.

de-a2-verspaetet-amt.scene: You had an appointment but you have waited two hours at the office. Explain the situation to the clerk, ask what happened and find out where to send a written complaint.
de-a2-verspaetet-amt.partner: a clerk overwhelmed by the rush but still polite
de-a2-verspaetet-amt.openingTr: I'm sorry it's taken so long today. What was it you needed?
de-a2-verspaetet-amt.goal: The wait has been described, the reason has been found out and it is clear where a written complaint should go.

de-a2-bibliothek.scene: You want to join the library. Ask what is needed, find out how many books you can take and for how long, and look for a book.
de-a2-bibliothek.partner: an assistant who explains the library rules
de-a2-bibliothek.openingTr: Good afternoon! Would you like to apply for a card?
de-a2-bibliothek.goal: The joining conditions and the loan period have been found out, a book has been looked for and one rule has been confirmed.

de-a2-volkshochschule.scene: You have come to the adult education centre and you want to enrol on a course. Ask which courses they offer, find out when it starts and enrol.
de-a2-volkshochschule.partner: an adviser holding the course programme
de-a2-volkshochschule.openingTr: Good afternoon! Are you interested in a particular course?
de-a2-volkshochschule.goal: A course has been chosen, the start date and the timetable have been found out and the enrolment has been completed.

de-a2-zukunftsplaene.scene: You and a friend are talking about your plans for the coming years. Describe at least two goals in the future tense and say why one of them matters.
de-a2-zukunftsplaene.partner: a friend who describes their own plans too
de-a2-zukunftsplaene.openingTr: And where do you see yourself in five years?
de-a2-zukunftsplaene.goal: At least two goals have been described in the future tense, one has been justified and your friend has given their own plan.

de-a2-traumjob.scene: You are talking to an adviser at the job centre. Say which occupation you want and why, and ask what steps are needed.
de-a2-traumjob.partner: an adviser who guides people through choosing a career
de-a2-traumjob.openingTr: Tell me: what would you like to do for a living?
de-a2-traumjob.goal: An occupation and the reason for it have been given, the training needed has been found out and a next step has been agreed.

de-a2-deutschland-leben.scene: A German friend is asking whether you have settled in here. Describe two things you find strange and compare them with how it is in your own country.
de-a2-deutschland-leben.partner: a friend who wants to see their own country from the outside
de-a2-deutschland-leben.openingTr: Tell me honestly: what struck you most here?
de-a2-deutschland-leben.goal: At least two observations have been described in comparative form and your friend has given their own view.

de-a2-pruefung.scene: You have an exam tomorrow and you are talking to a friend. Say how you have prepared, say how nervous you are and get some advice from your friend.
de-a2-pruefung.partner: a friend who has taken the same exam and is trying to calm you down
de-a2-pruefung.openingTr: Tomorrow's the day. Are you nervous?
de-a2-pruefung.goal: The preparation has been described, the nerves have been voiced and your friend has given a concrete piece of advice.

de-a2-a2-rueckblick.scene: It is the last day of the course and your teacher is asking what you have learnt this term. Say what you have managed, what is still hard and what you will do next.
de-a2-a2-rueckblick.partner: a teacher closing the term who is proud of their student
de-a2-a2-rueckblick.openingTr: That was our last day of the course. What can you do now that you couldn't do before?
de-a2-a2-rueckblick.goal: At least two gains and one difficulty have been described and the next step has been given.

de-b1-bewerbung.scene: You are at a job interview at a company. Say why you applied with 'weil' and how long you have been working or studying with 'seit'; talk about your strengths.
de-b1-bewerbung.partner: an HR specialist, professional but warm
de-b1-bewerbung.openingTr: Good afternoon, glad you could come! Tell me: why are you applying to us?
de-b1-bewerbung.goal: Why you applied, your experience and your strengths have been described, and the interviewer has said how the process goes on.

de-b1-lebenslauf.scene: You are at a job interview and the interviewer wants you to talk through your CV. Say where you worked, when you moved on and what you were responsible for, in order.
de-b1-lebenslauf.partner: an HR specialist taking notes and asking for detail
de-b1-lebenslauf.openingTr: Please tell us briefly about your career. Where did you start?
de-b1-lebenslauf.goal: The places you worked, when you moved on and your responsibilities have been described in order.

de-b1-staerken.scene: At the interview you are asked about your strengths and weaknesses. Give a strength, describe a weakness with a reservation, and add that you are working on it.
de-b1-staerken.partner: an interviewer who asks directly but without prejudice
de-b1-staerken.openingTr: Let's come to a classic question: what are your strengths and weaknesses?
de-b1-staerken.goal: Your strength, your weakness and what you are doing about that weakness have been described.

de-b1-anschreiben.scene: At the interview you are asked why you want this job. Describe why you applied, what your goal is and what draws you to it, in clauses of purpose.
de-b1-anschreiben.partner: a department head who wants to hear reasons and is open to being convinced
de-b1-anschreiben.openingTr: Why are you applying to us in particular? What is your motivation?
de-b1-anschreiben.goal: Why you applied, your goal and what draws you to this job have been described.

de-b1-probearbeit.scene: It is your first day at work and a colleague is helping you. Ask what you do not know with the embedded question pattern, and find out who to turn to.
de-b1-probearbeit.partner: a patient colleague ready to show you anything
de-b1-probearbeit.openingTr: Welcome to the team! Do you have any questions about how things work?
de-b1-probearbeit.goal: What you did not know has been asked and you have found out who to turn to.

de-b1-arbeitszeiten.scene: You are discussing the working hours in your new job. Ask how flexitime works, find out what counts as overtime, and describe your own preference in conditional clauses.
de-b1-arbeitszeiten.partner: a team leader who explains the system in detail
de-b1-arbeitszeiten.openingTr: We have flexitime here. Do you know how that works?
de-b1-arbeitszeiten.goal: How flexitime works and what overtime is have been found out, and your own preference has been given.

de-b1-gehalt.scene: At the interview you are asked what salary you expect. Give your figure in polite forms, ask whether there is room to negotiate, and say you find it reasonable.
de-b1-gehalt.partner: an employer with a fixed budget but some flexibility
de-b1-gehalt.openingTr: Let's talk about salary. What did you have in mind?
de-b1-gehalt.goal: Your salary expectation has been given, the room to negotiate has been asked about and a range has been agreed.

de-b1-absage-bewerbung.scene: A friend is asking about the outcome of your application, and it was a rejection. Describe how the process went in order, say how you felt and say what you will do next.
de-b1-absage-bewerbung.partner: a close friend trying to keep your spirits up
de-b1-absage-bewerbung.openingTr: And? Have you had an answer to your application yet?
de-b1-absage-bewerbung.goal: How the process went has been described, how you felt has been said and your next step has been given.

de-b1-kuendigung.scene: You are telling your manager that you are resigning. Explain your reasons, say when you are leaving and ask for a written reference.
de-b1-kuendigung.partner: a manager who does not want you to go but understands
de-b1-kuendigung.openingTr: You wanted to speak to me? What is it about?
de-b1-kuendigung.goal: Your reasons for resigning have been explained, a leaving date has been settled and a written reference has been asked for.

de-b1-networking.scene: You are at a company stand at a careers fair. Introduce yourself, ask politely what the company does and whether they are recruiting, and share your contact details at the end.
de-b1-networking.partner: an energetic stand attendant who talks to a hundred people a day
de-b1-networking.openingTr: Hello! Are you interested in our company?
de-b1-networking.goal: What the company does and whether they are recruiting have been found out, and contact details have been shared.

de-b1-wohnung.scene: You are on the phone to a landlord about a flat advertisement. Ask about the flat with the patterns 'Ich würde gern …' and 'Könnten Sie …?', find out the rent and arrange a viewing.
de-b1-wohnung.partner: a slightly formal but helpful landlord
de-b1-wohnung.openingTr: Good afternoon! You're interested in the flat, is that right?
de-b1-wohnung.goal: The state of the flat and the rent have been found out and a viewing has been arranged.

de-b1-besichtigung.scene: You have come to view a flat and the landlord is showing you round. Find out about the service charges, the deposit and when you could move in, using polite question forms.
