de-b1-besichtigung.partner: a landlord seeing many applicants and weighing them up
de-b1-besichtigung.openingTr: Do come in! What would you like to know about the flat?
de-b1-besichtigung.goal: The service charges, the deposit and when you could move in have all been found out.

de-b1-mietvertrag.scene: You are going through the tenancy agreement with the landlord. Ask about the clauses you do not understand, find out about the deposit and the notice period, and make clear what you are liable for.
de-b1-mietvertrag.partner: a landlord who knows the agreement and explains it clause by clause
de-b1-mietvertrag.openingTr: Here is the tenancy agreement. Do you have questions about any of the points?
de-b1-mietvertrag.goal: The clauses you did not understand have been explained and the deposit and the notice period have been made clear.

de-b1-nachbarn-streit.scene: Your upstairs neighbour makes a lot of noise at night and you have knocked on their door. Describe the trouble in polite forms, say it without blame, and suggest a solution together.
de-b1-nachbarn-streit.partner: a neighbour who is defensive at first but comes round
de-b1-nachbarn-streit.goal: The trouble has been described without blame and a solution both sides accept has been found.

de-b1-wg.scene: You have gone to see a house share as a candidate. Say what matters to you, ask about the rules of living together and suggest a compromise on the chores.
de-b1-wg.openingTr: Good to have you here! Tell me: what matters to you about living together?
de-b1-wg.goal: What matters to you has been said, the house rules have been found out and a compromise on the chores has been reached.

de-b1-reparatur-vermieter.scene: Something at home has broken and you have rung the landlord. Describe what is broken, say in formal language that it has to be repaired and ask for a deadline.
de-b1-reparatur-vermieter.partner: a landlord inclined to put things off but open to being persuaded
de-b1-reparatur-vermieter.openingTr: Hello, Meier speaking. You called — what's the matter?
de-b1-reparatur-vermieter.goal: The fault has been reported in formal language and a deadline has been agreed.

de-b1-nebenkosten.scene: The service charge statement has come and the extra payment looks very high. Ask how it was worked out, say you find it too much and exercise your right to object.
de-b1-nebenkosten.partner: a landlord who defends the figures but is willing to show the paperwork
de-b1-nebenkosten.openingTr: You've had the statement. Is there a problem with it?
de-b1-nebenkosten.goal: How the statement was arrived at has been found out, your objection has been put and it has been said how things go on.

de-b1-einrichtung-stil.scene: A friend is furnishing their new place and asking about your taste. Say which style you like, describe the rooms with adjectives and make a suggestion.
de-b1-einrichtung-stil.partner: a friend who trusts your taste and is asking your advice
de-b1-einrichtung-stil.openingTr: I'm just redecorating. Which style do you actually like?
de-b1-einrichtung-stil.goal: The style you like has been described, the rooms have been described and a concrete suggestion has been made to your friend.

de-b1-umzugshelfer.scene: It is moving day and a friend has come to help. Split the jobs by time: what happens before you start, what they do while you do something, and what comes afterwards.
de-b1-umzugshelfer.partner: a friend who likes organising and takes responsibility
de-b1-umzugshelfer.openingTr: Right, I'm here! What do we do first?
de-b1-umzugshelfer.goal: The jobs have been shared out in time order and it has been settled what happens at the end of the day.

de-b1-untermiete.scene: You are looking for a furnished room for a year and talking to the tenant. Say how long you are staying, give your verdict on the room and make the terms clear.
de-b1-untermiete.partner: a tenant letting their room while they go abroad for a year
de-b1-untermiete.openingTr: Hello! So you're looking for a room for a while — how long for, then?
de-b1-untermiete.goal: How long you are staying, the state of the room and the terms have all been made clear.

de-b1-damit.scene: You are talking to a friend about your plans for next year: saving money, a course, a holiday. Give the aim of each plan with 'damit'; your friend will ask you 'warum?' each time.
de-b1-damit.openingTr: Hey! You said you had big plans for next year. Tell me — what are you going to do, and why?
de-b1-damit.goal: The aim of each plan has been given and your friend has said which one they are most curious about.

de-b1-um-zu.scene: A goals meeting with an adviser at a language course: say why you are learning German and why you are taking the exam with 'um … zu'; the adviser questions your plan.
de-b1-um-zu.partner: a course adviser whose questions are clear and encouraging
de-b1-um-zu.openingTr: Good afternoon! Glad you could come. First tell me: what are you actually learning German for?
de-b1-um-zu.goal: Your aim in learning German and in taking the exam has been described and the adviser has assessed your plan.

de-b1-obwohl.scene: Your friend is questioning your decision to resign from a well-paid job. Defend your decision with 'obwohl' and 'trotzdem': you are not happy, you are tired, you want something new.
de-b1-obwohl.openingTr: What? You really want to resign? But the salary is great. Why, then?
de-b1-obwohl.goal: Your decision to resign has been defended in clauses of contrast and your friend has understood it.

de-b1-als-wenn.scene: A new acquaintance is asking about your childhood. Tell one-off memories with 'als' and repeated habits with 'immer wenn'.
de-b1-als-wenn.partner: an acquaintance who listens with interest and asks questions
de-b1-als-wenn.openingTr: So you grew up in Izmir? What was your childhood like there? Tell me about those days.
de-b1-als-wenn.goal: Your one-off memories and your repeated habits have each been told separately.

de-b1-nachdem.scene: Someone you met at an integration course is asking how you came to Germany. Tell the events in order: 'Nachdem … hatte, …', 'Zuerst …, danach …'.
de-b1-nachdem.partner: a curious fellow student who shares their own story too
de-b1-nachdem.openingTr: I came two years ago. And you — how was it for you? What did you do first, after you had arrived?
de-b1-nachdem.goal: The story of how you came here has been told event by event, in the right order.

de-b1-bevor-waehrend.scene: You are planning a cinema evening with a friend: dinner before the film, tickets, the rules during the film, then a café. Put it in order with 'bevor' and 'während'.
de-b1-bevor-waehrend.partner: a practical friend who likes making plans
de-b1-bevor-waehrend.openingTr: So, cinema at eight. What are we doing before that — shall we eat something before the film starts?
de-b1-bevor-waehrend.goal: A plan has been put in order for before the film, during the film and afterwards.

de-b1-deshalb-trotzdem.scene: You are explaining to your boss why you were late for the meeting: the reason (denn/deshalb), what you got done all the same (trotzdem), and what you will do from now on.
de-b1-deshalb-trotzdem.partner: a manager who is serious but fair
de-b1-deshalb-trotzdem.openingTr: You're twenty minutes late. What happened?
de-b1-deshalb-trotzdem.goal: The reason for being late, what you got done all the same and the step you will take from now on have all been given.

de-b1-je-desto.scene: Someone just starting to learn German is asking you for advice. Give at least three tips with 'je … desto'; the other person will ask 'stimmt das wirklich?' about each one.
de-b1-je-desto.partner: a beginner who is a little anxious
de-b1-je-desto.openingTr: You speak so well already! I'm only just starting. Have you got any tips for me?
de-b1-je-desto.goal: At least three tips have been given and the other person has said which one they will try.

de-b1-entweder-oder.scene: A weekend plan with a friend: deciding between two options (entweder…oder), doing both (sowohl…als auch), and what you do not want to do (weder…noch).
de-b1-entweder-oder.partner: an indecisive friend who keeps producing options
de-b1-entweder-oder.openingTr: Saturday: hiking or the museum? Or both? I can't decide — what do you think?
de-b1-entweder-oder.goal: The options for the weekend have been weighed up and a single plan has been agreed.

de-b1-geschichte.scene: Tell a friend a small thing that happened to you (being late, losing something, a surprise) from start to finish: zuerst, nachdem, während, plötzlich, deshalb, am Ende.
de-b1-geschichte.partner: a friend who wants the detail and keeps asking 'und dann?'
de-b1-geschichte.openingTr: You look like something's happened to you. Tell me from the beginning — what happened?
de-b1-geschichte.goal: The event has been told from start to finish in order and how it ended has been said.

de-b1-relativ-nom.scene: You are in a new workplace and an acquaintance is asking about the team. Introduce each colleague with a relative clause built on 'der/die/das': who does what, and what they are like.
de-b1-relativ-nom.partner: a curious acquaintance who enjoys a chat
de-b1-relativ-nom.openingTr: So, what are the people in your new team like? Who stood out on your first day?
de-b1-relativ-nom.goal: At least three people on the team have been introduced and your acquaintance can tell who is who.

de-b1-relativ-akk.scene: A friend is looking for a film for the evening. Recommend films and series you like with relative clauses built on 'den/die/das' and say why you like them.
de-b1-relativ-akk.openingTr: I need a film for this evening. What have you watched lately that was really worth it?
de-b1-relativ-akk.goal: At least two things have been recommended and your friend has decided what to watch this evening.

de-b1-relativ-dativ.scene: You are talking to a friend about trust: who you trust, whose advice you listen to, who you tell everything, in relative clauses built on 'dem, der, denen'.
de-b1-relativ-dativ.partner: a plain-spoken friend who makes you think
de-b1-relativ-dativ.openingTr: Be honest: is there anyone you can really tell everything to?
de-b1-relativ-dativ.goal: Who you trust and whose advice you listen to have been described, and your friend has given their own answer.

de-b1-relativ-praep.scene: Someone who has just moved to the city is asking about your area. Describe the district you live in, the place you grew up and the places nearby, with relative clauses after a preposition.
de-b1-relativ-praep.partner: a new neighbour who knows nothing about the city and asks about everything
de-b1-relativ-praep.openingTr: I've just moved here and I don't know anything yet. Which district do you live in?
de-b1-relativ-praep.goal: The district you live in, where you grew up and the places nearby have all been described.

de-b1-traumhaus.scene: You are sitting with an estate agent and describing the house of your dreams: what sort of house, in what surroundings, what your budget is. Build the descriptions with relative clauses.
de-b1-traumhaus.partner: a slightly hurried estate agent who asks realistic questions
de-b1-traumhaus.openingTr: Just tell me: what sort of house are you actually looking for, and where should it be?
de-b1-traumhaus.goal: The features of your dream house, its surroundings and your budget have been made clear, and the agent has made a suggestion.

de-b1-menschen-beschreiben.scene: In an interview you are asked about the people who left a mark on your life. Describe each one with a relative clause: what they were like, what they did, what they gave you.
de-b1-menschen-beschreiben.partner: a calm interviewer who knows how to listen
de-b1-menschen-beschreiben.openingTr: Looking back: who are the people who shaped you most?
de-b1-menschen-beschreiben.goal: At least two people who left a mark on your life have been described, along with what they gave you.

de-b1-gegenstand.scene: You are in an electronics shop and you do not know the name of the part you want. Describe what it does and what it looks like with relative clauses; let the assistant narrow it down with questions.
de-b1-gegenstand.partner: a patient assistant who asks a lot of questions
de-b1-gegenstand.openingTr: Good afternoon! You're looking for something but you don't know the name — no problem. What do you need the part for?
de-b1-gegenstand.goal: The part you wanted has been found by describing it, or an alternative has been suggested.

de-b1-lieblingsort.scene: A friend is tired and looking for a place that will do them good. Describe your favourite place with relative clauses: where it is, what you do there, why it helps.
de-b1-lieblingsort.openingTr: I'm completely worn out. Is there a place where you can really switch off?
de-b1-lieblingsort.goal: Your favourite place has been described and your friend has decided to go there.

de-b1-fundbuero.scene: You are at the lost property office. Describe what you lost with relative clauses: what it looks like, what make it is, what was inside, where you lost it.
de-b1-fundbuero.partner: a clerk who speaks formally and wants the detail
de-b1-fundbuero.openingTr: Good afternoon. What exactly have you lost, and where might it have happened?
de-b1-fundbuero.goal: Your item has been described, you have found out whether it has been handed in and you have been told what happens next.

de-b1-rezept-empfehlen.scene: A friend has guests coming this evening and does not know what to cook. Suggest a dish: describe the dish, the ingredients and the side with relative clauses.
de-b1-rezept-empfehlen.partner: a flustered friend who is a beginner in the kitchen
de-b1-rezept-empfehlen.openingTr: I've got guests coming this evening and I've no idea. Do you know a dish that's quick and still good?
de-b1-rezept-empfehlen.goal: A dish has been suggested, its ingredients and side have been given, and your friend has decided to make it.

de-b1-passiv.scene: You are asking a worker in front of the building site in your area: what is being built, when it will be finished, which roads are closed. Put your questions and what you understand in the passive.
de-b1-passiv.partner: a hurried but well-informed site worker
de-b1-passiv.openingTr: You'll be wanting to know what's going on here. What exactly would you like to find out?
de-b1-passiv.goal: What is being built, when it will be finished and which road is closed have all been found out.

de-b1-passiv-vergangen.scene: A friend is asking what happened to your application. Describe every step of the process in the past passive: when it was submitted, what was checked, what was decided.
de-b1-passiv-vergangen.openingTr: And? Have you finally had an answer? What happened with your application?
de-b1-passiv-vergangen.goal: The application process has been described step by step and the outcome has been given.

de-b1-auslaenderbehoerde.scene: You are talking to an official at the immigration office about extending your residence permit. Ask which documents are needed, say when your permit runs out and find out how long it takes.
de-b1-auslaenderbehoerde.partner: an official who speaks formally, clearly and helpfully
de-b1-auslaenderbehoerde.openingTr: Good afternoon. You have an appointment about an extension — what is it about exactly?
de-b1-auslaenderbehoerde.goal: The documents needed have been found out, the expiry date of the permit has been given and the processing time has been said.

de-b1-widerspruch.scene: At an advice centre you are describing to the adviser the decision you want to appeal against: which decision, why you think it is unfair, what you are going to ask for. Put your requests in a 'dass' clause.
de-b1-widerspruch.partner: a calm adviser who works through it step by step
de-b1-widerspruch.openingTr: Do sit down. So you want to lodge an appeal — against which decision exactly?
de-b1-widerspruch.goal: The decision to be appealed against, your reasons and what you will ask for have all been made clear.

de-b1-fuehrerschein.scene: You are asking for advice at a driving school: what steps the process goes through, how many lessons are needed, how long it takes. Sum up what you understood in the passive.
de-b1-fuehrerschein.partner: an experienced course adviser who talks fast
de-b1-fuehrerschein.openingTr: Welcome! You'd like to take your driving test — have you ever been to a driving school before?
de-b1-fuehrerschein.goal: The steps of the process, the number of lessons needed and how long it takes have all been found out.

de-b1-steuer.scene: You are discussing your tax return with an accountant: which costs you can claim, which documents are needed, when the refund comes. Describe the steps of the process in the passive.
de-b1-steuer.partner: a meticulous accountant who talks in figures
de-b1-steuer.openingTr: Good afternoon. Let's get your tax return out of the way — what have you got ready?
de-b1-steuer.goal: Which costs you can claim, the documents needed and when the refund comes have all been found out.

de-b1-versicherung.scene: You are ringing the insurance company to report some damage: what happened, when it happened, what you did afterwards. Put the earlier event one step further back as you order it.
de-b1-versicherung.partner: a calm insurance clerk who asks the questions in order
de-b1-versicherung.openingTr: Nordstern Insurance, good afternoon. You'd like to report some damage — what exactly happened?
de-b1-versicherung.goal: The damage has been reported in order and you have been told what happens next.

de-b1-termin-verschieben.scene: You are ringing the office to move your appointment: give the reason briefly, ask for a new date, ask for the confirmation in writing. Put your requests in the subjunctive.
de-b1-termin-verschieben.partner: an appointments clerk who sticks to the rules but will bend them
de-b1-termin-verschieben.openingTr: Registration office, good afternoon. You'd like to change your appointment? Which appointment is it about?
de-b1-termin-verschieben.goal: The reason for moving it has been given, a new date has been taken and it has been settled that the confirmation will come in writing.

de-b1-vollmacht.scene: You are at the enquiries desk to give power of attorney to a relative: say who may do what and until when, and ask which documents are needed.
de-b1-vollmacht.partner: an enquiries clerk who speaks briefly and clearly
de-b1-vollmacht.openingTr: Good afternoon. You'd like to make out a power of attorney — who is to represent you?
de-b1-vollmacht.goal: Who may do what and until when has been made clear and the documents needed have been found out.

de-b1-einbuergerung.scene: You are sitting with a citizenship adviser and asking what you do not know: which conditions apply, when the test is, which documents are needed. Put your questions indirectly.
de-b1-einbuergerung.partner: a well-informed citizenship adviser who gives detail
de-b1-einbuergerung.openingTr: Glad you could come. You're interested in citizenship — what would you like to know first?
de-b1-einbuergerung.goal: The conditions required, the date of the test and the documents needed have all been found out.

de-b1-infinitiv-zu.scene: You are talking to a friend about your plans for the year: what you intend to learn, which habit you want to build, what you will give up. Describe your plans with the zu infinitive.
de-b1-infinitiv-zu.partner: a friend who takes your plans seriously and asks questions
de-b1-infinitiv-zu.openingTr: You said this year was going to be different. So what have you set yourself?
de-b1-infinitiv-zu.goal: What you intend to learn, which habit you will build and what you will give up have all been described.

de-b1-lernziele.scene: You are having a goals meeting with a course adviser: what you want to achieve in what time, what your intermediate steps are, how you will measure progress.
de-b1-lernziele.partner: a course adviser who wants concrete numbers
de-b1-lernziele.openingTr: Before we pick a course: what exactly do you want to achieve in the next six months?
de-b1-lernziele.goal: The timescale, the goal and the intermediate steps have been made clear, and it has been settled how progress will be measured.

de-b1-sprachkurs.scene: You are at the office of a language school: compare the intensive course with the evening course, ask about the price, the pace and the group size, then choose one with your reasons.
de-b1-sprachkurs.partner: an honest course secretary who knows both courses well
de-b1-sprachkurs.openingTr: We have two courses that would suit you. What would you like to decide on?
de-b1-sprachkurs.goal: The two courses have been compared and one has been chosen with reasons.

de-b1-pruefung-b1.scene: You are talking to your teacher before the exam: say what you are apprehensive about, which part you find hard and what you will do if it happens. Build your sentences with conditional clauses.
de-b1-pruefung-b1.partner: a teacher who calms you down and gives concrete advice
de-b1-pruefung-b1.openingTr: You seem tense. What do you have most respect for in the exam?
de-b1-pruefung-b1.goal: The part you are apprehensive about has been named, what you will do if it happens has been discussed and a strategy has been agreed.

de-b1-weiterbildung.scene: You are discussing a request for training with your boss: say why you want it in clauses of purpose, say what the company gains, and discuss the funding and the working arrangements.
de-b1-weiterbildung.partner: a boss who thinks about the budget but keeps an open mind
de-b1-weiterbildung.openingTr: You wanted to talk about some training. What exactly do you need it for?
de-b1-weiterbildung.goal: The aim of the training, what the company gains and the funding have been discussed, and your boss has given an answer.

de-b1-studium.scene: You are at the university's student advice service: ask about the application deadline, the documents needed and which course would suit you. Put your questions indirectly.
de-b1-studium.partner: a practical student adviser who has talked to a great many students
de-b1-studium.openingTr: Do sit down. You're interested in studying with us — what would you like to clear up first?
de-b1-studium.goal: The application deadline, the documents needed and the course that suits you have all been found out.

de-b1-praktikum.scene: At a job interview you are describing your internship: which company, how long it lasted, what work you did, what you got out of it. Tell it in the past tense of written German.
de-b1-praktikum.partner: an HR specialist taking notes and asking for detail
de-b1-praktikum.openingTr: There's an internship on your CV. Do tell us briefly: what did you do there?
de-b1-praktikum.goal: Where the internship was, how long it lasted, the work you did and what you got out of it have all been described.

de-b1-lernmethoden.scene: You and a fellow student are comparing how you learn: what you study and how, what works, what does not. Say two things at once with paired conjunctions.
de-b1-lernmethoden.partner: a curious fellow student who defends their own method
de-b1-lernmethoden.openingTr: Tell me, how do you actually learn? My method isn't getting me anywhere at the moment.
de-b1-lernmethoden.goal: Your two methods have been compared and you have decided to try something from each other.

de-b1-fehlerkultur.scene: You are talking to a friend about the fear of making mistakes: why you hold back when you speak, what you carry on in spite of, how you take your mistakes. Build clauses of contrast.
de-b1-fehlerkultur.partner: a reassuring friend who talks about their own mistakes freely
de-b1-fehlerkultur.openingTr: You hardly say a thing in class, even though you know a lot. What's holding you back?
de-b1-fehlerkultur.goal: The reason for holding back has been described and what you will carry on in spite of has been said.

de-b1-mentor.scene: You are discussing a career decision with your mentor: describe your options, ask what they would do, ask for feedback. Build the exchange of advice in the subjunctive.
de-b1-mentor.partner: an experienced mentor who speaks directly
de-b1-mentor.openingTr: So you're facing a decision. Tell me what options you can see — what would you most like to do?
de-b1-mentor.goal: The options have been described, your mentor's view has been heard and a next step has been settled.

de-b1-meinung.scene: You are discussing a new decision in the city with an acquaintance: restricting cars in the centre. Give your opinion, justify it, and separate the points you agree with from the ones you do not.
de-b1-meinung.partner: an acquaintance who defends their own view and enjoys an argument
de-b1-meinung.openingTr: Have you heard? Cars are going to be banned from the city centre soon. What do you make of that?
de-b1-meinung.goal: Your opinion has been given with reasons and the points you agree and disagree with have been separated.

de-b1-pro-contra.scene: A friend is thinking of moving out of the city and is asking what you think. Set the pros and cons side by side with paired conjunctions, and say at the end which weighs more.
de-b1-pro-contra.partner: an undecided friend who wants to hear both sides
de-b1-pro-contra.openingTr: We're thinking of moving to the country. Be honest: what's for it and what's against it?
de-b1-pro-contra.goal: The pros and cons have been weighed up and it has been said which weighs more.

de-b1-diskussion-hoeflich.scene: In a meeting you disagree with a colleague's proposal. First show that you have understood them, then put your reservation in soft forms, and suggest a compromise at the end.
de-b1-diskussion-hoeflich.partner: a reasonable colleague who is attached to their proposal
de-b1-diskussion-hoeflich.openingTr: I suggest we put the project back by three months. How do you see it?
de-b1-diskussion-hoeflich.goal: The other side has been shown to be understood, the reservation has been put and a compromise has been suggested.

de-b1-medienkonsum.scene: At a parents' evening you are discussing children's screen time: how much you think is right, what it depends on, how it should be limited. Build your opinion with fixed-preposition verbs.
de-b1-medienkonsum.partner: an anxious parent who wants firm rules
de-b1-medienkonsum.openingTr: Two hours a day — that's far too much for a child. Do you see it that way too?
de-b1-medienkonsum.goal: How much is right, what it depends on and how it should be limited have all been discussed.

de-b1-fake-news.scene: An acquaintance is telling you a surprising piece of news. Question the claim: find out where it came from, who said it and whether it has been confirmed, with indirect questions.
de-b1-fake-news.partner: an excitable acquaintance who believes what they hear straight away
de-b1-fake-news.openingTr: Have you read this? From next year it's supposedly going to be banned completely. Did you know that?
de-b1-fake-news.goal: The source of the claim has been questioned and it has been made clear whether it has been confirmed.

de-b1-serienabend.scene: You and a friend are arguing about the finale of the series you watched: what you liked, what you liked it in spite of, what ending you would have expected. Build clauses of contrast and expectation.
de-b1-serienabend.partner: a friend who loved the finale and is trying to win you over
de-b1-serienabend.openingTr: Well I thought the finale was superb. But you pulled such a face — what didn't you like?
de-b1-serienabend.goal: What you liked and disliked about the finale has been said and the ending you expected has been described.

de-b1-buchclub.scene: At the book club you are discussing the book you read: which part moved you, where it was heavy going, who you would recommend it to. Describe the book with relative clauses.
de-b1-buchclub.partner: a club member who gave up halfway and wants to be persuaded
de-b1-buchclub.openingTr: I got stuck on page eighty. Is it really worth reading on?
de-b1-buchclub.goal: The moving and the heavy parts of the book have been described and it has been said who it is for.

de-b1-musikgeschmack.scene: You and a friend are arguing about your taste in music: which is better, why, what matters more to you. Compare, and close the argument politely.
de-b1-musikgeschmack.partner: a jokey friend who defends their own music
de-b1-musikgeschmack.openingTr: How can you listen to that? It's the same rhythm all the way through. What do you see in it?
de-b1-musikgeschmack.goal: Your tastes have been compared and the argument has been closed politely.

de-b1-kunstausstellung.scene: You have come out of an exhibition and you are telling a friend about it: which work stayed with you, what it reminded you of, how it made you feel. Build it with fixed-preposition verbs.
de-b1-kunstausstellung.partner: a curious friend who does not know much about art
de-b1-kunstausstellung.openingTr: So, how was the exhibition? I don't understand much about art — what stayed with you?
de-b1-kunstausstellung.goal: The work that stayed with you, what it called to mind and how it made you feel have all been described.

de-b1-debatte-kurz.scene: You are in a short debate: the subject is shops opening at the weekend. Give your view, line up your reasons and close your turn with a summary.
de-b1-debatte-kurz.partner: a debating opponent who argues the other side and keeps the time
de-b1-debatte-kurz.openingTr: Two minutes each. I'll start: shops should stay shut on Sundays. What do you say to that?
de-b1-debatte-kurz.goal: Your view has been given, at least two reasons have been lined up and the turn has been closed with a summary.

de-b1-hausarzt.scene: You are at the GP's describing a complaint that has gone on for months: since when, when it gets worse, what it might be connected with. Describe it with fixed-preposition verbs.
de-b1-hausarzt.partner: a GP who takes their time and asks for detail
de-b1-hausarzt.openingTr: Do sit down. You said on the phone it's been going on a while — since when exactly?
de-b1-hausarzt.goal: How long the complaint has lasted and what it might be connected with have been described, and the doctor has said the next step.

de-b1-facharzt.scene: You are ringing a specialist's practice: say you have a referral, ask for an appointment, and ask about the waiting time and what you need to bring.
de-b1-facharzt.partner: a receptionist with a full appointment book who talks fast on the phone
de-b1-facharzt.openingTr: Dr Ahrens' practice, good afternoon. Do you have a referral from your GP?
de-b1-facharzt.goal: An appointment has been made and the waiting time and what to bring have been found out.

de-b1-apotheke-b1.scene: You are asking for advice at the pharmacy: say which medicines you are already taking, ask whether the new one can be taken with them, ask about the dose and the timing. Put your questions in conditional clauses.
de-b1-apotheke-b1.partner: a careful pharmacist who checks the leaflet
de-b1-apotheke-b1.openingTr: Good afternoon. Before I give you this: are you taking any other medicines at the moment?
de-b1-apotheke-b1.goal: The medicines you take have been given, the interaction has been asked about and the dose and timing have been made clear.

de-b1-ernaehrung.scene: You are talking to a nutritionist: how you eat, what you are trying to change, what you find hard. Build your sentences with infinitive phrases.
de-b1-ernaehrung.partner: a nutritionist who does not judge and gives concrete suggestions
de-b1-ernaehrung.openingTr: Just tell me about an ordinary day: what do you eat in the morning, at midday, in the evening?
de-b1-ernaehrung.goal: How you eat has been described, along with what you are trying to change and what you find hard.

de-b1-rueckenschmerz.scene: You are discussing your back pain with a physiotherapist: when it starts, how you sit during the day, what they recommend. Discuss the advice in the subjunctive.
de-b1-rueckenschmerz.partner: a physiotherapist who gives practical advice and gets you moving
de-b1-rueckenschmerz.openingTr: Show me how you sit at your desk. When does it hurt most?
de-b1-rueckenschmerz.goal: When the pain started and how you sit have been described, and a concrete suggestion has been taken away.

de-b1-schlaf.scene: You are talking to a sleep consultant: your habits before bed, what happens in the night, how you wake in the morning. Describe the order with bevor and während.
de-b1-schlaf.partner: a sleep consultant who asks about the daily routine step by step
de-b1-schlaf.openingTr: Please describe your evening to me: what do you do in the two hours before you go to bed?
de-b1-schlaf.goal: Your habits before bed, what happens in the night and how you wake in the morning have all been described.

de-b1-psychische-gesundheit.scene: You are telling a friend you trust that you have been struggling lately: what is weighing on you, when it started, what helps. Build it with fixed-preposition verbs.
de-b1-psychische-gesundheit.partner: a friend who knows how to listen and does not rush you
de-b1-psychische-gesundheit.openingTr: You've seemed different for a few weeks. Do you want to tell me what's going on?
de-b1-psychische-gesundheit.goal: What is weighing on you and when it started have been described, and what helps has been discussed.

de-b1-notaufnahme.scene: You are telling the nurse at the emergency department what happened: what happened, in what order, and where it hurts now. Order it by pulling the earlier event back.
de-b1-notaufnahme.partner: an emergency nurse who asks quick, clear questions
de-b1-notaufnahme.openingTr: Just stay sitting quietly. Tell me briefly: what happened and when was that?
de-b1-notaufnahme.goal: What happened has been told in order and where it hurts now has been said.

de-b1-impfung.scene: You are at your vaccination appointment: ask what you need to bring, about the possible side effects and when the booster is due. Repeat the passive sentences you hear in your own words.
de-b1-impfung.partner: a practice worker who speaks briefly and clearly
de-b1-impfung.openingTr: Good afternoon. Have you got your vaccination card with you? Then we'll see what's being done today.
de-b1-impfung.goal: What you need to bring, the possible side effects and the timing of the booster have all been found out.

de-b1-krankenhaus-besuch.scene: You are visiting a relative in hospital: ask how they are, offer help, cheer them up. Soften your offers with the subjunctive.
de-b1-krankenhaus-besuch.partner: a relative who is tired but wants to talk
de-b1-krankenhaus-besuch.openingTr: How lovely that you're here. Sit down — and tell me something from outside, will you?
de-b1-krankenhaus-besuch.goal: How they are has been asked, help has been offered and their spirits have been lifted.

de-b1-muelltrennung.scene: You are asking a neighbour about the rubbish rules in the building you have just moved into: which rubbish goes in which bin, how the deposit is claimed back, which day it is collected.
de-b1-muelltrennung.partner: a slightly meticulous neighbour who knows the rules well
de-b1-muelltrennung.openingTr: You're new here, aren't you? Everyone gets the rubbish wrong at first — what would you like to know?
de-b1-muelltrennung.goal: Which rubbish goes where and how the deposit is claimed back have both been found out.

de-b1-energie-sparen.scene: You are discussing the rising electricity bill with your flatmate: what you suggest changing and why. Give the aim of your suggestions with um … zu.
de-b1-energie-sparen.partner: a flatmate who likes their comfort and is wary of saving
de-b1-energie-sparen.openingTr: The electricity bill has got really high. But I don't want to sit in the dark — what do you suggest?
de-b1-energie-sparen.goal: At least two suggestions have been made along with their aim, and one has been agreed on.

de-b1-verkehrswende.scene: You are arguing with a colleague about how to get to work: by car, by bike or by public transport. Set both sides out with paired conjunctions and justify your own choice.
de-b1-verkehrswende.partner: a practical colleague who is attached to their car
de-b1-verkehrswende.openingTr: You cycle every day now? In this weather? Well, I'm sticking with the car — go on, convince me.
de-b1-verkehrswende.goal: The pros and cons of both sides have been given and your own choice has been defended with reasons.

de-b1-nachhaltig-einkaufen.scene: You and a friend are talking about your shopping habits: which products you go for, which shops you go to, why. Describe your choices with relative clauses.
de-b1-nachhaltig-einkaufen.partner: a friend who watches the price but is open to persuasion
de-b1-nachhaltig-einkaufen.openingTr: You only shop at the packaging-free shop now? Isn't that much more expensive? Do tell.
de-b1-nachhaltig-einkaufen.goal: Which products and shops you go for has been described along with your reasons.

de-b1-garten-projekt.scene: You are explaining the rules to someone who wants to join the community garden: when the work happens, how the harvest is shared, who is responsible for what. Give the rules in passive sentences.
de-b1-garten-projekt.partner: an eager new member who knows nothing at all
de-b1-garten-projekt.openingTr: I'd love to join in. How does it actually work here — do you have to come every week?
de-b1-garten-projekt.goal: The work day, the sharing of the harvest and the responsibilities have been described, and the new member has said what they have decided.

de-b1-wetterextrem.scene: You are talking to a neighbour about how the weather has changed: how it used to be, how it is now, what you notice. Describe the change with comparative forms.
de-b1-wetterextrem.partner: a long-standing neighbour who likes comparing the years
de-b1-wetterextrem.openingTr: We never used to have a summer like this. Do you notice it too, or am I imagining it?
de-b1-wetterextrem.goal: Then and now have been compared and what you have noticed has been described.

de-b1-ehrenamt.scene: You are at an introductory meeting at a voluntary organisation: say why you want to volunteer, how much time you have a week and what you could do.
de-b1-ehrenamt.partner: a warm but realistic volunteer coordinator
de-b1-ehrenamt.openingTr: Glad you could come. First tell me: why do you want to get involved with us?
de-b1-ehrenamt.goal: Your reason for volunteering, the time you can give and what you could do have all been described.

de-b1-stadtentwicklung.scene: You are talking about the changes with someone who has lived in the area a long time: what has been done up, what has closed, what has happened to the rents, who has left. Describe the change in the past passive.
de-b1-stadtentwicklung.partner: a resident who resents the change and misses the old area
de-b1-stadtentwicklung.openingTr: You should have seen this neighbourhood ten years ago. Do you know what's disappeared from here?
de-b1-stadtentwicklung.goal: What has been done up, what has closed and what has happened to the rents have all been discussed.

de-b1-demo.scene: A journalist is talking to you at a demonstration: why you are here, what you are demanding, what you want changed. Give your aim in damit clauses.
de-b1-demo.partner: a local journalist who wants short, clear answers
de-b1-demo.openingTr: Excuse me, briefly for our paper: why are you here today?
de-b1-demo.goal: Why you are there and what you are demanding have been said, and what you want changed has been described.

de-b1-tierheim.scene: You are talking to a worker at the animal shelter: which animal you could look after, what sort of home is needed, what the daily responsibility is. Describe the animals with relative clauses.
de-b1-tierheim.partner: an honest shelter worker who knows the animals very well
de-b1-tierheim.openingTr: Come with me, I'll show you the animals. Are you looking for an animal for yourself or for the family?
de-b1-tierheim.goal: Which animal you could look after, what sort of home is needed and the daily responsibility have all been discussed.

de-b1-irreal.scene: You and a friend are playing a 'what if' game: what you would do if you were rich, where you would live, what you would not change. Build your answers with unreal conditional clauses.
de-b1-irreal.partner: a friend who loves daydreaming and keeps producing questions
de-b1-irreal.openingTr: Imagine you win a million tomorrow. What would you do first?
de-b1-irreal.goal: What you would do if you were rich, where you would live and what you would not change have all been said.

de-b1-wuensche.scene: You and a friend are sharing your wishes: what you would ask for if you had three wishes, which wish has still not come true. Build your answers in the subjunctive.
de-b1-wuensche.partner: a warm friend who tells you their own wishes too
de-b1-wuensche.openingTr: If you had three wishes free — but honestly, no millions: what would your three be?
de-b1-wuensche.goal: Three wishes have been given and it has been said which one has still not come true.

de-b1-vergangen-bereuen.scene: You are telling a friend about a decision you made in the past: what had happened, what you should have done looking back, whether you regret it now. Use the patterns of regret.
de-b1-vergangen-bereuen.partner: a friend who does not judge and tells you their own regrets
de-b1-vergangen-bereuen.openingTr: You said the other day you still think about that business a lot. What would you have done differently?
de-b1-vergangen-bereuen.goal: The decision has been described, what you should have done looking back has been said and how you see it today has been given.

de-b1-zukunftsangst.scene: You are talking to someone close about your fears for the future: what you are afraid will go wrong, what you would do in the worst case, what reassures you.
de-b1-zukunftsangst.partner: someone close who calms you down and makes you think with questions
de-b1-zukunftsangst.openingTr: You've seemed on edge since the decision came up. What's the worst possibility you're thinking of?
de-b1-zukunftsangst.goal: The fear has been named, what you would do in the worst case has been said and what reassures you has been discussed.

de-b1-freundschaft-pflegen.scene: You have run into an old friend after years: what has happened in between, why the friendship lapsed, how things are now. Order it by pulling the earlier event back.
de-b1-freundschaft-pflegen.partner: a talkative old friend who is sorry to have lost touch
de-b1-freundschaft-pflegen.openingTr: I don't believe it — how long has it been? Tell me, what's been happening with you?
de-b1-freundschaft-pflegen.goal: What happened in between has been described, the reason for the lapse has been discussed and you have promised to meet again.

de-b1-liebeserklaerung.scene: You are telling someone you have been friends with for a long time how you feel: what you feel, what you are suggesting, and that you want to keep the friendship whatever the answer. Soften your sentences with the subjunctive.
de-b1-liebeserklaerung.partner: a surprised but warm friend who asks for time to think
de-b1-liebeserklaerung.openingTr: You wanted to talk about something and you look so serious. Now I'm curious — what is it?
de-b1-liebeserklaerung.goal: Your feeling has been said, an offer has been made and it has been made clear that the friendship will go on whatever the answer.

de-b1-konflikt-loesen.scene: You are talking through a problem between you and someone close: what happened, how you felt, what you want to happen. Instead of blame, give your aim in damit clauses.
de-b1-konflikt-loesen.partner: someone close who is defensive at first but opens up to listening
de-b1-konflikt-loesen.openingTr: You've been odd with me for days. Will you please tell me what's actually going on?
de-b1-konflikt-loesen.goal: What happened and how you felt have been described without blame, and what you want to happen has been said.

de-b1-heimweh.scene: Someone is asking you about your life between two countries: what it was like when you arrived, what you miss, where you feel you belong now. Tell the past moments with als.
de-b1-heimweh.partner: an unhurried acquaintance who is genuinely interested
de-b1-heimweh.openingTr: May I ask you something personal? Where do you actually feel at home — here or there?
de-b1-heimweh.goal: How your arrival was, what you miss and where you feel you belong now have all been described.

de-b1-lebenstraum.scene: You are telling someone about your big dream: what it is, why you want it, what the first step would be and what is holding you back. Build the dream with infinitive phrases.
de-b1-lebenstraum.partner: a supportive listener who asks realistic questions
de-b1-lebenstraum.openingTr: You once told me about a plan you'd had in mind for years. What became of it?
de-b1-lebenstraum.goal: Your dream, your reason, the first step and what is holding you back have all been described.

de-b1-rueckblick.scene: You are having a mid-course review with your teacher: how the road has gone, what was hardest, what you are proud of, what you will do next.
de-b1-rueckblick.partner: a proud teacher who has followed you from the start
de-b1-rueckblick.openingTr: We're at the end of the first part. Look back a moment: what was the most important moment for you?
de-b1-rueckblick.goal: How the road has gone, the hardest part, what you are proud of and your next goal have all been described.

de-b1-rezept-lesen.scene: A friend is asking you for a recipe from your home country. List the ingredients, then describe the steps in order and in the passive.
de-b1-rezept-lesen.partner: a curious friend who is just learning to cook
de-b1-rezept-lesen.openingTr: You said you were cooking something from home. How is that actually made?
de-b1-rezept-lesen.goal: The ingredients have been listed, the steps have been described in order and your friend could repeat the recipe.

de-b1-im-gasthaus.scene: You have come to an inn for two. You are being seated, talking to the waiter and ordering, and asking for the bill at the end.
de-b1-im-gasthaus.partner: a polite waiter who is rushed off their feet
de-b1-im-gasthaus.openingTr: Good evening! Have you booked, or shall I show you to a table?
de-b1-im-gasthaus.goal: You have been seated, food and drink have been ordered, the bill has been asked for and the tip has come up.

de-b1-markt-frisch.scene: You are at a stall at the market. You compare two products, ask about the price and the freshness, then make your choice and have it weighed.
de-b1-markt-frisch.partner: a jokey stallholder who praises their own goods
de-b1-markt-frisch.openingTr: All fresh today! What can I get you — the mushrooms, or the carrots?
de-b1-markt-frisch.goal: Two products have been compared, the price has been asked, the choice has been made with reasons and it has been weighed.

de-b1-zum-essen-eingeladen.scene: You are invited to dinner at a friend's home. First you ask what to bring, then at the table you praise the food and ask for a recipe.
de-b1-zum-essen-eingeladen.partner: a hospitable host who is proud of their table
de-b1-zum-essen-eingeladen.openingTr: Lovely that you're here! Do sit down — how do you find the food?
de-b1-zum-essen-eingeladen.goal: What to bring has been discussed, the table has been praised and a recipe has been asked for.

de-b1-heimatgericht.scene: You are at a barbecue. You introduce the dish you brought and describe who made it and how it is made, with relative clauses.
de-b1-heimatgericht.partner: a sociable neighbour who wants to taste everything
de-b1-heimatgericht.openingTr: That smells fantastic! What have you brought, then?
de-b1-heimatgericht.goal: The dish you brought has been introduced and who made it and how it was cooked have been described with relative clauses.

de-b1-lokal-reklamation.scene: The wrong dish has come to your table at a restaurant and there is a mark on the plate. You say so politely, give your reason and ask for a solution.
de-b1-lokal-reklamation.partner: a restaurateur who is defensive at first but then finds a solution
de-b1-lokal-reklamation.openingTr: Right, one schnitzel — enjoy your meal! Is everything all right for you?
de-b1-lokal-reklamation.goal: The wrong order has been raised, the reason has been given and a solution has been agreed.

de-b1-haltbar-machen.scene: A lot is left over after a big meal. You and your flatmate discuss what to keep and how, and what to do with what tomorrow.
de-b1-haltbar-machen.partner: an organised flatmate who cannot bear waste
de-b1-haltbar-machen.openingTr: Well, that really is a lot left over. What are you going to do with it?
de-b1-haltbar-machen.goal: A plan has been given for each of the leftovers and the two of you have agreed who does what.

de-b1-esskultur-b1.scene: You and a German friend are comparing table customs: what time people eat, what they drink, how a guest is treated. Describe the differences with paired conjunctions.
de-b1-esskultur-b1.partner: a curious friend who likes questioning their own customs
de-b1-esskultur-b1.openingTr: Tell me, you eat a hot meal in the evening, don't you? With us it's quite different.
de-b1-esskultur-b1.goal: At least three customs have been compared and the similarities and differences have been given with paired conjunctions.

de-b1-kuchen-backen.scene: There is a celebration at home and you have two hours left. You share out the work with a friend: who does what, and which job comes before which.
de-b1-kuchen-backen.partner: a friend who has come to help but does not know what to do
de-b1-kuchen-backen.openingTr: I'm here! Just tell me what to do — what do we start with?
de-b1-kuchen-backen.goal: The jobs have been put in order and it has been settled who does what and when.

de-b1-abschied-am-tisch.scene: You are at the end of a lovely meal and you have to go. You thank your host, offer to help, arrange the next meeting and say goodbye.
de-b1-abschied-am-tisch.partner: a warm host who does not want to let you go
de-b1-abschied-am-tisch.openingTr: Is it that late already? Do stay a bit longer — there's coffee coming.
de-b1-abschied-am-tisch.goal: Thanks have been given, help has been offered, the next meeting has been arranged and goodbyes have been said.

de-b1-preis-vergleichen.scene: You have seen the same product in two places. You and a friend compare the prices, the discount and the quality and decide where to buy it.
de-b1-preis-vergleichen.partner: a careful friend who never buys without comparing
de-b1-preis-vergleichen.openingTr: Have you compared the two prices? Which is cheaper?
de-b1-preis-vergleichen.goal: The two sellers have been compared on price and quality and a decision has been made with reasons.

de-b1-umtausch.scene: You have gone back to the shop to exchange something you bought two weeks ago. You give your reason, show the receipt and say clearly what you want.
de-b1-umtausch.partner: an assistant who sticks to the rules but looks for a solution
de-b1-umtausch.openingTr: Good afternoon! What can I do for you — would you like to exchange something?
de-b1-umtausch.goal: The reason for the return has been given, the receipt has been shown and an exchange or a refund has been agreed.

de-b1-bank-konto.scene: You have come to the bank to open an account. You find out about the fees, the card and the conditions for withdrawing money, with indirect questions.
de-b1-bank-konto.partner: an unhurried bank clerk who enjoys explaining
de-b1-bank-konto.openingTr: Good afternoon! You'd like to open an account — have you any questions already?
de-b1-bank-konto.goal: The type of account, the fees and how the card is used have been found out and the next step to open it has been agreed.

de-b1-online-bestellen.scene: There is a problem with something you ordered online: the wrong model came and the manual is missing. You ring customer service and describe what happened in order.
de-b1-online-bestellen.partner: a methodical agent who asks for the order number first
de-b1-online-bestellen.openingTr: Customer service, good afternoon! What is it about your order?
de-b1-online-bestellen.goal: What was ordered, what arrived and what is missing have been described and a solution has been agreed.

de-b1-kleidung-kaufen.scene: You are trying clothes on in a shop. You talk about the size, the fabric and the price, describing what you are after with adjectives in front of the noun.
de-b1-kleidung-kaufen.partner: a keen assistant who wants you to try everything on
de-b1-kleidung-kaufen.openingTr: Can I help you? Are you looking for anything in particular?
de-b1-kleidung-kaufen.goal: The item you wanted has been described with adjectives, tried on, and it has been decided whether to buy it.

de-b1-material-waehlen.scene: You are in a hardware shop and you do not know the name of the part you want. You describe what it is made of, what it does and where it goes.
de-b1-material-waehlen.partner: a patient shopkeeper who listens and tries to find the right part
de-b1-material-waehlen.openingTr: What are you looking for? Just describe it — what do you need it for?
de-b1-material-waehlen.goal: The part has been described by its material and its function and the shopkeeper has found the right one.

de-b1-wirtschaft-reden.scene: You and a colleague are discussing how your industry is going: production, competition, imports. Give both sides of each view with paired conjunctions.
de-b1-wirtschaft-reden.partner: a pessimistic colleague who is open to the figures
de-b1-wirtschaft-reden.openingTr: Tell me, how do you see the state of our industry at the moment?
de-b1-wirtschaft-reden.goal: A view has been given on at least three points, both sides of each have been said and a shared conclusion has been reached.

de-b1-gewinn-verlust.scene: You are presenting last year's figures at a small meeting. You describe what the table shows, interpret one figure and answer the questions.
de-b1-gewinn-verlust.partner: a team member who asks about the reason behind the figures
de-b1-gewinn-verlust.openingTr: Thanks for the table. What exactly is being shown there?
de-b1-gewinn-verlust.goal: The content of the table has been described, one figure has been interpreted and at least one question has been answered.

de-b1-anzeige-lesen.scene: You and a friend are looking at a second-hand advertisement. You describe the advert, say what is good and what is doubtful about it, and list the missing details.
de-b1-anzeige-lesen.partner: an optimistic friend who is ready to be taken in by the advert
de-b1-anzeige-lesen.openingTr: Look at this advert here — sounds great, doesn't it?
de-b1-anzeige-lesen.goal: The advert has been described, at least two missing details have been listed and the questions to ask the seller have been decided.

de-b1-reklamation-brief.scene: You are ringing an authority: the document you sent has been lost. You describe what you sent, what you are expecting and what you will put in a written complaint.
de-b1-reklamation-brief.partner: a polite official who avoids taking responsibility
de-b1-reklamation-brief.openingTr: Administration office, good afternoon. How can I help you?
de-b1-reklamation-brief.goal: The lost document has been described, your expectation has been put politely and an address for a written complaint has been taken.

de-b1-bahn-fahren.scene: You are looking for your train at the main station. You did not quite catch the announcement: you ask about the platform, the departure time and whether your ticket is valid for the return.
de-b1-bahn-fahren.partner: a helpful station attendant who is in a hurry
de-b1-bahn-fahren.openingTr: Can I help you? You look as if you're looking for something.
de-b1-bahn-fahren.goal: The platform, the departure time and what the ticket covers have been found out and the passenger has been sent to the right train.

de-b1-am-flughafen.scene: Your flight has been delayed and you have missed your connection. At the airport desk you describe what happened in order and ask for a new solution.
de-b1-am-flughafen.partner: an airline agent checking the system and looking for a solution
de-b1-am-flughafen.openingTr: Good afternoon! What's happened — which flight had you booked?
de-b1-am-flughafen.goal: What happened has been described in order and a new flight or a place to stay has been found.

de-b1-auto-unterwegs.scene: You and a friend are setting off on a long drive. You talk about what you will do if things come up on the way: petrol, breaks, the weather.
de-b1-auto-unterwegs.partner: a travelling companion who wants every eventuality talked through
de-b1-auto-unterwegs.openingTr: Six hours' driving — what do we do if we get tired?
de-b1-auto-unterwegs.goal: What to do has been settled with conditional clauses for at least three eventualities.

de-b1-verkehrsregeln.scene: You are explaining the traffic rules here to a friend who has just arrived in the country: right of way, one-way streets, the pavement, parking. Give the rules impersonally.
de-b1-verkehrsregeln.partner: a friend who has driven in another country and likes comparing
de-b1-verkehrsregeln.openingTr: It was quite different where I come from — what's actually forbidden here?
de-b1-verkehrsregeln.goal: At least three rules have been described impersonally and one difference between the two countries has been given.

de-b1-unterkunft-suchen.scene: You and a friend are comparing two places to stay on holiday: price, location, quiet. In the end you choose one.
de-b1-unterkunft-suchen.partner: a friend who watches the budget but will not give up comfort
de-b1-unterkunft-suchen.openingTr: So, cabin or hotel? I really can't decide.
de-b1-unterkunft-suchen.goal: The two options have been compared on at least three criteria and a decision has been made with reasons.

de-b1-hafenstadt.scene: You have visited a port city. You are telling a friend about the places you saw: what you could see from which tower, which ferry took you where.
de-b1-hafenstadt.partner: a friend planning a trip to the same city who asks for detail
de-b1-hafenstadt.openingTr: Tell me — what did you like best in the port city?
de-b1-hafenstadt.goal: At least three places have been described with relative clauses after a preposition and a recommendation has been given.

de-b1-berg-und-tal.scene: You went walking in the mountains last weekend and the weather turned. You are telling a friend what happened, in order.
de-b1-berg-und-tal.partner: a friend who loves hill walking and asks for detail
de-b1-berg-und-tal.openingTr: I heard you were up in the mountains. How was it — did you have any luck with the weather?
de-b1-berg-und-tal.goal: The start of the walk, the change in the weather and the way back have been told in order.

de-b1-wohnort-wechseln.scene: You are talking to a new acquaintance about where you have lived: which cities, which districts, why you moved. Use the past tense of written German as you tell it.
de-b1-wohnort-wechseln.partner: an acquaintance who wants to tell you their own moving story too
de-b1-wohnort-wechseln.openingTr: You've moved a lot, haven't you — where did you live before?
de-b1-wohnort-wechseln.goal: At least two former homes and the reasons for moving have been described in order.

de-b1-notfall-unterwegs.scene: A friend has broken down on the road and is ringing you. You calm them down, suggest what they should do in the subjunctive and tell them who to call.
de-b1-notfall-unterwegs.partner: a flustered friend who is talking fast
de-b1-notfall-unterwegs.openingTr: I'm stuck here at the side of the road and I don't know what to do — what should I do?
de-b1-notfall-unterwegs.goal: The situation has been understood, at least three steps have been advised and it has been settled who to call.

de-b1-reise-erzaehlen.scene: You are back from a long journey. You are telling a friend about the day that stayed with you most: what happened, and what had happened before it.
de-b1-reise-erzaehlen.partner: a friend who listens without interrupting and asks for detail afterwards
de-b1-reise-erzaehlen.openingTr: Back at last! Tell me — which day stayed with you most?
de-b1-reise-erzaehlen.goal: One day has been told with two layers of the past and your friend's question has been answered.

de-b1-koerper-teile.scene: You are at the doctor's. You describe where the pain is, how long it has been going on and what makes it worse.
de-b1-koerper-teile.partner: a GP who asks short, clear questions
de-b1-koerper-teile.openingTr: Good afternoon! Tell me exactly — where does it hurt?
de-b1-koerper-teile.goal: Where the pain is, how long it has lasted and when it gets worse have been described, and the doctor has said the next step.

de-b1-kleine-verletzung.scene: You are on a first aid course. You explain to the instructor which steps are taken, and in what order, for a small wound.
de-b1-kleine-verletzung.partner: a first aid instructor who questions each step in turn
de-b1-kleine-verletzung.openingTr: Good. And what is done if someone cuts their finger?
de-b1-kleine-verletzung.goal: At least four steps have been described in order and impersonally, and one exception has been given.

de-b1-vorsorge-alltag.scene: A friend is constantly ill and asking you for advice. You describe what you do and how you do it.
de-b1-vorsorge-alltag.partner: a friend who answers every piece of advice with 'but how'
de-b1-vorsorge-alltag.openingTr: You never get ill — what do you do differently from me?
de-b1-vorsorge-alltag.goal: At least three pieces of advice have been given, each with how it is put into practice.

de-b1-schwangerschaft.scene: A baby is on the way in the family. You are talking to a close friend about the news, your hopes and your worries.
de-b1-schwangerschaft.partner: a friend who has been through the same and shares their experience
de-b1-schwangerschaft.openingTr: That's wonderful news! And — how are you feeling about it?
de-b1-schwangerschaft.goal: The news has been shared and at least one hope and one worry have been put in a subordinate clause.

de-b1-familie-gross.scene: You are showing a friend a family photo. You describe who is who and your relationship to each of them, with relative clauses.
de-b1-familie-gross.partner: a friend asking about everyone in the photo and trying to work out the family tree
de-b1-familie-gross.openingTr: So many people! Who's who in this photo?
de-b1-familie-gross.goal: At least four relatives have been introduced and your relationship to each has been described with a relative clause.

de-b1-generationen.scene: You and a friend are talking about the gap between generations: what your grandparents' youth was like, what has changed today, what has stayed the same.
de-b1-generationen.partner: a friend who tells you their own grandparents' story too
de-b1-generationen.openingTr: Tell me — what was it like when your grandparents were young?
de-b1-generationen.goal: A period in the past has been described and at least two differences from today have been given with reasons.

de-b1-pflege-zuhause.scene: You and your sibling are discussing how to share the care of an older relative: who does what, a care home or care at home, and the aim behind each decision.
de-b1-pflege-zuhause.partner: your sibling, busy with work but wanting to take responsibility
de-b1-pflege-zuhause.openingTr: We really do have to sort this out now — who takes on what?
de-b1-pflege-zuhause.goal: The work has been shared out, the aim of each decision has been given and a next step has been settled.

de-b1-in-pension.scene: You are chatting to a retired neighbour: what is not as it used to be, what they still do themselves, where they ask for help.
de-b1-in-pension.partner: a witty retired neighbour who values their independence
de-b1-in-pension.openingTr: Oh, you know — it all used to go much faster. How is it with you?
de-b1-in-pension.goal: At least three comparisons have been made, a preference has been given and an offer of help has been discussed.

de-b1-beim-friseur.scene: You are at the hairdresser's. You describe what you want, ask for one correction while the work is going on, and ask about a product at the end.
de-b1-beim-friseur.partner: a chatty hairdresser who asks about every step
de-b1-beim-friseur.openingTr: Do take a seat! And — what would you like today?
de-b1-beim-friseur.goal: The style you wanted has been described, a correction has been asked for and a product has been asked about.

de-b1-sucht-gespraech.scene: You have noticed that a close friend has been drinking a lot lately. You raise it without blame, say you are worried and offer help.
de-b1-sucht-gespraech.partner: a friend who tries to change the subject at first but then listens
de-b1-sucht-gespraech.openingTr: What's the matter? You look so serious — has something happened?
de-b1-sucht-gespraech.goal: The subject has been raised without blame, the worry has been said and concrete help has been offered.

de-b1-geraet-anschliessen.scene: A friend cannot set up the device they have just bought and is ringing you. You describe the steps in order and impersonally.
de-b1-geraet-anschliessen.partner: an impatient friend who started without reading the manual
de-b1-geraet-anschliessen.openingTr: I've got three cables here and no idea — what gets done first?
de-b1-geraet-anschliessen.goal: At least four steps have been described in order and the device is working.

de-b1-computer-problem.scene: Your computer will not start. You ring the technical support line, list the symptoms, and say what you have tried and whether you have a backup.
de-b1-computer-problem.partner: a support agent who asks the questions in turn and works step by step
de-b1-computer-problem.openingTr: Technical support, good afternoon. Can you describe to me what exactly is happening?
de-b1-computer-problem.goal: The symptoms have been listed, a likely cause has been given and a next step has been settled.

de-b1-netz-stoerung.scene: The internet at home has been down for three days. You ring the provider and find out the cause, when it will be fixed and whether you get a refund, with indirect questions.
de-b1-netz-stoerung.partner: a call centre agent who talks in set phrases but gives information when pressed
de-b1-netz-stoerung.openingTr: Thank you for your call. Which address is it about?
de-b1-netz-stoerung.goal: The cause of the fault, how long it is expected to last and the question of a refund have all been found out.

de-b1-werkzeug-leihen.scene: You want to put a shelf up on the wall but you have not got the tool. You knock on your neighbour's door, explain what you are doing and ask to borrow one.
de-b1-werkzeug-leihen.partner: a neighbour ready to help but attached to their tools
de-b1-werkzeug-leihen.openingTr: Oh, hello! You look as if you need something — what can I do?
de-b1-werkzeug-leihen.goal: What you are doing has been described, the tool has been asked for politely and it has been said when it will come back.

de-b1-putzen-teilen.scene: You and your flatmate are discussing the cleaning routine: who does what and how often, and the aim behind each rule.
de-b1-putzen-teilen.partner: a flatmate who is more relaxed about cleaning than you are
de-b1-putzen-teilen.openingTr: Do we really have to make a plan? Doesn't it work as it is?
de-b1-putzen-teilen.goal: The work has been shared out, the aim of at least two rules has been given and a routine has been agreed.

de-b1-einbruch-melden.scene: You came home and saw that the door had been forced. You report it to the police, list what has been taken and say when you noticed.
de-b1-einbruch-melden.partner: a police officer taking a statement and asking the questions in turn
de-b1-einbruch-melden.openingTr: Good afternoon. Please describe it to me exactly — when did you notice?
de-b1-einbruch-melden.goal: The incident has been reported, what was taken has been listed and the details needed for the statement have been given.

de-b1-grafik-lesen.scene: You are presenting a graphic at a small meeting. You describe what each thing is with relative clauses and answer the questions.
de-b1-grafik-lesen.partner: a participant who cannot see the graphic from where they are and asks for detail
de-b1-grafik-lesen.openingTr: Sorry, I can't see it very well from here — what exactly does the graphic show?
de-b1-grafik-lesen.goal: What the graphic shows has been described, at least two elements have been identified and one question has been answered.

de-b1-alte-technik.scene: You and a friend are talking about old technology: cassettes, radio, the first phones. You compare what was better and what was worse.
de-b1-alte-technik.partner: a nostalgic friend who is suspicious of every new thing
de-b1-alte-technik.openingTr: I found an old cassette yesterday — do you remember what that was like?
de-b1-alte-technik.goal: At least three comparisons have been made and a conclusion has been reached about what has really improved.

de-b1-reparieren-lassen.scene: You have taken your broken device to a repair shop. You explain what happened, ask the price and decide whether repairing it or buying a new one makes more sense.
de-b1-reparieren-lassen.partner: an honest repairer who does not want to lose the job either
de-b1-reparieren-lassen.openingTr: Let me have a look. How long has the device been playing up?
de-b1-reparieren-lassen.goal: The fault has been described, the price has been asked and a decision has been made with reasons between repair and replacement.

de-b1-technik-diskussion.scene: You and a friend are arguing about how technology has changed your lives: what it has made easier, what it has made harder, where dependence begins.
de-b1-technik-diskussion.partner: a friend who admits being very attached to technology but defends it
de-b1-technik-diskussion.openingTr: I can't manage without my phone any more — do you actually think that's a bad thing?
de-b1-technik-diskussion.goal: Both sides have been given on at least three points and a personal conclusion has been reached.

de-b1-berufe-vorstellen.scene: You are at a careers day at a school. You introduce three occupations to the young people, describing what each one does and what it requires.
de-b1-berufe-vorstellen.partner: a curious student who does not know which career to choose
de-b1-berufe-vorstellen.openingTr: I really don't know what to be — what do people in your job actually do?
de-b1-berufe-vorstellen.goal: At least three occupations have been described by what they involve, and the training needed for each has been given.

de-b1-lehre-machen.scene: You are talking to a careers adviser: an apprenticeship or university, which documents are needed, what you think is worth it.
de-b1-lehre-machen.partner: an adviser who knows both paths and is trying to make the decision easier
de-b1-lehre-machen.openingTr: You're caught between two paths, aren't you? Which appeals to you more — an apprenticeship or a degree?
de-b1-lehre-machen.goal: The two paths have been compared, a decision has been given with reasons and the documents needed have been found out.

de-b1-experte-fragen.scene: You have rung an institute to get an expert opinion on something. You ask what you want to know with indirect questions and arrange an appointment.
de-b1-experte-fragen.partner: an expert who answers briefly but explains when pressed
de-b1-experte-fragen.openingTr: Institute for Research, good afternoon. What can I help you with?
de-b1-experte-fragen.goal: At least three questions have been asked indirectly and a meeting has been arranged.

de-b1-buero-alltag.scene: You are in a short office meeting. You list the week's jobs, ask who is doing what, and share out what is left.
de-b1-buero-alltag.partner: a colleague willing to take jobs on but short of time
de-b1-buero-alltag.openingTr: Right, a quick run through the week — what's all needed by Friday?
de-b1-buero-alltag.goal: The jobs have been listed, who is doing what has been asked and the remaining jobs have been shared out.

de-b1-arbeitsrecht.scene: You have been dismissed and gone to a trade union adviser. You describe what happened in order, ask about your rights and find out what to do.
de-b1-arbeitsrecht.partner: a calm union adviser who knows the rights well
de-b1-arbeitsrecht.openingTr: Do sit down. Please tell me — when were you given notice?
de-b1-arbeitsrecht.goal: The events have been described in order, the rights have been asked about and a next step has been settled.

de-b1-chefin-gespraech.scene: You are in a short meeting with your manager. You describe a problem in the team, suggest a solution and discuss how the decision will be announced.
de-b1-chefin-gespraech.partner: a manager who speaks briefly and wants reasons
de-b1-chefin-gespraech.openingTr: You wanted to speak to me — what is it about?
de-b1-chefin-gespraech.goal: The problem has been described, a suggestion has been put politely and a next step has been settled.

de-b1-stellensuche.scene: A friend is looking for work and asking how you found yours. You describe the process in order: what you did first, what happened next.
de-b1-stellensuche.partner: a friend starting the same road who asks about every step
de-b1-stellensuche.openingTr: You managed it — how did it actually go for you?
de-b1-stellensuche.goal: The process has been described in at least four steps and with two layers of the past.

de-b1-projekt-praesentieren.scene: You are presenting the results of a project to a small team. You give both sides of every figure and answer the objections in a balanced way.
de-b1-projekt-praesentieren.partner: a team member who distrusts figures and asks for sources
de-b1-projekt-praesentieren.openingTr: Before you start — where do these figures actually come from?
de-b1-projekt-praesentieren.goal: The source has been explained, both sides of at least two figures have been given and one objection has been answered.

de-b1-selbststaendig.scene: You are describing your business idea to a business adviser: what you will make, who you will sell it to, and the aim behind each decision.
de-b1-selbststaendig.partner: a supportive business adviser who questions the risks
de-b1-selbststaendig.openingTr: Tell me about your idea — what exactly do you want to set up?
de-b1-selbststaendig.goal: The business idea has been described, the aim of at least three decisions has been given and one risk has been discussed.

de-b1-arbeitszufriedenheit.scene: You and a colleague are talking over your lunch break: is the work tiring, is it dull, what would you change.
de-b1-arbeitszufriedenheit.partner: a colleague who complains about the job but does not think of leaving
de-b1-arbeitszufriedenheit.openingTr: Be honest — do you actually still enjoy the work?
de-b1-arbeitszufriedenheit.goal: The good and the hard sides of the job have been given and one thing you would change has been voiced.

de-b1-migration.scene: You are on the introductions round at a language course. You describe where you came from, what the early days were like and what has changed.
de-b1-migration.partner: a curious fellow student who tells their own story too
de-b1-migration.openingTr: Let's introduce ourselves briefly — would you like to tell us how you came to be here?
de-b1-migration.goal: Your arrival, the early difficulties and how things are today have been told in order.

de-b1-konsulat.scene: You are at the consulate. You find out which documents are needed, whether your diploma is recognised and how long it takes, with indirect questions.
de-b1-konsulat.partner: a consulate official dealing with a crowd but giving clear information
de-b1-konsulat.openingTr: Next, please. What is it about?
de-b1-konsulat.goal: The documents needed, the recognition of the qualification and the timescale have been found out and a next step has been settled.

de-b1-sprache-akzent.scene: You and a friend are talking about being bilingual: which is easier, where you use which language, what you find hard.
de-b1-sprache-akzent.partner: a curious friend who grew up with one language
de-b1-sprache-akzent.openingTr: Do you actually think in German, or in your mother tongue?
de-b1-sprache-akzent.goal: The two languages have been compared on at least three counts and one difficulty has been described.

de-b1-minderheit-mehrheit.scene: You and a friend are arguing about whose voice gets heard in society. Give both sides of every view with paired conjunctions.
de-b1-minderheit-mehrheit.partner: a friend with firm views who is still open to listening
de-b1-minderheit-mehrheit.openingTr: I think it gets talked about too much — do you see it that way too?
de-b1-minderheit-mehrheit.goal: Both sides of at least three views have been given and common ground has been found.

de-b1-politik-reden.scene: You and a friend are discussing a current issue. Put your view in a subordinate clause and use the pattern of doubt when you disagree.
de-b1-politik-reden.partner: a friend who thinks differently from you but enjoys an argument
de-b1-politik-reden.openingTr: Have you heard what was decided yesterday? Honestly, I think it's wrong.
de-b1-politik-reden.goal: A view has been given with reasons and an opposing view has been answered with the pattern of doubt.

de-b1-vor-gericht.scene: You are telling a friend about a court case you read about in the paper: what happened, who said what, what was decided.
de-b1-vor-gericht.partner: a friend who has not heard the story and asks for detail
de-b1-vor-gericht.openingTr: What happened there? I only saw the headline.
de-b1-vor-gericht.goal: The incident, the proceedings and the decision have been told in order and impersonally.

de-b1-verbrechen-melden.scene: You witnessed an incident in the street. You describe to the police what you saw: who you saw, what they did, when it happened.
de-b1-verbrechen-melden.partner: a police officer taking the description down and wanting detail
de-b1-verbrechen-melden.openingTr: You saw something? Please describe the person to me.
de-b1-verbrechen-melden.goal: The person and the incident have been described with relative clauses and the timing has been given.

de-b1-regeln-verstehen.scene: You have read the rules for using a building. You explain to a newcomer what is allowed, what is restricted and what the exception is.
de-b1-regeln-verstehen.partner: someone who finds the rules long and is looking for the exception
de-b1-regeln-verstehen.openingTr: So many rules — what actually applies here?
de-b1-regeln-verstehen.goal: At least three rules have been explained impersonally and one exception has been given.

de-b1-religion-frieden.scene: You are talking to someone from a very different background from your own. You accept the differences but look for common ground.
de-b1-religion-frieden.partner: an acquaintance who is distant at first and then opens up
de-b1-religion-frieden.openingTr: We come from completely different worlds — can that even work?
de-b1-religion-frieden.goal: At least two differences have been accepted and at least one thing in common has been found.

de-b1-engagement-buerger.scene: There is a problem in your area and you want to do something about it. You and a neighbour discuss what could be done and the aim of each step.
de-b1-engagement-buerger.partner: a neighbour who has tried before and lost hope
de-b1-engagement-buerger.openingTr: We tried that years ago — do you really believe it will get anywhere?
de-b1-engagement-buerger.goal: At least three steps have been suggested, the aim of each has been given and the neighbour has taken one on.

de-b1-oper-konzert.scene: You went to a concert last night. You describe the hall, the piece that was played and how the evening went to a friend.
de-b1-oper-konzert.partner: a friend who is a stranger to classical music but curious
de-b1-oper-konzert.openingTr: You were at the opera yesterday? How was it — is it worth it?
de-b1-oper-konzert.goal: The venue and the piece have been described, how the evening went has been told and a recommendation has been given.
