de-b1-literatur-lesen.scene: A friend is asking for a book recommendation. You describe the last one you read, tell them what it is about and say why you liked it.
de-b1-literatur-lesen.partner: a friend who is put off by long books but wants to read
de-b1-literatur-lesen.openingTr: I need something to read — have you got a tip for me?
de-b1-literatur-lesen.goal: The book has been described, what it is about has been told and the reason for recommending it has been given.

de-b1-fest-feiern.scene: You are describing a day you spent at carnival: what you did beforehand, what happened during it, how it ended.
de-b1-fest-feiern.partner: a friend who has never been to a carnival and asks about every detail
de-b1-fest-feiern.openingTr: Carnival — I've never been to one. How does a day like that go?
de-b1-fest-feiern.goal: The before, during and after of the day have been told with conjunctions of time.

de-b1-sport-treiben.scene: You have gone to a sports club for information. You ask which sports there are, the times and the fee, and say what you would like to try.
de-b1-sport-treiben.partner: an energetic coach who wants to sign everyone up for something
de-b1-sport-treiben.openingTr: Welcome! Are you looking for something in particular, or would you like to have a look round first?
de-b1-sport-treiben.goal: The sports and the conditions have been found out and a trial session has been arranged.

de-b1-wettkampf.scene: You are telling a friend who missed yesterday's match about it: what happened, who did what, what the result was.
de-b1-wettkampf.partner: a friend who missed the match, does not want to know the result but cannot resist
de-b1-wettkampf.openingTr: Don't tell me! … No, go on, tell me. How did it end?
de-b1-wettkampf.goal: How the match went and the result have been described and at least two incidents have been given impersonally.

de-b1-natur-erleben.scene: You went out into the countryside at the weekend. You are telling a friend about the day: where you went, what you did, whether it was worth it.
de-b1-natur-erleben.partner: a slightly envious friend who spent the weekend indoors
de-b1-natur-erleben.openingTr: You were outdoors? I sat inside all day — how was it?
de-b1-natur-erleben.goal: The course of the day has been told in order and whether it was worth it has been said.

de-b1-wetter-extrem.scene: The weather turned suddenly on a walk. You and a friend are discussing what has changed and what you should do.
de-b1-wetter-extrem.partner: a walking companion who is cold and wants to turn back
de-b1-wetter-extrem.openingTr: It's getting colder and colder — shall we turn back or carry on?
de-b1-wetter-extrem.goal: The change in the weather has been described with comparisons and a shared decision has been made.

de-b1-tiere-natur.scene: You are in a wildlife park describing the animals you see to a friend: which one eats what, which one is dangerous.
de-b1-tiere-natur.partner: a curious friend who is a little wary of animals
de-b1-tiere-natur.openingTr: What's that back there? Is it dangerous?
de-b1-tiere-natur.goal: At least two animals have been described with relative clauses and what they eat has been said.

de-b1-freizeit-planen.scene: You and a friend are planning the weekend: what you will do, when, and for how much. Put your suggestions politely.
de-b1-freizeit-planen.partner: a friend who objects to every suggestion but comes round in the end
de-b1-freizeit-planen.openingTr: So, the weekend — have you got anything on?
de-b1-freizeit-planen.goal: At least three suggestions have been made, one has been settled and the time and place have been fixed.

de-b1-b1-abschluss.scene: You have finished B1. You are having a final review with your teacher: what you have achieved, what you still find hard, what you will do next.
de-b1-b1-abschluss.partner: a proud teacher who has followed you through a hundred and eighty lessons
de-b1-b1-abschluss.openingTr: That was the last lesson at B1. Tell me honestly — what can you do today that you couldn't at the start?
de-b1-b1-abschluss.goal: The gains and the remaining difficulties have been given in balance and a next goal has been set.

de-b2-praesentation.scene: You are opening your presentation at a team meeting. State your aim, announce the plan of the talk, say when the audience may ask questions and move on to the first section.
de-b2-praesentation.partner: an interested department head who cuts in with questions
de-b2-praesentation.openingTr: Before you begin: how much time have you allowed, and do you want questions as we go or at the end?
de-b2-praesentation.goal: The aim of the talk, the plan and the arrangement for questions have been announced, and the first section has been reached.

de-b2-folien.scene: You are talking a colleague through the chart of the quarterly results: which way the trend is going, what stands out, what the reason might be. Describe the figures in the past passive.
de-b2-folien.partner: a colleague who questions the figures and asks for sources
de-b2-folien.openingTr: I see quite a jump here in May. Where does that come from — and have the figures been checked yet?
de-b2-folien.goal: The trend, the striking point and the likely reason have been described, and how the figures were verified has been said.

de-b2-meeting-leiten.scene: You are chairing a team meeting. Open the agenda, steer the discussion, listen if there is an objection, minute the decision and close the meeting with a summary.
de-b2-meeting-leiten.partner: a team member inclined to stray from the point who has an objection
de-b2-meeting-leiten.openingTr: Before we start: can we bring the last item forward? It's time-critical for me.
de-b2-meeting-leiten.goal: The agenda has been worked through, a decision has been minuted and the meeting has been closed with a summary.

de-b2-protokoll.scene: You and a colleague are going over the minutes of yesterday's meeting: which decisions were taken, who said what, which item is missing. Report what was said in reported speech.
de-b2-protokoll.partner: a meticulous colleague who traces every item back to its source
de-b2-protokoll.openingTr: I've skimmed the minutes. Something's missing at point three — what exactly was decided there?
de-b2-protokoll.goal: The decisions taken have been reported, the missing item has been found and it has been settled how the minutes will be corrected.

de-b2-rueckfragen.scene: Your presentation is over and you are in the question round. Repeat the question in your own words, put one question off politely, correct a misunderstanding and close the round.
de-b2-rueckfragen.partner: a listener asking hard but fair questions
de-b2-rueckfragen.openingTr: Thank you for the talk. A question first: you say the method saves time — what figures are you basing that on?
de-b2-rueckfragen.goal: The questions have been handled, one has been put off, a misunderstanding has been corrected and the round has been closed.

de-b2-smalltalk-business.scene: You have met a senior manager in the lift and you have six floors. Open a short conversation, bring up a small matter in passing and close politely before you reach your floor.
de-b2-smalltalk-business.partner: a polite senior manager who is in a hurry
de-b2-smalltalk-business.openingTr: Good morning! You're in early today. Is everything all right in your team?
de-b2-smalltalk-business.goal: A short conversation has been had, a matter has been raised in passing and it has been closed with a non-committal word.

de-b2-delegieren.scene: In a busy week you are sharing out the work with your team: what can be done this week, what has to wait and who takes on what.
de-b2-delegieren.partner: a team member who says their capacity is full
de-b2-delegieren.openingTr: Before you hand things out: I've still got two things from last week. What really has priority?
de-b2-delegieren.goal: The priority has been set, who takes on what has been shared out and a new date has been given for what was put off.

de-b2-deadline.scene: You are discussing the delivery date with a client. Say what is possible on what condition, name one exception, offer to speed the process up if need be and agree a date.
de-b2-deadline.partner: an insistent but reasonable client who wants the date brought forward
de-b2-deadline.openingTr: We'd need it a week earlier. Is that feasible — and if so, on what conditions?
de-b2-deadline.goal: What is possible on what condition has been said, one exception has been named and a delivery date has been agreed.

de-b2-homeoffice-regeln.scene: You are discussing the remote working arrangement with HR: how many days a week you can work from home, which days you must be in the office, how availability is defined.
de-b2-homeoffice-regeln.partner: an HR specialist who knows the rules by heart and is wary of flexibility
de-b2-homeoffice-regeln.openingTr: You wanted to talk about the home working policy. First tell me: how do you picture the week?
de-b2-homeoffice-regeln.goal: How many days will be worked from home, the office requirement and the availability condition have all been made clear.

de-b2-konferenz.scene: You are in the break at a specialist conference and you go up to one of the panel speakers. Introduce yourself and your field, ask about something they said on the panel and suggest a concrete step to keep in touch.
de-b2-konferenz.partner: a speaker who has just presented and responds with interest
de-b2-konferenz.openingTr: You were in hall two just now, weren't you? What brought you to this subject?
de-b2-konferenz.goal: You have introduced yourselves, learnt each other's fields and settled on a concrete step for keeping in touch.

de-b2-verhandeln.scene: You are negotiating the price of the annual contract with a supplier. Put your offer in the subjunctive, ask for a concession, respond to the counter-offer and agree on a figure or a condition.
de-b2-verhandeln.partner: an experienced sales manager who does not discount easily
de-b2-verhandeln.openingTr: Our offer is forty-eight euros a unit. What did you have in mind?
de-b2-verhandeln.goal: Offers have been exchanged and a price or a condition has been agreed.

de-b2-beschwerde-formell.scene: You are on the phone to a customer services manager making a formal complaint: what you are referring to, what the problem is, what you are demanding and what deadline you are setting.
de-b2-beschwerde-formell.partner: a polite customer services manager who avoids taking responsibility
de-b2-beschwerde-formell.openingTr: You've written to us already, haven't you? Just tell me briefly what it's about.
de-b2-beschwerde-formell.goal: The subject and grounds of the complaint have been given, a concrete demand and a deadline have been stated and the other side has said what they will do.

de-b2-hotline.scene: The internet has been down for three days and you have rung technical support. Describe the fault, say what you have tried, ask when it will be fixed and get a solution or an engineer's appointment.
de-b2-hotline.partner: a support agent reading from a script who asks the standard questions first
de-b2-hotline.openingTr: Technical support, my name is Weber. Please describe the fault to me — how long has it been going on?
de-b2-hotline.goal: The fault has been described, what was tried has been said and a solution or an engineer's appointment has been settled.

de-b2-schadenersatz.scene: You are talking to a representative of a removals firm: your things were damaged in the move. Describe what happened, say where the responsibility lies, state your claim with a figure and find out about the process.
de-b2-schadenersatz.partner: a company representative who shares out the responsibility and asks for paperwork
de-b2-schadenersatz.openingTr: I have your damage claim in front of me. Please tell me: what exactly happened?
de-b2-schadenersatz.goal: The damage has been described, the responsibility has been discussed, a claim with a figure has been put and the process has been explained.

de-b2-kompromiss.scene: Two sides have got stuck on a joint project: you will not move on the date, they will not move on the budget. Say where you think they are right, state your own limit, offer a concession and agree a shared solution.
de-b2-kompromiss.partner: a project partner with fair grounds who is open to compromise
de-b2-kompromiss.openingTr: We're going round in circles. Tell me honestly: where can you really not give way?
de-b2-kompromiss.goal: Both sides' limits have been stated, a concession has been offered and a solution both sides accept has been agreed.

de-b2-eskalation.scene: An angry customer is ringing you: the delivery is late for the third time. First acknowledge how they feel, bring the matter back to the facts, explain what happened and offer a solution.
de-b2-eskalation.partner: a customer who raises their voice but is not in the wrong
de-b2-eskalation.openingTr: This is the third time now! I really have had enough of excuses — what are you going to do?
de-b2-eskalation.goal: The anger has been acknowledged, the matter has been brought back to the facts and a concrete solution the customer accepts has been settled.

de-b2-vertrag-kuendigen.scene: You have rung a gym's customer line and you want to cancel your membership. Give notice, state the date, answer the offers to keep you firmly and ask for written confirmation.
de-b2-vertrag-kuendigen.partner: a customer adviser offering a discount and a freeze to keep you
de-b2-vertrag-kuendigen.openingTr: It's a shame you want to leave. May I ask what the reason is? Perhaps we can find a solution.
de-b2-vertrag-kuendigen.goal: Notice has been given, the date has been made clear, the offers to keep you have been declined and written confirmation has been promised.

de-b2-nachbarschaftsstreit.scene: Your upstairs neighbour makes noise almost every night until late. State the facts without blame, say what you want, suggest a time limit together and settle it without going to the management.
de-b2-nachbarschaftsstreit.partner: a neighbour who is defensive at first and then reasonable
de-b2-nachbarschaftsstreit.openingTr: You wanted to speak to me? If it's about the music — we're not having a party every evening, are we?
de-b2-nachbarschaftsstreit.goal: The facts have been given without blame, a time limit has been suggested and a solution has been agreed without going to the building management.

de-b2-reklamation-b2.scene: The same device has broken for the third time and you are in the shop. List in order what has been done so far, say the device is unusable, ask for a replacement or a refund and bring it to a conclusion.
de-b2-reklamation-b2.partner: a shop assistant who suggests another repair and consults a manager when you insist
de-b2-reklamation-b2.openingTr: You've been here before, haven't you? Let me send it in once more, that's the quickest way.
de-b2-reklamation-b2.goal: The repairs carried out have been listed, the offer of another repair has been declined and a conclusion has been reached on a replacement or a refund.

de-b2-feedbackgespraech.scene: You are giving a team member difficult feedback: the deliveries are constantly late. First acknowledge how careful and willing they are, pass on your observation without making it personal, make a suggestion and leave the decision to them.
de-b2-feedbackgespraech.partner: a team member who is defensive at first and then listens
de-b2-feedbackgespraech.openingTr: You wanted to talk? If it's about the deadlines again — I'm stuck on three deliveries myself.
de-b2-feedbackgespraech.goal: The appreciation and the observation have been given separately, a suggestion has been made and what they will do has been settled together.

de-b2-passiv-perfekt.scene: You are in the weekly status meeting with your boss. Report which jobs have been completed, which are still waiting and why, in the past passive; give dates for the rest.
de-b2-passiv-perfekt.partner: a department head who wants short answers and asks for dates
de-b2-passiv-perfekt.openingTr: I haven't much time — tell me briefly: what has been done this week and what hasn't?
de-b2-passiv-perfekt.goal: The finished and unfinished jobs have been listed, the reason for the delay has been given and dates have been set for the rest.

de-b2-passiv-modal.scene: You are at the enquiries desk of an authority asking which steps your application has to go through: what must be submitted, what will be examined, how long it takes, which document has to be approved.
de-b2-passiv-modal.partner: an official who explains the rules in the language of the regulations
de-b2-passiv-modal.openingTr: We have your application. Before it can be processed, though, something still has to be cleared up — do you know what is missing?
de-b2-passiv-modal.goal: The missing document has been found out, the order and length of the steps have been made clear and it has been said when a decision will come.

de-b2-zustandspassiv.scene: You are talking to a building attendant: which door opens when, what is open now, which entrance is permanently closed. Ask and explain, keeping the process apart from the state.
de-b2-zustandspassiv.partner: a building attendant who knows the rules by heart and speaks briefly
de-b2-zustandspassiv.openingTr: You're at the wrong door — the main entrance is closed today. Where are you trying to get to?
de-b2-zustandspassiv.goal: Which entrance is open, which is closed and when the doors are opened have all been found out.

de-b2-passiversatz-lassen.scene: A colleague is proposing a new working arrangement. Say what in the proposal can be done, what has to be sorted out and what is not possible, and reach a shared conclusion.
de-b2-passiversatz-lassen.partner: a colleague attached to their proposal but willing to hear objections
de-b2-passiversatz-lassen.openingTr: I've had an idea: we move the meeting to Monday morning. Can that be done?
de-b2-passiversatz-lassen.goal: The workable and unworkable parts of the proposal have been separated, the point to be sorted out has been named and a shared conclusion has been reached.

de-b2-herstellung.scene: You are on a tour of a chocolate factory. Ask about the steps of production in order, sum one step up in your own words and ask about a detail you are curious about.
de-b2-herstellung.partner: a factory guide who loves the work and loves giving detail
de-b2-herstellung.openingTr: Welcome! We're right at the beginning of production here. Do you know how cocoa gets to us in the first place?
de-b2-herstellung.goal: The steps of production have been learnt in order, one step has been summed up by the learner and a question of detail has been answered.

de-b2-restaurierung.scene: You are on a city tour asking the guide how the old centre was restored: what was repaired, what could be preserved, which building is listed, when the work finished.
de-b2-restaurierung.partner: a city guide who loves the history and gives detail
de-b2-restaurierung.openingTr: You can see it best from here: this row of houses was completely renovated three years ago. Does anything strike you?
de-b2-restaurierung.goal: What was repaired, what was preserved and when the work finished have all been found out.

de-b2-unfallbericht.scene: You witnessed an accident and you are giving a statement to a police officer: what you saw, in what order it happened, who raised the alarm, what happened next. Tell the events in order and objectively.
de-b2-unfallbericht.partner: a police officer taking notes and asking for the date and time
de-b2-unfallbericht.openingTr: You saw the accident? Then let's start at the beginning: what exactly happened first?
de-b2-unfallbericht.goal: The events have been told in order, who did what has been said and contact details have been given at the end of the statement.

de-b2-rezept-profi.scene: You are learning the tricks of a difficult recipe from a chef: ask how each thing has to be cooked, what must not be done and how you tell when it is ready.
de-b2-rezept-profi.partner: a chef who is in a hurry but likes to teach
de-b2-rezept-profi.openingTr: So you want to try it yourself? Good. First tell me: what do you start with?
de-b2-rezept-profi.goal: The cooking steps, one thing to avoid and how to tell when it is ready have all been learnt.

de-b2-wartung.scene: You are discussing the service on your car with the mechanic: find out what absolutely has to be done, what can wait, what it will cost and when it will be ready.
de-b2-wartung.partner: an honest mechanic who is in a hurry
de-b2-wartung.openingTr: I've had a look underneath. Two things are due, one of them urgent — do you want both done?
de-b2-wartung.goal: The essential and the postponable jobs have been separated, the price has been found out and a collection time has been settled.

de-b2-organisation.scene: The two of you are sharing the preparations for a street party. List what has to be done in the impersonal passive, discuss who takes on what and tie the running order to a date.
de-b2-organisation.partner: an eager but disorganised neighbour who keeps throwing in new ideas
de-b2-organisation.openingTr: Right, I've made a list already — it has got rather long, though. What shall we start with?
de-b2-organisation.goal: The jobs have been listed, who takes on what has been shared out and the running order has been tied to a date.

de-b2-schlagzeilen.scene: You and a friend are discussing today's headline. Say in your own words what the headline says, point out what it does not say, and discuss whether the story is overstated.
de-b2-schlagzeilen.partner: a friend inclined to believe the headline but open to persuasion
de-b2-schlagzeilen.openingTr: Have you seen this? 'Rents up by thirty per cent' — thirty! Where is this going to end?
de-b2-schlagzeilen.goal: What the headline says and what it does not say have been separated and a shared conclusion has been reached about whether it is overstated.

de-b2-er-sagte.scene: You are passing on a piece of news you heard to a friend. Give who said what in the reporting mood, name your source and put your own opinion in a separate sentence.
de-b2-er-sagte.partner: a friend who questions the source and asks what you think
de-b2-er-sagte.openingTr: Hang on — are you saying that, or did someone else say it? That's a difference.
de-b2-er-sagte.goal: The source and the content have been given in the reporting mood and the speaker's own opinion has been stated separately.

de-b2-soll-angeblich.scene: A rumour is going round at work. Talking to a colleague, keep apart what you heard, what you know and what you are only guessing, and decide how to deal with the rumour.
de-b2-soll-angeblich.partner: a colleague eager to spread the rumour straight away
de-b2-soll-angeblich.openingTr: Have you heard? The department is supposedly going to be closed. Do you know anything more definite?
de-b2-soll-angeblich.goal: What was heard, what is known and what is guessed have been separated and it has been settled how to deal with the rumour.

de-b2-interview.scene: You are doing a short interview with someone for a local paper. Ask the reason, press further on one answer, insist politely against an evasive answer and get their approval by summing up what they said in your own words.
de-b2-interview.partner: a measured interviewee who avoids some questions
de-b2-interview.openingTr: Five minutes, I'm afraid that's all I have. So what's the occasion for your interview?
de-b2-interview.goal: The reason has been asked, one answer has been pressed further and what was said has been summed up and confirmed.

de-b2-leserbrief.scene: You are responding to a piece in a newspaper and talking to its author. Say where you agree, give the grounds for your objection and leave a concrete suggestion at the end.
de-b2-leserbrief.partner: an author who defends the piece but is open to a good argument
de-b2-leserbrief.openingTr: You've read my piece and you want to disagree — go ahead. Where shall we start?
de-b2-leserbrief.goal: The point of agreement and the objection have been given separately, the objection has been justified and a concrete suggestion has been left.

de-b2-doku.scene: You are telling a friend about the documentary you watched yesterday: what it shows, which scene shook you, what the film lacks and who you would recommend it to.
de-b2-doku.partner: a friend who does not like documentaries and needs persuading
de-b2-doku.openingTr: A documentary? Honestly, I usually fall asleep in those. What was so special about it?
de-b2-doku.goal: The subject, the most striking scene and the shortcoming of the documentary have been described, and your friend has decided whether to watch it.

de-b2-podcast-b2.scene: You are recording your own podcast episode and you have a guest. Open the episode, introduce your guest, ask two questions and finish with a closing line.
de-b2-podcast-b2.partner: an excitable podcast guest who gives long answers
de-b2-podcast-b2.openingTr: Thanks for the invitation! Tell us briefly: who is your podcast actually meant for?
de-b2-podcast-b2.goal: The episode has been opened, the guest introduced, at least two questions asked and the episode finished with a closing line.

de-b2-pressefreiheit.scene: You are discussing the role of the press with an acquaintance. Keep apart what you know, what you have heard and what you guess, state your view carefully but clearly, and answer their objection.
de-b2-pressefreiheit.partner: an acquaintance who distrusts the media and asks for examples
de-b2-pressefreiheit.openingTr: I haven't believed the media for a long time. Why should I trust what's written there at all?
de-b2-pressefreiheit.goal: What is known, heard and guessed have been separated, the view has been given with reasons and the objection has been answered.

de-b2-influencer.scene: You and a friend are arguing about the line between advertising and genuine opinion on social media: what has to be labelled, who stays credible, what you trust.
de-b2-influencer.partner: a friend who defends the people they follow
de-b2-influencer.openingTr: She always says she uses it herself. Why shouldn't I believe her?
de-b2-influencer.goal: The line between advertising and genuine opinion has been discussed with examples and a shared test of what to trust has been reached.

de-b2-falschmeldung.scene: An acquaintance is telling you a story you know to be false. Restate the claim in your own words, question the source, set the truth against it and show how it could be checked.
de-b2-falschmeldung.partner: an acquaintance who shared the story and does not give up easily
de-b2-falschmeldung.openingTr: It was everywhere! Are you telling me they all just made it up?
de-b2-falschmeldung.goal: The claim has been restated, the source questioned, the truth set against it and a way of checking has been shown.

de-b2-partizip-1.scene: You and an acquaintance are discussing a trend that has grown in recent years (screen time, rents, the cost of travel — whichever you choose). Describe what is rising, what is falling and what you have noticed yourself.
de-b2-partizip-1.partner: an acquaintance who is keen on figures and asks for examples
de-b2-partizip-1.openingTr: Something's struck me lately: everything is getting dearer, but nobody talks about the running costs. What do you observe?
de-b2-partizip-1.goal: The rising and falling trends have been described with examples and the two of you have met on a shared observation.

de-b2-partizip-2.scene: A new method is being proposed at work. Ask how it was developed, whether it has been tested and what results were obtained; then give your own assessment.
de-b2-partizip-2.partner: a project lead who defends the method and can give detail
de-b2-partizip-2.openingTr: The newly developed method saves us a third of the time. Where do you see the problem?
de-b2-partizip-2.goal: How the method was developed and tested has been found out and the learner's assessment has been given with reasons.

de-b2-ki-alltag.scene: You and a colleague are arguing about how much room artificial intelligence should have in your work: what can be automated, what should not be, and where the responsibility stays.
de-b2-ki-alltag.partner: a colleague keen on AI who sees no limits
de-b2-ki-alltag.openingTr: I have almost everything drafted for me now — it saves an enormous amount of time. Where would you draw the line?
de-b2-ki-alltag.goal: The work that can and should not be automated has been separated and where the responsibility stays has been discussed.

de-b2-studie.scene: You are telling a friend about a study you read: what it found, how many people took part, how reliable the result is and what you think.
de-b2-studie.partner: a friend who is sceptical of studies and asks about the method
de-b2-studie.openingTr: Studies say something different every year. How many people were even in it?
de-b2-studie.goal: The finding, the method and the sample of the study have been described and a shared conclusion has been reached about how reliable it is.

de-b2-experiment.scene: You are explaining a simple experiment that can be done at home: what is needed, how it is done, what is measured and why the result is surprising. Describe each step with a clause of means.
de-b2-experiment.partner: a curious listener who questions every step
de-b2-experiment.openingTr: An experiment in the kitchen? All right — but first tell me: what exactly is it meant to find out?
de-b2-experiment.goal: The aim, the steps and the result of the experiment have been described, and the listener could sum it up in their own words.

de-b2-datenschutz.scene: You are discussing with a service provider's agent how your data is used: what is stored, who it is passed to, how long it is kept and what you can object to.
de-b2-datenschutz.partner: an agent who knows the rules but does not want to go into detail
de-b2-datenschutz.openingTr: You have a question about data protection? In principle we of course comply with all requirements. What exactly would you like to know?
de-b2-datenschutz.goal: Which data is stored, who it is shared with and how long it is kept have been found out, and an objection has been put.

de-b2-weltraum.scene: You and a friend are arguing about how far climate measures should reach into everyday life. Justify your view, answer the other side's objection and meet on common ground.
de-b2-weltraum.partner: a friend who finds the measures excessive but does care about nature
de-b2-weltraum.openingTr: Bans on everything — and the threatened forest doesn't grow any faster for it. Do you really think that's right?
de-b2-weltraum.goal: Both sides have justified their view, the objections have been answered and common ground has been found.

de-b2-medizin-fortschritt.scene: You are telling an acquaintance about a medical advance you heard of: what was found, how and how far it was tested, what it means for whom and what to be careful about.
de-b2-medizin-fortschritt.partner: an acquaintance who is hopeful but wary of hype
de-b2-medizin-fortschritt.openingTr: I heard about that — apparently it has all been tested already. Is that really true?
de-b2-medizin-fortschritt.goal: What the advance is, how it was tested and what it means for whom have been described, and a warning against the hype has been given.

de-b2-technikfrust.scene: Your computer keeps freezing and you are asking a friend who knows about technology for help. Describe the problem, say when it happens, say what you have tried and repeat the fix in your own words.
de-b2-technikfrust.partner: a patient friend who always asks 'have you restarted it' first
de-b2-technikfrust.openingTr: Wait, slowly. When does it freeze — always, or only with certain programs?
de-b2-technikfrust.goal: The problem has been described, what was tried has been said and the fix has been learnt and repeated back.

de-b2-zukunftstechnologien.scene: You and an acquaintance are arguing about the future of a new technology. Keep apart what is certain, what is likely and what is only hearsay; justify your own prediction and say where you might be wrong.
de-b2-zukunftstechnologien.partner: an excitable acquaintance who believes every new claim at once
de-b2-zukunftstechnologien.openingTr: In five years nobody will be driving themselves, they say. Do you believe that too?
de-b2-zukunftstechnologien.goal: The certain, the likely and the hearsay have been separated, your own prediction has been justified and where you might be wrong has been said.

de-b2-wegen-trotz.scene: An event you were going to has been cancelled because of the weather. Talk to the organiser: find out why it was cancelled, ask whether anything can still go ahead, and discuss a new date or a refund.
de-b2-wegen-trotz.partner: a sorry organiser trying to come up with a solution
de-b2-wegen-trotz.openingTr: We had to cancel because of the storm — I really am sorry. Had you already set off?
de-b2-wegen-trotz.goal: The reason for the cancellation has been found out and a conclusion has been reached about a new date or a refund.

de-b2-aufgrund-infolge.scene: An authority's service has been suspended and you have rung for information. Ask the grounds for the decision, find out how long it will last, describe how it affects you and ask for an alternative.
de-b2-aufgrund-infolge.partner: an official who speaks formally and repeats the rules
de-b2-aufgrund-infolge.openingTr: In view of the current situation the service has been suspended for the time being. What is it about in your case?
de-b2-aufgrund-infolge.goal: The grounds and length of the decision have been found out, the effect has been described and an alternative or an exception has been discussed.

de-b2-inflation.scene: You and an acquaintance are talking about the cost of living: where you feel it most, what you have changed, what is different from last year. Use concrete examples.
de-b2-inflation.partner: an acquaintance who gives their own examples and makes comparisons
de-b2-inflation.openingTr: I looked at the receipt yesterday and couldn't believe it. Where do you notice it most?
de-b2-inflation.goal: Where the cost of living is felt most and the habits that have changed have been described on both sides.

de-b2-wohnungsmarkt.scene: You and an acquaintance are talking about the housing market: why rents have risen so far, what the difference is between the centre and the country, what can be done. Make the link with clauses of proportion.
de-b2-wohnungsmarkt.partner: an acquaintance who tells their own flat-hunting story and is keen on solutions
de-b2-wohnungsmarkt.openingTr: I've been looking for four months and still found nothing. What's actually behind it?
de-b2-wohnungsmarkt.goal: The reason rents have risen has been explained with clauses of proportion and at least one solution has been discussed.

de-b2-arbeitsmarkt.scene: You are talking to the manager of a business that cannot find staff: which posts are open, why they cannot be filled, what has been tried and what could be done.
de-b2-arbeitsmarkt.partner: a tired business manager looking for a solution
de-b2-arbeitsmarkt.openingTr: We've been looking for a year — the post simply cannot be filled. Have you any idea why that is?
de-b2-arbeitsmarkt.goal: Which posts are open and why has been discussed, what has been tried has been found out and at least one suggestion has been made.

de-b2-ehrenamt-b2.scene: You are talking to a representative of a voluntary organisation: what exactly the organisation does, how it manages it, how you could contribute and how much time it takes.
de-b2-ehrenamt-b2.partner: a representative who loves describing the work and is looking for new volunteers
de-b2-ehrenamt-b2.openingTr: How nice that you ask! Most people have no idea how much here runs unpaid. What are you interested in?
de-b2-ehrenamt-b2.goal: What the organisation does and how it manages it have been found out, and a concrete step has been settled on how and for how long you would contribute.

de-b2-generationen.scene: You and an acquaintance from a different generation are arguing about an issue between the generations (work ethic, technology, housing). Say what each side is right about, name the prejudices and find common ground.
de-b2-generationen.partner: an acquaintance who defends their own generation but is open to listening
de-b2-generationen.openingTr: Your generation wants everything at once, that's the problem. Or do you see it differently?
de-b2-generationen.goal: What each generation is right about has been said, the prejudices have been named and common ground has been found.

de-b2-landflucht.scene: You and an acquaintance are arguing about whether it is better to live in the city or the country. Link the advantages of each with clauses of proportion, justify your own preference and concede one of their points.
de-b2-landflucht.partner: an acquaintance who is seriously thinking of moving to the country
de-b2-landflucht.openingTr: I'm seriously thinking of moving to the country. But everyone says I'd regret it. What do you think?
de-b2-landflucht.goal: The advantages of both sides have been linked with clauses of proportion, your preference has been justified and one of their points has been conceded.

de-b2-steuern-b2.scene: You and an acquaintance are arguing about where public money should be spent: what should get more, where cuts could be made, who benefits. Justify your view.
de-b2-steuern-b2.partner: an acquaintance who questions every item and asks for examples
de-b2-steuern-b2.openingTr: I pay a good deal of tax every month and see little of it. What is the money actually spent on?
de-b2-steuern-b2.goal: Where the money goes has been discussed with examples, the case for spending more on one item has been justified and agreement has been reached on one point.

de-b2-wahl.scene: You and an acquaintance are talking about a coming election: what has been promised, what the polls show, what you expect and what you decide on. Keep the promises, the polls and your own prediction apart.
de-b2-wahl.partner: an undecided acquaintance who does not know which promise to believe
de-b2-wahl.openingTr: They all promise the same thing and in the end nothing gets done. What do you decide on, then?
de-b2-wahl.goal: The promises, the polls and your own prediction have been separated and a concrete test for deciding has been given.

de-b2-roman.scene: You are recommending a novel you have read to a friend: what it is about, what the narrator is like, what it does well and who it suits. Introduce the book with relative clauses.
de-b2-roman.partner: a friend who is put off by thick books and needs persuading
de-b2-roman.openingTr: Six hundred pages? Tell me in one sentence what it's about — then I'll decide.
de-b2-roman.goal: The subject and the strength of the book have been described and your friend has decided whether to read it.

de-b2-dessen-deren.scene: You and a friend are talking about works you love: which book's ending, which film's music, which band's lyrics moved you. Introduce each in one sentence with a relative clause of possession.
de-b2-dessen-deren.partner: a curious friend who gives their own examples too
de-b2-dessen-deren.openingTr: I like asking this: is there a book whose ending really floored you?
de-b2-dessen-deren.goal: At least two works have been introduced with relative clauses of possession and why they moved you has been described.

de-b2-theater.scene: You are coming out of the theatre and giving your verdict on the play to the person beside you: what you think of the staging, the acting and the set, what you did not like and whether you would recommend it anyway.
de-b2-theater.partner: a theatregoer who loved the play and is curious about your objections
de-b2-theater.openingTr: I thought that was magnificent — the set especially. How did you like it?
de-b2-theater.goal: A separate judgement has been given on the staging, the acting and the set, and whether to recommend it has been said.

de-b2-museum-fuehrung.scene: You are guiding a small group round a museum. Say where the tour began, introduce one work (when it was made, from which period), answer a question and lead the tour on to the next room.
de-b2-museum-fuehrung.partner: a curious visitor who asks for detail
de-b2-museum-fuehrung.openingTr: Excuse me — do you know when this painting was actually made?
de-b2-museum-fuehrung.goal: When a work was made and its period have been described, a question has been answered and the tour has been led on to the next stop.

de-b2-musik-analyse.scene: You and a friend are talking about why music affects people. Describe a piece that moves you, say how it has its effect with a clause of means, and listen to their example too.
de-b2-musik-analyse.partner: a friend who knows about music and gives technical detail too
de-b2-musik-analyse.openingTr: Some pieces lodge in my memory straight away — and I don't quite know why. Do you know that feeling?
de-b2-musik-analyse.goal: A piece that moves you has been described, how it has its effect has been explained and the other person's example has been discussed too.

de-b2-fotografie.scene: You are coming out of a match and giving your verdict with the supporter beside you: who played better, whether the referee's decisions were right, whether the defeat was deserved and what happens in the title race.
de-b2-fotografie.partner: a supporter defending their own team and angry with the referee
de-b2-fotografie.openingTr: Did you see that? Without the referee we'd have won that match — or do you see it differently?
de-b2-fotografie.goal: The course of the match and the referee's decisions have been judged and whether the defeat was deserved has been argued.

de-b2-architektur.scene: An old building in your area is to be demolished and replaced with a new one. You and a neighbour are arguing: should the building be preserved, what do the planning rules say, what could the alternative be.
de-b2-architektur.partner: a practical neighbour who is in favour of the new building
de-b2-architektur.openingTr: The old house has stood empty for years. Why shouldn't it just be pulled down?
de-b2-architektur.goal: Whether the building is worth preserving has been justified from both sides and an alternative has been discussed.

de-b2-festival.scene: You are telling a friend about the festival you went to: which performance was the best, what the atmosphere was like, what was hard and whether you would go again.
de-b2-festival.partner: a friend thinking of going who asks practical questions
de-b2-festival.openingTr: I'm thinking of going next year. Was it worth it — honestly?
de-b2-festival.goal: The best performance, the atmosphere and the difficulties have been described, and whether you would go again has been said.

de-b2-kabarett.scene: You are planning a holiday and taking advice: which region is supposedly worth seeing, what you are not sure is true, what you are guessing yourself. Keep what you heard apart from what you guess.
de-b2-kabarett.partner: a friend who has not been but repeats what an acquaintance told them
de-b2-kabarett.openingTr: Everyone says the coast there is supposed to be completely unspoilt. Do you really believe that?
de-b2-kabarett.goal: What was heard and what is guessed have been given separately and a conclusion has been reached about whether to go.

de-b2-kunstmarkt.scene: You and an acquaintance are arguing about the price of works of art: does it make sense to pay millions for a painting, what sets the value, what you would pay for. Make the link with clauses of proportion.
de-b2-kunstmarkt.partner: an acquaintance who finds the art market absurd and asks for examples
de-b2-kunstmarkt.openingTr: Two million for a picture anyone could copy — can you explain that to me?
de-b2-kunstmarkt.goal: What sets the value has been argued, both sides have given reasons and a shared test has been discussed.

de-b2-gehaltsverhandlung.scene: You are in your annual review with your boss and you want a rise. Put your expectation in the subjunctive, justify it with figures, answer the objection and settle on an outcome or a new date.
de-b2-gehaltsverhandlung.partner: a department head who cites the budget but is open to a good case
de-b2-gehaltsverhandlung.openingTr: You wanted to talk about pay. Before we start: what did you have in mind?
de-b2-gehaltsverhandlung.goal: The expectation has been given with a figure, justified, and tied to an outcome or a date for a further meeting.

de-b2-sparen-anlegen.scene: You are discussing a savings plan with a bank adviser: how much you can put aside, how much risk you can take, which term suits you. Discuss risk against return with clauses of proportion.
de-b2-sparen-anlegen.partner: a bank adviser inclined to sell a product but honest in answering
de-b2-sparen-anlegen.openingTr: You'd like to invest something. First tell me: how long can you do without the money?
de-b2-sparen-anlegen.goal: The term, the amount and the level of risk have been made clear and a plan has been agreed.

de-b2-selbststaendig.scene: You are discussing your plan with a start-up adviser: what you want to set up, who your customers are, on what condition it works and what would make you give up. Tie every step to a condition.
de-b2-selbststaendig.partner: a start-up adviser who questions your optimism and asks for figures
de-b2-selbststaendig.openingTr: Before we talk about the idea: how long could you hold out if there's hardly any turnover in the first year?
de-b2-selbststaendig.goal: The idea, the customers and how long you could hold out have been described, and the condition for going on and the point of giving up have been said.

de-b2-buerokratie-gruendung.scene: You are at the enquiries desk of the chamber of commerce asking what is needed to set up on your own: which registration, which documents, in what order, how long it takes and what it costs.
de-b2-buerokratie-gruendung.partner: an enquiries clerk who lists the steps formally and points you to forms
de-b2-buerokratie-gruendung.openingTr: You'd like to register a business. Have you any idea yet what legal form it should take?
de-b2-buerokratie-gruendung.goal: The documents needed, the order of the steps and the timescale have been found out and a concrete next step has been settled.

de-b2-work-life.scene: You are talking to your boss about your workload: messages after hours, availability at the weekend and how the load is shared. Say what you want in clauses of purpose, suggest a limit without blame and agree an arrangement.
de-b2-work-life.partner: a well-meaning boss who takes availability for granted
de-b2-work-life.openingTr: You've seemed tense lately. Is it the amount, or is there something else?
de-b2-work-life.goal: Where the load lies has been described without blame, a concrete limit has been suggested and agreed.

de-b2-networking-b2.scene: You are talking to a contact in your field and asking them for a recommendation or an introduction. Say what you are looking for, describe briefly what you do, ask for the recommendation and say what you can offer in return.
de-b2-networking-b2.partner: a contact who is willing to help but careful about who they recommend
de-b2-networking-b2.openingTr: Good to hear from you. Tell me — what exactly are you looking for?
de-b2-networking-b2.goal: What you are looking for and what you do have been described, a concrete recommendation or introduction has been asked for and what you offer in return has been said.

de-b2-jobwechsel.scene: A friend is thinking of leaving a secure job and asking what you think. Describe your own experience or observation in clauses of contrast, name the risks and give them a concrete piece of advice.
de-b2-jobwechsel.partner: an undecided friend who is both excited and afraid
de-b2-jobwechsel.openingTr: The job is secure, the money is fine — and still I want to leave. Am I mad?
de-b2-jobwechsel.goal: The risks and the reasons have been discussed in clauses of contrast and a concrete piece of advice has been given.

de-b2-rente.scene: You are discussing your pension plan with an adviser: what you have paid in so far, what the gap will be, what you can do. Keep the certain, the likely and the hearsay apart.
de-b2-rente.partner: a pension adviser who talks in figures and does not rush you
de-b2-rente.openingTr: A lot of people put this off. First tell me: what have you paid in so far?
de-b2-rente.goal: The current position, the expected gap and a concrete step to take have been discussed.

de-b2-nebenjob.scene: You and a friend are talking about taking a second job: why it is needed, how much time it takes, whether permission is required and when the load becomes too much. Build cause and contrast with genitive prepositions.
de-b2-nebenjob.partner: a friend who has a second job and shares their experience
de-b2-nebenjob.openingTr: I've been doing it on the side for a year. Honestly, there are a few things I should have known first — what do you want to know?
de-b2-nebenjob.goal: The reason, the time it takes and the question of permission have been discussed and a conclusion has been reached about whether to do it.

de-b2-teures-hobby.scene: An acquaintance is surprised at your expensive hobby. Say what you spend on what, defend why it is worth it, say what you give up in return and explain where you draw the line.
de-b2-teures-hobby.partner: an acquaintance who finds the spending unnecessary but is curious
de-b2-teures-hobby.openingTr: So much money for a hobby whose point I can't see — what does it actually give you?
de-b2-teures-hobby.goal: The size of the spending, why it is worth it and what is given up have been described, and the other person has at least said they understand.

de-b2-als-ob.scene: You and a friend are talking about the recent behaviour of someone you both know: how they are behaving, how it seems to you, what might really be going on and what you should do.
de-b2-als-ob.partner: a worried friend who does not want to jump to conclusions
de-b2-als-ob.openingTr: He acts as if everything's fine — but something isn't right. Do you notice it too?
de-b2-als-ob.goal: The observations have been shared, hasty conclusions have been avoided and a concrete step has been settled.

de-b2-vermutungen.scene: You and a colleague are reading an uncertain situation (a delay, a silence, a decision). Give each guess according to how sure you are, say which possibilities you rule out, and settle the next step.
de-b2-vermutungen.partner: a colleague who jumps straight to the worst case
de-b2-vermutungen.openingTr: Three days and no answer. That can only mean one thing, can't it?
de-b2-vermutungen.goal: The guesses have been graded by certainty and a next step has been settled without jumping to the worst case.

de-b2-koerpersprache.scene: You have a difficult meeting tomorrow and you and a friend are discussing how to carry yourself: how to stand, what not to do, how to take the edge off the nerves. Build each piece of advice with a clause of means.
de-b2-koerpersprache.partner: a friend who has had many such meetings and gives concrete advice
de-b2-koerpersprache.openingTr: I can always tell straight away when someone's nervous. What do you normally do with your hands?
de-b2-koerpersprache.goal: At least two concrete pieces of advice on how to behave have been given and the learner has said in their own words what they will do tomorrow.

de-b2-missverstaendnis.scene: Something you said was misunderstood and the other person is hurt. Accept how it sounded, explain what you meant, apologise if you need to and suggest a step to put the relationship right.
de-b2-missverstaendnis.partner: a close friend who is hurt but willing to talk
de-b2-missverstaendnis.openingTr: I thought for a long time about whether to bring it up. It sounded as if you wanted to show me up in front of everyone — was that what you meant?
de-b2-missverstaendnis.goal: How it sounded has been accepted, what was meant has been explained and a concrete step to put things right has been settled.

de-b2-motivation-psy.scene: You are talking to a friend about something you have been putting off for months: what you are putting off, what excuses you use, what the first step could be and how you will keep going.
de-b2-motivation-psy.partner: a friend who does not judge but wants a concrete step
de-b2-motivation-psy.openingTr: You've been talking about it for months. What's the smallest thing you could do this week?
de-b2-motivation-psy.goal: The thing put off and the excuses have been named and the smallest concrete step for this week has been settled.

de-b2-gewohnheiten.scene: You and a friend are talking about building a habit: which habit you want, what your trigger is, which bad habit you want to drop and what your plan is for the first week.
de-b2-gewohnheiten.partner: a friend who likes planning and describes their own attempts
de-b2-gewohnheiten.openingTr: I've tried three times and given up three times. What's the trigger for you?
de-b2-gewohnheiten.goal: The habit wanted, its trigger and the plan for the first week have been discussed and both of you have made a concrete promise.

de-b2-empathie.scene: A friend is telling you about a disagreement with a third person. Listen first, then set out the other side's point of view as well, ask a question without judging and think together about what they could do.
de-b2-empathie.partner: a hurt friend who is sure they are in the right
de-b2-empathie.openingTr: She just hung up. After everything I've done for her — am I really overreacting?
de-b2-empathie.goal: Your friend's story has been heard, the other side's view has been set out without judgement and a next step has been thought through together.

de-b2-streitkultur.scene: You and someone close are talking about how your last argument went: what went wrong, who did what, which rule you will keep to next time. Use 'I' language instead of blame.
de-b2-streitkultur.partner: a well-meaning person close to you who is ready to get defensive
de-b2-streitkultur.openingTr: We both said things yesterday that we didn't mean. How do we do it better next time?
de-b2-streitkultur.goal: What went wrong has been said in 'I' language and at least two rules for next time have been agreed.

de-b2-perfektionismus.scene: You are talking to a friend about the high standards you set yourself: where you push yourself, where the standard comes from, what you could let go and what 'good enough' means to you.
de-b2-perfektionismus.partner: a friend who knows you and has noticed your extreme standards
de-b2-perfektionismus.openingTr: You rebuilt that presentation four times. When is it good enough for you?
de-b2-perfektionismus.goal: The standard you set yourself has been named, where it comes from has been discussed and what could be let go has been said.

de-b2-veraenderung-b2.scene: A friend is on the edge of a big change and hesitating. Ask what they are afraid of, discuss on what condition they could do it, find the smallest first step together and decide when they will take it.
de-b2-veraenderung-b2.partner: a friend at the point of decision who is both willing and afraid
de-b2-veraenderung-b2.openingTr: I know that I want it. But every time I'm nearly there, I find a reason to wait. Do you know that feeling?
de-b2-veraenderung-b2.goal: The fear has been named, the condition for doing it has been discussed and the first step and its date have been settled.

de-b2-formeller-brief.scene: A colleague has to write a formal letter and is asking for your help. Work out together what goes in the subject line, which salutation to use, what to say in what order in the body and how to close.
de-b2-formeller-brief.partner: a colleague new to formal writing who asks step by step
de-b2-formeller-brief.openingTr: I have to write to the authority and I don't even know how to start. What actually comes first?
de-b2-formeller-brief.goal: The subject line, the salutation, the order of the body and the closing have been worked out together.

de-b2-anfrage.scene: You are asking a company for a quotation and for information: the price, the delivery time, the terms. Ask in polite forms, clear up a point left open and ask for written confirmation.
de-b2-anfrage.partner: a helpful company employee who wants everything in writing
de-b2-anfrage.openingTr: Many thanks for your interest. What exactly would you like to know?
de-b2-anfrage.goal: The price, the delivery time and the terms have been found out and written confirmation has been promised.

de-b2-angebot-vergleichen.scene: You and a colleague are comparing three quotations: what each offers on price, scope and time, what the risk is and which one you choose. Justify your decision.
de-b2-angebot-vergleichen.partner: a colleague who backs the cheapest and plays down the risks
de-b2-angebot-vergleichen.openingTr: The cheapest is a thousand euros less. Is there a reason we shouldn't take it?
de-b2-angebot-vergleichen.goal: The three quotations have been weighed on price, scope and risk and one has been chosen with reasons.

de-b2-bewerbungsgespraech-b2.scene: You are at the end of a job interview and it is your turn to ask. Ask at least three things (the process, the team, the probation period or the expectations), sum one answer up in your own words and find out when you will hear.
de-b2-bewerbungsgespraech-b2.partner: a plain-spoken employer who answers questions in detail
de-b2-bewerbungsgespraech-b2.openingTr: That's everything from our side. Now it's your turn — what else would you like to know?
de-b2-bewerbungsgespraech-b2.goal: At least three questions have been asked, one answer has been summed up and confirmed and it has been found out when you will hear.

de-b2-praesentation-abschluss.scene: You are at the end of your presentation. Sum up your findings, give your conclusion in one sentence, add a short look ahead, thank the audience and answer the final question.
de-b2-praesentation-abschluss.partner: a listener who asks about the next step at the close
de-b2-praesentation-abschluss.openingTr: Before you close: what does that mean for us in concrete terms next quarter?
de-b2-praesentation-abschluss.goal: The findings have been summed up, the conclusion and the look ahead have been given and the final question has been answered to close the talk.

de-b2-verabschiedung-kollegen.scene: A colleague is leaving and you are at their leaving party. Recall the time you spent together, say what they gave you, pass on your good wishes and get a promise to keep in touch.
de-b2-verabschiedung-kollegen.partner: a colleague who is moved and looking back
de-b2-verabschiedung-kollegen.openingTr: Five years — I can hardly believe it. Do you remember how chaotic my first day was?
de-b2-verabschiedung-kollegen.goal: A shared memory has been recalled, good wishes have been passed on and a concrete promise to keep in touch has been made.

de-b2-empfehlung-schreiben.scene: A former teammate is asking you for a reference. Discuss which strengths you will write about, ask which example to use, say where the limit of your honesty lies and say when it will be ready.
de-b2-empfehlung-schreiben.partner: an excited former teammate who wants a lot written about them
de-b2-empfehlung-schreiben.openingTr: Would that be all right with you? And could you write something about my leadership qualities too?
de-b2-empfehlung-schreiben.goal: Which strengths and which example will go in have been settled, the limit of honesty has been stated and a delivery time has been given.

de-b2-kulturschock-rueckwaerts.scene: You have gone back to your old home after a long time and you are talking to someone close: what has changed, how you have changed, where you feel you belong and how it will be from now on.
de-b2-kulturschock-rueckwaerts.partner: someone close who has missed you but has noticed you have changed
de-b2-kulturschock-rueckwaerts.openingTr: You're back — and yet something is different. Is it us or is it you?
de-b2-kulturschock-rueckwaerts.goal: What has changed has been described from both sides, the sense of belonging has been expressed and something has been said about what comes next.

de-b2-c1-vorbereitung.scene: You are discussing your preparation for C1 with a teacher: which skill you are good at, where you are weak, how long you need and how you will work.
de-b2-c1-vorbereitung.partner: a teacher who assesses honestly and likes making plans
de-b2-c1-vorbereitung.openingTr: You've finished B2 — well done. Tell me honestly: where do you think there is still a gap?
de-b2-c1-vorbereitung.goal: The strong and weak skills have been named, a timescale has been discussed and a concrete study plan has been settled.

de-b2-rueckblick.scene: You are having a review with your teacher at the end of B2: how the road has gone, what was hardest, what you can really do now, what you are proud of and what comes next.
de-b2-rueckblick.partner: an honest and supportive teacher who has followed you from the start
de-b2-rueckblick.openingTr: A hundred lessons done. Before we close: what can you do today that you couldn't at the start?
de-b2-rueckblick.goal: The road travelled, the hardest part and what you can now do have been described, and the next goal has been given.

de-c1-fvg-treffen.scene: You are in a board meeting and a hard decision has to be made. Say which options are in question, rule one out with reasons, state the scope of the decision and bring it to a resolution.
de-c1-fvg-treffen.partner: a board member who wants a quick decision and plays down the risks
de-c1-fvg-treffen.openingTr: We've been going round in circles for two meetings. In your view, which options are still in question at all?
de-c1-fvg-treffen.goal: The options in question have been listed, one has been ruled out with reasons, the scope of the decision has been stated and a resolution has been reached.

de-c1-fvg-stellen.scene: You are making a formal request to an institution: what you are applying for, which right you want to exercise, what reservation you have and when it takes effect. Use institutional language.
de-c1-fvg-stellen.partner: an official bound to the formalities who knows the set phrases by heart
de-c1-fvg-stellen.openingTr: You'd like to submit an application — what exactly does your request relate to?
de-c1-fvg-stellen.goal: The subject of the application, the right relied on and the date of effect have been made clear, and a reservation has been put on record.

de-c1-diplomatisch.scene: You disagree with your superior's proposal in a meeting. First show that you have understood, put your objection in the subjunctive, justify your reservation and offer an alternative. If you are turned down, hold your position without damaging the relationship.
de-c1-diplomatisch.partner: a senior manager attached to their proposal who takes objections personally
de-c1-diplomatisch.openingTr: I get the impression you're not convinced. Do say it straight out — what's bothering you?
de-c1-diplomatisch.goal: The objection has been made with reasons and tact, an alternative has been offered and the conversation has been brought to a conclusion without damaging the relationship.

de-c1-zwischen-zeilen.scene: A colleague has criticised you indirectly. Say what you have sensed, ask directly, put your own reservation without hiding it and clear the matter up between you.
de-c1-zwischen-zeilen.partner: a colleague who avoids speaking plainly and talks in hints
de-c1-zwischen-zeilen.openingTr: Well, in itself your draft is fine. Actually I'd only have … well, done it differently. Do you know what I mean?
de-c1-zwischen-zeilen.goal: The criticism behind the hint has been said openly, both sides have put their reservations directly and the matter has been cleared up.

de-c1-krisenkommunikation.scene: Something has gone wrong at your organisation and a journalist is talking to you. Express regret, describe what happened in corporate language, say which measures have been started and say when you will report back.
de-c1-krisenkommunikation.partner: an insistent journalist looking for someone to blame and wanting a name
de-c1-krisenkommunikation.openingTr: Who bears the responsibility for this? And please don't tell me that measures have been initiated.
de-c1-krisenkommunikation.goal: Regret has been expressed, the incident and the measures have been described, the question of responsibility has been met rather than dodged and a date for the next update has been given.

de-c1-verhandlung-c1.scene: You are putting a new subject on the table in a negotiation that has long been stuck. Open the subject, say what risk you are taking on, say what you want in return and bring it to a conclusion or a further round.
de-c1-verhandlung-c1.partner: an experienced and patient counterpart who does not concede easily
de-c1-verhandlung-c1.openingTr: We're at the same point as three weeks ago. Have you brought anything new?
de-c1-verhandlung-c1.goal: A new subject has been put on the table, the risk taken on and the return asked for have been stated and it has been brought to a conclusion or a further round.

de-c1-fuehrung.scene: You are running a project without any formal authority and someone on the team is letting their work slip. Name the problem, give direction without giving orders, leave the responsibility with them and say you will support them.
de-c1-fuehrung.partner: a well-meaning team member who questions your authority
de-c1-fuehrung.openingTr: With respect — you're not formally my line manager. Why should I do it that way now?
de-c1-fuehrung.goal: The problem has been named, direction has been given without an order, the responsibility has been left with them and support has been promised.

de-c1-buerojargon.scene: You are talking to a colleague after a meeting: work out together what the jargon in the meeting actually meant, make clear who has taken on what and settle the next step.
de-c1-buerojargon.partner: a colleague fluent in the jargon but open to making things clear
de-c1-buerojargon.openingTr: 'We'll take that away and align on it afterwards' — honestly, do you know who's doing what now?
de-c1-buerojargon.goal: The real meaning behind the jargon has been worked out, who has taken on what has been made clear and the next step has been tied to a date.

de-c1-pitch.scene: You are giving a three-minute pitch to an investor. Bring the listener in, state the problem and the solution, explain what sets you apart, answer the 'why now' question and ask for a next step.
de-c1-pitch.partner: an investor who cuts you short and asks hard questions
de-c1-pitch.openingTr: You have three minutes. And please don't start with the company history — what problem are you solving, and with what?
de-c1-pitch.goal: The problem, the solution and what sets you apart have been described, 'why now' has been answered and a concrete next step has been asked for.

de-c1-konfliktmoderation.scene: You are mediating between two colleagues. Report what each side has said impartially, find the common ground, make a suggestion and bring them to a step both will accept.
de-c1-konfliktmoderation.partner: a colleague certain they are in the right and unwilling to hear the other side
de-c1-konfliktmoderation.openingTr: Let me say straight away: I have done nothing wrong. What has the other side claimed, then?
de-c1-konfliktmoderation.goal: Both sides' views have been reported impartially, common ground has been found and a step both accept has been agreed.

de-c1-doch.scene: A friend does not want to come to an event. Invite them, argue against their reasons, answer their negative questions with the positive 'doch' and bring it to a decision.
de-c1-doch.partner: a reluctant friend who finds an excuse for everything but can be talked round
de-c1-doch.openingTr: You're not seriously trying to talk me into this thing, are you?
de-c1-doch.goal: The invitation has been made, the excuses have been argued against and it has been decided whether your friend is coming.

de-c1-ja-mal.scene: You have run into someone in the street you have not seen for a long time. Show your surprise, ask them to tell you something, give your own news and arrange something to meet again.
de-c1-ja-mal.partner: an old acquaintance who is delighted to see you and has a lot to tell
de-c1-ja-mal.openingTr: I don't believe it — is that really you? How long has it been now?
de-c1-ja-mal.goal: News has been exchanged both ways and something concrete has been arranged to meet again.

de-c1-eben-halt.scene: Something has gone wrong that you cannot change (a cancellation, a delay, a missed chance). Talk to a friend: say what happened, say you are angry, then move into the tone of acceptance and settle what you will do next.
de-c1-eben-halt.partner: a friend who tries to fix it first and then accepts it with you
de-c1-eben-halt.openingTr: And there's really nothing more to be done? Nothing at all?
de-c1-eben-halt.goal: The setback has been described, the anger has been voiced, the tone has moved to acceptance and a step for what comes next has been settled.

de-c1-wohl.scene: You and a colleague are talking about a decision that has not been announced. Give your guesses while showing you are not sure, keep apart what you have grounds for and what you have not, and decide what you will do.
de-c1-wohl.partner: a colleague who likes to speak in certainties and presents guesses as facts
de-c1-wohl.openingTr: They'll have decided it long ago. Or have you got any grounds to think otherwise?
de-c1-wohl.goal: What is grounded and what is not have been separated, the guesses have been given without certainty and it has been settled what to do.

de-c1-schon.scene: A friend has had bad news and is low. Listen first, then calm them, give hope without overdoing it and offer something concrete.
de-c1-schon.partner: a sad friend who is not easily comforted but wants to talk
de-c1-schon.openingTr: Please don't tell me it'll all be fine again. I've heard that so often — what is there to get better?
de-c1-schon.goal: Your friend has been heard, calmed without empty comfort, and concrete help has been offered.

de-c1-partikel-streit.scene: You are waiting on a piece of work and the other side keeps putting it off. Show your impatience in measure, give a warning, acknowledge that you are pressing them and agree a deadline.
de-c1-partikel-streit.partner: someone who keeps putting it off and always has an excuse ready
de-c1-partikel-streit.openingTr: I know, I know — I'm on it. Does it really have to be today?
de-c1-partikel-streit.goal: Impatience has been shown in measure, a warning has been given and a binding deadline has been agreed.

de-c1-untertreibung.scene: You are giving your verdict on a colleague's work. Give measured praise, say what is lacking politely, explain if they ask whether you disliked it, and give a clear conclusion.
de-c1-untertreibung.partner: a colleague used to lavish praise who finds measured language cold
de-c1-untertreibung.openingTr: 'Not bad' — does that mean good or bad? One never knows with you lot.
de-c1-untertreibung.goal: Measured praise and polite criticism have been given separately, the misunderstanding has been cleared up and a clear conclusion has been stated.

de-c1-smalltalk-c1.scene: You are making small talk with a stranger at a work function. Open the conversation, find a subject in common, take it further with an impersonal question and leave politely.
de-c1-smalltalk-c1.partner: a polite guest who is quiet at first and opens up as they talk
de-c1-smalltalk-c1.openingTr: Hardly anyone knows anyone here, do they? Do you come to these things often?
de-c1-smalltalk-c1.goal: The conversation has been opened, a subject in common has been found and the talk has been closed with a polite goodbye.

de-c1-telefonton.scene: You are ringing an institution and the person you need is not there. Explain your situation politely, ask to be put through, leave a message if that fails and arrange a time for a call back.
de-c1-telefonton.partner: a switchboard operator who sticks to the rules and does not put people through easily
de-c1-telefonton.openingTr: Good afternoon, switchboard. I'm afraid Mr Baumann is not in the building today — what is it about?
de-c1-telefonton.goal: The matter has been explained, a message has been left and a time for a call back has been arranged.

de-c1-partikel-pruefung.scene: You are talking to a friend about something that has upset your plans. Change your tone three times in the conversation: first inviting and softening, then mild reproach, and at the end comfort and acceptance.
de-c1-partikel-pruefung.partner: a friend who upset the plan, defensive at first but apologising in the end
de-c1-partikel-pruefung.openingTr: Tell me, are you cross now? It really wasn't my fault.
de-c1-partikel-pruefung.goal: The reproach has been voiced, the other side's reasons have been heard and the conversation has closed with acceptance and a new plan.

de-c1-inversion.scene: You are giving your verdict on a talk you both heard as you come out of a conference. Say what you found impressive and what you did not in sentences with emphatic word order, explain why and answer the other side's objection.
de-c1-inversion.partner: a listener who found the talk ordinary and wants reasons
de-c1-inversion.openingTr: Honestly, I thought it was overrated. What exactly impressed you about it?
de-c1-inversion.goal: What was impressive and what was not have been given with reasons and the two of you have reached a shared verdict.

de-c1-dreierfigur.scene: You are defending your idea in a meeting and your speech is thought too long. Gather your idea into three points, give each in one sentence, answer the question briefly and close concisely.
de-c1-dreierfigur.partner: a chair who tires of long speeches and says 'keep it short'
de-c1-dreierfigur.openingTr: We've got five minutes left. Can you say it in three points?
de-c1-dreierfigur.goal: The idea has been gathered into three points, one question has been answered briefly and a concise close has been made.

de-c1-metapher-vortrag.scene: You are explaining a complex subject from your own field to a listener who is not an expert. Use at least two images, make the main thread clear, answer the question with another image and round it off.
de-c1-metapher-vortrag.partner: a listener new to the subject who is curious and asks questions
de-c1-metapher-vortrag.openingTr: Honestly, I know nothing at all about your field. Could you explain it to me as if I were twelve?
de-c1-metapher-vortrag.goal: The subject has been explained with at least two images, the main thread has been made clear and the listener has said in their own words that they understood.

de-c1-publikum.scene: Your presentation is over and one of the audience has asked an aggressive question. Stay calm, take the question on, refute the claim, concede one point where they are right and close the round.
de-c1-publikum.partner: an assertive listener who interrupts and is not easily convinced
de-c1-publikum.openingTr: I know your figures differently. Are you working with a flattering selection there?
de-c1-publikum.goal: The question has been taken on, the claim refuted, one fair point conceded and the question round closed calmly.

de-c1-stegreif.scene: You have been given the floor in a meeting when you did not expect it. Buy yourself time, divide your answer into three, say honestly where you do not know and hand back with a summing-up.
de-c1-stegreif.partner: a chair who has caught you unprepared and expects a lot
de-c1-stegreif.openingTr: You've been with this subject longest — would you sum up briefly where we stand?
de-c1-stegreif.goal: Time has been bought, the answer has been divided into three, an unknown has been admitted honestly and the floor has been handed back with a summing-up.

de-c1-moderation.scene: You are hosting an event and the programme has slipped: the speaker is late. Greet the room, announce the situation politely, build a bridge to fill the gap and restart the programme.
de-c1-moderation.partner: a flustered event manager passing on news from backstage
de-c1-moderation.openingTr: She'll be at least ten minutes. Can you bridge that somehow?
de-c1-moderation.goal: The room has been greeted, the delay announced politely, a bridge has been built and the programme restarted.

de-c1-schlagfertig.scene: Someone at a celebration keeps making barbed remarks at you. Meet the first calmly, turn the second back to the subject, and if they go too far draw a polite but firm line and end the conversation.
de-c1-schlagfertig.partner: a guest trying to seem witty who goes too far
de-c1-schlagfertig.openingTr: Well, if it isn't the famous expert! So? Did everything get finished on time this time?
de-c1-schlagfertig.goal: The barbs have been met calmly, the subject has been taken back and, where needed, a polite but firm line has been drawn.

de-c1-storytelling.scene: You are telling a story at dinner about something that happened to you. Set up the opening, hold the tension, do not give the ending away early, weave the interruptions into the story and deliver the point at the end.
de-c1-storytelling.partner: an impatient listener who keeps asking 'and then?'
de-c1-storytelling.openingTr: Wait — first tell me: does the story end well?
de-c1-storytelling.goal: The story has been told with the tension held, the interruptions have been woven in and the point has been delivered at the end.

de-c1-abschlussrede.scene: You are leaving a team you have worked with for a long time and giving a farewell speech. Open with an image, thank a few people by name, tell one memory briefly and close with good wishes.
de-c1-abschlussrede.partner: a colleague who has known you for years and throws in short remarks
de-c1-abschlussrede.openingTr: Before you start: be honest, did you prepare this or are you making it up as you go?
de-c1-abschlussrede.goal: The speech has opened with an image, at least two people have been thanked, a memory has been told and it has closed with good wishes.

de-c1-debatte-c1.scene: You are in a short debate on a contested subject. Concede the other side's strongest argument, then line up your own reasons, refute one objection and say at the end what weighs more.
de-c1-debatte-c1.partner: a well-prepared opponent with solid arguments
de-c1-debatte-c1.openingTr: I'll start: the benefit is short-term, the costs remain. How do you propose to counter that?
de-c1-debatte-c1.goal: The other side's strongest argument has been conceded, your own reasons have been lined up and what weighs more has been said at the end.

de-c1-daumen.scene: A friend has an important exam or interview tomorrow. Support them, listen to their worry, tell them their plan is sound and ask whether there is something they want to talk through in private. Use idioms in measure.
de-c1-daumen.partner: a nervous friend who lacks confidence but wants to talk
de-c1-daumen.openingTr: I think I'm going to make a mess of it tomorrow. Tell me honestly — does my plan actually hold water?
de-c1-daumen.goal: The worry has been heard, an honest verdict has been given on the plan and support has been offered with something concrete.

de-c1-tomaten.scene: You are making a joint decision (a holiday, a move, a purchase). Say which points matter to you and which you do not mind about; accept putting up with one thing unwillingly and reach a conclusion.
de-c1-tomaten.partner: a friend who finds fault in every detail and does not decide easily
de-c1-tomaten.openingTr: Well, honestly, it isn't all the same to me. You go first: what really matters to you?
de-c1-tomaten.goal: The points that matter and those that do not have been separated, one concession has been made and a joint decision has been reached.
