de-c1-tiere-idiome.scene: You are telling a friend about a narrow escape: what happened, why you were lucky, whose word you trusted and what you would do differently. Use idioms where they fit.
de-c1-tiere-idiome.partner: a friend listening keenly and asking for detail
de-c1-tiere-idiome.openingTr: Tell me from the beginning — and were you really just jammy, or was it skill?
de-c1-tiere-idiome.goal: The event has been told from the beginning, luck and skill have been told apart and what you would do again has been said.

de-c1-wetter-idiome.scene: The atmosphere at work has turned tense and you are talking to a friend: where the tension comes from, whether it is being blown up, whether there is a hopeful sign and what you should do. Use the metaphors where they fit.
de-c1-wetter-idiome.partner: a friend who thinks it is being blown up but takes your worry seriously
de-c1-wetter-idiome.openingTr: Is it really that bad, or isn't it more of a storm in a teacup?
de-c1-wetter-idiome.goal: The source of the tension has been described, how much is exaggeration has been weighed and a conclusion has been reached about what to do.

de-c1-farben-idiome.scene: A colleague often shirks the work and it lands on you. Talk it through: what you have noticed, how you feel, whether management needs to sign anything off and how you will go on.
de-c1-farben-idiome.partner: a colleague who denies it at first and then explains the reason
de-c1-farben-idiome.openingTr: Tell me, have you got some problem with me? You've been looking at me like that all week.
de-c1-farben-idiome.goal: What you noticed has been said without blame, the reason has been heard and how to go on has been settled.

de-c1-sport-idiome.scene: You are stuck on something you have run for a long time and you are thinking of giving up. Talk to a friend: describe why it is hard, admit your own part, weigh what giving up would mean and reach a decision.
de-c1-sport-idiome.partner: a friend against your giving up who still listens to your reasons
de-c1-sport-idiome.openingTr: You want to throw in the towel? After two years? First tell me exactly what isn't working any more.
de-c1-sport-idiome.goal: The difficulty has been described, your own part has been admitted and a decision has been reached about going on or giving up.

de-c1-geld-idiome.scene: You are discussing a shared purchase and you think it is unnecessary. Say why it is money down the drain, mention your own situation politely, suggest a cheaper alternative and reach a decision.
de-c1-geld-idiome.partner: a friend defending the expensive option who will pay for quality
de-c1-geld-idiome.openingTr: I know it's dear. But buying cheap often means buying twice — or do you see it differently?
de-c1-geld-idiome.goal: Both sides' reasons have been given, the budget position has been mentioned politely and a decision has been reached.

de-c1-musik-idiome.scene: You are trying to work out who really carries weight in a team you have just joined. Ask a colleague: who sets the tone, how decisions are made, how you can find your place. Use idioms in measure.
de-c1-musik-idiome.partner: a plain-spoken but diplomatic colleague who knows the team well
de-c1-musik-idiome.openingTr: You're new, so I'll tell you straight away: on paper the management decides. And in reality? Have a guess.
de-c1-musik-idiome.goal: The real balance of power in the team has been learnt and a concrete piece of advice on finding your place has been taken away.

de-c1-falsche-freunde-idiome.scene: You are trying to explain an English idiom to a German-speaking friend. First say it word for word, notice why it makes no sense, explain what it means and find the German equivalent together.
de-c1-falsche-freunde-idiome.partner: a German friend who is curious about languages and tries to suggest an equivalent
de-c1-falsche-freunde-idiome.openingTr: Say it literally once more — I honestly can't make head nor tail of it. What is that supposed to mean?
de-c1-falsche-freunde-idiome.goal: The real meaning of the idiom has been explained and a German equivalent has been found together.

de-c1-idiome-alltag.scene: You are telling a friend about a busy day. Use idioms in measure: three or four at most, each fitting its context. If the other person says you are overdoing it, adjust.
de-c1-idiome-alltag.partner: a friend who knows you well and pulls you up when you overdo it
de-c1-idiome-alltag.openingTr: Tell me, how was your day? And please, no book of proverbs — just say it as it was.
de-c1-idiome-alltag.goal: The day has been described, the idioms have been used in measure and the other person has said it sounded natural.

de-c1-konjunktiv1.scene: You are passing on what was said in a meeting to a colleague who was not there. Give who said what in the reporting mood, put your own assessment in a separate sentence and say what is certain and what is only claimed.
de-c1-konjunktiv1.partner: a colleague who wants to know exactly who said what and asks for detail
de-c1-konjunktiv1.openingTr: And what exactly did the management say — in their words, not with your assessment?
de-c1-konjunktiv1.goal: What was said has been given in the reporting mood, the speaker's own view has been separated and what is certain and what is claimed have been marked.

de-c1-pressebericht.scene: You are reporting an incident to a local radio station. Keep apart what has been confirmed, what is only claimed and what the state of the sources is; give an assessment without overstating.
de-c1-pressebericht.partner: a radio presenter who wants a definite sentence and asks 'yes or no'
de-c1-pressebericht.openingTr: Very briefly and without the subjunctive: has someone been injured there or not?
de-c1-pressebericht.goal: The confirmed and the claimed have been separated, the state of the sources has been given and an assessment has been made without overstating.

de-c1-wissenschaftssprache.scene: You are presenting your own finding at a working meeting. Report the finding in impersonal language, say which assumption it rests on, concede one limitation and say how far the result can be generalised.
de-c1-wissenschaftssprache.partner: a researcher who questions the method and asks about the limits of generalisation
de-c1-wissenschaftssprache.openingTr: Before we talk about the interpretation: what assumption does your finding actually rest on?
de-c1-wissenschaftssprache.goal: The finding has been reported impersonally, the assumption and one limitation have been given and its generalisability has been stated.

de-c1-quellenkritik.scene: An acquaintance is making a strong claim on the basis of a study. Question the source, separate what is reported from what is proven, ask about the interests involved and reach a shared conclusion about how far it can be trusted.
de-c1-quellenkritik.partner: an acquaintance who trusts the study and thinks questioning the source is unnecessary
de-c1-quellenkritik.openingTr: It's in the study, isn't it. What more do you want — shall I ring the authors?
de-c1-quellenkritik.goal: The reported claim and the proven fact have been separated, the source and the interests have been questioned and agreement has been reached about how far to trust it.

de-c1-abstract.scene: Someone at a conference asks about your work and you have one minute. Give the research question, your method, your main finding and what you have left open, in that order; answer the question briefly.
de-c1-abstract.partner: a colleague with little time who is genuinely interested
de-c1-abstract.openingTr: I've got exactly one minute — what is your work about and what is the one result that counts?
de-c1-abstract.goal: The research question, the method, the main finding and the open point have been given in one minute and a question has been answered.

de-c1-vortrag-uni.scene: You are defending your work at a colloquium. Raise the strongest objection yourself first, then answer it; concede one point where the examiner is right and still hold your thesis.
de-c1-vortrag-uni.partner: a well-prepared examiner who criticises the method
de-c1-vortrag-uni.openingTr: With respect — your sample does not support the conclusion. How do you meet that objection?
de-c1-vortrag-uni.goal: The strongest objection has been raised first and answered, one point has been conceded and the thesis has been held.

de-c1-fachdiskussion.scene: An expert is putting a claim to you in very compressed sentences. Get the phrase you did not follow unpacked, simplify it in your own words, ask what the premise is and say where a distinction has to be drawn.
de-c1-fachdiskussion.partner: an expert who talks fast and technically and resists simplifying
de-c1-fachdiskussion.openingTr: The assumption underlying the method is, put briefly, trivial. Do you see it differently?
de-c1-fachdiskussion.goal: The compressed phrase has been unpacked, the claim has been simplified and it has been said which part of the premise is contested.

de-c1-populaerwissenschaft.scene: You are explaining your specialist subject to a wide audience for a podcast. Build an analogy, say where the analogy breaks down, give a rule of thumb and answer the presenter's question by simplifying.
de-c1-populaerwissenschaft.partner: a curious podcast presenter who keeps summing up with 'so you mean'
de-c1-populaerwissenschaft.openingTr: Please explain it to me so that I can pass it on over dinner this evening — is that possible?
de-c1-populaerwissenschaft.goal: An analogy has been built, its limit has been named, a rule of thumb has been given and the presenter has summed the subject up correctly in their own words.

de-c1-zitat.scene: Your words have been quoted in a text but taken out of context. Talk to the author: report exactly what you said, show where it has been distorted, ask for a correction and say how it should be attributed.
de-c1-zitat.partner: an author who defends the quotation as accurate but is open to listening
de-c1-zitat.openingTr: I quoted you word for word — you can check. Where exactly do you see the problem?
de-c1-zitat.goal: The whole of what was said has been reported, the distortion has been shown and a correction has been agreed.

de-c1-podiumsdiskussion.scene: You are on a panel on a contested subject and you have to balance your speaking time against the other side's claims. Take the floor, concede where they are right, draw a distinction and hand back with a short closing sentence.
de-c1-podiumsdiskussion.partner: a panel guest who runs on and keeps interrupting
de-c1-podiumsdiskussion.openingTr: I'll be brief — really brief: the figures simply do not bear out your position. Would you like to answer that?
de-c1-podiumsdiskussion.goal: The other side's fair point has been conceded, their claim has been distinguished and the floor has been handed back with a short closing sentence.

de-c1-vertragsklauseln.scene: There are clauses you do not understand in a contract you are about to sign. Ask the other side: what each clause means, how long the term is, what happens on a delay and which clause you want changed.
de-c1-vertragsklauseln.partner: a company representative who defends the contract and calls it a standard clause
de-c1-vertragsklauseln.openingTr: This is our standard contract — everyone signs it as it is. Which clause is worrying you?
de-c1-vertragsklauseln.goal: The clauses not understood have been explained, the term and the consequence of delay have been made clear and at least one change has been requested.

de-c1-agb.scene: The terms and conditions of a service contain a clause that excludes liability entirely. Talk to customer services: say in your own words what the clause says, say why it is too wide and state what you are asking for.
de-c1-agb.partner: a customer services manager with limited authority who treats the clause as standard
de-c1-agb.openingTr: The clause is in our terms and conditions and is therefore taken as agreed. What are you getting at?
de-c1-agb.goal: The meaning of the clause has been put in your own words, why it is too wide has been stated and a concrete demand has been made.

de-c1-miete-recht.scene: A fault in your flat has gone unrepaired for months. Talk to the landlord: report the fault and how long it has lasted, set a deadline for the repair, raise a claim for a rent reduction and ask for written confirmation.
de-c1-miete-recht.partner: a landlord who avoids responsibility and calls it a small thing
de-c1-miete-recht.openingTr: It's a trifle, surely. Do you really want to cut the rent over that?
de-c1-miete-recht.goal: The fault and its duration have been reported, a deadline has been set, a reduction has been claimed and written confirmation has been asked for.

de-c1-arbeitsrecht.scene: A colleague has had a formal warning and is in a panic. Pass on what you heard from a solicitor, keep your own view separate, say which step has to be taken by when and calm them down.
de-c1-arbeitsrecht.partner: a panicking colleague who is thinking of resigning at once
de-c1-arbeitsrecht.openingTr: I'll just resign myself before they throw me out. Or what did your solicitor say?
de-c1-arbeitsrecht.goal: The solicitor's view has been reported in the reporting mood, the speaker's own view has been kept separate and the first step has been given with its date.

de-c1-datenschutz-c1.scene: You are asking a service provider how your data is processed. Ask which data is processed for what purpose and whether it is passed to third parties; withdraw your consent and make a request for erasure.
de-c1-datenschutz-c1.partner: a data protection officer reading from the text who avoids detail
de-c1-datenschutz-c1.openingTr: The processing is carried out on the basis of your consent. What information do you need specifically?
de-c1-datenschutz-c1.goal: The data processed and its purposes have been found out, third-party transfer has been asked about, consent has been withdrawn and erasure has been requested.

de-c1-polizei-aussage.scene: You are giving a statement about an incident you witnessed. Give what you saw yourself in the plain indicative and what you heard from others in the reporting mood; mark clearly what you do not remember and have your statement put on record.
de-c1-polizei-aussage.partner: an officer who wants definite answers and presses for detail
de-c1-polizei-aussage.openingTr: Only what you saw yourself, please. So: what exactly did you observe?
de-c1-polizei-aussage.goal: What was seen and what was heard have been reported separately, the gaps in memory have been marked clearly and the statement has been put on record.

de-c1-versicherungsfall.scene: The insurer has refused your claim. Talk to the representative: find out the grounds for the refusal, say which point you accept, hold your claim nevertheless and state the next step.
de-c1-versicherungsfall.partner: an insurance representative who defends the grounds and does not give way easily
de-c1-versicherungsfall.openingTr: The case has been examined: the obligation was not met, so there is no entitlement. What would you like to object to?
de-c1-versicherungsfall.goal: The grounds for refusal have been found out, the point accepted has been said, the claim has been held and the next step has been stated.

de-c1-buergschaft.scene: Someone close is asking you to stand surety for them. Talk it through together: in what case you would be liable, how great the risk is, on what condition you could accept, or why you are refusing.
de-c1-buergschaft.partner: someone close who trusts you, plays down the risk and will not let it go
de-c1-buergschaft.openingTr: It's only a formality, the bank just wants to see it. You'll never actually have to pay — or don't you believe me?
de-c1-buergschaft.goal: The consequences of standing surety have been described, the risk has been discussed and the acceptance or refusal has been stated clearly with reasons.

de-c1-einspruch.scene: You are going to appeal against a decision from an authority but the deadline is closing in. Talk to the enquiries desk: ask how to lodge an appeal that protects the deadline, find out by when the grounds must be complete and ask for confirmation.
de-c1-einspruch.partner: an official strict on procedure who gives you a form number
de-c1-einspruch.openingTr: The deadline expires in two days. Have you got your grounds ready, then?
de-c1-einspruch.goal: How to lodge a deadline-protecting appeal has been found out, the final date for the grounds has been made clear and confirmation has been promised.

de-c1-gericht.scene: You watched a court hearing and you are reporting it to someone who was not there. Give who said what in the reporting mood, state the court's decision separately, keep your own impression apart and describe what happens next.
de-c1-gericht.partner: an acquaintance who is curious about the outcome and has taken a side
de-c1-gericht.openingTr: And? Did they believe him or not? Tell me from the beginning.
de-c1-gericht.goal: What was said has been reported in the reporting mood, the court's decision has been given separately, the personal impression has been kept apart and the next step has been described.

de-c1-partizipial.scene: You and a colleague are going over a formal text. Unpack one long phrase and say in your own words what it says, then compress a passage yourself and argue about which version reads better.
de-c1-partizipial.partner: a colleague who defends the compressed style and says formal texts are like that
de-c1-partizipial.openingTr: The sentence is perfectly clear. What exactly don't you understand about it?
de-c1-partizipial.goal: One phrase has been unpacked, one passage has been compressed and a shared conclusion has been reached about which reads better.

de-c1-gerundiv.scene: You are at a project handover meeting. List the jobs that have to be done, the risks that must not be underestimated and the decisions still waiting; say which is urgent and complete the handover.
de-c1-gerundiv.partner: a colleague taking the project on who wants detail and asks about priority
de-c1-gerundiv.openingTr: Before you go: what is the one thing I must on no account underestimate?
de-c1-gerundiv.goal: The jobs to be done and the risks have been listed, the priority has been stated and the handover has been completed.

de-c1-schachtelsatz.scene: A friend cannot make sense of a formal letter and is asking for your help. Find the core of the sentence together, break it into parts, rebuild it in your own words and say clearly what the letter is asking for.
de-c1-schachtelsatz.partner: a friend afraid of formal letters who keeps starting the sentence again
de-c1-schachtelsatz.openingTr: I've read the sentence five times now. Can you just tell me what they want from me?
de-c1-schachtelsatz.goal: The core of the sentence has been found, the text has been rebuilt in one plain sentence and what the letter asks for has been said clearly.

de-c1-nominal-verbal.scene: You and a colleague are going over a text and you think it is too heavy. Show which sentences should be made plainer, say the reworked version and accept where it has to stay formal.
de-c1-nominal-verbal.partner: a colleague who takes the formal style as a mark of seriousness
de-c1-nominal-verbal.openingTr: If we rewrite it like that, doesn't it sound less serious straight away? Where exactly does the style bother you?
de-c1-nominal-verbal.goal: The sentences to be made plainer have been shown, their reworked versions have been given and it has been agreed where the text stays formal.

de-c1-apposition.scene: You are introducing two people to each other at an event. Introduce each with parenthetical asides (who they are, what they do, what they are known for), find a subject in common and leave them to talk.
de-c1-apposition.partner: a guest being introduced who adds things about themselves
de-c1-apposition.openingTr: I don't think we've met yet. Would you introduce us briefly?
de-c1-apposition.goal: Both people have been introduced with parenthetical asides, a subject in common has been found and the conversation has been handed over to them.

de-c1-verweiswoerter.scene: You are deciding between two options. Sum both up briefly, refer back to one of them with reference words, say which you prefer and why, and leave one point for later.
de-c1-verweiswoerter.partner: a colleague who could argue either side and pushes you to give reasons
de-c1-verweiswoerter.openingTr: So: first the quick way, second the thorough one. Which do you argue for?
de-c1-verweiswoerter.goal: Both options have been summed up, the preference has been justified with reference words and one point has been deliberately left for later.

de-c1-ellipse.scene: A notice is too long and has to be cut. Show what can go, defend what has to stay, give the shortened version and check that it is still clear.
de-c1-ellipse.partner: a colleague who thinks every sentence is necessary and resists cutting
de-c1-ellipse.openingTr: If we cut that, nobody will understand it any more. What exactly do you want to strike out?
de-c1-ellipse.goal: What can go has been shown, what has to stay has been defended and the clarity of the shortened version has been checked together.

de-c1-doppeldeutig.scene: You are asked about something you cannot yet explain. Answer without lying and without promising anything; when they press, state your limit openly and say when you will be able to talk.
de-c1-doppeldeutig.partner: an insistent colleague who will not leave without an answer
de-c1-doppeldeutig.openingTr: Just say yes or no. Is the department being closed?
de-c1-doppeldeutig.goal: An answer has been given without lying or promising, the limit has been stated openly and it has been said when you can talk.

de-c1-textsorten.scene: You have to describe the same event to two different people: first to a formal superior, then to a close friend. Say the same content in two registers and name the difference yourself.
de-c1-textsorten.partner: a listener who plays first the formal superior and then the close friend
de-c1-textsorten.openingTr: Officially first, please: what has occurred?
de-c1-textsorten.goal: The same content has been told in two registers and the difference between them has been named.

de-c1-praezision.scene: A text has some wrong word choices and you are talking to its author. Explain which word is wrong and why, suggest the right one, listen to the author's objection and settle the final version together.
de-c1-praezision.partner: an author who thinks word choice does not matter and says it is clear enough
de-c1-praezision.openingTr: It's the same thing, surely — scheinbar, anscheinend, where's the difference?
de-c1-praezision.goal: The difference between the words has been explained with an example, the right one has been suggested and the final version of the text has been settled together.

de-c1-als-ob-c1.scene: There is something in a team that everyone knows about and nobody talks about. Name the situation, say what ignoring it does, acknowledge the other person's discomfort and tie the conversation to a step.
de-c1-als-ob-c1.partner: a colleague uncomfortable with raising it who prefers to say everything is fine
de-c1-als-ob-c1.openingTr: Does it really have to be now? We're getting along quite well, aren't we?
de-c1-als-ob-c1.goal: The unspoken matter has been named, the consequence of ignoring it has been said and a concrete step has been settled.

de-c1-konzessiv.scene: You are defending a contested decision. Accept the other side's objection about cost, say why the decision is right in spite of it, soften your own wording at one point and draw a line.
de-c1-konzessiv.partner: an opponent who puts the cost first and talks in figures
de-c1-konzessiv.openingTr: The costs are three times the estimate. How do you still propose to defend that?
de-c1-konzessiv.goal: The objection has been accepted, the decision has been justified in spite of it and a limit or condition has been set.

de-c1-hypothesen.scene: The other person is making a strong claim. Assume for a moment that it is true, look at the consequences together, show where it collapses and say which part of the assumption still stands.
de-c1-hypothesen.partner: a debater confident in their claim and willing to play the hypothesis game
de-c1-hypothesen.openingTr: Let's assume for the sake of it that I'm right. What would be so bad about that?
de-c1-hypothesen.goal: The claim has been accepted hypothetically, its consequences have been examined together and the part that still stands has been named.

de-c1-migrationsdebatte.scene: Someone asks you where you are 'originally' from and the question wears you down. Name the assumption behind it, describe your own belonging from both sides, state your limit without blaming them and end the conversation constructively.
de-c1-migrationsdebatte.partner: a well-meaning acquaintance who does not know why the question is wearing
de-c1-migrationsdebatte.openingTr: I don't mean it badly — but where are you originally from?
de-c1-migrationsdebatte.goal: The assumption behind the question has been named, the belonging has been described from both sides and the conversation has been ended constructively without blame.

de-c1-klimadebatte.scene: You and an acquaintance are arguing about responsibility for the climate: the individual or the system. Name the shifting of responsibility, say what an individual step does and does not do, show the conflict of aims and meet on a shared test.
de-c1-klimadebatte.partner: an acquaintance who puts everything down to individual behaviour
de-c1-klimadebatte.openingTr: If everyone starts with themselves, the problem is solved. Or are you just making excuses?
de-c1-klimadebatte.goal: Individual and systemic responsibility have been separated, the conflict of aims has been shown and a shared test has been agreed.

de-c1-bildungsdebatte.scene: You are arguing about the education system at a parents' evening. Say what was neglected in the past with unreal conditions, separate what can be done today, accept the other side's objection and leave a concrete suggestion.
de-c1-bildungsdebatte.partner: a parent who defends the system and thinks looking back is pointless
de-c1-bildungsdebatte.openingTr: If only, if only — what good does that do us? Tell me instead what we should do now.
de-c1-bildungsdebatte.goal: The past neglect has been stated with unreal conditions, what can be done today has been separated and a concrete suggestion has been left.

de-c1-ethik-ki.scene: You are arguing about whether a decision should be left to artificial intelligence. Separate in your language the qualities attributed to the machine, ask who the responsibility is imputed to, say where you draw the line and propose a shared rule.
de-c1-ethik-ki.partner: a colleague who argues the system decides better than a person
de-c1-ethik-ki.openingTr: The system decides more objectively than any of us. Why shouldn't we leave it to that?
de-c1-ethik-ki.goal: The qualities attributed to the machine have been separated in language, who bears the responsibility has been discussed and a shared rule on the limit has been proposed.

de-c1-generationenvertrag.scene: You are arguing with someone from another generation about pensions and the burden of contributions. Say who loses out and how, accept the other side's fair point, hold your own point nevertheless and propose a fair test.
de-c1-generationenvertrag.partner: an acquaintance who defends their own generation's due and knows the figures
de-c1-generationenvertrag.openingTr: We paid in for forty years. Do you want to call that into question now?
de-c1-generationenvertrag.goal: Who loses out and how has been said, the other side's fair point has been accepted and a fair test has been proposed.

de-c1-meinungsfreiheit.scene: Something someone said in a discussion has drawn a reaction. Separate freedom of expression from insult, say where the other side is right, justify where you draw the line and look for a shared test.
de-c1-meinungsfreiheit.partner: a debater who calls every criticism censorship and rejects the idea of a limit
de-c1-meinungsfreiheit.openingTr: Surely one is still allowed to say anything. Or do you want to lay down rules as well now?
de-c1-meinungsfreiheit.goal: Freedom of expression and insult have been separated, the point where the other side is right has been said and a shared test has been sought.

de-c1-zukunftsvision.scene: You are designing a scenario for 2050 at a workshop. Build the scenario in the unreal mood, say which step has to start today, meet the 'utopian' objection and tie the design to a concrete first step.
de-c1-zukunftsvision.partner: a participant who dismisses every imaginative idea as unrealistic
de-c1-zukunftsvision.openingTr: A fine vision — but that's pure utopia. What do you propose to start with?
de-c1-zukunftsvision.goal: The scenario has been built in the unreal mood, the 'utopian' objection has been met and the design has been tied to a concrete first step from today.

de-c1-ironie.scene: A colleague made an ironic remark after the meeting and you are not sure what they meant. Say what you heard, ask what they meant, state your own view plainly and clear the matter up.
de-c1-ironie.partner: a colleague with a dry wit who avoids saying things directly
de-c1-ironie.openingTr: Well, that went brilliantly today. Didn't you think so too?
de-c1-ironie.goal: What the ironic remark meant has come out and both sides have stated their view plainly.

de-c1-sarkasmus-grenze.scene: A joke you made in a meeting has upset someone. Talk to them: accept how it landed, explain what you meant, take the remark back and talk about what happens next — without getting defensive.
de-c1-sarkasmus-grenze.partner: a colleague who was upset but does not want to make a thing of it
de-c1-sarkasmus-grenze.openingTr: It's all right. But honestly, in front of everyone it was a bit much — did you notice?
de-c1-sarkasmus-grenze.goal: How the joke landed has been accepted, the remark has been taken back and something has been said about what happens next.

de-c1-wortspiele.scene: A friend has made a play on words in German and you did not get it. Say you did not, work it out together, discuss whether there is an equivalent in English and give an example from your own language.
de-c1-wortspiele.partner: a friend who loves wordplay and enjoys explaining
de-c1-wortspiele.openingTr: You have to let that one melt on your tongue. Can you see where the double meaning is?
de-c1-wortspiele.goal: The wordplay has been worked out together, the limit of translation has been discussed and the learner has given an example from their own language.

de-c1-regionale-kultur.scene: An acquaintance is talking in clichés about your country or the area you live in. Accept where the cliché comes from, describe what you have observed, object politely to the sweeping judgement and put a question back to them.
de-c1-regionale-kultur.partner: an acquaintance who means no harm but talks in clichés
de-c1-regionale-kultur.openingTr: People are much more open where you're from than here in the north, aren't they?
de-c1-regionale-kultur.goal: The source of the cliché has been accepted, your own observation has been described and the sweeping judgement has been politely objected to.

de-c1-dialekte-hoeren.scene: You are talking to someone from another region and you do not understand some of their words. Say so politely, ask what they mean, describe the usage where you live and keep the conversation going.
de-c1-dialekte-hoeren.partner: an acquaintance who speaks in their own dialect and gladly explains when asked
de-c1-dialekte-hoeren.openingTr: Would you like a Semmel? Or do you call it something else where you're from?
de-c1-dialekte-hoeren.goal: The words not understood have been asked about and learnt, your own regional usage has been described and the conversation has been kept going.

de-c1-duzen-siezen-c1.scene: You are in a new working environment and someone offers to move to first-name terms. Respond to the offer, ask what the custom is there, state your own preference politely and leave the relationship easy.
de-c1-duzen-siezen-c1.partner: a colleague who wants an informal atmosphere and takes the offer as natural
de-c1-duzen-siezen-c1.openingTr: We don't really use Sie here. Shall we stick with du?
de-c1-duzen-siezen-c1.goal: The offer has been answered, the custom of the place has been found out and your own preference has been given politely.

de-c1-komplimente-c1.scene: A colleague has pulled off something difficult. Give them credit — concrete, measured and without overdoing it. If they play it down, insist, ask what they learnt and end the conversation warmly.
de-c1-komplimente-c1.partner: a colleague who struggles to take praise and plays it down at once
de-c1-komplimente-c1.openingTr: Oh, that was nothing special. Anyone could have managed it, couldn't they?
de-c1-komplimente-c1.goal: Concrete and measured credit has been given, the playing-down has been met and the conversation has been ended warmly.

de-c1-peinlichkeiten.scene: You said the wrong thing at a party and the room went cold. Accept the gaffe, apologise without trying to save yourself, close the subject and start the conversation again.
de-c1-peinlichkeiten.partner: a host who noticed the gaffe and is trying to smooth it over
de-c1-peinlichkeiten.openingTr: No drama — but that was a bit unfortunate just now. Shall we simply put it behind us?
de-c1-peinlichkeiten.goal: The gaffe has been accepted, an apology has been made without getting defensive and the conversation has been started again.

de-c1-deutscher-humor.scene: You and a friend are comparing the humour of two cultures: what is laughed at, what is not, how dry humour works and why a joke dies in translation. Give an example from your own language.
de-c1-deutscher-humor.partner: a friend who defends their own humour and asks for examples
de-c1-deutscher-humor.openingTr: Give me an example: what do people laugh at where you're from, and what never here?
de-c1-deutscher-humor.goal: The humour of the two cultures has been compared with examples and why a joke does not survive translation has been explained.

de-c1-kulturschock-fein.scene: You are explaining to a newcomer what is different here: punctuality, direct criticism, sparing praise. Name it without judging, describe your own beginning and give them a concrete piece of advice.
de-c1-kulturschock-fein.partner: a newcomer who takes some of the behaviour for rudeness
de-c1-kulturschock-fein.openingTr: Are people here always so blunt? Yesterday someone corrected me in front of everyone — was that meant unkindly?
de-c1-kulturschock-fein.goal: The cultural difference has been named without judgement, your own experience has been described and a concrete piece of advice has been given to the newcomer.

de-c1-krisensitzung.scene: A problem has grown and you are chairing the crisis meeting. Sum the situation up in one sentence, say which measures will be taken, share out who does what and give the time of the next review.
de-c1-krisensitzung.partner: a panicking team member who keeps listing new problems
de-c1-krisensitzung.openingTr: Reports are coming in from everywhere. What do we start with?
de-c1-krisensitzung.goal: The situation has been summed up, the measures and responsibilities have been shared out and the time of the next review has been given.

de-c1-improvisation.scene: On the day of the event the main solution has failed. Suggest a stopgap, state its limits honestly, say how long it will hold and give a date for the permanent fix.
de-c1-improvisation.partner: a manager who is relieved and inclined to treat the stopgap as permanent
de-c1-improvisation.openingTr: So it's working again now? Then we can just leave it like that, can't we?
de-c1-improvisation.goal: A stopgap has been suggested, its limits and how long it will hold have been stated honestly and a date has been given for the permanent fix.

de-c1-vermittlung.scene: Two people are misunderstanding each other and you are in the middle. Unpack a culturally loaded phrase, tell both sides what was meant, clear the misunderstanding up and hand the conversation back to them.
de-c1-vermittlung.partner: an offended party who takes the other side's phrasing for rudeness
de-c1-vermittlung.openingTr: He said it was 'not bad'. Am I to take that as praise or as criticism?
de-c1-vermittlung.goal: The loaded phrase has been explained, the misunderstanding has been cleared up and the conversation has been handed back to them.

de-c1-grosse-rede.scene: You are going to speak on an important occasion. Build an opening that catches the audience, line up three points, use an image, meet one objection in advance and finish with a sentence that stays with them.
de-c1-grosse-rede.partner: a friend who listens to your speech beforehand and gives feedback
de-c1-grosse-rede.openingTr: Try the opening out on me — how do you begin?
de-c1-grosse-rede.goal: An opening, three points, an image and a resonant close have been built, and your friend has given their feedback.

de-c1-verhandlungsfinale.scene: You are in the last round of a long negotiation. Put your final offer softly, offer an improvement on one point, meet the other side's last request and close the deal with a handshake — or end it politely.
de-c1-verhandlungsfinale.partner: a tough but fair negotiator who asks for one more thing at the last moment
de-c1-verhandlungsfinale.openingTr: One more thing, then I'll sign: could you come towards me on the term?
de-c1-verhandlungsfinale.goal: The final offer has been made, the last request has been met and the negotiation has been closed with an agreement or a polite ending.

de-c1-pruefungssimulation.scene: You are in a C1 exam simulation: give a short talk, answer the two questions that follow and gather what you said into one sentence at the end. The examiner may remind you of the criteria.
de-c1-pruefungssimulation.partner: an impartial examiner who keeps the time and reminds you of the criteria
de-c1-pruefungssimulation.openingTr: You have two minutes to speak, then two questions. Your subject, please?
de-c1-pruefungssimulation.goal: A short talk has been given, two questions have been answered and what was said has been gathered into one sentence.

de-c1-mentoring-c1.scene: Someone just starting to learn German is asking you for advice. Describe your own road, separate what worked from what did not, set a realistic expectation and send them off with a concrete first step.
de-c1-mentoring-c1.partner: an eager but impatient new learner who asks how long it takes
de-c1-mentoring-c1.openingTr: How long did it take you? And be honest — what could I have spared myself?
de-c1-mentoring-c1.goal: Your own road has been described, what worked and what did not have been separated and the new learner has been given a concrete first step.

de-c1-zweisprachig-leben.scene: Someone is asking you what it is like to live in two languages. Describe how you change with the language, separate what is lost from what is gained, correct a misunderstanding and justify why it is a richness.
de-c1-zweisprachig-leben.partner: a well-meaning acquaintance who takes bilingualism for a lack
de-c1-zweisprachig-leben.openingTr: Doesn't one feel a bit torn — between two languages like that?
de-c1-zweisprachig-leben.goal: What living in two languages feels like has been described, the loss and the gain have been separated and the case for it being a richness has been made.

de-c1-sprachwandel.scene: An acquaintance says the language is deteriorating. Separate change from decline, give a historical example, accept the point where they are right and propose a shared test.
de-c1-sprachwandel.partner: an acquaintance troubled by loanwords who says it was better before
de-c1-sprachwandel.openingTr: Just listen to it — not a sentence left without English. Isn't that decline?
de-c1-sprachwandel.goal: Change and decline have been separated, a historical example has been given and a shared test has been proposed.

de-c1-finale.scene: You are having a last review with your teacher at the end of C1: how the road has gone, which moment was the turning point, what you can do now, what the language has come to mean to you and what comes next.
de-c1-finale.partner: an honest and warm teacher who has followed you from the start
de-c1-finale.openingTr: Five hundred lessons. Before we close: which moment was the turning point for you?
de-c1-finale.goal: The turning point has been described, what you can now do has been listed, what the language means has been said and the next goal has been given.

cando.A1.SPK.1: I can introduce myself: my name, where I am from and where I live.
cando.A1.SPK.2: I can greet people, ask how they are and say goodbye.
cando.A1.SPK.3: I can place a simple order and ask the price in a café, a bakery or a shop.
cando.A1.SPK.4: I can say numbers, the time, the date and my phone number.
cando.A1.SPK.5: I can describe my job, my family and my hobbies in a few sentences.
cando.A1.SPK.6: I can answer simple questions if people speak slowly and clearly, and ask them to repeat when I do not understand.
cando.A1.LS.1: I can understand greetings, introductions and simple instructions said slowly and clearly.
cando.A1.LS.2: I can understand numbers, prices and times when I hear them.
cando.A1.LS.3: I can catch what a short answerphone message is about (who, when).
cando.A1.LS.4: I can understand simple sentences said to me in a shop or a café.
cando.A1.LS.5: I can understand the name, origin and job of somebody introducing themselves.
cando.A1.RD.1: I can read and understand signs, menus and simple notices.
cando.A1.RD.2: I can understand a short message or postcard (a greeting, an invitation, a thank you).
cando.A1.RD.3: I can read a simple form (name, address, date of birth) and understand what is being asked for.
cando.A1.RD.4: I can find the basic facts in a short, simple description of a person or a product.
cando.A1.RD.5: I can find the time and the place in a programme or a timetable.
cando.A1.WR.1: I can fill in a form with my personal details.
cando.A1.WR.2: I can write a short greeting, thank you or invitation message.
cando.A1.WR.3: I can write 3–5 sentences introducing myself.
cando.A1.WR.4: I can build simple main clauses and join them with 'und' and 'aber'.
cando.A1.WR.5: I can write about my daily routine in simple sentences.
cando.A1.GR.1: I can use the article of a noun (der/die/das) and its plural correctly.
cando.A1.GR.2: I can conjugate verbs in the Präsens for the subject (ich/du/er…).
cando.A1.GR.3: I can put the verb in second place in a main clause and build a question.
cando.A1.GR.4: I can use sein, haben and the basic modal verbs (können, möchten).
cando.A1.GR.5: I can choose the personal and possessive pronouns correctly (ich/mein, du/dein…).
cando.A1.GR.6: I can place separable verbs (aufstehen, anrufen) correctly in a main clause.
cando.A2.SPK.1: I can make an appointment on the phone and agree a day and a time.
cando.A2.SPK.2: I can give directions and follow directions I am given.
cando.A2.SPK.3: I can tell what I did in the past (yesterday, at the weekend, on holiday) with the Perfekt.
cando.A2.SPK.4: I can tell the doctor what is wrong and ask for medicine at the pharmacy.
cando.A2.SPK.5: I can talk about size, colour and price when shopping and ask to return something.
cando.A2.SPK.6: I can answer an invitation, make a suggestion and accept or refuse one.
cando.A2.SPK.7: I can explain a simple problem (a broken appliance, noise) politely.
cando.A2.LS.1: I can understand the platform, the time and the delay in train and bus announcements.
cando.A2.LS.2: I can understand the main points of a phone call about an appointment or an order.
cando.A2.LS.3: I can follow the subject of a slow conversation and what the people want.
cando.A2.LS.4: I can get the weather, the traffic or an event from a short radio or podcast item.
cando.A2.LS.5: I can understand simple instructions given to me by a doctor, an official or a shop assistant.
cando.A2.RD.1: I can understand the request, the date and the place in a short email or message.
cando.A2.RD.2: I can pick the advert that suits me (a flat, a job, something second-hand).
cando.A2.RD.3: I can understand a simple notice or information text (rules, opening hours).
cando.A2.RD.4: I can understand what a short newspaper report is about.
cando.A2.RD.5: I can follow the steps in a recipe or a set of instructions.
cando.A2.WR.1: I can write a message suggesting a meeting to a friend with a place and a time.
cando.A2.WR.2: I can write a short email accepting or refusing an invitation.
cando.A2.WR.3: I can describe my holiday or my weekend in 5–8 sentences with the Perfekt.
cando.A2.WR.4: I can write a short note of complaint or apology.
cando.A2.WR.5: I can write sentences of reason and condition with weil, dass and wenn.
cando.A2.GR.1: I can build the Perfekt (haben/sein + Partizip II) with regular and common irregular verbs.
cando.A2.GR.2: I can choose the Akkusativ and Dativ articles and prepositions correctly (mit, für, zu…).
cando.A2.GR.3: I can put the verb last in weil/dass/wenn clauses.
cando.A2.GR.4: I can use the modal verbs (müssen, dürfen, sollen, wollen) in the Präsens and the Präteritum.
cando.A2.GR.6: I can make comparisons (größer als, am besten).
cando.B1.SPK.1: I can give my view on a subject and back it with two or three reasons.
cando.B1.SPK.2: I can tell the outline of a film, a book or an event.
cando.B1.SPK.3: I can explain what I need at an official body (the council, a bank) and get the information I want.
cando.B1.SPK.4: I can put a complaint politely but clearly and suggest a solution.
cando.B1.SPK.5: I can talk about my plans and my dreams (würde, möchte, wenn).
cando.B1.SPK.6: I can take the floor in a conversation and say whether I agree with the other person.
cando.B1.SPK.7: I can give a short two-minute presentation (myself, my town, my job).
cando.B1.LS.1: I can understand the main idea and most of the detail in a conversation at everyday speed.
cando.B1.LS.2: I can understand the main headlines of a news bulletin.
cando.B1.LS.3: I can follow a person's view and their reasons in an interview.
cando.B1.LS.4: I can understand the instructions and decisions in a meeting at work.
cando.B1.LS.5: I can work out from a voice message what is wanted and when it is to be done.
cando.B1.RD.1: I can understand the writer's view in a column or a forum comment.
cando.B1.RD.2: I can understand the request and the deadline in a formal letter or email.
cando.B1.RD.3: I can pick out the points that matter to me from an information text (health, insurance, rent).
cando.B1.RD.4: I can read a short story or a personal account and follow the plot.
cando.B1.RD.5: I can understand the requirements and the application steps in a job advert.
cando.B1.WR.1: I can write a text of 80–120 words setting out my view with reasons.
cando.B1.WR.2: I can write a formal email (an application, a request for information, a complaint).
cando.B1.WR.3: I can tell an event or an experience in time order and with conjunctions.
cando.B1.WR.4: I can write a comment on a forum and reply to somebody else's view.
cando.B1.WR.5: I can choose between the informal and the formal register (du/Sie, the greeting, the close).
cando.B1.GR.1: I can build subclauses with conjunctions like obwohl, damit and während.
cando.B1.GR.2: I can build polite requests and hypotheses with the Konjunktiv II (würde, hätte, könnte).
cando.B1.GR.3: I can build the Passiv in the Präsens and the Präteritum.
cando.B1.GR.4: I can build a Relativsatz (der/die/das … ist).
cando.B1.GR.5: I can use the Präteritum with the verbs of narration (war, hatte, ging, kam).
cando.B1.GR.6: I can get the Genitiv right in its basic uses (wegen, trotz, des Vaters).
cando.B2.SPK.1: I can defend my view in a debate and answer the opposing one.
cando.B2.SPK.2: I can discuss an abstract subject (the environment, technology, education) with its pros and cons.
cando.B2.SPK.3: I can describe my experience and my strengths in detail at a job interview.
cando.B2.SPK.4: I can describe a problem and set out its causes and possible solutions.
cando.B2.SPK.5: I can give a structured five-minute presentation and answer questions on it.
cando.B2.SPK.6: I can move naturally between the formal and the informal register.
cando.B2.LS.1: I can follow the outline and the arguments of a long talk or lecture.
cando.B2.LS.2: I can tell the speakers' positions apart in a radio discussion.
cando.B2.LS.3: I can catch the implications and the shifts of tone in a dialogue at natural speed.
cando.B2.LS.4: I can take detailed information from a documentary or a podcast episode.
cando.B2.LS.5: I can listen to the minutes of a meeting and note the decisions and who is responsible.
cando.B2.RD.1: I can understand the writer's stance and the implied meaning in a long column or interview.
cando.B2.RD.2: I can understand the terms in a contract, a tenancy or business correspondence.
cando.B2.RD.3: I can understand an article outside my field (science, economics) with its main idea and evidence.
cando.B2.RD.4: I can analyse the structure of an essay (thesis, reasons, conclusion).
cando.B2.RD.5: I can gather information from different sources and compare it.
cando.B2.WR.1: I can write a text of 150–200 words weighing the pros and cons of a subject.
cando.B2.WR.2: I can write a formal letter of complaint or application and justify it.
cando.B2.WR.3: I can summarise a text and add my own view.
cando.B2.WR.4: I can give a structured reply to a view in a letter to the editor or a forum post.
cando.B2.WR.5: I can build flowing paragraphs with conjunctions and transitions (zwar…aber, einerseits…andererseits).
cando.B2.GR.1: I can use the Passiv in every tense and tell 'werden/sein + Partizip' apart.
cando.B2.GR.2: I can report speech with the Konjunktiv I.
cando.B2.GR.3: I can build adjective phrases with the Partizip I/II.
cando.B2.GR.4: I can move between Nominalisierung and Verbalisierung.
cando.B2.GR.5: I can use the paired conjunctions correctly (nicht nur…sondern auch, je…desto).
cando.B2.GR.6: I can use the Plusquamperfekt and the Futur II to relate events in time.
cando.C1.SPK.1: I can present and discuss a complex subject fluently and in a structured way.
cando.C1.SPK.2: I can use fine differences of meaning and register (irony, degrees of politeness).
cando.C1.SPK.3: I can look for a compromise in a negotiation with concessions and conditions.
cando.C1.SPK.4: I can bring idioms and set phrases into my speech naturally.
cando.C1.SPK.5: I can correct myself and rephrase in the middle of a long turn.
cando.C1.LS.1: I can understand long speech that is fast, dialectal or in a noisy setting.
cando.C1.LS.2: I can catch the unspoken stance, the irony and the hints in a panel or a debate.
cando.C1.LS.3: I can follow the structure of the argument in an academic lecture.
cando.C1.LS.4: I can understand colloquial speech and cultural references in films and series.
cando.C1.RD.1: I can understand long and complex texts (essays, articles, literature) with their implied meanings.
cando.C1.RD.2: I can extract the information I need from specialist texts (legal, medical, technical).
cando.C1.RD.3: I can analyse a writer's style and rhetorical devices.
cando.C1.RD.4: I can compare different views and assess them critically.
cando.C1.WR.1: I can write a long, clearly structured essay or report (300+ words).
cando.C1.WR.2: I can adapt my style to the reader and the purpose (formal, academic, journalistic).
cando.C1.WR.3: I can summarise a complex subject and add a critical comment.
cando.C1.WR.4: I can hold a long text together with conjunctions and references.
cando.C1.GR.1: I can build complex syntax (nested subclauses, Partizipialkonstruktionen).
cando.C1.GR.2: I can use the Modal Partikeln (doch, ja, mal, eben) and the markers of register naturally.
cando.C1.GR.3: I can build the past and the finer uses of the Konjunktiv II (hätte…sollen).
cando.C1.GR.4: I can use the set verb-noun combinations (Funktionsverbgefüge).
cando.A1.GR.11: I can use am, is and are in positive, negative and question sentences.
cando.A1.GR.12: I can choose between a and an, and use the when I talk about something known.
cando.A1.GR.13: I can make nouns plural: -s, -es and irregular forms like men, women, children.
cando.A1.GR.14: I can show possession: my, your, his, her and 's added to a name.
cando.A1.GR.15: I can build the present simple: -s in the third person, do and does for questions and negatives.
cando.A1.GR.16: I can choose the right prepositions of time and place: in, on, at.
cando.A1.GR.17: I can give instructions with the imperative: Turn left, Don't worry.
cando.A1.GR.18: I can build a question: the question word first, then the auxiliary, then the subject.
cando.A2.GR.11: I can build the past simple: regular -ed, irregular verbs, did for questions and negatives.
cando.A2.GR.12: I can talk about the ongoing past: was/were + -ing, with when and while.
cando.A2.GR.13: I can use the present perfect: ever, never, since, for, already, yet and just.
cando.A2.GR.14: I can compare: -er and -est, more and most, as … as.
cando.A2.GR.15: I can talk about the future: going to for a plan, will for a decision made on the spot.
cando.A2.GR.16: I can express ability, advice and obligation with can, should, must and have to.
cando.B1.GR.11: I can choose between the present perfect and the past simple: the past simple when the time is finished, the present perfect when the experience still counts.
cando.B1.GR.12: I can put two past events in order: the earlier one goes into the past perfect, had plus the third form.
cando.B1.GR.13: I can talk about the future in three ways: the present continuous for a fixed arrangement, going to for an intention, will for a prediction or an on-the-spot decision.
cando.B1.GR.14: I can build first and second conditionals: if with the present goes with will, if with the past goes with would.
cando.B1.GR.15: I can build relative clauses with who, which and that, and leave the pronoun out when it is the object.
cando.B1.GR.16: I can report what someone said: the tense steps back, and pronouns and time words shift with it.
cando.B1.GR.17: I can build the passive in the present and the past: is or was plus the third form, with by for the doer where it matters.
cando.B1.GR.18: I can draw conclusions with must, might and can't, and talk about obligation and advice with have to, don't have to and should.
cando.B1.GR.19: I can choose whether -ing or to follows a verb: enjoy doing, decide to do, and the difference between stop doing and stop to do.
cando.B1.GR.20: I can hold a long sentence together with linking words: although, however, so that, in order to and despite.
cando.B2.GR.11: I can speculate about the past and express regret: must have been, can't have done, should have said.
cando.B2.GR.12: I can build third and mixed conditionals: if plus past perfect, then would have, for a past that did not happen and its result today.
cando.B2.GR.13: I can report information whose source is unclear with a passive structure: it is said that and he is thought to.
cando.B2.GR.14: I can move the emphasis to the front with a cleft sentence: what I need is and it was … who.
cando.B2.GR.15: I can use inversion after a negative adverbial at the front: rarely have I and not only did he.
cando.B2.GR.16: I can join two sentences with a participle clause: having finished and being asked.
cando.B2.GR.17: I can use non-defining relative clauses and relative pronouns after a preposition: …, which is why and the person to whom.
cando.B2.GR.18: I can speak from a point in the future: the future perfect for what will be finished, the future continuous for what will be going on.
cando.B2.GR.19: I can turn a verb into a noun for a formal register: the introduction of the rule instead of they introduced the rule.
cando.B2.GR.20: I can soften a claim and steer the text: arguably, admittedly, to some extent, that said.
cando.C1.GR.11: I can leave out what does not need saying: I would if I could, so do I, the former and the latter.
cando.C1.GR.12: I can push the weight to the end and carry the stress to the front: Into the hall came and What he did next was.
cando.C1.GR.13: I can choose the fixed forms of formal request: I insist that he be, were it not for and lest.
cando.C1.GR.14: I can set the tone of concession and contrast: granted, albeit, whereas and much as I.
cando.C1.GR.15: I can use settled collocations and light verbs: take issue with, bear the brunt, draw a distinction.
cando.C1.GR.16: I can say the same content in three registers: legal language, neutral language and spoken language.
cando.C1.GR.17: I can load the judgement onto the reporting verb: he claimed, he conceded, he alleged.
cando.C1.GR.18: I can set the distance with modal nuance: may well, might have been expected to, would tend to.
cando.C1.GR.19: I can build and hear understatement and irony: not exactly cheap, I wouldn't say no.

prose.Mert otelde kalmayacaklarını söylüyor: \: Mert says they will not stay in a hotel: "my cousin has a flat near the sea. We're going to stay there for three nights."

prose.Can sıkıntısını savunan kısa bir köşe ya: You are going to read a short column in defence of boredom: what the writer claims, which evidence they use, what they suggest.

prose.„Marta didn't laugh. She told us that fe: „Marta didn't laugh. She told us that fear is normal …“ — the writer stresses the teacher's understanding; no harshness and no joke.

prose.Üç konuşmacılı bir panel dinleyeceksin:: You are going to hear a panel of three speakers: why volunteers leave, why exit interviews do not work, and what can be done.

prose.Notta \"I have already booked a room for: The note says "I have already booked a room for you at the hotel" and adds that she should not pay for it, as it is their present.

prose.„Ich habe deine Anzeige in der Bibliothe: „Ich habe deine Anzeige in der Bibliothek gelesen“ and Murat's question confirms it: „Du suchst also einen Tandem-Partner?“
prose.\"We've got a big sale on bread too — bu: The sentence "We've got a big sale on bread too — buy two, get one free." says that if you buy two loaves you get one free.
prose.Bir orman görevlisi gruba ormanı gezdiri: A forester takes a group round the wood: he describes what has changed, what they are planting and what he expects of visitors.
prose.Yan cümle birinci öğedir; ikinci sıra fi: The clause is the first element; second place belongs to the verb and the subject falls behind it: Weil ich krank war, bin ich zu Hause geblieben.
prose.„Some people do use them exactly that wa: „Some people do use them exactly that way. It is simply not the reason the bench was redesigned.“ — true, but not the reason.
prose.Almancada „ch“ iki ayrı sestir: ince ünl: In German „ch“ is two different sounds: soft after a front vowel (ich) and from the throat after a back one (Buch). Neither exists in Turkish.
prose.Bir kış aksaklığının ardından yazılmış ç: You are going to read an analysis written after a winter breakdown: which decisions were each reasonable, and why the system still collapsed.
prose.\"It's at the Green Garden Hotel, near t: The place follows from "It's at the Green Garden Hotel, near the train station"; not the airport but next to the station.
prose.\"On Saturday, we're open from eight to: The sentence "On Saturday, we're open from eight to eight" says they are open from eight in the morning to eight at night, so it is true.
prose.„You asked in a meeting, with you in the: „You asked in a meeting, with you in the room. That is not the same as an open call.“ — the way the question was put decided the answer.
prose.Arkadaşın Ayla köpek almayı düşünüyor ve: Your friend Ayla is thinking of getting a dog and asks what you think; first form two sentences, then write your view and reasons in reply to her email.
prose.\"For a birth certificate or proof of ad: It says "For a birth certificate or proof of address, please come to the third floor, room 214.": the third floor, room 214.

prose.Almancada vurgu yeri anlamı taşır: ayrıl: In German the place of the stress carries meaning: a separable prefix is stressed, an inseparable one is not, and in a compound the first part comes forward.

prose.\"You must bring your ID card and your l: The sentence "You must bring your ID card and your last bill when you pay for water" says so. Cash is also no longer accepted.
prose.Bu egzersizde gezideyken yazılan bir kar: In this exercise you will practise a postcard written while travelling: where you have arrived, what you have done and what you will do tomorrow.
prose.Geçen hafta sonunu anlatan kısa bir kart: You will practise writing a short postcard about last weekend and using the past tense (was/were, -ed, irregular verbs).
prose.Notta \"Breakfast is only in the morning: The note says "Breakfast is only in the morning. We serve it from 8:00 to 11:00." The café is open until 19:00 but breakfast is only in the morning.
prose.Tam tersi: „staff … are not the villains: The opposite: „staff … are not the villains of this story; they have been handed a social problem in the form of a cleaning schedule.“
prose.Bu derste bir mağazaya arızalı ürün için: In this lesson you will practise complaining to a shop about a faulty item, mentioning the guarantee and the receipt, and politely asking for a refund.

prose.\"Our offices are open from Monday to Fr: The sentence "Our offices are open from Monday to Friday, from eight thirty in the morning" says they open at half past eight.
prose.„Zehn Nachbarn helfen hier“ ve „Wir repa: „Zehn Nachbarn helfen hier“ and „Wir reparieren nicht für Sie, wir reparieren mit Ihnen“ — neither a shop nor a course, but working together.
prose.Anonsta \"The train to Manchester is lea: The announcement says "The train to Manchester is leaving from platform five at nine fifteen." The Manchester train goes from platform five.
prose.Metinde \"More than three hundred people: The text says "More than three hundred people came to the small park next to the river at nine o'clock", so they came at nine.
prose.„improved seating“ gibi bir ifade kararı: „improved seating“ makes both the decision and the decider invisible; „Nobody has to defend a policy that was never written down.“
prose.\"We have already received your deposit: According to the sentence "We have already received your deposit of £60" the hotel has had 60 pounds so far; 240 pounds is the total price.
prose.Kapıda kalanlara yönelik bir tüketici re: You are going to read a consumer guide for people locked out: what to ask on the phone, what to watch for, what to do if the bill is extortionate.
prose.Son bölümde \"The council will plant fif: The last section says "The council will plant fifty new trees along the river path next spring"; they will plant fifty new trees next spring.
prose.„a low score can cost someone their work: „a low score can cost someone their work, so they give five stars to anyone who was not rude“ — a rating is not an assessment but a decision.
prose.\"Passengers for Liverpool can wait in t: We know it from "Passengers for Liverpool can wait in the café next to platform three."; the café is beside platform three and it is open.

prose.Ana da Dilara'yı beğeniyor; tartışma sür: Ana thinks well of Dilara too; the argument is about the process: „I would like to see an external shortlist as well, even if we end up choosing her.“
prose.Ev arkadaşına market listesi bırakmayı ç: You will practise leaving a shopping list for your flatmate: saying what has run out, giving quantities and asking politely.
prose.Radyo sunucusu, tatillerini ev takasıyla: A radio presenter talks to Leyla, who spends her holidays swapping houses: how the system works, why she was worried at first, what she thinks now.
prose.„Tabletten mit Rezept bekommen Sie nur i: „Tabletten mit Rezept bekommen Sie nur in der Apotheke, nicht in der Drogerie.“ In Germany a Drogerie sells no medicine — it sells soap and shampoo.
prose.„Wir treffen uns einmal im Monat, immer: „Wir treffen uns einmal im Monat, immer am zweiten Samstag.“ — „am zweiten Samstag“ says which Saturday of the month, not how many.
prose.İngilizcenin iki geçmiş zamanını ayırmay: Learn to tell the two English pasts apart: when have + past participle and when -ed; the markers since/for, already/yet, ever/never.

prose.\"the store is closing at eight o'clock: The sentence "the store is closing at eight o'clock this evening" says closing is at eight; three is when the announcement is made.
prose.Bir kasabanın sokak lambalarını doksan d: You are going to read a report about the night a town turned its street lights off for ninety minutes: whose idea it was, what was measured, what comes next.
prose.„If we teach a generation that quiet mea: „If we teach a generation that quiet means dangerous and loud means safe, we will have solved this decade's problem and created the next one.“
prose.„In dieser knappen Zeit muss das Anliege: „In dieser knappen Zeit muss das Anliegen auf dem Tisch liegen.“ The Werdegang and the technical apology are named in the text as the commonest mistake.
prose.Yazı boyunca ölçeğin ikiye indiği, örnek: Throughout the article the scale collapsing to two, the sample being skewed and the pressure being added are described; the last paragraph defends feedback itself.
prose.„What we test for is whether a listener: „What we test for is whether a listener can tell … that the car is approaching … Not whether they like it.“ Liking comes later and from repetition.

prose.Ev sahibine yazılan kısa bir e-postada e: You will practise a short email to the landlord reporting a fault in the flat, saying how long it has been going on and asking politely for help.

"It's Ayse Demir." The family name is Demir.
