task.reply.checklist\u0000En az bir dönüşlü f: Did you use at least one reflexive verb in the right order („Ich muss mich …“)?
task.reply.checklist\u0000Orada ne yaptığını: Did you write what you did there with „haben“ (habe … gemacht / unternommen)?
task.reply.checklist\u0000Sorunu bir sıfatla: Did you describe the problem with an adjective (fehlerhaft / beschädigt / zerbrochen)?
task.reply.checklist\u0000Karşılıklı anlamı t: Did you use the reciprocal reflexive pronoun („wir haben uns …“)?
task.reply.checklist\u0000Emeği süresiyle bir: Did you write the effort together with how long it took („Ich habe … lange trainiert / gelernt“)?
task.reply.checklist\u0000Nereye gittiğini ye: Did you write where you went with a verb of movement (bin … gefahren / verreist)?
task.reply.checklist\u0000Sorunun tam olarak: Did you name exactly what the problem is (uncertainty, the address, the timing)?
task.free.prompt\u0000Foruma kahvaltını anlat: Describe your breakfast on the forum (4-5 sentences). What do you eat, what do you drink, what do you not like?
task.free.prompt\u0000Evini anlat (4-5 cümle): Describe your home (4-5 sentences). How many rooms are there, what sort of place is it, which pieces of furniture stand where?
task.free.prompt\u0000Foruma yaz (4-5 cümle):: Write on the forum (4-5 sentences): What do you like wearing, which colours do you like, do you buy expensive clothes?
task.free.prompt\u0000Arkadaşına evine nasıl: Write to a friend explaining how to get to your home (4-5 sentences). Give at least two directions, name a means of transport and say how long it takes.
task.free.prompt\u0000Ev arkadaşına market no: Write a shopping note for your flatmate (4-5 sentences). Say what you are going to cook, ask for at least three things and give the quantities.
task.free.prompt\u0000Arkadaşının mesajına ce: Write a reply to your friend's message (4-5 sentences). Say whether you have time at the weekend, suggest a plan and give a time.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir aile fotoğrafını an: Describe a family photograph (4-5 sentences). Say who is in it, how many of them there are and how old one of them is.
task.free.prompt\u0000Foruma yaz (4-5 cümle):: Write on the forum (4-5 sentences): Which sport do you do, and how often? What music do you listen to? What do you do when the weather is fine?
task.free.prompt\u0000Foruma kısa bir mesaj y: Write a short message on the forum (3-4 sentences). Cover these: your name, where you come from, your job and which languages you speak.
task.free.prompt\u0000Arkadaşının mesajına ce: Write a reply to your friend's message (4-5 sentences). Write how to get there from the station, how long it takes and what there is nearby.
task.free.prompt\u0000Haftanı anlat (5-6 cüml: Describe your week (5-6 sentences). Use at least three names of days, write what you did on each day and use at least one separable verb.
task.free.prompt\u0000Şehrini soran birine ce: Write a reply to somebody asking about your town (4-5 sentences). Suggest at least two places to visit, give directions to one of them and suggest a way of getting there.
task.free.prompt\u0000Arkadaşının mesajına ce: Write a reply to your friend's message (4-5 sentences). Suggest a present, say why you like it, give a price and write where it can be bought.
task.free.prompt\u0000Kurs forumuna aileni ta: Write a short message introducing your family on the course forum (4-5 sentences). Say how old you are and describe your parents and any brothers or sisters.
task.free.prompt\u0000Deniz kenarında tatilde: You are on holiday by the sea. Write a postcard to a friend: where you are, what the weather is like, what you do every day, when you are coming back.
task.free.prompt\u0000Apartman görevlisine no: Write a note to the caretaker (4-5 sentences). Say what is broken, how long it has been like that, when you are at home, and ask about the price.
task.free.prompt\u0000Evlenen bir arkadaşına: Write a short message of congratulation to a friend who is getting married (4-5 sentences). Congratulate them, say what you will bring and write that you would like to celebrate together.
task.free.prompt\u0000Gününü anlat (5-6 cümle: Describe your day (5-6 sentences). Write what time it started, what you did first and afterwards, and what you did in the evening. Use at least two times of day.
task.free.prompt\u0000Arkadaşına taşınma için: Write a message to a friend asking for help with a move (4-5 sentences). Say when it is, what has to be done and what to be careful about.
task.free.prompt\u0000Aşağıdaki ilana e-posta: Answer the advertisement below by email. Introduce yourself, explain why you would like to take part, say which days suit you and ask a question.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir arkadaşın iki hafta: A friend is going to look after your home for two weeks. Write instructions: the plants, the post, the bins, one appliance that needs special handling, what to do in an emergency and how to reach you.
task.free.prompt\u0000İyi tanıdığın bir dükkâ: Review a shop or a cafe you know well on the internet: where it is, what it sells, what you liked, one thing that could be better, and how many stars you give it.
task.free.prompt\u0000Aşağıdaki duyuruya kuru: Reply to the announcement below with an opinion piece addressed to the institution itself. Show that you understand the decision, give reasons for your objection and put forward a concrete suggestion.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bıraktığın ve sonra yen: Describe a habit you gave up and then took up again: what it was, why you had given it up, what brought you back, what changed, and whether you would recommend it to anybody else.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir firmadaki açık pozi: Write a covering letter for an open position at a company. Introduce yourself, say what experience you have, give reasons for wanting the job and ask for an interview.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir teknik sorunu bildi: Report a technical problem: what happened and when, what you have tried, what is not working now, what you want done and by when. Use a formal salutation and closing.
task.free.prompt\u0000Geç anladığın bir şeyi: Describe something you understood late: what you believed at the time, what shook you, what you think today, why it took so long, and what is left of your old view.
task.free.prompt\u0000Arkadaşın seni cumartes: A friend has invited you to a picnic by the lake on Saturday but you cannot go. Write a message (4-5 sentences): say thank you, give a clear no, give your reason and suggest ANOTHER day.
task.free.prompt\u0000Hafta sonunu foruma yaz: Write about your weekend on the forum (5-6 sentences), all of it in the PAST: where you went, what you did, what you saw or heard. Build at least one sentence with „sein“ and one with „haben“.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir pazar alışverişini: Describe a trip to the market: where you went, what you bought (at least five things, with numbers), what the prices were like, and what you did not buy and why. Watch the plural forms after the numbers.
task.free.prompt\u0000Arkadaşın iş bulduğunu: Your friend has written to say they have found a job. Reply with a short message: congratulate them, say how pleased you are, ask one or two questions about the job, suggest meeting up and write when you have time.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir daire ilanına e-pos: Write an email about a flat advertisement. Introduce yourself briefly (who you are, what you do), ask three questions (the floor, the heating costs, when it is free) and ask for a viewing.
task.free.prompt\u0000Birkaç haftadır yeni bi: You have been doing something new for a few weeks (sport, a choir, a course, volunteering — you choose). Write to a friend: when you started, how it is going, what the first day was like, and invite them along.
task.free.prompt\u0000Derneğin forumunda bir: A proposal is being discussed on the association's forum. Write your contribution: take a clear position, give two reasons, mention an objection you take seriously and make a concrete proposal that would improve the plan.
task.free.prompt\u0000Odanı boşaltıyorsun. Bi: You are clearing out your room. Write a small advertisement to sell one of your things: what you are selling, what it looks like, how old it is, how much you want, and when and where the buyer can collect it.
task.free.prompt\u0000İçinde kimlik ve adres: You have found a wallet with an ID card and an address in it. Write an email to the owner: what you found, where and when, what is inside, how and when they can have it back, and how they can reach you.
task.free.prompt\u0000Hastasın ve yarınki der: You are ill and cannot go to your class or your work tomorrow. Write a message (4-5 sentences): say that you are ill, write what hurts, state that you have a doctor's appointment and say when you will be back.
task.free.prompt\u0000Yurt dışında yaşayan es: Write a letter to an old friend living abroad: apologise for not writing for so long, tell them what has changed in your life, ask about theirs, invite them to visit and write a warm closing.
task.free.prompt\u0000Ev sahibine yazılı bir: Write a formal notice of a fault to your landlord: say what has broken, how long it has been going on, what you have tried and by when you expect it to be put right. Write impersonally and plainly, with no accusation.
task.free.prompt\u0000Forumda biri yeni bir ş: Somebody on the forum is asking how to make friends in a new town. Answer from your own experience: how long you have been there, what you tried, what worked, what did not, and give one concrete piece of advice.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir başvurunun reddedil: You have learnt that an application of yours has been turned down. Write a short, polite email to the company: say thank you, ask for brief feedback, and ask them to let you know if a new position comes up.
task.free.prompt\u0000Tanıdığın bir kişiyi an: Describe somebody you know: who they are, how you met, which quality of theirs left a mark on you, and why you are describing them. Use at least three relative clauses (der/die/das and den).
task.free.prompt\u0000Taşındığını ya da taşın: Announce that you have moved or are about to move: the old place and the new one, when, why, what is good about the new place and what is missing, and how to get there. Use at least one 'in + time' and one 'nach + time'.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir çevrimiçi siparişle: Write about an online order: what you ordered and when, what was missing or wrong, which documents you have, what you want, and by when. Use a formal salutation and closing.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir randevuyu erteleyen: Write a formal email postponing an appointment: which appointment (day and time), why you cannot keep it, which dates would suit you and that you would like confirmation. Use a formal salutation and closing.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir yolculuktan bir gec: Describe one night or one incident from a journey: where and when, what happened, how you felt at the time, what stayed with you. Let at least three of your sentences start with a subordinate clause (Als …, Wenn …, Nachdem …).
task.free.prompt\u0000Kaldırımın kime ait old: Write a short column on who the pavement belongs to: describe your observation concretely, name the conflict, weigh up the interests of at least two sides, take a clear position and finish with one single concrete measure.
task.free.prompt\u0000Odanı beş ay için devre: You want to sublet your room for five months. Write an advertisement: the size of the room and its furnishings, which dates it is free, the rent and the bills, a sentence about the flatmates, and who would suit.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir kuruma ya da firmay: Write a formal letter of complaint to an institution or a company: what you bought and when, what the problem is, whom you spoke to and what happened, what you want, and by when. Use at least two genitives (des/der).
task.free.prompt\u0000Forumda şehrin çeşme ya: The forum is discussing whether the town should build a fountain. Write your contribution: take a clear position, give two reasons, concede one argument from the other side that you find fair, and finish with a concrete proposal.
task.free.prompt\u0000Katıldığın (ya da katıl: Describe voluntary work you do (or would like to do): what, where, since when, what good it does, what did not work, and what you would say to other people. Use at least two 'ohne … zu' sentences.
task.free.prompt\u0000Yaşadığın ya da bildiği: Describe a neighbourhood you live in or know: what it used to be like, what has changed, what has got better, what has got worse, and what you think about its future. Use at least two of 'viel/viele' and one 'wenig/wenige'.
task.free.prompt\u0000Derneğin ya da apartman: Describe an event you took part in for the association's or the building's newsletter: when and where it was, how many people came, what was done, whether anything went wrong, how it ended and whom you are thanking.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir dileğini yaz: ne di: Write about a wish: what you would wish for, why, what would change in your life if it came true, and what you can do about it now. Use at least three Konjunktiv II sentences and let wäre or hätte appear in at least one.
task.free.prompt\u0000Sevdiğin bir yemeği tar: Describe and recommend a dish you like: the name of the dish and where it comes from, the ingredients you need, the order of preparation (zuerst / danach / zum Schluss), and why you recommend it. Use at least one infinitive with 'zu'.
task.free.prompt\u0000Yönetime bir öneri yaz:: Write a proposal to the management: what you are proposing, why (at least two reasons), what is needed, what the risk is, and by when you would like an answer. Use a formal salutation and closing. Use at least two 'dass' sentences.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir kuralı açıkla (işye: Explain a rule (a workplace, a building, a course — you choose): what the rule is, whom it applies to, whether there are exceptions, what happens if it is broken, and why such a rule exists. Use at least two 'Es ist …, dass …' sentences.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir yavru köpeği ilk ke: Write instructions for people raising a puppy for the first time: what the first week is like, what it has to get used to, what to avoid, when and what to report, and how it ends. Use short headings.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir yazıya okur mektubu: Object to an article in a letter to the editor: name the point you agree with, formulate your objection precisely, back it up with an example or a figure, anticipate the counter-argument, and finish by saying what you want.
task.free.prompt\u0000Çevre için değiştirdiği: Describe a habit you changed for the sake of the environment: what you used to do, what you do now, how hard the change was, and what you would recommend to other people. Use at least two 'statt … zu' sentences.
task.free.prompt\u0000Arkadaşın soğuk algınlı: Your friend has written to say they have a cold. Reply to them (4-5 sentences): say you are sorry, give at least two pieces of advice (in the imperative), write when they ought to see a doctor and finish with „Gute Besserung“.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir yolculuğu anlat: ne: Describe a journey: where you went, by which means of transport, what happened on the way, how long it took, and what the return was like. Use at least three different prepositions of direction (nach / in / zu) and at least two 'mit dem/der' statements of transport.
task.free.prompt\u0000Küçük bir anketi raporl: Report a small survey (real or imagined): how many people were asked, the three commonest answers, one surprising result, and the recommendation that follows. Use at least three 'die meisten / viele / einige' sentences.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir aksaklıktan sonra e: Write an assessment note for the team after something went wrong: what happened, what was defensible on the day and why, what could have been done differently, the pattern behind it, and two concrete consequences. Use headings.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir konuda görüşünü yaz: Write your opinion on a subject: introduce the subject, list at least one point for and one against, give your own view with your reasons, and answer the opposing view politely. Use at least one 'da-' compound (davon, daran, darüber).
task.free.prompt\u0000Muayenehaneye resmî bir: Write a formal email to a doctor's practice (4-5 sentences): open with a polite salutation, write that you would like to change your Wednesday appointment, ask which day would suit, leave your telephone number and finish with the RIGHT closing.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir başvurunun reddine: Write a letter of objection to the refusal of an application: which decision you are objecting to (date and number), why you are objecting, which documents you are enclosing and what you want. Use a formal salutation and closing.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir ürünü iade etmek ya: Write to return or exchange a product: what you bought and when, what the problem is, whether you have the receipt, what you want (an exchange or your money back), and by when you expect an answer. Use a formal salutation and closing.
task.free.prompt\u0000İnternette bir tatil ev: You have found a holiday house on the internet. Write an email to the owner: when and how many of you would like to come, ask whether the house is free on those dates, ask about the price and one or two details such as the kitchen or parking, and ask for a reply.
task.free.prompt\u0000İki yer arasında bir ha: Describe a life lived between two places (your own or somebody's you know): when the move happened, what was missed at the start, what has changed today, and how that is lived with. Use at least one 'hierher' and one 'dorthin'.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir kutlama ya da doğa: Plan a celebration or a day out: what, where, when and how long it will last, who is bringing what, and what could go wrong. Use at least two statements of duration (accusative without a preposition) and at least one 'erst' or 'schon'.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir lokantada yaşadığın: Write about a problem you had in a restaurant: where and when, what exactly the problem was, what you said at the time, how the owner took it, and what you expect. Be polite but clear. Use at least one 'etwas' or 'nichts' with an adjective.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir meslektaşına yaptığ: Write a short, polite note to a colleague about a mistake they made: what the mistake is, why you are writing (not to accuse but to have it put right), a concrete suggestion and a good closing. Set a tone that does not accuse.
task.free.prompt\u0000Aileni anlat: kaç kişis: Describe your family: how many of you there are, who lives where, who is close to whom, a generation gap or a change (a move, a birth, a separation) and a family habit. Use at least two names of relatives in the accusative or the dative.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir alışkanlığını anlat: Describe a habit of yours and set up a proportion: what changes when you do more of it? Use at least two 'je … desto' sentences. Write what the habit is, when it started, what it was like at first and what it is like now.
task.free.prompt\u0000Sağlığın için değiştird: Describe a habit you changed for your health: what it used to be like, what you changed and why, how the first week went, and what you notice now. Use a modal verb in at least two subordinate clauses (weil … kann / muss / will).
task.free.prompt\u0000Hastanede yatan bir tan: Write a message to somebody you know who is in hospital: wish them well, explain why you could not visit (with a modal in the past), say what you would like to bring, suggest when you will come, and finish with a cheering sentence.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir konuda kısa bir tar: Write a short contribution to a discussion: state the subject in one sentence, bring two arguments (erstens / zweitens), answer one argument from the other side, and sum up at the end. Use at least one 'weil' sentence and one 'wegen' sentence.
task.free.prompt\u0000Çocukluğundan bir anı y: Write a memory from your childhood. Say where and when it was, describe something that happened every time (jedes Mal, wenn …), then describe something that happened once (als …), and write why that moment matters to you.
task.free.prompt\u0000Ortak bir evde temizlik: Write a cleaning rota for a shared flat: which areas there are, who does what, how often, which rule causes the most argument and how you settled it. Use at least two 'auch' or 'nur' sentences and mind their position.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bu yıl için öğrenme hed: Write your learning goals for this year: what you want to achieve, how you have planned it (how often, how much), how you will measure your progress, and what has not worked so far. Use at least two infinitives with 'zu'.
task.free.prompt\u0000Güvendiğin bir insanı a: Describe somebody you trust: who they are, where you met, which behaviour of theirs gives you that trust, and whether they have ever let you down. Use at least two dative relative clauses (dem / denen).
task.free.prompt\u0000Kendi Almanca yolculuğu: Write about your own German journey on the forum (6-7 sentences): When did you start? What was it like at the beginning? How did you work at it? What can you do now? What will you do next? Use „war“ and the Perfekt together when you write about the past.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir yüksekokula bilgi i: Write a formal email to a college asking for information: introduce yourself, say which field you are interested in, ask at least three questions (the start of term, the number of exams, working alongside), and ask for a reply. Use at least two 'ob' sentences.
task.free.prompt\u0000Aidiyet üzerine bir gör: Write an opinion on belonging: what does 'belonging here' mean to you, which criterion matters and which does not, an experience of your own or one you know of, and an answer to an opposing view. Use at least two sentences with 'sein/werden + a bare predicate'.
task.free.prompt\u0000Okuldan ya da bir eğiti: Write about your plans after school or after a course of training: which path you have chosen (an apprenticeship, school, work), why, which step you will take when, what is uncertain and whom you will ask. Use at least two 'gehen/lernen/helfen + infinitive' sentences.
task.free.prompt\u0000Üyesi olduğun bir derne: Ask an association you belong to for a reduced subscription. Write who you are and how long you have been a member, explain what has changed in your situation, say exactly what you want, state which document you are enclosing and write a polite closing.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir yerel ödülün jürisi: You are on the jury of a local prize. Write the reasons for your decision on the basis of the short dossier below: explain which criterion you used, justify the work you chose, mention the other candidate fairly and gather the decision into one sentence.
task.free.prompt\u0000B1 yolculuğunu kapat: n: Close your B1 journey: where you started, what was hardest, when you first said 'I have got it', what you can do now and what you still cannot, and what you will do next. Use at least three subordinate clauses and put the verbs in the right place.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir bilgilendirme topla: You attended an information meeting. Write an email to those who could not come: pass on what was announced, who objected to what, what was promised and what was left open, and finish with a suggestion. Report what was said in indirect speech.
task.free.prompt\u0000Uzun süredir devam eden: Describe a long-standing friendship: whom you have known and since when, how you met, how distance or time has affected the friendship, and what you do to keep it going. Use at least one 'kennen' sentence and one 'wissen' sentence.
task.free.prompt\u0000Evde bakım için bir pla: Write a plan for care at home: for whom, which tasks are hard, who will help and when, which small changes are needed, and what has to be discussed within the family. Use at least three nominalised infinitives (das Aufstehen, beim Anziehen, zum Waschen).
task.free.prompt\u0000Kurs sonunda kendi metn: Write your own text at the end of the course: What could you not do with your German a year ago? What can you do today? What gave you the most trouble and what is your goal now? Use at least one reason (weil), one condition (wenn) and one comparison (als).
task.free.prompt\u0000Okuduğun ya da izlediği: Write a club review of something you have read or watched: its name and its kind, its subject in brief, what you liked and what you did not (with the gefallen pattern), and whether you recommend it to other people. Use at least one 'freuen auf' or 'freuen über' sentence.
task.free.prompt\u0000Aşağıdaki durum için bi: Write the opening of a speech for the situation below (6-9 sentences). Use these: at least one inverted sentence (the subject must NOT be in first position), a triad, and a metaphor — but think about the logic the metaphor brings with it and do not create an enemy. At the end state the main line in one sentence.
task.free.prompt\u0000Aşağıdaki başvuruya olu: Write a negative reply to the application below that still leaves the door open. Separate the quality from the reason for the refusal, state the reservation plainly, show a concrete way forward, and use at least one light-verb phrase (in Frage kommen, zur Verfügung stehen, in Anspruch nehmen, Abstand nehmen).
task.free.prompt\u0000Aşağıdaki verilerle alt: Write a pitch of six to eight sentences using the data below. Start with a scene, name the need, state the distinguishing point with „Der Clou daran ist, dass …“, prove it with at least two figures, and at the end name a weakness yourself. Do not overstate; do not fall into the mistake Team B makes in the text.
task.free.prompt\u0000Yakın bir arkadaşın büy: A close friend has made a big decision and wants your honest view. Write a reply: say first that you are pleased, name your concern once and precisely, admit what you cannot judge, offer concrete help and close warmly. Use the small words of everyday speech.
task.free.prompt\u0000Sunuculuk yapıyorsun ve: You are hosting and the technical team needs two minutes. Fill the gap: set up a short situation, give a turning point (without announcing it), state a conclusion and at the end tie it to the handover to the next speaker. You have no script, so keep the sentences short. Do not trail the turning point in advance.
task.free.prompt\u0000Aşağıdaki basın açıklam: Write the INTERNAL version of the press release below, for the team, covering the same event. Unlike the outward-facing text: name the actor in every important sentence, say what was done and who did it, do not hide the open point, and write what you expect from the team. Use at least one light-verb phrase.
task.free.prompt\u0000Emekliye ayrılan bir me: Write a short farewell speech for a colleague who is retiring (7-10 sentences). The rules: do NOT open with a quotation; acknowledge their worth with at least two concrete details; state the mark they leave as evidence rather than as a claim; put a quotation at the end if you like. Avoid the cliches („Türen schließen sich“ and the like).
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir aboneliği (spor sal: Write a formal letter cancelling a subscription (a gym, a magazine, a phone contract — you choose). State your customer number and the date, write that you are cancelling within the notice period, ask for written confirmation and withdraw the consent you gave for advertising. Keep it short and give no reason — cancelling needs none, and that is part of the text as well.
task.free.prompt\u0000Dün katıldığın (ya da h: Write the minutes of a meeting you attended yesterday (or imagined). What was on the agenda, which decision was taken, who stated what and what is awaiting approval? Use the passive past at least once (ist … worden or wurde beschlossen) and the reporting mood at least once (sei / seien). The language of minutes does not use the first person singular.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir şeyi nasıl öğrendiğ: Describe how you learnt or measured something: a small experiment, a calculation, a comparison, a survey — real or imagined. Write the WAY, not the result. Use indem or dadurch, dass at least twice. At the end name the limit of the method as well: what could you not measure, what margin of error is there? If you give a figure, say where it comes from.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir iç görüş notu (Stel: Write an internal statement (Stellungnahme). The incident is below. Reject both escape moves — neither „the algorithm did it“ nor „a human took the final decision“ — and write concretely which levels the responsibility is assigned to and on what grounds. Use „Davon zu unterscheiden ist …“ or „insofern …, als …“ at least once. At the end propose three concrete measures.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir denemenin ya da küç: Report the result of a trial or a small piece of research — a software trial, a new way of working, an arrangement tried out at home, you choose. Keep this order: what was tried and how, what worked, what stayed open, what you propose. Shorten finished actions with a Partizip II attribute and give ongoing states with a Partizip I. If you give a figure, say where it comes from.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir toplumsal tartışmay: Write a short contribution to a public debate: housing, prices, the labour market or volunteering. Keep this structure: what the problem is, why the commonest explanation falls short, the real cause as you see it, and a concrete proposal. Use at least one je-desto sentence and at least one nominalised figure. Give the opposing view a sentence and take it seriously.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bildiğin bir sürecin na: Describe how a process you know works: making a product, handling an application, preparing a meal at home — you choose. Give the steps in order and use the passive throughout; do not escape into 'ich' or 'man'. Build the sequence with zuerst, dann, anschließend, zum Schluss. At the end say in one sentence why one of the steps is the hardest.
task.free.prompt\u0000Okuduğun bir yazıya oku: Write a letter to the editor about an article you have read — a real article or an editorial you invent. Keep this order: why you are writing, the point where you agree, the point where you disagree, and what you want. Link the concession and the objection with zwar … jedoch or einerseits … andererseits; use a participial attribute at least once as well. The tone may be sharp but not insulting.
task.free.prompt\u0000Ekibine kısa bir e-post: Write a short email to your team: report who has taken on what for an upcoming delivery, who is chiefly responsible, and on what condition the deadline will be met. Use a structure that stands in for the passive at least once (lässt sich … / ist zu …) and a conditional expression once (sofern or es sei denn). Write without cornering anybody, but leave nobody unclear about what they are doing.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir kuruma resmî bir şi: Write a formal letter of complaint to an institution: what you are referring to, what you have sent so far, how long you have waited, what you are demanding and what you will do if the deadline passes. Carry your anger in the grammar rather than the tone: use at least one nominalisation (die Verzögerung der …) and once a distanced expression of compulsion (Ich sehe mich gezwungen, … zu …). Use no exclamation marks.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir haftanın durum rapo: Write a status report for a week (your own work, a project or an imagined production unit — you choose). Let it have three parts: what has been done, what has to be done, and the present state. Use the passive past for what has been done (ist … worden), the modal passive for what has to be done (muss … werden), and the state passive with sein for the present state. Put the facts before the first person singular.
task.free.prompt\u0000Yöneticine bir e-posta: Write an email to your manager asking for a meeting about your pay. Keep this order: a short greeting and the subject, how long you have been there and in which role, what has changed in that time, the size of increase you expect and a suggestion for a meeting. Give the figure in the Konjunktiv II -ich hätte mir … vorgestellt- and tie the reason in with gemessen an. Do not be emotional and do not threaten; write things that can be counted.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir etkinliğin ya da hi: Announce that an event or a service is suspended for the time being — weather, building work, a fault, a shortage of staff, you choose. Write the same news TWICE. First for the group, short and everyday: with wegen and trotz, addressing them directly. Then for the notice board, formally: with aufgrund, infolge or angesichts, in the passive and with nominalisations, addressing nobody. Let the content stay the same; let only the register change.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir firmaya ya da kurum: Write a formal request for information to a company or an institution: an ambiguity in an offer, a clause in a contract, a fee, a deadline. Keep this structure: a subject line, which document you are referring to, two or three clear questions, by when you expect an answer, and a closing. Ask the questions in the Konjunktiv II and number them. No feeling, no reproach and no unnecessary explanation; every sentence either gives information or asks for it.
task.free.prompt\u0000Katılmadığı bir toplant: Report a meeting in writing to a colleague who was not there (real or imagined). Keep three things apart: who said what, what was decided, and what is only rumour. Give what was said in indirect speech (er sagte, … komme / sei), mark the rumour with angeblich or es heißt, and write the decisions in short sentences. If you add your own comment, put it in a separate sentence and mark it plainly.
task.free.prompt\u0000Zor bir dönemden geçen: Write a message to somebody going through a hard time: a lost job, illness, a separation, a move. Keep this order: what you have heard, how you see their situation, what you feel when you put yourself in their place, and a concrete offer. Avoid empty comfort - do not write 'bestimmt wird alles gut'. Use the pattern An deiner Stelle or Wie würdest du dich fühlen at least once and make the offer concrete: a day, a time, a task.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir yanlış anlamayı anl: Describe a misunderstanding: it may have come from language, from culture or simply from the tone of one sentence. Keep this order: the situation and the sentence that was said, how you understood it, what the other person meant, how it was cleared up and what you think today. Use als ob or als + Konjunktiv II at least once, and once a modal of supposition -dürfte, könnte, müsste-. Do not try to put anybody in the wrong.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir halk toplantısında: Write a two-minute speech for a public meeting — the subject could be an investment, a bus route, a budget item or a closure. It is a speech, so keep the sentences short and address the listener directly. Use sowohl … als auch or weder … noch at least once, and je-desto once. Give the opposing view in its strongest form rather than in your own words, and then answer it. Leave one single concrete demand at the end.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir kitap, film, sergi: Write a short review of a book, a film, an exhibition or a concert. Keep this order: what it is and what it is about, its best side, its weak side and whom you recommend it to. Do not give the ending away while you summarise. Use at least two relative clauses; let one of them be built with a preposition -über den, mit dem, von der- or with dessen/deren. Give reasons for what you did not like as well; 'it was good' or 'it was bad' is not a review on its own.
task.free.prompt\u0000Çevrende yayılmış bir y: Write a short text correcting a piece of misinformation going around you — for a neighbourhood group, a workplace or a community. Keep the four steps apart: the claim that is circulating, where the claim came from, what is actually the case, and what the reader should do from now on. Use the Konjunktiv I or soll when you report the claim, and give the facts in plain indicative sentences. Do not accuse; the point is to correct the information, not to embarrass anybody.
task.free.prompt\u0000Birlikte çalıştığın, ok: Write a reference for somebody you have worked with, studied with or seen at work — real or imagined. Keep this order: who, in which period, in which role; what they did; the concrete occasion on which they showed themselves; and the closing recommendation. The rule: back every piece of praise with an occasion. Use at least two participial attributes -die von ihm geleistete Arbeit and the like- and at least one passive Perfekt. Do not overstate; an inflated reference is worthless.
task.free.prompt\u0000Kurmayı düşündüğün ya d: Describe a business you are thinking of starting or have imagined, in one page — a workshop, a service, a small shop, freelance work. Keep this order: what you would do, for whom, on which conditions you would start, the money for the first year and what you see as risky. Build the conditions with sofern, tie the purposes together with um … zu, and write the formal steps with nominalisations. At the end an honest sentence to yourself: why might this business fail?
task.free.prompt\u0000Bir okur mektubu yaz (L: Write a letter to the editor (Leserbrief). The subject: a proposal to ban private cars from the town centre. The method is compulsory: (1) take the opposing view apart from the inside with a HYPOTHESIS structure — „Angenommen, …“ or „Gesetzt den Fall, …“ — and name where it breaks; (2) state the conflict of aims with both its halves, not one; (3) write your own position plainly at the end. Do not accuse the other side of bad faith; show the breaking point.
task.free.prompt\u0000Aklında kalan bir günü: Describe a day that has stayed with you: a concert, a match, a festival, a journey. Keep this order: where you went and what you expected, what happened there, the single moment you remember most, and what you think looking back today. The rule: do not fob it off with adjectives like 'wonderful', 'super' or 'really lovely'. Instead describe the effect with indem at least once, use a nominalisation at least once -beim Auftritt …, die Stimmung der Menge- and a participial attribute once.
task.free.prompt\u0000Emekliye ayrılan meslek: Write a three-minute farewell speech for a colleague who is retiring. The rules: (1) let the praise be CONCRETE — tell one single occasion instead of piling up adjectives; (2) use a mistake of your own somewhere, in a way that is funny and does not belittle the other person; (3) do not overstate — expressions like „unglaublich, einmalig, der beste Mensch“ are banned; (4) end with a wish, not with a tearful closing. The audience is a team of fifteen; the tone is warm but measured.
task.free.prompt\u0000Şimdiki rahatlık ile il: Write yourself a note about a decision that means choosing between comfort now and a result later: changing jobs, taking on extra work, starting something expensive, starting to save. Keep this order: what the decision is, what you lose now, what you gain later, the biggest risk and your decision today. Use at least one obwohl clause and at least one genitive phrase built with trotz or während. Do not try to talk yourself into it; write the other side out in full as well.
task.free.prompt\u0000İki kapanıştan birini y: Write one of two closings. A: The last two minutes of a presentation — a summary of at most three points, then a look ahead -what, when, who- and at the end a concrete question put to the room. B: A short farewell speech for a colleague who is leaving or retiring — start with a memory, then say concretely what you admired, and at the end leave the door open. Whichever you choose: add no new information, and give dates and names concretely. If you choose B, build at least one nachdem sentence and get the sequence of tenses right.
task.free.prompt\u0000Bugün Almancaya başlaya: Write a letter to somebody starting German today. The rules: (1) give at least two CONCRETE pieces of advice — a doable step, not general encouragement; (2) do not make light of the difficulty, say honestly how long it took you; (3) describe a setback and write not how it passed but what you thought at the time; (4) build a sentence about being bilingual, but do not use the cliche 'it is an enrichment' as it stands — say it in your own words; (5) let the last sentence resonate without carrying a new argument. Write it as a letter, not as an end-of-course statement.

task.build.hint\u0000je yan cümlede fiil sond: In the je clause the verb goes last; after desto the verb comes straight away.
task.build.hint\u0000Yüklemdeki sıfat çekilme: An adjective in the predicate takes no ending.
task.build.hint\u0000indem yan cümlesinde özn: In an indem clause the subject is repeated and the verb goes last.
task.build.hint\u0000Ayrılabilen fiil: önek s: A separable verb: the prefix goes last.
task.build.hint\u0000Yer öne alınınca fiil ik: When the place is fronted, the verb is in second position.
task.build.hint\u0000Zaman öne alınınca fiil: When the time is fronted, the verb is in second position.
task.build.hint\u0000lassen artı dönüşlü zami: lassen plus a reflexive pronoun; the infinitive goes right at the end.
task.build.hint\u0000als ob Konjunktiv II ist: als ob wants the Konjunktiv II; in the clause the verb goes last.
task.build.hint\u0000Edilgen Perfekt: sein, o: Passive Perfekt: sein, the participle, and the shortened worden at the end.
task.build.hint\u0000Sahip nötr olduğu için d: The owner is neuter, so dessen; the noun that follows takes no article.
task.build.hint\u0000Eşitlik kalıbı → so … wi: The pattern for equality → so … wie.
task.build.hint\u0000Kişiye gidiş → zu + Dati: Going to a person → zu + Dativ.
task.build.hint\u0000Ölçü de edatsız Akkusati: A measurement is accusative without a preposition too.
task.build.hint\u0000Geçmişte tek seferlik: a: A single occasion in the past: als.
task.build.hint\u0000Özne aynı kalıyor: um …: The subject stays the same: um … zu.

task.build.hint\u0000„aus“ + Dativ, zamirin ö: „aus“ + Dativ, in front of the pronoun.
task.build.hint\u0000Samimi hâl: „Wie geht es: The familiar form: „Wie geht es dir?“
task.build.hint\u0000Aynı kural: fiil ikinci: The same rule: the verb in second position.

task.build.hint\u0000Burası gerçek bir KOŞUL: This is a real CONDITION → wenn.

task.build.hint\u0000Muayeneyi doktor yapar →: The doctor does the examining → lassen.

task.build.hint\u0000Tek istisna: zu Fuß, art: The one exception: zu Fuß, with no article.

task.build.hint\u0000„entstehen“ durum değişi: „entstehen“ is a change of state → sein.

task.build.hint\u0000Tekrarlanan olay: jedes: A repeated event: jedes Mal, wenn …
task.build.hint\u0000Bağlaç → dass; nesne art: The conjunction → dass; the object article → das.
task.build.hint\u0000Burada gerçek özne var →: There is a real subject here → a plural verb.

task.build.hint\u0000lassen artı dönüşlü zami: lassen plus a reflexive pronoun; the infinitive last.
task.build.hint\u0000Soru kelimesi başta, fii: The question word first, the verb in second position.

task.build.hint\u0000Yardımcı fiil ikinci sır: The auxiliary in second position, the participle at the end.

task.build.hint\u0000„bremsen“ hareket değil: „bremsen“ is an action, not a movement → haben.
task.build.hint\u0000Süren durum → seit + Dat: A state that lasts → seit + Dativ, with the present tense.
task.build.hint\u0000„den ganzen Tag“ — edat: „den ganzen Tag“ — no preposition, but the accusative.

task.build.hint\u0000Sayı zarfı öne alınınca: When the adverb of number is fronted, the verb is in second position.
task.build.hint\u0000sich lassen + mastar: ed: sich lassen + infinitive: it carries a passive sense.
task.build.hint\u0000Uyan şey öznedir: die Ho: What fits is the subject: die Hose passt, the person is mir.
task.build.hint\u0000„es gibt“ nesne ister: e: „es gibt“ wants an object: einen klaren Vorteil.
task.build.hint\u0000„nicht“ nesneden SONRA,: „nicht“ comes AFTER the object and before the participle.
task.build.hint\u0000Öznesiz edilgen: bei mir: A subjectless passive: bei mir wurde eingebrochen.

task.build.hint\u0000Zaman zarfı öne alınınca: When the time adverb is fronted, the verb is in second position.

task.build.hint\u0000„trotzdem“ de zarftır: f: „trotzdem“ is an adverb too: the verb comes straight after it.

task.build.hint\u0000Burada özne gerçekten iş: Here the subject really is the work → the adjective describes the work.
task.build.hint\u0000Dönüşlü uns ile; teklif: With the reflexive uns; the offer comes as a question.

task.build.hint\u0000Edilgen: fail söylenmiyo: The passive: the agent is not named, the action comes forward.
task.build.hint\u0000in Kraft setzen: in Kraf: in Kraft setzen: the phrase in Kraft comes before the verb.
task.build.hint\u0000Kısa ve kuru: özne, fiil: Short and dry: subject, verb, object. No reasons.
task.build.hint\u0000nachdem yan cümlesi; ana: A nachdem clause; the main clause starts with the verb.
task.build.hint\u0000Ortaç II: test bitmiş, e: Partizip II: the test is finished and it carries a passive sense.
task.build.hint\u0000statt … zu: iki seçeneği: statt … zu: it sets the two options against each other.
task.build.hint\u0000Şimdiki zaman edilgeni;: The present passive; the agent is given with von.
task.build.hint\u0000Tarih sıra sayısıyla: am: The date with an ordinal: am + the number + -ten/-sten.
task.build.hint\u0000um … zu kalıbı doğaçlama: The um … zu pattern is the pulling-together move when you improvise.
task.build.hint\u0000-ieren ile biten fiiller: Verbs ending in -ieren take no ge- in the Perfekt.
task.build.hint\u0000„leider“ birinci öğe değ: If „leider“ is not the first element, the subject stays at the front.
task.build.hint\u0000Artikelsiz kullanımda da: Adjective endings apply with no article as well.
task.build.hint\u0000aufgrund tamlayan hâli i: aufgrund wants the genitive: der kurzen Zeit.
task.build.hint\u0000Ayrılabilen fiil: önek c: A separable verb: the prefix stays at the end of the sentence.
task.build.hint\u0000Burada gerçek özne var (: There is a real subject here (niemand), so no „es“.
task.build.hint\u0000Dolaylı soru: bağlaçtan: An indirect question: after the conjunction the verb goes last.
task.build.hint\u0000dürfen'in dilek kipi tel: The subjunctive of dürfen is the standard opening on the phone.
task.build.hint\u0000geltend machen: sabit öb: geltend machen: a fixed phrase, the object goes in between.
task.build.hint\u0000İki yarıda da karşılaştı: A comparative is used in both halves.
task.build.hint\u0000infolge sonucu vurgular: infolge stresses the consequence and belongs to the formal register.
task.build.hint\u0000Kalıp cümlenin başında d: The pattern stands at the start of the sentence and the subject moves back.
task.build.hint\u0000Kaynak belirtilince fiil: Once a source is named the verb goes into the reporting mood.
task.build.hint\u0000Nötr isim, belirsiz arti: A neuter noun with an indefinite article: ein kleinES Foto.
task.build.hint\u0000Ortaç II sıfatı artı edi: A Partizip II attribute plus the passive: the language of formal procedure.
task.build.hint\u0000„deshalb“ zarftır: hemen: „deshalb“ is an adverb: the verb comes straight after it.
task.build.hint\u0000„solange“ yan cümlesi; a: A „solange“ clause; the main clause starts with the verb.
task.build.hint\u0000als + Konjunktiv II, fii: als + Konjunktiv II, the verb straight after als.
task.build.hint\u0000Burada iki ayrı isim var: There are two separate nouns here, joined by „für“.
task.build.hint\u0000dass yan cümlesinde çeki: In a dass clause the finite verb goes right to the end.
task.build.hint\u0000Dolaylı aktarımda Konjun: Konjunktiv I in indirect speech: sei instead of ist.
task.build.hint\u0000Edilgen sıfat: kimin har: A passive participle: who excluded it is not said.
task.build.hint\u0000indem yöntemi bildirir;: indem states the method; the verb goes last in the clause.
task.build.hint\u0000lassen artı dönüşlü zami: lassen plus a reflexive pronoun stands in for the passive.

task.build.hint\u0000Yan cümlede fiil EN SONA: In a subordinate clause the verb goes RIGHT TO THE END: „… dass das ein guter Vorschlag ist“.
task.build.hint\u0000Yeşil ışık verilen taraf: Whoever is given the green light is in the dative; the adjective declines with no article.
task.build.hint\u0000„rechnen mit“ nesnesi bi: If the object of „rechnen mit“ is a clause, the preposition is announced first as „damit“.
task.build.hint\u0000Sıfat sonuna karşılaştır: The adjective takes the comparative ending and „als“ stands between the two things.
task.build.hint\u0000Sıklık kalıbı: „zweimal: The pattern for frequency: „zweimal pro Woche“. „Sport machen“ is built with no article.
task.build.hint\u0000Alman ölçeğinde „nicht s: On the German scale „nicht schlecht“ is not the middle but the start of the positive side.
task.build.hint\u0000Gişede sabit kalıp: „Ein: The fixed phrase at the counter: „Einmal nach …, bitte.“ The city comes with „nach“.
task.build.hint\u0000İzin soruluyor → „dürfen: Permission is being asked → „dürfen“. The modal moves to the front and the main verb stays last.
task.build.hint\u0000sein + zu + mastar: edil: sein + zu + infinitive: it stands in for the passive, and here it states an impossibility.
task.build.hint\u0000Üç kural bir arada: zama: Three rules together: time in front → the verb second → the separable prefix at the end.
task.build.hint\u0000„das Haar“ tarifte çoğul: „das Haar“ is used in the plural when you describe it: lange Haare. In the plural the adjective takes -e.
task.build.hint\u0000„um … zu“ amaç bildirir;: „um … zu“ states a purpose; if it is fronted the main clause starts straight away with the verb.
task.build.hint\u0000Cinssiz isim, belirsiz a: A neuter noun with an indefinite article: the adjective takes a two-letter ending — hellblaues.
task.build.hint\u0000Cümle „Mir“ ile başlayab: The sentence can start with „Mir“: „Mir gefällt …“ — and the verb is still in second position.
task.build.hint\u0000Dolaylı soruda edat soru: In an indirect question the preposition merges with the question pronoun (worauf) and the verb goes last.
task.build.hint\u0000Edilgen Perfekt: yardımc: The passive Perfekt: the auxiliary sein, the participle, and the shortened worden at the end.
task.build.hint\u0000Fiyat sorarken „Was kost: To ask the price you use „Was kostet …?“; „Wie viel kostet …?“ works too.
task.build.hint\u0000Hareket var, soru NEREYE: There is movement and the question is WHERE TO → the accusative (an die). Same preposition, different case.
task.build.hint\u0000Yine -er + als; sıfat is: Again -er + als; and because the adjective is in front of the noun it takes a declension ending as well.
task.build.hint\u0000„man“ belirsiz özne: kiş: „man“ is an indefinite subject: nobody in particular. „Was kann man …“ = what can be seen.
task.build.hint\u0000„zu Fuß“ değişmez bir ka: „zu Fuß“ is an invariable phrase: on foot. With a vehicle we would say „mit dem Bus“.
task.build.hint\u0000AYRILABİLİR FİİL: aufste: A SEPARABLE VERB: aufstehen → „stehe … auf“. The prefix goes to the END of the sentence.
task.build.hint\u0000Neye iyi geldiği „gegen“: What it is good for is said with „gegen“, and that preposition brings the accusative.
task.build.hint\u0000Resmî emir: fiil başta,: A formal imperative: the verb first, Sie straight after it; the separable prefix at the end.
task.build.hint\u0000Yaş için kalıp „ist … Ja: The pattern for age is „ist … Jahre alt“; adjectives (gut) take no ending in the predicate.
task.build.hint\u0000Adlaştırma: die Zunahme: A nominalisation: die Zunahme der Preise. Pulling the participle forward puts the stress there.
task.build.hint\u0000Bu bağlaç yan cümle açar: This conjunction opens a subordinate clause and the verb goes RIGHT TO THE END: „… weil ich hier arbeite“.
task.build.hint\u0000Çekince bağlacı sona ata: The conjunction of reservation sends the verb to the end; if the clause comes first the main clause starts with the verb.
task.build.hint\u0000dürfte yüksek olasılık;: dürfte is high probability; müsste is a logical inference and könnte a weak possibility.
task.build.hint\u0000Yine „war“ — „ist gewese: „war“ again — not „ist gewesen“. „alles“ counts as singular: war, not waren.
task.build.hint\u0000„Das Wetter ist …“ — sıf: „Das Wetter ist …“ — the adjectives stand at the end of the sentence and take no ending: schön, warm.
task.build.hint\u0000„mal“ cümleyi gündelikle: „mal“ makes the sentence casual and takes the edge off it; it does not mean „once“.
task.build.hint\u0000abbiegen ayrılabilir: „B: abbiegen is separable: „Biegen Sie … ab“. In the imperative too the prefix stays at the END.
task.build.hint\u0000Dilek kipi teklifi öneri: The subjunctive turns the offer into a suggestion; the reflexive pronoun straight after the verb.
task.build.hint\u0000sein + zu + mastar edilg: sein + zu + infinitive stands in for the passive: it gives the sense of 'has to be done'.
task.build.hint\u0000Yer değiştirme anlatan „: „ziehen“ describes a change of place, so its Perfekt is built with sein: bin … gezogen.
task.build.hint\u0000Bu bir edat, yan cümle k: This is a preposition, it opens no clause. Because it is at the front, the subject drops behind the verb.
task.build.hint\u0000İki nesne varsa kişi önc: With two objects the person comes first in the dative, the thing after it in the accusative.
task.build.hint\u0000Yol tarifinde emir kipi: Directions use the imperative, and in the formal form the verb comes FIRST: „Gehen Sie …“
task.build.hint\u0000Aktarılan soruda da Konj: A reported question takes the Konjunktiv I as well and the verb of the clause goes last.
task.build.hint\u0000So sehr …, so oft …: iki: So sehr …, so oft …: in neither half is the verb last, and the second half starts with the verb.
task.build.hint\u0000umtauschen ayrılabilir a: umtauschen is separable, but with „möchte“ it stands as an infinitive at the END and does not split.
task.build.hint\u0000Zaman bilgisi („zum Früh: The time expression („zum Frühstück“) comes straight after the verb, and the object after that.
task.build.hint\u0000Zaman sözcüğü başa gelin: When the time word is fronted the verb still stays in SECOND position: Morgen fahren wir …
task.build.hint\u0000„gehen“ yer değiştirmedi: „gehen“ is a change of place → the auxiliary is SEIN. „Ich habe gegangen“ is wrong.
task.build.hint\u0000anfangen ayrılabilir: „f: anfangen is separable: „fängt … an“. And a → ä changes as well: ich fange, er fängt.
task.build.hint\u0000die Mutter dişil olduğu: die Mutter is feminine, so „meine“; der Vater is masculine, so „mein Vater“.
task.build.hint\u0000Kalıp sabittir: „allergi: The pattern is fixed: „allergisch gegen“ + Akkusativ. The plural is used: gegen Nüsse.
task.build.hint\u0000Samimi emir: „schick“ (s: The familiar imperative: „schick“ (no final -e). „mir“ is dative, „eine Nachricht“ accusative.
task.build.hint\u0000Soru NEREDE → yönelme hâ: The question is WHERE → the dative (in der). For something lying there you use „liegen“.
task.build.hint\u0000„dauern“ süre bildirir v: „dauern“ states a length of time and takes the accusative: dauert zwei Tage, dauert eine Stunde.
task.build.hint\u0000„möchten“ Akkusativ iste: „möchten“ wants the accusative: der Kaffee → einen Kaffee. Feminine eine, neuter ein.
task.build.hint\u0000Bu bağlaç söz dizimine d: This conjunction does not touch the word order: after the comma an ordinary sentence, the verb second.
task.build.hint\u0000Bu fiil hem dönüşlü zami: This verb wants both a reflexive pronoun and the preposition „an“, and that preposition brings the accusative.
task.build.hint\u0000je yan cümle (fiil sonda: je is the subordinate clause (verb last), desto the main clause (verb straight after the comparative).
task.build.hint\u0000Zaman ifadesi başa gelin: When the time expression is fronted the verb is in second position again: Das nächste Mal KOMME ich …
task.build.hint\u0000„für“ edatından sonra Ak: After the preposition „für“ comes the accusative: für eine Woche. The month takes „im“: im Juli.
task.build.hint\u0000„haben“ ile de kurulur,: It works with „haben“ and with „Es gibt“ alike: Es gibt drei Zimmer in meiner Wohnung.
task.build.hint\u0000„suchen“ Akkusativ ister: „suchen“ wants the accusative: die Jacke → eine Jacke; der Pullover → einen Pullover.
task.build.hint\u0000Almancada gecikme „haben: In German a delay is built with „haben“: „hat Verspätung“ — not „ist verspätet“.
task.build.hint\u0000En üstün derece belirli: The superlative comes not with a definite article but with an adjective ending: „meine größte Stärke“.
task.build.hint\u0000Olay anlatıldığı için Pe: The Perfekt, because an event is being told: „verschlafen“ has an unstressed prefix, so the participle takes no „ge“.
task.build.hint\u0000Partizip I süren bir eyl: Partizip I describes an ongoing action (gehen → gehend) and it declines like an adjective too.
task.build.hint\u0000Soruda modal fiil en baş: In a question the modal moves right to the front; the main verb (feiern) still stays at the end.
task.build.hint\u0000Yine süren bir durum: „s: An ongoing state again: „seit“ + the present tense. The adjective is a predicate, so it takes no ending.
task.build.hint\u0000„man darf nicht/kein…“ g: „man darf nicht/kein…“ states a general prohibition. If nobody in particular is meant, you use „man“.
task.build.hint\u0000„müssen“ ile mastar SOND: With „müssen“ the infinitive stands at the END and the separable verb does not split: muss ich umsteigen.
task.build.hint\u0000„Yoktu“ = sahip olmak fi: Not having something is the short past of the verb to have plus a negative. With a masculine noun: keinen.
task.build.hint\u0000Edilgen cümlede eylemi k: In a passive sentence who did it need not be said; what comes forward is the action itself.
task.build.hint\u0000Emirde fiil başa geçer;: In an imperative the verb moves to the front; the separable prefix drops to the end and shows the direction.
task.build.hint\u0000Sahte özne es ve mastar: The dummy subject es and an infinitive phrase: with a separable verb the zu goes in the middle (vorzustellen).
task.build.hint\u0000„seit“ süre anlatır ve D: „seit“ states a stretch and wants the dative; in the Perfekt the Partizip II stays at the end of the sentence.
task.build.hint\u0000Meslek söylerken artikel: With a job NO article is used: „Ich bin Verkäufer“ — not „ein Verkäufer“.
task.build.hint\u0000„sich lassen“ edilgenin: „sich lassen“ stands in for the passive and means the same as „kann belegt werden“.
task.build.hint\u0000Ayrılabilen fiilin Parti: In the participle of a separable verb the „ge-“ slips BETWEEN the prefix and the stem: teil-ge-nommen.
task.build.hint\u0000Cümlenin başına özne dış: If anything other than the subject opens the sentence, the finite verb still stays in SECOND position.
task.build.hint\u0000Cümlenin başına yer ya d: You can put a place or an object at the front of the sentence; the finite verb still stays in second position.
task.build.hint\u0000Modal fiil ikinci sırada: The modal is in second position and the main verb (empfehlen) stays bare at the end of the sentence.
task.build.hint\u0000Samimi emir kipi: fiilin: The familiar imperative: the verb stem stays BARE and „du“ drops — „trink“, not „trinke“.
task.build.hint\u0000„dass“ de yan cümle kura: „dass“ opens a subordinate clause too: the subject first, the finite verb (bekomme) last. The comma is compulsory.
task.build.hint\u0000„die Flasche“ sayıdan so: „die Flasche“ goes plural after a number: zwei Flaschen. But „Mineralwasser“ does not change.
task.build.hint\u0000Burada „können“ İMKÂN/ri: Here „können“ marks POSSIBILITY or a request — not ability. English uses "can" for both as well.
task.build.hint\u0000Burada „können“ YETENEK: Here „können“ marks ABILITY. The infinitive stands at the END of the sentence: kann … schwimmen.
task.build.hint\u0000doch daveti ısrar değil: doch does not press the invitation, it encourages; it answers a refusal that has not been spoken.
task.build.hint\u0000Teklif kurarken fiil BAŞ: When you make a suggestion the verb comes FIRST: „Gehen wir …?“ — „Wollen wir …?“ does the same job.
task.build.hint\u0000„brauchen“ akkusatif ist: „brauchen“ wants the accusative: einen Termin. The standard opening for making an appointment on the phone.
task.build.hint\u0000„Es gibt“ + Akkusativ: e: „Es gibt“ + Akkusativ: es gibt einen/keinen Aufzug. It is what English says with "there is" and "there is no".
task.build.hint\u0000„haben“ Akkusativ ister:: „haben“ wants the accusative: der Bruder → einen Bruder. The feminine does not change: eine Schwester.
task.build.hint\u0000anprobieren ayrılabilir: anprobieren is a separable verb, but with „kann“ it stands as an infinitive at the END and does not split.
task.build.hint\u0000Burada ağrıyan yer ÖZNE: Here the place that hurts becomes the SUBJECT and a possessive is used. „wehtun“ is separable: the prefix at the end.
task.build.hint\u0000Cümle zaman bilgisiyle b: When the sentence opens with a time expression the verb stays in SECOND position and the subject comes after it.
task.build.hint\u0000Yan cümlede geçmiş zaman: There is a past tense in the clause: the participle first, the auxiliary right at the END — „angerufen haben“.
task.build.hint\u0000„ein bisschen“ fiilden s: „ein bisschen“ comes after the verb, in front of the object: Ich spreche ein bisschen Deutsch.
task.build.hint\u0000„obwohl“ bir yan cümle a: „obwohl“ opens a subordinate clause and sends the verb to the end; the clause can stand in front or behind.
task.build.hint\u0000das Geld nötr → „kein Ge: das Geld is neuter → „kein Geld“. In the feminine and the plural it becomes „keine“: keine Zeit, keine Kinder.
task.build.hint\u0000Gerçekleşmemiş dilek Kon: A wish that has not come true wants the Konjunktiv II: „würde + Infinitiv“, the infinitive at the end.
task.build.hint\u0000Kısa kalıp, fiilsiz. „Ma: A short phrase, with no verb. „Mach dir keine Sorgen“ is the long form; in everyday speech the short one is enough.
task.build.hint\u0000„funktionieren“ makine v: „funktionieren“ is used for machines and electrics; it means the same as „kaputt sein“ in reverse.
task.build.hint\u0000Aynı randevu kalıyor, ya: The same appointment stays, only the time changes → „ändern“. The object goes into the accusative.
task.build.hint\u0000„ja“ karşındakinin zaten: „ja“ points to something the listener already knows and puts the sentence on common ground.
task.build.hint\u0000„aber“ iki ana cümleyi b: „aber“ joins two main clauses and does not disturb the order; „würde“ stays second and the infinitive last.
task.build.hint\u0000Aitlik fiilinde eşya ÖZN: With the verb of belonging the thing becomes the SUBJECT and the owner stands in the dative — as English says "it belongs to me".
task.build.hint\u0000İlgi cümlesi ismin hemen: A relative clause slips in straight after the noun, is marked off by two commas, and its verb goes last.
task.build.hint\u0000„sein + zu + mastar“ da: „sein + zu + infinitive“ also stands in for the passive; depending on the context it states possibility or obligation.
task.build.hint\u0000Cümle başına zaman ifade: Either a time expression or an object can open the sentence; what you choose decides what is brought forward.
task.build.hint\u0000Perfekt iki parçalıdır:: The Perfekt has two parts: the auxiliary (habe) in second position, the Partizip II (gefunden) right at the end.
task.build.hint\u0000„aber“ kelime sırasını d: „aber“ does not change the word order; when the time expression is fronted the verb still stays in second position.
task.build.hint\u0000„immer“ gibi sıklık sözc: Adverbs of frequency such as „immer“ come straight after the verb; adjectives in the predicate take no ending.
task.build.hint\u0000DİKKAT: özne „es“ — „ich: CAREFUL: the subject is „es“ — you do NOT say „ich klappe nicht“. It says whether the thing worked, not the person.
task.build.hint\u0000En üstünlük iki parçalı:: The superlative has two parts: the merged preposition in front, the syllable at the end. No word of comparison is used.
task.build.hint\u0000Ödünç ALAN için yanında: The one who BORROWS has a dative pronoun beside them: „mir ausleihen“ = to borrow for oneself.
task.build.hint\u0000Partizip II sıfat olarak: The Partizip II comes in front of the noun as an adjective and declines like one: abgestellt → abgestellten.
task.build.hint\u0000Partizip'i başa almak vu: Putting the participle first strengthens the emphasis; the second order brings the negated element forward instead.
task.build.hint\u0000„trotzdem“ yan cümle açm: „trotzdem“ opens no subordinate clause, it is an element in a main clause; fronted, the verb comes straight after it.
task.build.hint\u0000„zu“ + sıfat = fazla: zu: „zu“ + adjective = too much: zu teuer, zu kurz, zu klein. „sehr teuer“ only means very expensive.
task.build.hint\u0000Eskisini bırakıp yenisin: You give up the old one and take a new one → „wechseln“. English uses one word for both, German does not.
task.build.hint\u0000Miktardan sonra ad ARTİK: After a quantity the noun comes with NO article and in the plural: ein Kilo Tomaten — not „ein Kilo die Tomaten“.
task.build.hint\u0000Yön bildiren „in“ Akkusa: Directional „in“ wants the accusative; and because „ziehen“ describes movement its Perfekt is built with sein.
task.build.hint\u0000„unternehmen“ yer değişt: „unternehmen“ involves no change of place → „haben“. The unstressed prefix means no „ge“ in the participle: unternommen.
task.build.hint\u0000Doktorun söylediği aktar: What the doctor said is being reported → „sollen“. With the time adverb in front, the subject drops behind the verb.
task.build.hint\u0000Modal fiil (kannst) ikin: The modal (kannst) stands in second position and the main verb (abholen) goes bare to the END of the sentence.
task.build.hint\u0000Vorgangspassiv: werden +: Vorgangspassiv: werden + Partizip II. Who does it is not said, because what matters is the action itself.
task.build.hint\u0000„als“ tek başına kullanı: When „als“ is used on its own the verb comes straight after it; the time adverb can stand in either position.
task.build.hint\u0000„möchte“ kibar biçimdir;: „möchte“ is the polite form; „ich will“ sounds blunt in this context. The second verb goes to the end as an INFINITIVE.
task.build.hint\u0000Bitmiş bir nokta → „vor“: A finished point → „vor“ and the PAST tense. With the time expression in front, the subject drops behind the verb.
task.build.hint\u0000Edilgen çatı „werden + P: The passive is built with „werden + Partizip II“: werden in second position, the participle at the end of the sentence.
task.build.hint\u0000Ağrıyan yer ÖZNEDİR: „Me: The place that hurts is the SUBJECT: „Mein Kopf tut weh.“ — „Ich tue weh“ is WRONG. „weh tun“ separates: tut … weh.
task.build.hint\u0000DİKKAT: Almancada „halb“: CAREFUL: German „halb“ points at the NEXT hour. Half past eight = halb neun, half past nine = halb zehn.
task.build.hint\u0000Geçmişteki gerçekleşmemi: An unrealised possibility in the past: „hätte“ + two infinitives; the modal turns into an infinitive, not a participle.
task.build.hint\u0000Kip fiili geçmişte kısa: The modal takes its short form in the past and the main verb stays at the END. No article goes in front of the job.
task.build.hint\u0000DİKKAT: müzik aleti ARTİ: CAREFUL: a musical instrument comes with NO article — „Ich spiele Gitarre / Klavier“. You do not say „die Gitarre spielen“.
task.build.hint\u0000Araçla gitmek „fahren“;: Going by vehicle is „fahren“; the vehicle comes with „mit dem/der“: mit dem Bus, mit der Bahn. Walking is „gehen“.
task.build.hint\u0000Dönüşlü zamir YÖNELME hâ: The reflexive pronoun is in the DATIVE (mir) and in front of the injured part there is a definite article, not a possessive (den).
task.build.hint\u0000„helfen“ Dativ ister: mi: „helfen“ wants the dative: mir, dir, ihm — NOT „mich helfen“. It is the same logic as English "help me" with an object.
task.build.hint\u0000Kip fiilinin bu biçimi d: This form of the modal does not demand, it asks — with the neighbours it is always the one used first time round.
task.build.hint\u0000„Leider“ başa gelince fi: When „Leider“ is fronted the verb comes straight after it: Leider KANN ich … That is the German verb-second rule.
task.build.hint\u0000Süre hâlâ sürüyor → „sei: The stretch is still going → „seit“ and the verb stays in the PRESENT. The preposition brings the dative: seit drei Jahren.
task.build.hint\u0000Soruda yardımcı fiil baş: In a question the auxiliary moves to the front, the participle stays at the end, and the separable prefix opens it: ausgeschaltet.
task.build.hint\u0000Olmak fiili geçmişte Per: The verb to be does not build a Perfekt in the past, it takes its short form: war. With the time expression in front the subject drops back.
task.build.hint\u0000„verreisen“ yer değiştir: „verreisen“ is a verb of movement → it takes „sein“. Because the time expression is in front, the subject drops behind the verb.
task.build.hint\u0000İkinci biçim: kişi DATİF: The second pattern: the person in the DATIVE („mir“), the organ with an article. „Mein Hals tut weh“ is right too, and both are used.
task.build.hint\u0000Dolaylı aktarımda fiil K: In indirect speech the verb goes into the Konjunktiv I; if the plural form looks like the indicative, the Konjunktiv II is used.
task.build.hint\u0000„weil“ yan cümle kurar:: „weil“ opens a subordinate clause: the finite verb (hatte) goes to the END of the sentence. English "because" leaves the order alone.
task.build.hint\u0000Geçmişe dönük gerçek dış: An unreal condition looking back: Konjunktiv II + the passive → „gemeldet worden wäre“. In the main clause „wären … entstanden“.
task.build.hint\u0000Partizipialattribut: „di: Partizipialattribut: „die Studie, die veröffentlicht wurde“ is pulled into an adjective phrase and slips BETWEEN the article and the noun.
task.build.hint\u0000KURALDIŞI: „bleiben“de h: AGAINST THE RULE: there is NO movement in „bleiben“ and yet the auxiliary is „sein“ again. This is where learners trip most often — learn it by heart.
task.build.hint\u0000Almancada „duruyor“ için: German has three verbs for standing about: things that stand UPRIGHT take stehen, things that LIE take liegen, things that HANG take hängen. A sofa stands upright.
task.build.hint\u0000„gehen“ bir yer değişimi: „gehen“ is a change of place, so its Perfekt is built with „sein“: bin … gegangen. With the time in front the verb is in second position again.
task.build.hint\u0000„gefallen“ Dativ ister v: „gefallen“ wants the dative and the third person changes form: er → ihm, sie → ihr, sie (plural) → ihnen. „Das gefällt sie“ is WRONG.
task.build.hint\u0000Almanya'da davete bu SOR: In Germany this IS asked when you are invited, and bringing something is expected. „mitbringen“ separates: soll ich … mitbringen (the infinitive last, written as one word).
„die Heimat“ = home country. CAREFUL: some countries carry an article — „die Türkei“, „die Schweiz“ — and most do not (Deutschland, Italien).
task.build.hint\u0000Cümle zaman bilgisiyle b: If the sentence opens with a time expression the verb stays in SECOND position and the subject comes after the verb: „Heute lerne ich“ — NOT „Heute ich lerne“.
task.build.hint\u0000Perfekt iki parçalıdır:: The Perfekt has two parts: the auxiliary (habe) in second position, the participle at the END of the sentence. With a separable verb the ge- slips into the middle: an-ge-fangen.
task.build.hint\u0000CÜMLE KISKACI: „habe“ ik: THE SENTENCE BRACKET: „habe“ in second position, the participle „gekauft“ RIGHT AT THE END; everything else stays between the two. „kaufen“ is no movement → haben.
task.build.hint\u0000Nominalstil: yan cümle y: Nominalstil: a noun phrase instead of a subordinate clause. „Nach der Digitalisierung der Bestände“ instead of „Nachdem die Bestände digitalisiert worden waren“.
task.build.hint\u0000Ayrılabilen fiilin ortac: In the participle of a separable verb the „ge-“ goes INSIDE the prefix: auf·GE·standen. There is no such thing as „geaufstanden“. And getting up is a change of place → sein.
task.build.hint\u0000DİKKAT: Türkçedeki „beğe: CAREFUL: the subject is the other way round from English "like". The person who likes is in the dative (mir) and the thing liked is the SUBJECT: „Die Jacke gefällt mir“ — NOT „Ich gefalle die Jacke“.
task.build.hint\u0000DİKKAT: „sein“ Perfekt K: CAREFUL: „sein“ does NOT use the Perfekt. „Ich bin krank gewesen“ is hardly ever heard — even in speech you say „war“. The same holds for „haben“ (hatte).
task.build.hint\u0000Nesneyi ikinci kez adlan: You do not name the object a second time, you point at it with a PRONOUN — and the pronoun follows the object's article: der Pullover → ihn, die Jacke → sie, das Hemd → es. Through A1 you learnt „mir/dir“; this is the third-person form.

task.task.stimulus\u0000OLAY NOTU\n\nKredi ba:
INCIDENT NOTE

For six months a loan pre-screening system rejected applications from one particular postcode at three times the average rate. The system does not use the postcode directly; it reached the same result indirectly, through income stability and how often the address had changed.

Process: the system produces a score and a recommendation. An employee approves the recommendation. Measurement: employees approve 98% of the recommendations unchanged; the average review takes 40 seconds per application.

The system was built by a supplier; the training data is the bank's own past decisions. The product owner is the marketing department, technical operation is IT, and oversight sits with internal audit.

mock.exchange.tr\u0000Zorunlu bir süreci yanl: I think a compulsory procedure is wrong. It drags everything out for years and wears down the very people who have the least time. What do you think?
